### § 51.1-162. Death before retirement.

**A.** If a member dies before retirement, and if no benefits are payable under subsection B, the amount of his accumulated contributions shall be paid to the designated beneficiary or to a surviving relative according to the order of precedence set forth in this section. This amount shall be reduced by the amount of any retirement allowance previously received by the member under this chapter or the abolished system. Each member shall designate who is to receive a refund of accumulated contributions credited to his account in the event of the death of the member prior to retirement. The designation must be made in a manner prescribed by the Board.

If no designation has been made, or the death of the designated person occurs prior to the death of the member and another designation has not been made, the proceeds shall be paid to the persons surviving at the death of the member in the following order of precedence:

First, to the spouse of the member;

Second, if no surviving spouse, to the children of the member and descendants of deceased children, per stirpes;

Third, if none of the above, to the parents of the member;

Fourth, if none of the above, to the duly appointed executor or administrator of the estate of the member;

Fifth, if none of the above, to other next of kin of the member entitled under the laws of the domicile of the member at the time of his death.

**B.** To the extent required by § 401(a)(37) of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended or renumbered, and the regulations thereunder applicable to governmental plans, if a member dies in service, including a member performing active duty military service in the armed forces of the United States, and if no benefits are payable under subsection C of this section, a retirement allowance shall be paid to the person or persons designated as provided in subsection A of this section if the person is the member's (i) surviving spouse, (ii) minor child, or (iii) parent(s). If no designation has been made, or if the death of the designated person occurs prior to the death of the member and another designation has not been made, a retirement allowance shall be paid in the following order of precedence to the member's (a) surviving spouse, (b) minor children, or (c) parent(s). The retirement allowance shall be paid to the first person qualifying in the orders of precedence set out in this subsection. If more than one minor child survives the deceased member, the allowance shall be divided among them in a manner determined by the Board. If more than one parent survives the deceased member, the allowance shall be divided among them in a manner determined by the Board. The retirement allowance shall be continued during the lifetime of the person or in the case of a minor child until the child dies or attains the age of majority, whichever occurs first. The retirement allowance shall equal the decreased retirement allowance that would have been payable under the joint and survivor option so that the same amount would be continued to such person after the member's death. If the member dies prior to his fifty-fifth birthday, then, for purposes of this subsection, the member shall be presumed to be age 55 on his date of death. However, if the member dies in service prior to his sixtieth birthday and is (1) a person who becomes a member on or after July 1, 2010, (2) a member who does not have at least 60 months of creditable service as of January 1, 2013, or (3) a member of the hybrid retirement program described in § 51.1-169, then, for purposes of this subsection, the member shall be presumed to be age 60 on his date of death. When determining the allowance that would have been payable to the member had the member retired on the date of his death, the provisions of subdivision A 4 of § 51.1-155 shall not apply. If the person elects in writing, the amount of the member's accumulated contributions or lump sum payment shall be paid to him exclusively, in lieu of any other benefits under this section. This amount shall be reduced by the amount of any retirement allowance previously received by the member under this chapter.

**C.** If a member dies in service from a cause compensable under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act (§ 65.2-100 et seq.), a retirement allowance shall be paid to the member's surviving spouse. If no compensation is finally awarded under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act due to legal proceedings or otherwise resulting in settlement from the persons causing such death, the Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission shall determine whether the member's death was from a cause compensable under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act. If the member leaves no surviving spouse or the surviving spouse dies, any minor children of the deceased member shall be paid an allowance until the children die or attain the age of majority, whichever occurs first. If more than one minor child survives the deceased member, the allowance shall be divided in a manner determined by the Board. If the deceased member leaves neither surviving spouse nor minor child, the allowance, divided in a manner determined by the Board, shall be paid to the member's parents during their lives.

The retirement allowance payable hereunder to a qualifying survivor shall be the annual amount which when added to the compensation payable under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act for the death of the member equals 50 percent of the member's average final compensation if the survivor does not qualify for death benefits under the provisions of the Social Security Act in effect on the date of the death of the member. If the survivor qualifies for death benefits under the provisions of the Social Security Act in effect on the date of the death of the member, the allowance payable from the retirement system when added to the compensation payable under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act shall equal thirty-three and one-third percent of the member's average final compensation.

Any beneficiary entitled to the entire amount of a retirement allowance under the provisions of this subsection as a result of the death of a member shall be entitled to waive his rights to the allowance by written notification to the Board within ninety days after the death of the member<u>, except as subdivision G 4 of § 51.1-142.4 provides,</u> in order to make available a retirement allowance under the provisions of subsection B of this section.

## 2. Section-by-section summary in plain English

**For the Editor, in three sentences.** The bill lets a Virginia state employee who is a veteran buy
up to four years of prior active-duty military service at a price based on what that service would
have cost had it been credited when the employee was first hired — the plan's published normal cost
rate applied to the employee's own first three years of state pay, plus 6 percent interest to a
valuation date — instead of the much higher "actuarial equivalent cost" the employee pays today for
missing a 24-month deadline that ran out years ago. Only employees who need the purchased months to
reach an unreduced retirement — and who are already within reach of one on the day they apply, on the
service they actually have — may buy at that price, they must actually retire within a 12-month window
that opens when the purchase is credited, and the Virginia Retirement System may not accept an
election at all unless it has first certified and set aside the Commonwealth's share of the cost
within a $3 million aggregate ceiling and a per-member ceiling. The program runs for four years, applies only to state agency
employees — no locality, school division or teacher is touched — and nothing in it creates any debt
a member can be billed for after a purchase.

| Provision | What it does |

The actuarial-equivalent-cost sentence is left **untouched** in revision 2 — that is what makes the "no worse than current law" ceiling measurable. Neither sentence changes for the eight categories in B 1 or for anyone outside the pilot. |

## 4. What could not be drafted without the MOO-39 answer

MOO-39 asks whether a Plan 1 member's early-retirement reduction is measured back from age 65 or
from the date the member *would have* reached 30 years of creditable service. It is worth 32 percent
of the S9 score. **S8 as drafted above does not depend on the answer, and nothing in §1 is held for
it.** Three items are:

1. **The S9 reduction-waiver provisions are not drafted.** S9 buys off the early-retirement
   reduction instead of selling service credit. Its operative sentence has to say what is being
   waived, measured how — and that is precisely the open question. **Conditional on MOO-39:** if the
   answer is "projected," an S9 provision can be drafted as a purchased waiver of the reduction
   computed under § 51.1-155 with the unreduced date determined as though service had continued; if
   the answer is "frozen," the waiver is worth roughly 35 percent more and the price, the cap and the
   per-member ceiling all have to be reset before any language is useful.
2. **MOO-39's owner should be pointed at § 51.1-155, not § 51.1-153.** This is MOO-44's finding
   outside its assignment and it is correct, and I can now confirm it from the live text I retrieved
   for the conforming amendment. § 51.1-155 A 3 states the measure as *"the first date on which the
   sum of his then attained age plus his then creditable service **would have been equal to 90 or
   more had he remained in service until such date**"* and A 2 as *"the first date on which he
   **would have completed** a total of 30 years of creditable service."* **That is the projected
   reading, expressly so in A 3.** The Code is not silent on this question. Routing to Policy
   Director rather than acting on it, because MOO-39 is not mine.
3. **The per-member subsidy ceiling cannot be carried across to S9.** The bracketed figure, whatever
   MOO-48 returns, will be derived from the S8 run, on this definition, at a chosen window length. A
   single ceiling across two designs needs both priced on the same basis.

Note also that the eligibility test in § 51.1-142.4 A and the quantity limit in subsection C now
turn on the defined term "unreduced retirement eligibility date," which **as revised in revision 7**
cites § 51.1-155 **A 1, A 2 and A 3** by name — the positive limb routes to the normal-retirement
computation in A 1 and the negative limb excludes the two reduction provisions. That is a strict
improvement for MOO-39 purposes, and revision 7 makes it a larger one: the draft no longer pretends
§ 51.1-153 settles the reduction question, and any future S9 language has one defined term to attach
to whose both limbs are explicit. **For MOO-39 specifically** — whether a Plan 1 member's reduction
is measured back from age 65 or from the projected 30-year date — revision 7 changes nothing. The
definition asks whether an allowance **is** reduced under A 2 or A 3, not by how much or measured from
when, so the answer to MOO-39 moves the S9 price and not this bill's admission test.

### §6.0-69 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 69 — and one residual declined with its reason

1. **Whether to enact the Director's approved words as given.** f1-b's words are the reviewer's own, quoted verbatim on the card and approved verbatim. **They are reproduced word for word and two conforming limbs are added to them.** The test I applied is the one this document has applied to every approved sentence: a change that makes the approved words operate as approved is conformance and belongs in the text with a note; a change that moves a cost or settles a question the card put to the Director is not mine to make. Both limbs are of the first kind, both are recorded at §0.0-69 item 1, and **either can be reversed in one substitution.**

2. **Why the exception is confined to a retirement *"that is not a qualifying retirement."*** The approved words were confined only by *"for the purposes of this subdivision."* Subdivision G 4 uses the phrase *"a retirement before the date of death"* for **two** populations — the member who retired in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement, which is the carve-out's own subject, and the member who retired in a qualifying retirement, who is the subject of the branch's second condition. **Unconfined, the exception would have reached the second and pulled a retiree out of § 51.1-163 and into the death branch.** That is the class [MOO-161](/MOO/issues/MOO-161)'s F1 rated **fatal**, and the Policy Director's standing direction of 12 October 2026 exists to keep this sentence off it. The confinement is five words and it removes the argument rather than winning it.

3. **Why the second limb is needed and is not an enlargement.** The approved words make a statement about a **noun** — *"is not a retirement before the date of death."* The condition that lets the death branch operate is a **verb**: *"where clause (i) of this subdivision applies and **the member has not retired** before the date of death."* A reader could hold that a member whose effective date fell before her death *"has retired"* however the noun is defined. **The limb therefore does not widen the answer; without it the answer does not reach the class the card described.** It is drafted in the chapter's own formulation — *"shall not be treated as having"* — which subsection E and subdivision G 5 already use, so the act has one formulation for one concept and not two.

4. **One residual of f1-b, declined with its reason.** A disability retiree **already in payment** whose effective date the Board *re-determines* after her death is, on the words, a member whose effective date the Board determined after the death. **I have not drafted against it.** The better reading is that an effective date is *determined* once, when the retirement is approved, and that a later correction is not that determination; and the only drafted cure is **f1-a's** limb — *"and a retirement allowance has become payable to the member under that retirement"* — which is a limb of a form the Director considered and **did not** select. Taking it now would be re-deciding the card. It is named to the next counsel pass as the first thing to attack, and it is one substitution if the Director wants it.

5. **Why the non-coincident branch is a clause of the greater-of sentence and not a sentence of its own.** That sentence now contains **five** references to *"the preceding sentence"* where it contained two, and every one of them means the sentence that determines the benefit under § 51.1-162. **A new sentence would have given the references inside it a new antecedent — the greater-of sentence — and the branch would have been about the wrong benefit.** The semicolon keeps one referent for all five. **Any further amendment of this branch must stay inside that sentence for the same reason**, and that is recorded as a standing direction rather than left in this note.

6. **Two pronouns made express.** *"The benefit **it** provides"* becomes *"the benefit **that subdivision** provides"*, because *"it"* had two candidate antecedents in a sentence that decides who is paid; and the payee tail becomes *"shall pay it to **that person or those persons**"*, which is the set the new condition has just identified, in place of *"the person to whom the provision under which the greater benefit is determined requires it to be paid."* **Neither changes the rule.** The second is shorter because the condition now does the work the old formula did.

### §6.0-67 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 67 — and three findings declined with reasons

1. **Why § 51.1-162 is reproduced in full, and not cited.** The approved conforming amendment inserts eleven words into § 51.1-162 C. Article IV, Section 12 of the Constitution of Virginia requires that *"the act revived or the section amended shall be reenacted and published at length."* **An amendment to a section is therefore not available as a cross-reference; it requires the section.** So the title line, the first enactment clause and §1 all change together, and the whole of § 51.1-162 — subsections A, B and C, the five-step order of precedence and the two allowance-measure paragraphs — appears in §1 with one underlined clause and nothing else marked. **This is the only reason the act's footprint widened**, and it is the price of making MOO-189's F11 visible to the people who administer § 51.1-162.
2. **Where the eleven words go inside § 51.1-162 C, which the approval did not state.** They are placed after *"within ninety days after the death of the member"* and before *"in order to make available"*, set off by commas, so that they qualify **the period** and not the right to waive. Placed after *"in order to make available a retirement allowance under the provisions of subsection B of this section"* they would have read as an exception to the *purpose* of the waiver; placed before *"by written notification"* they would have read as an exception to the *manner*. **Only the enacted placement says what subdivision G 4 does, which is to extend a period.**
3. **One word of f7-a is changed and the change is recorded rather than silent.** The approved tail read *"or a lump sum in lieu of **it**."* Enacted: *"or a lump sum in lieu of **any other benefit under that section**."* Two reasons. § 51.1-162 B's own words are *"in lieu of any other benefits under this section"*, and **subdivision G 4 already uses the longer form twice** for the same election; a third formulation for one concept inside one section is a worse defect than the length. And *"it"* had two candidate referents in its own sentence — the allowance and the amount settled. **The meaning is unchanged and the Director's answer is unaffected.**
4. **Why f7-a bars the payment rather than deferring the settlement.** Subdivision G 4 settles the certified subsidy *"on … the date of the member's death"*, and the settlement date is what the whole redetermination machinery runs from. Deferring the **settlement** would have moved that date and with it the ninety-day redetermination, the release, the crediting deadline and the cap accounting. **f7-a leaves the settlement where it is and bars only the cash**, which is the smallest change that makes subdivision G 4's existing release operable.
5. **Why m8-a's ninety days is an aggregate and not a per-request limit.** Clause (ii) already caps *"the aggregate of all tolling under this subsection"*, and clause (i) already denies tolling to a second or subsequent request. **A per-request limit would therefore have been either redundant or an invitation to read clause (i) down.** The enacted words cap *"the aggregate of all periods so excluded"*, which is the same unit clause (ii) already uses.
6. **Why F3's repair corrects the certification instead of enacting the proposition.** The reviewer offered an operative disapplication of § 51.1-165 A. **That would take from a member the bargain she made** — under subdivision A 1 she elected an increased allowance in her own lifetime *"in lieu of any death benefits"*, and disapplying it would pay her survivors out of the trust fund for a trade she was paid for. **That decides who bears a loss and it is on the card.** What a drafter may do, and must, is stop the act compelling the Board to state as law something that is not. **The repair is also narrower than the finding**, verified at source on 12 October 2026: § 51.1-165 A 2 carries its own carve-out for a death before the effective date, A 3 says nothing about death benefits, and no option in § 51.1-165.01 extinguishes one. **Subdivision A 1 is the whole of the exposure**, and the certification now names it.
7. **Why F6 narrows the disapplication rather than adding a window.** The reviewer offered either. Adding a window for the non-member would have been a **second** express formula for the same review right; narrowing the disapplication **restores subdivision M 2's second sentence**, which already deems a certification a determination *"whether or not another provision of this section expressly provides for review of it"* and already carries the third window. **The smaller change is the one that leaves one route and not two.**
8. **Why F8's cure amends the definition and not the three windows that run from a certification.** *"Given"* is defined once, in subsection A, for a *"statement or notice."* Three places in the act run a period from a **certification**. Amending subsection A fixes all three at once and keeps one definition; amending the three would have left the definition still not reaching a certification. **Three occurrences of *"statement or notice"* are changed and eleven are not**, because the eleven name a particular statement or notice required by the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* and are not the defining rule. §5.45 direction 1.
9. **Why F9's window runs from three different events and not one.** Subdivision M 2's lateness limb reaches three failures — to make a determination, to give a notice, and to make a payment. **A single trigger cannot serve all three**: a late *payment* has no notice, and a late *determination* is an internal act the person never sees. The enacted words run the thirty days from the notice of the determination where the failure is a late determination, and from the giving of the notice or the making of the payment where it is one of the other two. **In every case the trigger is something the person adversely affected can observe.**
10. **Why F13's repair also carries § 51.1-162 A's offset, which the finding rated lower.** The finding is that the certification states one trigger for the order of precedence where the Code states two. The same sentence also omitted that the contributions are *"reduced by the amount of any retirement allowance previously received by the member."* **Both are corrected in one substitution**, because a member reading a compelled written statement of what her family will be paid should not be told a gross figure, and because re-opening the same clause in a later revision to add the second half is two changes where one will do.
11. **Why F14's repair cites the definition instead of completing the list.** Completing the enumeration would have put eight categories in subsection L and left two statements of one rule. **Citing the definition leaves one.** The reviewer's other option was deleting the sentence, which is not available: the sentence is the Policy Director's approved answer **f10-b**, enacted in store revision 62 to confirm the scope on the face of the act. **Placement is not changed** — the sentence stays in subsection L, where f10-b put it — and the reviewer's point that a state-system eligibility bar sits inside a local-mandate disclaimer survives as a card for the Director, not a drafting fix.

The reviewer's reduction holds: the branch applies where the member *died and had not retired at all*. **The enacted words are the ones the Policy Director verified and adopted and they are not changed.** What is wrong is the description, and a future reviewer who relied on it would reason wrongly about the qualifying-retiree case. **The description is corrected here and is not corrected in place in §0.0-62, because that record is a dated record of what was written.**

### §6.0-66 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 66

1. **Why the deeming sentence and not the alternative affirmative trigger, and the one weakness I accepted in choosing it.** MOO-196 left the form to me and recommended the insertion; I took the recommendation for the four reasons at §0.0-66, of which the controlling one is that **deeming the commanded release *into* subdivision D 7 keeps the second limb alive** — a release that followed a determination later rescinded or reversed still comes back, where an exclusion would have stranded it. **The weakness is that `For the purposes of the next sentence` is a reference by position, and position is the one thing a later amendment moves for free.** Anyone who inserts a sentence between the deeming sentence and the reinstatement sentence silently re-points the whole provision, and nothing in the text would complain. I accepted it because it is **the only device that confines the deeming to one sentence without naming the sentence**, and naming it (*"the sentence beginning 'Where a reservation has been released'"*) is both ugly and just as fragile — it breaks if the sentence's first words change. **The durable fix is structural: give the reinstatement sentence its own numbered subdivision, so the deeming can cite a designator instead of a position.** That renumbers subdivision G 4, which is a change of footprint nobody has agreed, so it is raised here and not drafted. **A drafter amending subdivision G 4 after this revision must read the deeming sentence first.**
2. **Why *"required or permitted"* and not *"required"* alone.** The releases that caused the defect are all commanded, so *"required"* would have been enough for every case I could find. I used the pair anyway because **a release the act permits without commanding would otherwise have fallen into the 60-day *"learns of the release"* limb by the same mechanism, and the omission would have been invisible** — exactly the way the original defect was invisible. The pair is not new vocabulary: subsection F already reads *"Nothing **required or permitted** by subdivision G 2, G 3, G 4, or G 5."* **The act's own words, used for the act's own idea.**
3. **Why *"including"* and not an exhaustive list, and why I named three releases when the cut reaches four.** The deeming sentence's general words are *"a release that this section required or permitted the Board to make at the time it was made"*; the three named — subdivision G 1, this subdivision, subdivision D 3 on settlement — are counsel's and are **illustrative**. That is load-bearing, because **there is a fourth commanded release the finding does not list: subdivision G 4's death-case release** (*"the Board shall release the amount settled under this subdivision and shall restore it to the amount available under the limitation stated in the first sentence of subdivision D 2"*). It is reached by the general words and by *"by this subdivision"* in the list. **Had I converted the list into an exhaustive one, I would have re-created the defect for that case and for any release a later amendment adds.** *"Including"* is doing real work here and should not be tidied away.
4. **Why the five-percent floor keeps *"an employer"* when everything around it becomes *"state agency"* — the one place I deliberately left two words for what may look like one concept.** My own rule is never to use two words for one concept, and this is a considered exception, not an oversight. **They are two concepts.** The floor sentence disqualifies a **class of funds** — *"funds other than funds paid by an employer to or on behalf of the member"* — and its purpose is to stop the member's own five percent being paid with somebody else's money. **The § 51.1-124.3 term is wider than *"state agency"*, and in an anti-circumvention floor the wider class is the protective one.** Conforming it would have **narrowed the disqualification and loosened the floor**, which is a substantive policy change and squarely the thing MOO-196 told me not to make. The second and later sentences name an **actor with a duty**, and there the term must be the narrow, defined, real one. So: *"employer"* where the question is *whose money*, *"state agency"* where the question is *who must act*. **If the Policy Director would rather have one word, the way to get it is to say so and accept the narrower floor; I will not make that trade by drafting choice.**
5. **The publication duty still has no deadline and no consequence, and I did not add one.** Subdivision B 4 e now ends *"The state agency shall publish the policy"* — a named actor and a real duty, which is what finding A2b asked for and what the cut delivers. **It is still missing two of the four things a duty needs: by when, and or else.** Nothing says where, in what form, or by what date the agency publishes, and nothing follows if it never does — unlike the *filing* duty, whose consequence is built in (the Board does not accept elections by that agency's employees until the policy is filed). **The obvious repair is to tie publication to the filing moment and give it the same consequence**, for instance *"shall publish the policy on its website no later than the date it files the policy with the Board, and the Board shall not accept an election by an employee of a state agency that has not published its policy."* **That is a new provision and nobody has agreed it, so it is raised here and not drafted in.** It is one sentence whenever the Director wants it.
6. **Why *"state agency from whose appropriation an amount was paid"* and not *"state agency that paid."*** Counsel suggested these words and I used them, but the reason is worth recording because the shorter form is tempting. **A state agency does not have its own money; it spends from an appropriation.** *"That paid"* invites the question of who paid when an agency is reorganised, abolished or merged between the payment and the refund, and the answer *"the agency from whose appropriation it came"* is the one that identifies a real fund and a real claimant. It also makes *"in proportion to the amounts each paid"* determinate where a member moved between agencies mid-purchase. **The cost is length: 38 characters each, ten times, which is 380 of the revision's 825.** Worth it, because the phrase is the thing that makes the refund and review limbs administrable.
7. **What I did not draft, and none of it is silence.** (a) **No statewide single policy.** MOO-196 offered the alternative of naming an officer or agency to adopt one policy for the Commonwealth, with the Department of Human Resource Management the obvious candidate, and a provision that a state agency may pay only in accordance with it. **I drafted the per-agency form because it is the one MOO-196 recommended and the one that needs no new institution**; the statewide form is a different policy with a different queue (one order of precedence across all of state government, not one per agency) and real distributive consequences. **If the Lab wants it, it is not a redraft of B 4 e but a new provision, and the fiscal consequences of a single statewide queue should go to Fiscal & Impact Modeler before it is drafted.** (b) **Subdivision B 4 e is not extended beyond the Program.** Its policy condition is keyed to *"employees who are eligible members as defined in § 51.1-142.4"*, which only a state agency can ever have, so as drafted it cannot reach a purchase outside the Program. **That is a footprint question, not a drafting one.** (c) **The four curly apostrophes in §1 are not normalised.** MOO-196 offered it as a separate minor tidy; the cut did not need it, because the anchor was chosen to stop before the apostrophe, and doing it would have put a cosmetic change in a revision that should be readable as two findings and nothing else.
8. **An open question for the Policy Director that the cut exposed and did not create.** The deeming sentence fixes the *trigger*, so an ordinary commanded release no longer drags the Board through reinstatement, the money-committee notice, the excess certification and the shutdown. **It does not touch the *consequence* side, and one piece of that still reads oddly for the cases that legitimately do come back:** the compelled notice sentence requires the Board to state *"the nature of any error"* on **every** reinstatement, including one that follows a rescission where the Board did nothing wrong at all. *"Any"* arguably lets the Board state that there was none, which is how I read it and why I did not touch it. **It is one word (*"any error"* → *"any error"* qualified, or *"the nature of any error, where the release was in error"*), it was not in MOO-196's scope, and it should be decided rather than drafted by me.** Raised here for the Director; counsel's next bounded pass will see it either way.

### §6.0-65 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 65

1. **Why *"is advised to review"* and not *"should review"*, and why neither is *"shall review."*** The series it joins is six propositions of law, each introduced by *"that"*, and a seventh item reading *"that the member **should** review"* would have read as a statement of what the law requires of the member. **It is not a duty, and it must not be capable of being read as one** — a member who does not review her designation breaks nothing, loses no right and is not late for anything. *"Is advised to review"* states the only thing that is true: the Board's certification carries advice. **The operative verb belongs to the Board's carrier sentence** — *"The Board shall not accept an election until the Board has, in writing, certified to the member … that …"* — so the actor, the addressee, the writing and the moment are all already named, and the advisory adds no unnamed actor. This is the Policy Director's wording change at MOO-188 §3.3 and the reason is recorded there.
2. **Why it is its own semicolon item and not an appendage to the § 51.1-162 B proposition.** The designation is subsection B's fact, which is the argument for putting the advice inside B's item, and it is the wrong argument: **B's item states what the law does, and the advisory states what the member is advised to do.** Merging them would have buried advice inside a proposition of law and made it arguable that the advice is part of what B provides. Separate, the propositions stay together and the advice is visibly advice.
3. **Why the full citation *"subsection A of § 51.1-162"* and not *"subsection A of that section."*** §1 uses the short form three times, and each time inside a sentence that has already named § 51.1-162. The advisory is a **new item** and the item that follows it restarts with the full citation (*"that subsection C of § 51.1-162"*), so the short form would have made the referent depend on an item two places back. §5.43 direction 1.
4. **Why *"designation of beneficiary"* is the right noun and not a second word for one concept.** § 51.1-162 A, verified at source on 12 October 2026, requires each member to *"designate who is to receive a refund of accumulated contributions"*, pays *"the designated beneficiary"*, and calls the act *"the designation"*; B pays *"the person or persons designated as provided in subsection A."* **The advisory therefore points the member at the cited subsection using that subsection's own noun**, while §1's own *"designation"* carries the same meaning it already carries.
5. **Why *"before completing payment"* and not a date, a period, or *"before the Board accepts the election."*** The phrase is already in this subdivision — the certification states *"the member's right to cancel the election under subdivision G 5 at any time before completing payment"* — and in subdivision G 4. **The advisory's deadline is the same event, and it is the last moment at which the purchase can still be undone.** **Correction, store revision 68 — the second reason this item gave is not true and is withdrawn.** As written at store revision 65 the item continued *"and the whole window during which re-designating changes the outcome."* **Nothing in § 51.1-162 A fixes a designation at the completion of payment.** A's own words contemplate redesignation at any time — *"If no designation has been made, or the death of the designated person occurs prior to the death of the member and another designation has not been made"* — so the window in which re-designating changes the § 51.1-162 outcome runs to the earlier of the member's death and the last of the act's retirement-date legs: about 27 months on the act's own dials (subsection E's 12 months to pay and 1 to credit, and the two retirement-date definitions in subsection A), and without end for a member who does not retire. *"Before completing payment"* closes the **first** of those legs. [MOO-195](/MOO/issues/MOO-195) F2, verified at source on 12 October 2026. **The enacted deadline is the Policy Director's approved word and is not changed by this record revision**; whether to extend it, re-point it or leave it stand is before the Director at [MOO-191](/MOO/issues/MOO-191) with the words drafted. A fixed period would have needed a trigger, a definition and a consequence for missing it, and there is no consequence, because there is no duty.
6. **Why the advisory is not excepted from D 1's failure sentence, and what it costs.** **The Policy Director decided this at MOO-188 §3.4 before the cut, and I have not drafted around it.** Omitting the advice is a failure to state *"every matter this subdivision requires to be stated"*, so it is reviewable under subsection M and reportable under subsection J. The cost is that **a review channel now exists for the omission of a sentence that creates no right** — while the member lives it returns the only remedy that matters, which is time to re-designate before payment completes, and after she dies it adds nothing because no remedy can re-designate for her. **The Director has said that if the counsel pass thinks the channel is worth more argument than the advice is worth, they will re-take that one point; it is one clause either way, and the clause is this item.** **Correction, store revision 68 — this item sent that question to the wrong card.** As written at store revision 65 it named the counsel gate at [MOO-192](/MOO/issues/MOO-192), which is the subsection E1 gate and has the channel out of scope. **The question went to pass 21 at [MOO-195](/MOO/issues/MOO-195)**, which answered it: **keep the subsection J limb and drop the subsection M limb**, because M review's only possible output is a remand that can give the claimant nothing — § 2.2-4029 bars a court from supplying the agency action — while the J report puts the same fact before the money committees at no litigation cost and with no claimant needed. **That recommendation is not enacted here**: it reverses a point the Director decided at MOO-188 §3.4, and it is before the Director at [MOO-191](/MOO/issues/MOO-191) with the words drafted. [MOO-195](/MOO/issues/MOO-195) F3 and F10.
7. **What I did not draft, and it is not silence.** The advisory tells the member to look; it does **not** give her a way to re-designate inside the act, does not require the Board to send her her current designation with the certification, and does not toll anything while she reviews. § 51.1-162 A already lets her designate *"in a manner prescribed by the Board"* at any time, so the act needs no machinery, and **a notice that enclosed her designation of record would be a new duty with an administrative cost that nobody has agreed.** It is the kind of thing that belongs on MOO-97's card if anyone wants it, not in a cut commissioned as one edit.

F3 and F4 are cured by one bounded addition, and this is not a reversal of §6.0-61.** Store revision 61 removed *"other person to whom this section requires a notice to be given"* because, on the face of the act, it reached **the public** — subsection K requires the Board to *"give public notice"* — and the two money-committee Chairmen, whose notices are information-only and two of which are expressly anonymised. **What was wrong with that formula was the absence of a subject-matter boundary, not its generality.** The enacted words carry one: *"person to whom this section requires a notice to be given **in respect of a benefit payable on the death of a member**."* Subsection K's notice is of a fact, not of a death benefit; the Chairmen's notices are of reinstatements and excesses. **The accidental class stays out and the conservator of a minor beneficiary comes back in.**

**4. The adverse-determination gate is dropped entirely, not narrowed.** *"Person who claimed any benefit … and whom the Board determined is not entitled to it"* made standing turn on the Board having acted, so the Board could defeat review by never deciding — and M 2's **failure** limb, which exists for Board inaction, was unavailable to the person Board inaction hurts. *"Person who **has** claimed any benefit payable on the death of a member"* reaches the claimant whose claim was never determined. **A remedy that cannot be used by the person the duty protects is a defect, not a policy setting**, which is why this is drafted rather than carded.

**5. F4's wider formula is declined, with the residual named.** The reviewer offered *"or fiduciary of, or person to whom this section requires a notice to be given in respect of, a person in any of the foregoing classes."* **The enacted words reach every fiduciary the act actually writes to**, because the only fiduciary the act makes an addressee is the fiduciary of a death-benefit payee, in subdivision G 4's notice sentence. **The residual is a fiduciary acting for a living member under a disability** — she receives the subdivision D 1 certification and her conservator is in no class. No finding reaches it and no provision of the act requires notice to her fiduciary, so it is not drafted; it is flagged for the next pass and is in the routing table.

**6. F5 is cured in half, deliberately.** Four defects are cured in one substitution: the remedy reached only the six propositions and now reaches *"every matter this subdivision requires to be stated"*; it named *"a failure of the Board"*, which is not a category subdivision M 2 contains, and now names M 2's own category word for word; the member's period ran from a death notice she will never receive and now runs from the certification she was given; and M 2's second sentence, which deemed the certification a determination and had already closed her 30 days, is **expressly disapplied to such a failure**, so there is one window and not two. **What is not drafted is the reviewer's discovery rule** — *"or from the date she files written evidence of the omission, whichever is later"* — because an open-ended limitation period is a policy setting and not the resolution of a contradiction. §7 item 129 answer 3.

**7. F6's numeral is the chapter's own.** M 2's third window was empty for every provision but subdivision D 1: subsection C's statement duties, subdivision D 2's over-cap notice, the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"*, subdivision G 4's death notice and rescission notice and the reinstatement notices provide **no** period for review of a matter **omitted** from them. The enacted default is **30 days after the certification or notice is given**, which is the period the same sentence already uses for a determination, with a rider preserving any longer or later period a provision does supply. **No new numeral was invented.**

**8. F8's fix direction is corrected, and only the charging rule is enacted.** The reviewer asked for the general reinstatement sentence's *"charging rule and excess consequences"* by reference. **The excess consequences already applied.** Subdivision G 4's notice sentence opens *"The Board shall give written notice of every reinstatement under this subdivision"*, so the notice to the Chairmen, the notice to every subdivision D 5 waiting-list applicant, the subdivision D 3 confirmation, the certification of the excess to the Governor, the subsection J line and *"shall accept no further election until the excess is eliminated"* all reached a reinstatement under this release already. **Only the charging rule was missing**, and it is added in eighteen words. Adopting the consequences again by reference would have put two formulations of one concept in one subdivision.

**9. M2's stranded words are cured by deletion.** *"Together with any contingency amount released with it"* pointed at the preceding sentence, which releases only *"the amount settled"*; contingency amounts are released by subdivision G 4's redetermination sentence and by subdivision D 7. **Nothing was ever released with it.** Deleting four words is smaller than redirecting them and loses nothing.

**10. M9 is enacted as an anti-implied-repeal saving, not as a widening.** § 2.2-4026 A grants direct review to any *"party aggrieved by and claiming unlawfulness of a case decision"*, and subdivision M 3 disapplies only Articles 3 and 4 and the two deemed-approval sentences. The enumerated class in M 2's Article 5 sentence was therefore either inert or a silent withdrawal of an Administrative Process Act right, which would need express words. **The saving clause says which**, in one sentence, and it is the act's first citation of § 2.2-4026.

**11. m1 cross-refers § 8.01-2 rather than defining the terms.** *"Minor or … under a disability"* and *"guardian, conservator, committee, or other fiduciary"* were undefined for Title 51.1; § 8.01-2 defines both but opens *"As used in this title."* **A definition written into § 51.1-142.4 A would create a Title 51.1 meaning that could drift from Title 8.01's**, and the concept is the Code's, not this act's. The cross-reference is the smaller change and it is the act's only citation into Title 8.01.

**12. f10-b is enacted in the chapter form, and the Director should know the scope decision was already the law of the act.** The card's drafted sentence named *"the State Police Officers' Retirement System, … the Virginia Law Officers' Retirement System, or … the Judicial Retirement System."* **The definition of *"eligible member"* already provides that it *"does not include a member of a retirement system established under Chapter 2 (§ 51.1-200 et seq.), Chapter 2.1 (§ 51.1-211 et seq.), or Chapter 3 (§ 51.1-300 et seq.)."*** Three names and three chapters coincide today, but a fourth system established under one of those chapters would be caught by the chapters and missed by the names, and two formulations of one concept is a defect. **The enacted sentence uses the chapters**, and it sits in subsection L beside the existing sentence that restates the teacher exclusion the same definition carries — so the structure is the act's own. **It confirms the scope rather than changing it**, and because of that the sister-system question routed to the Statutory Researcher is now moot for this act rather than answered.

### §6.0-61 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 61

Fourteen. **All fourteen in full at** [`moo161-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-97#document-moo161-disposition) **§6. No policy was chosen by drafting choice.** The six a later reader must not undo are these.

**1. The fatal finding was answered by deletion and confinement, not by the carve-out the reviewer offered first.** F2 offered two forms: carve the disapplication (*"except that for the purposes of subdivision C 2 ... as though this sentence had not been enacted"*) or delete it. **Deletion is enacted**, because the citation check shows the disapplication was never load-bearing — § 51.1-163 reaches a pre-effective-date death only by the deeming in § 51.1-165 C 1, § 51.1-165 C 2 and § 51.1-165.01 F, and the sentence's notwithstanding already handles the first and third. **A carve-out would have preserved the words that caused F1.**

**2. The window is stated in D 1's words, not in the reviewer's.** The fix direction read *"after the Board has received a written notification of the member's effective date of retirement given under subdivision D 1 and before the effective date of retirement stated in it."* D 1's certification already says *"after the Board has received the notification of the member's effective date of retirement required by this subdivision and before that date,"* and **the act may not use two formulations for one concept.** The enacted words are D 1's, with *"this subdivision"* becoming *"subdivision D 1."*

**3. Confining the sentence is treated as restoring the agreed scope, not as deciding a policy.** A fatal finding may not be resolved by drafting choice. This one is not: the Director's answers (d), (f) and the certification all speak to the member who has filed her § 51.1-153 notice and not yet retired, and the sentence's reach beyond that window was an artefact of how store revision 58 was cut. **The wider alternative — keeping the disapplication and confining it instead to a member who has not retired — is drafted at §7 item 128 and is not enacted.**

**4. The release trigger's second branch needed a date and the card did not state one.** The Director's answer fires the release *"where no retirement allowance is payable ... because no such allowance is payable to any person"* — a case in which there is no election to date it from. The enacted words run it from the Board's determination that no such allowance is payable, on the model of every other period in this subdivision. **Without a date the duty would have had no deadline, which is an unenforceable duty.**

**5. F6's certification wording states C 2's payee by cross-reference and names nobody.** The reviewer's fix direction ended *"to the person entitled to it under the provision under which the greater benefit is determined"* — a payee rule. **That rule is F3's question and F3 is on the card**, so the enacted proposition says only that each of C 2's two benefits is *"payable to the person entitled to it under the provision under which it is determined"*, which is a statement of existing law and not a direction to pay anybody. **The certification is now accurate about a question the operative text has not yet answered, and §7 item 128 is where that is answered.**

**6. F14 is enacted as to the rider only.** The notice rider now reaches *"the amount of any benefit payable to that person"* as well as entitlement, so the Board is no longer compelled to state a figure it does not have. **The reviewer's companion cure — a supplemental notice with a fresh review period where the Board later determines an amount differently — is a new duty that was not agreed, and is drafted at §7 item 128 instead of enacted.**

**Two findings declined, with reasons.** **F16** (the deemed determination as a tolling lever) is declined on the reviewer's own analysis: M 2 caps the aggregate of all tolling at 120 days and denies tolling to a second request on the same determination, the cap holds, and the cost of closing the residue exceeds the exposure. **F21** (the new class reaches notices required by *"this section"* while M 2's tolling sentence reaches periods under § 51.1-142.2 as well) is declined because the cure would **widen** a class this revision narrows for F8, in the same breath and for the sake of symmetry alone. **Both are recorded so that neither is re-run as new.**

### §6.0-60 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 60

**Every one of the Director's eight answers is enacted as given. Four things inside those answers are mine, and they are listed first.**

1. **Item 117(a) is wider than the carded words, deliberately.** The card read *"an application filed **within a period set forth in** subsection A or B of § 51.1-156."* Enacted: *"an application **the filing of which did not require a waiver of** a ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of § 51.1-156."* The carded form reaches only the member inside the ninety days after termination. **It misses the purest class-4 case of all:** a member whose final qualifying retirement date passes while she is **still in service** — she has not retired at all, which is why subdivision 2 reduced her — and who then applies for a disability retirement allowance as *"[a]ny member in service"* under § 51.1-156 A, for whom **that subsection sets no period**. She needs no waiver, she broke no deadline, and on the carded words she was excluded while a member who filed eight months late was rescued. The enacted form is defined by the thing the class has in common — that no waiver was needed — and reaches both.

2. **Item 117(b) anchors on clause (ii) alone and not on the whole of subsection H.** § 51.1-156 H's mandatory limb has two conditions: (i) the member *"would otherwise qualify for disability retirement but for failing to comply"*, and (ii) the Medical Board's certification of three facts. **Clause (i) is supplied by the approval itself** — the trigger operates only where the member *"is thereafter approved for a disability retirement allowance"*, and a member who is approved has otherwise qualified. Anchoring on both would have made the Board prove a condition its own approval had already decided. **This is the point of the finding:** the enacted trigger is a **fact the Board can see in its file**, not a legal conclusion about what the Board *"was required"* to do.

3. **No express subsection J report line was drafted for item 103's determination, and no fallback was drafted for pass 17's M-9 — and the second of those is a decision, not an omission.** J 1 already reports *"every failure of the Board to make a determination, or to give a notice, within a period required by this section, stated separately for each provision"*, so an express line would be surplusage. **M-9 is CLOSED and needs no text.** It was held to item 103 on the ground that the redetermination clock has no fallback where the Board never makes the error determination. With item 103 enacted the gap is **self-consistent and remediable**: the clock sentence opens *"Where the Board rescinds a determination"*, and the rescission cannot occur without the determination, so a fallback date would start a clock that never runs. What the member needed was a **remedy for the absent determination**, and item 103 gives her one — a 30-day period, a notice duty, review under subsection M 2's failure limb, judicial review under Article 5, and a line in the J report. **Drafting a deemed determination instead would have been a policy choice nobody made.**

4. **Item 120(b) is enacted as a conjunctive duty, not as an exception.** The carded repair was *"the same words R2 enacted in the rescission branch"* — an *"except that where the member has died"* clause. **In the death branch the member has always died**, so the condition is always true and the exception form is nonsense. Enacted: *"and shall pay the whole of that refund to the member's estate … and shall apply no amount of it to the purchase of service credit."* The form also cures **pass 18's M18-3** as a by-product: as an exception restating the verb without a period, the death refund could be read to carry away the main clause's **60-day deadline**; as a conjunctive duty it cannot, and the estate keeps the deadline.

**Five further choices, none of which changes which member passes either definitional test.**

5. **Item 114's amendment leaves the two existing *notwithstanding* clauses standing.** They become surplusage. Deleting them would be tidier and would re-open the argument the amendment exists to foreclose — that the bar was never meant to catch these cases at all — and store revision 52 legislated twice on the strict historical-fact reading. **Surplusage is the cheaper of the two risks.** The record states it so a reader does not take the redundancy for a drafting slip.

6. **Item 114's *"in full"* is confined to the whole-reservation release and that is what makes it operative.** D 7 releases *"to the extent of any reduction"* on a D 6 recertification and releases the whole reserved amount in its other five limbs. Had the amendment read *"released in accordance with subdivision D 7 and has not been reinstated"* it would have cured nothing for the D 6 member, because her partial release is never reinstated — it was correct.

7. **Item 118(b)'s long-stop is the last sentence of J 1 and reads on *"report under this subdivision."*** The card attached it to limb (a) of the first sentence. Placed there it would not have reached the **third** sentence's further report, which has its own trigger, and the duty would still have been interminable on the facts item 118 describes. As the closing sentence it bounds **every** report J 1 requires, which is what the card's stated purpose — *"makes the duty terminable whatever happens"* — asks for. It is confined to *"this subdivision"*, so J 2 and J 3 are untouched.

8. **Item 103's route is confined to the period after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect.** Before that moment the Board is already under a **60-day** duty to determine whether clause (iii) applies, with a 15-day notice duty, a J report line and review under subsection M; an unconditioned member-filing route would have put a **second clock on one determination**, which is pass 18's M18-9. The gap the Director's answer was aimed at is the **later** determination in the rescission sentence — the one with no period, no route and no notice — and the enacted sentence reaches exactly that. **No conforming limb is needed to connect it to the rescission:** the rescission trigger reads *"or the Board thereafter determines that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board"*, which the new determination satisfies on its own words, and the redetermination clock already runs *"from the date on which … the Board makes the determination stated in this subdivision."*

9. **Item 120(a) is enacted although pass 18 shows its stated premise is false, and the part that would actually fix the problem is carded.** The card's ground was that *"G 4 credits the whole purchase on clauses (ii) and (iii) too."* It does not: G 4's crediting duties are confined to **death** and to the **rescission** branch, and clause (ii) switches off G 3's partial-crediting duty along with subdivisions 2 and 3. So for a member approved for a disability retirement allowance **before** completing payment, with no prior determination, there is **no crediting duty to lift a bar in front of**. The amendment is still right on its own terms — E's death-only exception conflicted on its face with G 4's unqualified *"Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision"* — and it is enacted on that narrower ground. **The crediting duty is §7 item 126**, drafted in full, enacted nowhere, and recommended: it decides what a partial payer is credited with and what she is refunded, which is a money question and the Director's.

### §6.0-59 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 59

**1. Option (d)'s class list was five revisions out of date, and carrying it verbatim would have reversed another revision's cure.** §7 item 88's option (d) was drafted in store revision 53 and opened *"Any member, retiree, beneficiary, or applicant."* Store revision 58 then widened subdivision M 2's class to six in **both** of its occurrences — adding *"personal representative of a deceased member's estate, or other person to whom this section requires a notice to be given"* — and one of the two **was** the judicial-review sentence (§5.37). **Resolved by enacting (d) with M 2's own six-class list.** The alternative was to enact the drafted words and silently take the Article 5 right from the rejected claimant and the subdivision B 4 e employer, which is a policy change nobody directed. *"Any member"* became *"A member"* for the same reason — it is how M 2's own first sentence opens, and the chapter should not have two forms for one class. **I regard this as conforming and not as a policy choice**, and it is flagged at item 88 so the Director can reverse it if the narrowing was intended.

**2. The limb and subdivision M 3 overlap, and the overlap is kept rather than cured.** § 2.2-4021 is in Article 3, so item 88's limb disapplies it to a reconsideration, and M 3 then disapplies its deemed-decision sentences *"to a determination of the Board under this section or to a reconsideration under subdivision 2."* **Resolved in favour of keeping both**, for three reasons: both were directed in those words; M 3's other half — determinations generally — is where counsel found the exposure **already live** and the limb does not reach it; and M 3 survives the removal of the limb, which is the thing most likely to be revisited. **The cost is a negative-implication argument** that a reader could build out of M 3 naming reconsiderations at all. I think it fails, and it is carded at item 123 with the one-substitution cure rather than resolved by me.

**3. The two 15-day clocks nearly duplicate an existing one, and both are kept.** Subdivision D 3's fifth sentence already requires the Board to *"act upon the application no later than 15 days after the confirmation is obtained."* The new D 1 sentence requires the certification to be **given** within 15 days of the same trigger. **Resolved by keeping both:** same period, same trigger, different act — *giving the certification* is what subdivision D 1 makes the condition of acceptance, and *acting upon the application* is the accept-or-wait-list decision. They cannot conflict. **Collapsing them into one would have required choosing which act the single clock governs, and that is a policy choice I was not given.**

**4. Where the deadline runs from, in subdivision J 1's new trigger.** The drafted form ended *"no later than the first December 1 following **it**"*, where *"it"* had two candidate antecedents — the rescission and the matter. **Resolved by naming them:** *"following that rescission or the date on which that matter arises, as the case may be."* A matter *arises* on a date and a rescission *occurs* on one; the two verbs are not interchangeable and the deadline needs a date for each. **No change of substance, recorded because it is a departure from text the Director approved.**

**5. Which sentence of subsection C carries the report duty — and the fact that I had it wrong.** Items 108 and 109 and [`moo153-counsel-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-145#document-moo153-counsel-disposition) §4 all called it the *"seventh"* sentence. **It is the eighth.** The sixth and seventh are the two boundary sentences — the characterisation boundary from store revision 48's edit 2, and the world-side boundary from pass 16's M-3 — and item 111, in the same document, numbered them correctly, so §4 was internally inconsistent. **The amended words were never in doubt**, because the target was identified by quotation and not by ordinal, and that is the whole argument for quoting. **Resolved by amending the sentence that contains the quoted words and correcting the label in both places.**

**6. Whether to record the disagreement on item 88 in the bill or only in the item list.** The Director's answer took the optional limb over a recommendation I had withdrawn on counsel's objection. **Resolved by recording it in both, in the §2 plain-English row, in §0.0-59 c and at item 88 — with the cost stated and not netted away.** A later reader of the bill alone must be able to see that disapplying Articles 3 and 4 removes the member's informal-fact-finding and formal-hearing rights in the reconsideration, that counsel objected, and that the direction was the Director's. **It is not my place to re-litigate it and I have not; it is my place to make sure nobody has to discover it.**

**7. What the document split is, and what it is not.** Item 112 directed the split *"before anything leaves Paperclip."* **Resolved by treating it as a document boundary and not as a control.** Both documents are internal issue documents on the same issue and anyone who can read one can read the other. The honest statement of the benefit is that releasing the bill text is now a separate act from releasing the item list; the honest statement of the limit is at item 125, which asks the release question I cannot answer.
