> F8. **For the Fiscal & Impact Modeler:** the reviewer's structural challenge — not a number in the model
> but the assumption underneath it, that every cost of the act flows through the certified subsidy. F1's cure
> restores that assumption; the residue is the C 2 greater-of, at about one case every three years.


> **STORE REVISION 60 — [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64)'s EIGHT ANSWERS OF 12 OCTOBER 2026 ENACTED IN
> THIRTEEN SUBSTITUTIONS IN FIVE PROVISIONS.** Items 114, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 103 and 104 are
> enacted, and of the cheap bundle 120(a), 120(b) and 121's subsection M 2 limb; **the interest limb was
> not selected and is not in the text.** The five provisions are the definition of *"unreduced retirement
> eligibility date"* in subsection A, subsection E, subdivision G 4, subdivision J 1 and subdivision M 2
> of § 51.1-142.4. **No figure moves, no designator is renumbered, no section is added or deleted, no
> defined term is added, and the title line does not change.** Narrative **§0.0-60**; sweep **§5.39**;
> drafter's note **§6.0-60**. **The closures for items 114 to 121, 103 and 104, and two new items 126 and
> 127, are in [`bill-text-s8-item-list`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-item-list)**, where store
> revision 59 moved the §7 list. Record, with every FIND and ENACTED string verbatim:
> [`moo64-rev60-record`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-moo64-rev60-record).
>
> **This is store revision 60, not 59, and the items are 126 and 127, not 123 and 124.** A concurrent run
> published store revision 59 under this cut — the §7 split and the answers to items 88 and 108 to 113 —
> and **item 113's enactment changed one of this revision's own anchors**, J 1's further-report sentence,
> which was re-anchored before item 118(b) was applied. **Store revision 59 touched none of the other
> twelve anchors and nothing in it is reversed, re-opened or renumbered.** §0.0-60 states it in full.
>
> **What the thirteen do.** The **settlement bar is amended once** instead of carrying a *notwithstanding*
> for each rescission route, which closes the two doors that still reached its D 7-release limb — the
> member whose purchase is reduced on a D 6 recertification and who then dies, and the
> involuntary-separation rescission. The **reversal sentence no longer commands settlement where none is
> due**. The **arrears formula is net rather than gross**, with a limb for a determination reversed in its
> entirety. The disability carve-out now reaches the member who **filed on time**, and its trigger is the
> **Medical Board's certification** rather than a counterfactual about what the Board was required to do.
> **Disability-application pendency counts against the 120-day aggregate**, and **J 1 has a twenty-year
> long-stop**. The § 51.1-155.1 confinement gains the **missing temporal rule**, so the member
> involuntarily separated at 50 can take the retirement G 4's hardship branch requires of her. The member
> may now **file written evidence of an error of the Board** and oblige a determination within 30 days,
> reviewable under subsection M. **J 1 reports reversals, restored credit and every amount paid or
> refunded.** Subsection E's crediting exception names the disability and error cases; the **death
> branch's refund no longer buys service credit for a dead member**; and **subsection M 2 reaches a
> failure to make a payment.**
>
> **Four wording changes inside the Director's answers are mine** and are at §6.0-60 items 1 to 4: item
> 117(a) is **wider** than the card, because the carded words missed the member still in service, for whom
> § 51.1-156 A sets no period at all; item 117(b) anchors on **clause (ii) alone**, the approval supplying
> clause (i); item 120(b) is a **conjunctive duty rather than an exception**, which also cures pass 18's
> M18-3; and item 103's route is **confined to the period after a determination has taken effect**, so one
> determination does not acquire two clocks. **Pass 17's M-9 is CLOSED with no text, and the reason is at
> §6.0-60 item 3.**
>
> **What is NOT done.** **[MOO-156](/MOO/issues/MOO-156)'s pass 18 — 6 serious, 11 moderate, 3 minor on
> store revision 57's six repairs — is NOT dispositioned.** Eighteen of its twenty findings are read and
> unanswered and are the next cut's work. **One of them, S18-6, defeats the stated premise of item 120(a),
> which is enacted anyway on a narrower ground, with the part that actually fixes the problem carded as
> §7 item 126 and enacted nowhere.** **These thirteen substitutions have had no adversarial pass of their
> own** — that is [MOO-167](/MOO/issues/MOO-167).
>
> **Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel or by DLS.
> Pre-decisional.**

> **STORE REVISION 59 — THE POLICY DIRECTOR'S SEVEN ANSWERS OF 12 OCTOBER 2026 ENACTED. Five
> provisions of § 51.1-142.4 amended, one new subdivision M 3, item 111 declined, and §7's item list
> split into its own document. No figure moves, no designator is renumbered, no section joins or
> leaves the act, no defined term is added, and the title line does not change.** Narrative
> **§0.0-59**; sweep **§5.38**; drafter's note **§6.0-59**. Dispositions at items 88, 108, 109, 110,
> 111, 112 and 113 of [`bill-text-s8-item-list`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-item-list).
> Answered and applied on [MOO-145](/MOO/issues/MOO-145).
>
> **The thing this revision fixes.** Subdivision D 3 must now **file** the Department of Planning and
> Budget request within 15 days of a completed application, and subdivision D 1 must **give** the
> certification within 15 days of the confirmation. Before them the Board could meet every period the
> section stated and still strand an eligible member for ever, because D 1 bars acceptance until the
> certification issues and nothing required it to issue. The existing 90-day applicant notice now
> fires at about **day 105** instead of never. Subsection C's reporting duty reaches a failure **to
> state**, and subdivision J 1's post-terminal further report has an **independent trigger** so a
> matter arising after the last report has somewhere to go without a rescission.
>
> **Item 88 is answered (d) WITH the optional second limb, over my own withdrawn recommendation, and
> the cost is stated and not netted away.** The completed reconsideration is a § 2.2-4001 case
> decision **by statute**, which answers pass 15's S-3 at the root — § 2.2-4026 A needs a case
> decision and a savings clause cannot create one. **But disapplying Articles 3 and 4 removes
> § 2.2-4019 informal fact finding, § 2.2-4020 formal hearings and the hearing officer from the
> reconsideration.** Counsel objected that this strips the member of hearing rights the bill exists to
> confer; I accepted that and withdrew my recommendation in store revision 56; **the Director's
> direction overrides it, which is the Director's to do.** M 2's own floor — 30-day window, written
> reasons, 90-day duty to act, tolling — is what remains. **One conforming change was not optional:**
> option (d)'s drafted class named four, and store revision 58 had widened M 2's class to six in both
> occurrences, one of which was this very sentence — so the six-class list is carried in rather than
> dropped (§6.0-59 ambiguity 1).
>
> **New subdivision M 3** disapplies § 2.2-4021 B's and C's deemed-decision sentences to a
> determination under the section and to a reconsideration, so agency silence cannot award a subsidy
> against the $170,000 and $3,000,000 limits. § 2.2-4021 read at source: it is in **Article 3**.
>
> **What is NOT done, and one of them is a gap this revision opened.** **Item 124:** because Article 3
> contains § 2.2-4021, the limb and M 3 together mean a reconsideration the Board never completes
> produces **no case decision at all**, so there is no Article 5 route — a position that was uncertain
> before and is now settled against the member by two express exclusions. The cure is drafted at item
> 124, recommends a deemed **denial** on the 91st day rather than a deemed win, and **is not enacted**.
> **Item 123** is the limb/M 3 redundancy. **Item 125** asks what happens to the item list on release.
> **Item 111 is declined**, so counsel's M-2 stands as an accepted cost. **And the eight substitutions
> of store revision 58 still have no adversarial pass of their own.**
>
> **§7 is now [`bill-text-s8-item-list`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-item-list).** This
> document went from 510,963 characters to **249,041**, of which §1 is 112,886 — about 275,000
> characters of headroom against the 524,288 ceiling, and the end of the pressure that forced seven
> record moves since store revision 33. **The split is a document boundary, not a containment
> control.**
>
> **Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed or cleared by
> counsel or by DLS. Not legally sufficient for introduction. Pre-decisional and internal. Nothing in
> store revision 59 is cleared for external use.**


> **STORE REVISION 58 — [MOO-154](/MOO/issues/MOO-154)'s COUNSEL PASS DISPOSED. Eight substitutions in
> subdivisions G 4, D 1 and M 2 of § 51.1-142.4, answering eleven of sixteen findings. No figure moves, no
> designator is renumbered, no section is added or deleted, no defined term is added, and the title line
> does not change.** Record: [`moo154-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-97#document-moo154-disposition).
> Narrative §0.0-58; sweep §5.37; drafter's note §6.0-58; the nine drafted answers §7 item 122. Cut and
> applied on [MOO-97](/MOO/issues/MOO-97).
>
> **The fatal finding.** (f)'s notwithstanding reached subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165 and **not subsection F
> of § 51.1-165.01**, which routes the same death to § 51.1-163 by its own force — so for every member who
> elects the partial lump sum the act did nothing, while the certification compelled the Board to tell her
> that no such option governed her death benefit. The notwithstanding now names **so much of subsection F as
> requires payment under § 51.1-163**, which leaves that subsection's own disapplication of the in-service
> requirement working for the member. **§ 51.1-165 C 2 is preserved rather than displaced**: the act pays the
> greater of C 2's benefit and (f)'s, so no member is worse off than under present law.
>
> **What else is in the text.** *"As on the death of a member in service"* is given the Code's own hook —
> § 51.1-165.01 F's *"the requirement that the member be in service shall not apply"* — because neither term
> is defined in § 51.1-124.3. The computation base becomes *"taking account of"* the credited service rather
> than *"on"* it, which was reading the allowance onto the purchased months alone and gave a widow about
> one-fourteenth of it. **Three of the certification's four compelled propositions of law were wrong** and are
> restated: only C 1 is displaced, § 51.1-162 B is also conditioned on § 51.1-162 C, and a death compensable
> under the Virginia Workers' Compensation Act is governed by § 51.1-162 C and not by A. The certification
> gains a **consequence** — a determination for subsection M and a line in the subsection J report — because
> the issue's premise that D 1's day-for-day extension carried it was wrong. The notice is owed to **each**
> person entitled, its period no longer vanishes when crediting is late, it starts afresh for a person
> identified later, and it may no longer state a period § 51.1-162 does not contain. **Subdivision M 2 now
> reaches any person the section requires a notice to be given** — the rejected claimant and the B 4 e
> employer, each of whom the act hands a notice and neither of whom could use it.
>
> **What is NOT done.** **F5, the ERF residual this issue was opened on, is not closed** — subsection E's
> second limb may leave the survivor a reduced allowance the Commonwealth priced as unreduced. It and eight
> more are drafted in full and enacted nowhere at §7 item 122; four of the nine decide who bears a loss.
> **These eight substitutions have had no adversarial pass of their own.**
>
> **Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel or by DLS.
> Pre-decisional.**


> **STORE REVISION 57 — [MOO-152](/MOO/issues/MOO-152)'s PASS 17 DISPOSITIONED. Six substitutions in
> four provisions of §1, four record corrections, no policy enacted, no designator renumbered, nothing
> added to or removed from the act, the title unchanged, and no figure moved.** Subdivision G 3 and
> subdivision G 4 carry the repairs; **subsection E is named but not amended**; the two definitions are
> untouched. Narrative **§0.0-57**; sweep **§5.36**; note **§6.0-57**; carded findings **§7 items 114 to
> 121**. Record: [`moo152-pass17-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-moo152-pass17-disposition).
>
> **Pass 17 returned 0 fatal, 8 serious, 9 moderate, 5 minor** on store revision 52's thirteen edits,
> verified all thirteen present in the live store as carded, re-opened § 51.1-156 H, A, B and D
> verbatim, replicated the engine's `g4_exposure` to the digit, and found **no constitutional defect**
> on single object, special legislation, Dillon's Rule, delegation, vagueness, takings or contract
> impairment.
>
> **Every repair is to words the Director's own answers put in**, and none changes which member passes
> either definitional test: a **payee** for the subdivision-3 rescission refund where the trigger is
> death, with its adverse-tax fallback yielding to that case; a reinstatement **deadline that is not
> already past**; the **two fallbacks subdivision 2 already has** for arrears on a reversal; item 96
> made **operative** at last, subsection E having carried the same deeming bar independently; and the
> authorised offset made **reciprocal** and stated as a **power**.
>
> **What is NOT here. No serious finding is cured.** S-1 — the settlement bar's release limb, reached by
> a member whose purchase is reduced on a D 6 recertification and who then dies — **is the fatal item 89
> cured through a different door, and it is carded as item 114 rather than fixed silently**, because
> amending the bar settles subsidies the bar on its face refuses and that spends money. **Publication is
> blocked on items 114, 115, 116 and 117**, the four pass 17 would not publish without. **M-9 is held to
> item 103** and **m-5 needs no edit**. **Item 105 is CLOSED** — the enacted arrears formula stands and
> its residual defect is item 116.
>
> **One claim of this record is withdrawn.** *"No priced quantity moves"* does not survive: the
> admission half is **sound and independently verified**, the settlement half is not. **The only
> statement authorised from here:** *no admission quantity moves; the settlement count moves upward by
> an amount the current engine cannot value.* The re-run is requested, not asserted, and **no figure in
> the package is restated**. **The six new strings have had no counsel pass of their own.**
>
**§8's status note for store revision 56 is moved verbatim** to [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2) **by store revision 61**, where a reference of the form *"§8's note for store revision N"* still resolves. §8 retains the five most recent: 61, 60, 59, 58, 57. **Nothing is rewritten or summarised away, and §1 is untouched by the move.**

**The status notes for store revisions 55, 54, 53 and 52 are moved verbatim** to [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2) in store revision 60, every blockquote, figure and caveat preserved, so a reference to the status note for any of those revisions still resolves there. **§8 now carries store revisions 60, 59, 58, 57 and 56** — the current note and the four before it, which is the retention this subsection states.

### 8.1 Status at store revision 51 and earlier — retained; moved to the retained-record document in store revision 58

**The status notes for store revisions 50, 49, 48, 47, 46 and 45 are moved verbatim** to [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2), every blockquote, figure and caveat preserved, so a reference to the status note for any of those revisions still resolves there. **§8 retains the current note and the four before it**, which is the retention the Director's answer to §7 item 53 set and which §8 had let slip to ten. **Store revision 62 made it six**, store revision 63 made it seven without saying so, store revision 64 added none, store revision 65 made it eight, store revision 67 said nine and **omitted §8's own note for store revision 66**, store revision 68 added a note without amending this sentence, and **store revision 69 makes it twelve, counted mechanically** — notes for store revisions 69, 68, 67, 66, 65, 63, 62, 61, 60, 59, 58 and 57 — because the ceiling no longer forces a move and moving another run's record in the heartbeat it was written is how a record gets double-stubbed. **The notes for store revisions 57 and 58 are the two to move first.**

**Why, and what it buys.** §7 item 53 is not a recommendation but the standing precondition for every further revision: this file has had to move a record to fit in store revisions 34, 36, 38, 40, 41, 47, 50 and 55. This revision moves §5.32, §5.33, §6.0-53, §6.0-54 and this section, and the headroom on departure is stated in §0.0-58's companion record. **No operative text moved. §1 is untouched by any of it.**

title: bill-text-s8 — §7 open-question item list, items 1 to 134 (split out of the bill in store revision 59)
body:
# bill-text-s8 — §7, the open-question item list: items 1 to 134

**Moved out of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) in store revision 59**, on the Policy Director's answer to §7 item 112 of 12 October 2026. Every numbered item, option, recommendation, table row and lettered label is preserved verbatim, so a reference of the form **§7 item n** resolves here. The bill document's §7 is now a pointer stub.

**Two things changed in the move and both are marked where they occur.** Seven items are dispositioned on the Director's direction of 12 October 2026 — items 88, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112 and 113 — and three are new: items 123, 124 and 125. Two stranded sentence ordinals are corrected. Nothing else is reworded.

**Items 114 to 121 were written after the §7.1 retained-record heading in store revision 57**, which put eight live items inside a stub that says its content was moved out, and left the list reading 1 to 113, then 122, then 114 to 121. The §7.1 heading and its three paragraphs now sit at the **end** of this document, after item 125, and **the numbered items run 1 to 125 in order**. Only positions changed: the reassembled file is **character-for-character the same length** as the file before the reordering, which is how the move was verified.

**INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed or cleared by counsel, not legally sufficient for introduction. Pre-decisional and internal. Nothing here is cleared for external use.**

---

## 7. Open questions for Policy Director

**What MOO-46 closed.** Three of revision 2's questions are answered and are off this list: the
acceleration counterfactual (item 3 of MOO-46 directed the repair and revision 2 had already drafted
it; **[MOO-53](/MOO/issues/MOO-53) has now confirmed it against a run** — the structure is right, the
double count is gone, the standard forecloses both zero-acceleration readings with margin, and the two
indeterminacies it found are drafted out in revision 5, §6.2); the per-member ceiling's *basis* (a
rule, not a figure — though the figure itself is now item 3 below); and the meaning of the
$3,000,000 (the appropriation, not a forecast, with the rate–cap linkage withdrawn). Revision 2's
item 7 — "the cap funds 56 percent of the design's own central-case demand" — is **not** closed by
that reframing but is changed by it: if $3,000,000 is the appropriation then exhaustion and the
denial rate are features to disclose rather than a mis-set dial, which is what item 9 below now asks.
**Revision 9: the FY2031 and 58 percent figures this paragraph carried are withdrawn** — superseded by
MOO-53 §6.2 and then by [MOO-48](/MOO/issues/MOO-48), and **no cap-utilisation figure is authorised
at all** while [MOO-71](/MOO/issues/MOO-71) is open. The question item 9 asks does not depend on the
figure, and it stays open.

**Two of these are new and both come out of MOO-46 item 4.** Items 1, 2 and 3 must be answered before
this goes to DLS or to a patron.

1. **MOVED TO THE RETAINED RECORD IN STORE REVISION 58 — this item is closed and is not an open question. The whole of it is at [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2), where a reference of the form §7 item 1 still resolves.** Its own statement of what was decided is retained here verbatim; where that statement refers to reasoning *"below"*, the reasoning is in that document and not here.

   **X2 — who pays the certified subsidy? CLOSED AND DRAFTED IN REVISION 9. Nothing is open here.**
   The Director answered **Alternative A — the Commonwealth pays** on the question card of 11 October
   2026. Subsection O is now operative text, the `[X2 — OBLIGOR …]` instruction block is deleted, and
   D 1, D 2, D 3 and subsection L all stand, so the cap machinery describes money that actually
   moves (§0.0000000a). The reasoning below is retained as the record of the choice, **not** as a
   live question, so that a reviewer does not re-open it against the 13 January 2027 prefile date.
   **Prior record:** MOO-46 item 1 may already have answered this and I was not going to assume it. […]

   **Pointers it carried:** none.

2. **MOVED TO THE RETAINED RECORD IN STORE REVISION 58 — this item is closed and is not an open question. The whole of it is at [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2), where a reference of the form §7 item 2 still resolves.** Its own statement of what was decided is retained here verbatim; where that statement refers to reasoning *"below"*, the reasoning is in that document and not here.

   **The window numeral — DECIDED AND DRAFTED IN REVISION 21 AT 12 MONTHS. Nothing is open here.**
   The Director answered **12 months — $1,411,988** on the question card of 12 October 2026, against
   the authorised ladder (0 months $1,661,819 · 6 $1,539,576 · 12 $1,411,988 · 18 $1,279,235 · 24
   $1,141,496). *"Final qualifying retirement date"* now reads *"the date that is 12 months after
   the member's earliest qualifying retirement date"* and the bracket is gone. **Three things follow
   and two of them are not mine. […]

   **Pointers it carried:** [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85); [Corrected in revision 18 —` [MOO-77](/MOO/issues/MOO-77); item 3; item 25; item 7

3. **The per-member ceiling figure — DRAFTED AT $170,000, AND REVISION 21 RE-OPENS ITS BASIS WITHOUT
   RE-OPENING THE FIGURE.** $170,000 was walked off the per-member certified-subsidy distribution at
   the **0-month** rung (90th percentile $160,468, maximum $208,905). The Director has now chosen the
   **12-month** rung, and a longer window moves every per-member subsidy down — later commencement,
   less acceleration charged — so the percentile the figure was chosen to sit at is not where
   $170,000 sits any more. **I have not moved the figure**: it is the Director's number, it is
   unbracketed in the Code text, and moving it on my own arithmetic would be exactly the error
   MOO-45 warned against. [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85) asks Fiscal & Impact Modeler for the
   distribution at the 12-month rung and for the figure the Director's own basis returns there; if it
   is materially different the Director should see both numbers before this goes to a patron. **The
   record of the original choice follows.** The Director
   directed the figure on 11 October 2026 and D 2 now carries it unbracketed. **Three things about it
   that are still live, none of them the figure itself.** (a) **The definition did not move with it
   and must not** — §0.0000000b: the two definitions collapse into one, and what moved between
   $100,000 and $170,000 is the **cohort**, not the measure. (b) **D 2 refuses rather than trims**, so
   every trim-basis quantity in the record below is the wrong quantity for this text — §0.0000000c and
   §7 item 19. (c) **The figure was set off [MOO-48](/MOO/issues/MOO-48)'s rung-1 distribution**, and
   the identical-set interval around a ceiling on this definition has collapsed to **$4,114**, so if
   the window numeral `[12]` moves off rung 1 the distribution moves and the figure has to be
   re-walked. That coupling is unchanged and it is item 2. Also closed by the direction: MOO-46
   Decision 2(e)'s rule is retired as the ceiling's basis, which moots item 16.
   **Everything below is the revision-5 record, retained and superseded.**

   **The per-member ceiling figure — `[$100,000]` as of revision 5, and the warning about applying
   MOO-46's rule now cuts the other way.** [MOO-53](/MOO/issues/MOO-53) §4 settles two things and
   opens one. **Settled:** `[$80,000]` is unworkable — it is below **$81,278**, the cheapest election
   the bill admits, so it excludes part of the subsidy of **100 percent** of the eligible cohort, and
   it is not a close call (the same sweep at the zero calendar gap gives an 86 percent exclusion rate
   on the A+B cohort). And MOO-46 Decision 2(e)'s own rule returns **$100,000** on the A+B cohort
   **and** on the Pathway-A-only cohort — *"the two cohorts give the same figure, which is the
   strongest thing that can be said for it: it does not depend on whether MOO-49 confirms clause
   (v)."* So the bracket now holds the rule's answer. **Still open:** the rule is applied to a
   distribution that the **window numeral** (item 2) moves, and nobody has yet been asked what it
   returns at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months. **[MOO-48](/MOO/issues/MOO-48) is the issue that should answer
   it, and I could not reach it** — it is one of this issue's own blockers and cross-issue writes were
   refused while this issue is dependency-blocked, so the request is in
   [`revision5-handoff`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-revision5-handoff) on this issue for you to route
   rather than in MOO-48's thread. **If it is already
   inside MOO-48's deadline-ladder scope, nothing needs doing.** **What is new and makes this harder than it was:** the ceiling has
   become a **sensitive** instrument. MOO-45's flat $30,000-wide identical-set band is gone, the
   identical-set interval around the figure has collapsed from $18,890 to **$4,114**, and every
   candidate figure now selects a materially different set of members. A figure chosen on the
   0-month distribution and left alone will not survive a window change the way $80,000 was expected
   to. **And state the cost of $100,000 when you carry it:** 69.1 percent of the bill-eligible cohort
   loses part of its subsidy and the worst-affected member faces **$70,343** of uncovered certified
   subsidy. If you would rather hold Pathway A whole, the figure is **$175,000** — it excludes nobody
   and does no fiscal work the model can see, and its only merit is that it bounds a salary-dispersion
   tail the model does not resolve.
4. **Keep the settlement redetermination in G 1, or cut it?** This is mine and I am flagging it
   rather than burying it. It is the most machinery revision 3 adds — three sentences — and it was
   not asked for. It exists because a window makes the certified subsidy indeterminate and every
   determinate alternative is worse (§6.1 item 11). What it buys: the cap reserves on the dearest
   case so it still binds; the Commonwealth pays on the fact rather than on an assumption; released
   excess funds other veterans; and in MOO-53's zero-acceleration case the subsidy collapses toward
   the price-discount floor instead of paying for an acceleration that did not occur. What it costs:
   a second actuarial determination per election, 90 days after each retirement, which VRS will price
   in the § 30-19.1:7 statement and may object to. **If you cut it, the honest fallback is to reserve
   and pay on the earliest-date valuation and to disclose the overstatement in the fiscal statement
   — not to leave the valuation date unnamed.**
5. **J 3's evaluation date — 1 December 2032 — and item 2 is now answered, so this is decidable.**
   At the 12-month window an election accepted in FY2032 is credited up to 12 months later and may
   retire up to 12 months after that, so **a FY2032 or FY2033 elector will not have retired by 1
   December 2032** and DPB would be evaluating a cohort that has not yet done the thing being
   evaluated. The three one-sentence options below are unchanged and the choice is still partly

20. **NEW IN REVISION 12 — pass 4's S7. G 1's lesser-of is a one-way ratchet. Make it two-way, or
    keep the certainty?** This is the one of my five live findings that revision 12 **did not**
    draft, because it cannot be fixed without a decision. As drafted, G 1 settles *"the amount so
    redetermined or the amount last certified and reserved for the election, whichever is less."* So
    if the member's actual retirement proves **cheaper** than the reservation, the general fund keeps
    the saving; if it proves **dearer**, the amount settled is capped at the reservation and **the
    trust absorbs the overrun.** Pass 4 reads that against art. X, § 11 — the trust is held *"solely
    in the interests of the members"* — and it is attacking machinery I added in revision 3 and
    flagged as my own judgment in item 4, so the review did exactly what I asked it to.

    The two-way version is one clause: delete *"or the amount last certified and reserved for the
    election, whichever is less"* and add —

    > <u>and the Commonwealth shall pay the amount so redetermined, whether or not it exceeds the
    > amount last certified and reserved for the election.</u>

    **What each side actually costs.** Two-way is the fiduciarily clean answer and it is how a
    pension trust should be made whole, but it **breaks the cap**: $3,000,000 stops being a
    limitation on what the Commonwealth can be asked to pay, because an overrun at settlement is
    payable whatever the balance, and D 2's admission arithmetic no longer bounds the appropriation.
    One-way keeps the cap exact — which is the whole architecture MOO-35 directed and MOO-44 said the
    clause needed — at the price of a provision VRS's fiduciary counsel can object to. **A middle
    option exists and I would take it if you want one**: keep the lesser-of for the cap, and pay any
    overrun from the contingency amount reserved under D 3, which is already inside the
    $3,000,000 and already exists for exactly this class of surprise. That bounds the trust's
    exposure to the overruns the contingency cannot absorb rather than to all of them, and it
    changes no figure. **It is three options and they are all one or two sentences; none of them is
    a redraft, and I will draft whichever you pick.**

33. **NEW IN REVISION 24, from pass 7's F-20. Nothing says whether a determination under this section is
    an Administrative Process Act "case decision," so M 2's saving clause may save a right that does not
    exist.** M 2 ends *"Nothing in this subsection limits the right … to judicial review pursuant to
    Article 5 (§ 2.2-4025 et seq.)."* Pass 7 checked § 2.2-4025 and VRS is **not** excluded from Article
    5, so the clause is not void at the agency level. But Article 5 review runs to a **case decision**,
    and the bill never characterises its determinations as such and never provides for the Article 3
    proceeding in which a case decision is ordinarily made. **Failure case:** a member refused under D 4
    petitions in Richmond Circuit Court; VRS moves to dismiss on the ground that the determination is
    *"solely the internal management or routine of an agency"* under § 2.2-4025 A (ii), that no Article
    3 proceeding was held or required, and that there is no case decision to review. Either way **the
    member who was promised review litigates about whether review exists** — and revision 24 has just
    added five more determinations carrying an express M 2 review right, so the clause is doing more
    work than it was.

    **MY RECOMMENDATION IS WITHDRAWN IN STORE REVISION 33, and the substitute is better.** The
    candidate text I had drafted and recommended was: *"A determination of the Board under this section
    is a case decision for the purposes of the Administrative Process Act, and the written
    reconsideration provided by this subsection constitutes the proceeding required by Article 3
    (§ 2.2-4018 et seq.) of that Act."* **Do not take it.**
    [MOO-95](/MOO/issues/MOO-95)'s pass 9, finding S-9, verified § 2.2-4021 B from source: in any
    informal fact-finding, formal proceeding or summary case decision proceeding in which a hearing
    officer is not used, the agency must decide **within 90 days**, and *"[i]f the agency does not render
    a decision within 90 days, the named party … may provide written notice to the agency that a
    decision is due. If no decision is made within 30 days from agency receipt of the notice, **the
    decision shall be deemed to be in favor of the named party**."* The three named exceptions are
    environmental boards; VRS is not among them, and § 2.2-4018's seven Article 3 exemptions do not reach
    retirement determinations. **So my sentence would have imported a statutory default judgment against
    the Board.** A member refused because her certified subsidy exceeds $170,000 requests
    reconsideration, the Board is silent, she serves the § 2.2-4021 B notice, and thirty days later her
    reservation exists by operation of law — against limitations D 2 declares *"self-executing and
    requir[ing] no further act of the General Assembly, the Board, or any other person."* **Those two
    cannot both be true**, and the route costs the applicant one letter.

    **The substitute, drafted and not inserted, and it is the Code's own formula.** § 51.1-124.11
    already contains the General Assembly's words for a VRS benefit determination, verified verbatim by
    pass 9: notice, *"an opportunity to be heard in accordance with the provisions of the Administrative
    Process Act,"* and an express entitlement to *"judicial review pursuant to Article 5 (§ 2.2-4025 et
    seq.)."* Adapted to M 2:

    > <u>The Board shall give a member, retiree, or beneficiary adversely affected by a determination
    > under this section reasonable prior written notice and an opportunity to be heard in accordance
    > with the Administrative Process Act (§ 2.2-4000 et seq.), and any member, retiree, or beneficiary
    > aggrieved by such a determination shall be entitled to judicial review pursuant to Article 5
    > (§ 2.2-4025 et seq.) of that Act.</u>

    **This is now my recommendation.** It gives the member a real and express review right, it is
    drafted in Title 51.1 for this agency and has been on the books since 1998, and it does **not**
    characterise anything as a case decision or engage § 2.2-4021's default. The one gap, stated
    honestly: it does not foreclose a § 2.2-4025 A (ii) *"internal management or routine"* argument —
    **but neither did the sentence I withdrew**, because that argument goes to the character of the
    action and not to the label a statute puts on it. If you would rather not legislate review at all,
    the alternative is still to delete M 2's last sentence and say nothing, which is honest and gives the
    member nothing.

40. **NEW IN STORE REVISION 33, from [MOO-95](/MOO/issues/MOO-95)'s pass 9, finding S-8. The over-cap
    reinstatement duty now carries four safeguards; the structural alternative is one sentence and I have
    not taken it.** G 4 requires the Board to reinstate a reservation released otherwise than in
    accordance with D 7 *"notwithstanding that the amount available to be reserved is thereby exceeded."*
    **Pass 9 accepts the choice** — the alternative is a member holding vested below-cost credit with no
    appropriation behind it, which is worse for the trust and worse under Va. Const. art. X, § 11 — and
    attacks what the sentence left out. **Its best point is one I had not seen: the sentence does not
    avoid the art. X, § 11 exposure, it relocates it.** Art. X, § 7 provides that *"[n]o money shall be
    paid out of the State treasury except in pursuance of appropriations made by law,"* so a settlement
    above the appropriation is not payable and the **trust carries the gap** — which is the single outcome
    the reservation architecture exists to prevent. And it does so silently: D 3's DPB confirmation is
    bypassed, because it is owed *"before reserving"* and reinstating is not reserving; D 3's
    money-committee notice is not triggered, because it attaches to a DPB refusal; and subsection K's
    shut-off is not triggered, because it attaches to a failure to appropriate. **The party who bears it
    is the wait-listed applicant, who appears in no stakeholder map and gets no notice saying why her
    turn moved.**

    **Enacted in store revision 33:** the contingency amount is reinstated with the reservation (pass 9's
    m-4 — *"it"* named only the reservation, and at $170,000 plus 20 percent the difference is $34,000);
    and the Board must give written notice of every reinstatement, of the amount of the excess and of the
    **cause of the release**, to the money-committee Chairmen **and to each applicant then on the waiting
    list**, within 15 days; must state every reinstatement and excess in the J report; and must accept no
    further election until the excess is eliminated. The last limb is already the law by operation of
    D 2; saying it stops the Board discovering it late.

    **The structural alternative, drafted and not inserted — and it is cheaper in every dimension except
    one.** *"A release of a reservation otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7 is void and of
    no effect, and the reservation shall be treated as never having been released."* On those words the
    headroom was never available, the cap is **never exceeded**, and the art. X, § 7 objection never
    arises. **The exception is the one that stopped me taking it**: the member accepted out of the
    wrongly-released headroom relied on a DPB confirmation and on the Board's acceptance, and void-ab-
    initio makes her acceptance ultra vires rather than valid-but-crowding. **That is a choice between two
    innocent members and it is yours, not mine.** If you take it, the four safeguards above stay useful
    and should stay. **Pass 9 also answered a sub-question I had asked it:** there is no time limit on
    reinstatement and that is correct rather than defective, because enactment 3 (ii) keeps the D 2
    limitations alive after 1 July 2033 expressly.

    than behaviour the text prices.

    - **(a) Price it — a minimum first payment**, in subsection E: *"<u>A reservation is released under

55. **NEW IN STORE REVISION 36, from [MOO-106](/MOO/issues/MOO-106)'s pass 11, findings 11 and 12, and it

    reportable under subsection J — and re-keys the Board's own 15-day member notice so it no longer runs
    from the date the Board *"learns"* of a separation nobody told it about. **What neither edit can fix is
    that the agency may have no way to know the duty applies to it.** Nothing tells an agency that the
    Board accepted an election; B 4 e gives a **paying** employer knowledge, and G 4 expressly contemplates
    transfer — *"A transfer of the member's employment from one state agency to another state agency shall
    not affect an election"* — so the separating agency may never have been the agency that knew. A member
    who elects at Agency A, transfers to Agency B and is separated by Agency B loses the branch through
    nobody's fault.

    **Two cures, each one sentence, and they trade a member's privacy against her protection.**

    - **(a) Tell the employer.** *"<u>The Board shall notify the member's employing state agency that the
      Board has accepted the member's election, and shall notify any state agency to which the member's
      employment is transferred of which the Board receives notice, no later than 15 days after the
      acceptance or after receiving notice of the transfer.</u>"* It makes the duty performable and

70. **NEW IN STORE REVISION 41, from [MOO-119](/MOO/issues/MOO-119)'s pass 13, findings F-3 and F-5 —

    the reservation sits against D 2's $3,000,000 indefinitely, and subdivision D 3 then requires a fresh
    DPB confirmation *"for each fiscal year in which any reservation remains in effect"* and bars
    acceptance of any further election until it is obtained. **The certified subsidy is positive, not
    zero**, because its *"shall not be less than"* limb is a **floor and not a ceiling**: the timing
    effect between the two valuation limbs does not vanish when the quantity does. **Who bears it:** the
    applicants on the subdivision **D 5** waiting list, whose remedy is express — D 3 makes a waiting-list

    5 APA review. **They are not in the stakeholder map as bearers of this cost, and that is routed to

    > <u>The Board shall not accept an election under which no service credit is to be purchased.</u>

    > In subdivision D 6, in the fourth sentence, for *"reduces the amount of service credit the member
    > may purchase under clause (ii) of subsection C to zero"* read <u>"reduces the amount of service
    > credit the member may purchase under clause (ii) of subsection C to zero, or where the service

    > subdivision or under clause (i) of subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2"</u>.

71. **P14-9 — the measuring point of the 12-month cap on the tolling date-setter. NEW. Mine, raised rather
    than resolved, and the reviewer's own fix direction does not work.** The date-setter in the definition
    of *"final qualifying retirement date"* gives the member, where tolling has prevented her from
    retiring, a date two months after the Board last acts on her request — *"and in no event later than 12
    months after the latest date the preceding sentence permits,"* which is the outer bound. The only route
    into the sentence is the Board over-running its own 90-day reconsideration deadline, and **nothing in
    the section bounds that over-run.** So the longer the Board takes, the less the sentence gives her, and
    past about 21 months it gives her nothing: outer bound 1 March 2033, request filed 1 February 2033,
    Board acts 1 September 2035, and she is capped at 1 March 2034 — eighteen months before the Board
    decides the very question her retirement turns on. That is the structural harm pass 12's F-1 condemned:
    the protective branch should never shorten the ordinary window.

    **The reviewer's fix is surplusage and I did not enact it.** It proposes *"in no event later than 12
    months after the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board last so acts"* —
    which bounds the sentence's own date by itself plus twelve months, so the cap could never bind.
    §6.0-43 item 4.

    **There is no middle option, and that is the point: the cap is the occupancy bound.** Her date is what
    releases the reservation, because G 2 matures 60 days after it. Any form that never cuts her off makes
    occupancy a function of Board delay.

    **(a) Leave it as drafted.** Occupancy per election is bounded on the face of the text at the outer
    bound plus 12 months. The cost is the member above: she loses the window for the Board's delay.

    **(b) Never cut her off. I lean to this and I will not enact it, because it unbounds occupancy.** One
    clause, and it leaves the cap doing its work in every case where the Board acts in time.

    > In the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"*, for *"and in no event later than 12 months
    > after the latest date the preceding sentence permits"* read <u>"and in no event later than 12 months
    > after the latest date the preceding sentence permits, except that where the Board acts upon the
    > request after that date the member's final qualifying retirement date is the first day of the second
    > month following the month in which the Board last so acts"</u>.

    **(c) Bound the Board's delay instead of her window.** Give M 2's 90 days a consequence. **I advise
    against the obvious form** — a deemed decision — for the reason §7 item 33 was withdrawn: § 2.2-4021 B
    already supplies a statutory default decision in the member's favour by the Article 3 route, and
    layering a second one on a capped benefit puts a $170,000 reservation into existence by operation of
    law against limitations D 2 calls *"self-executing."*

    **Figures: (a) moves nothing. (b) adds reservation occupancy in the tail of the Board-delay
    distribution and nothing at the central case**, because no central-case member reaches the sentence at
    all — it requires the Board to breach its own 90 days. Routed to Fiscal as a tail assumption, not as a
    reprice.

    **ADDENDUM, STORE REVISION 47 — pass 15's S-2 is this same question asked of the *rescission*
    date-setter, and it is now §7 item 85.** The two caps have the same structural problem and the answer
    should be one answer: a 12-month cap measured from any date earlier than the Board's own act either
    binds and names a date in the past or is subordinated and never binds. **Store revision 47 made the
    rescission cap determinate and did not make it a bound, and says so.** If you answer this item and
    item 85 the same way, one of the two edits becomes unnecessary and I will cut it.

72. **P14-10 — which reading of G 4's clock to enact. NEW. This is the one pass 14 put to you, and it is
    the only one of the four that is not mine.** G 4's clock runs from *"the later of the last day on which
    the member may retire in a qualifying retirement **under this subdivision** and the member's final
    qualifying retirement date, if any."* Pass 12 read the first limb as the ninetieth-day date, and that
    was right on the text as it then stood. Store revision 39's own proviso and one-extension cap have made
    it ambiguous, because a retirement on the ninetieth-day date is a *qualifying retirement* only if her
    final date has moved to reach it — and whether it has now depends on the proviso and the cap.

    **It is a fiscal ambiguity and not a member-protection one. Both readings are safe for the member.**
    They differ by about **three months of reservation occupancy per repeat separation**, because on the
    nominal reading the Board's determination, the refund and the release of up to $170,000 plus its
    contingency all slide to a date on which the member cannot in fact retire.

    **(a) Nominal — the phrase means the ninetieth-day date whatever her final date is.** Four words, and
    it is the member-neutral and fiscally worse reading.

    > …*"the last day on which the member may retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision*
    > <u>, determined as though the extension provided by this subdivision applied</u>*"*…

    **(b) Actual — the phrase means the last date on which a retirement would in fact qualify.** The
    *"later of"* then does nothing where the extension is switched off, and the reservation clears three
    months earlier.

    > …*"the last day on which the member may retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision*
    > <u> or, if earlier, under the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A</u>*"*…

    **I have no view on which you should pick** and neither did the reviewer. **One correction to what
    Fiscal has been told:** [`pass12-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass12-disposition) §6 says
    F-22 is *"closed by the one-extension cap."* On reading (a) it is closed as to the **window** and open
    as to **occupancy**, and the Modeler should be told which reading is enacted.

    **ADDENDUM, STORE REVISION 47 — pass 15's m-7, an adjacent ambiguity, not a new question.** G 4
    provides that a member's final qualifying retirement date *"shall not be extended under this
    subdivision by reason of more than one involuntary separation."* The rescission date-setter is keyed to
    a **rescission**, not to a separation, so on the face of it the one-extension cap does not reach it,
    though in substance the movement is by reason of a separation. **Bounded — at most one further movement
    of about four months.** One clause settles it either way — *"and the preceding sentence does not limit
    this sentence"*, or the converse — and whichever reading you take on this item, the drafting answer
    should be express rather than left to construction.

One point bears directly on the nullity question: store revision 47's E5, which replaced the nullity with a cure, **removed the only outer bound on how long a retirement allowance may lawfully be withheld** in the late-notice case — 120 days before, unbounded now. **If you restore the nullity, store revision 50's R-4 edit falls away with it**, as does part of item 100.
    NEW. Mine, and the direction of effect runs against the member.** Store revision 39 made a G 2
    determination that takes effect before the end of the member's notice period *"of no effect"*. **The
    section supplies no route to undo what the Board has already done on the strength of it** — within 60
    days it has refunded the member and her employer, and it has released a reservation that is now
    reserved for the next applicant off the waiting list. G 4's reinstatement sentence does not reach her,
    because that release **was** in accordance with D 7. So on a three-day mailing miscount her credit was
    never reduced, her reservation was never released, $150,000 of it is reserved for somebody else, and
    the aggregate charged exceeds $3,000,000 — an unfunded liability flowing into the employer contribution
    rate under art. X, § 11's actuarial-methods clause. **It is not an art. X, § 7 defect and no document
    of ours may concede one:** no money leaves the treasury without an appropriation.

    **Enacted (edit 9):** the determination *"takes effect instead on the first day on which it may take
    effect under this sentence."* Her 30-day floor and her M 2 period are preserved in full; what she loses
    is the windfall.

    **The alternative, drafted and not enacted.** Keep the nullity and give it the three verbs G 4's
    rescission limb has, plus the notices:

    > <u>and a determination that takes effect in contravention of this sentence is of no effect. Where a
    > determination is of no effect under this subdivision, the Board shall restore the service credit
    > reduced under it, shall reinstate the reservation and the contingency amount released on account of

    **What the alternative costs, stated plainly.** It is six lines rather than one, it puts the

    **ADDENDUM, STORE REVISION 47 — two things from pass 15 bear on this item and one of them is a reason
    to read it now.** **m-2:** G 4 keeps *"a determination made in contravention of this sentence is of no

74. **P14-6 — the deeming device for an undetermined involuntary separation. NEW. Mine, declined and
    drafted.** Store revision 43 gives the member an express route — she may file written evidence, and the

    members whose agency failed to file and whose Board failed to determine.

    - **(6) F11's authority, which is a request and not a drafting answer.** The reviewer reports the hidden-override risk as **constitutionally sound** — Article IV, Section 12 of the Constitution of Virginia requires reenactment of an *amended* section, and an act complete in itself that supersedes prior law by implication is not an amendment in that sense — **with one express limit: the reviewer verified the constitutional text but did not locate controlling Supreme Court of Virginia authority on the "complete in itself" doctrine within the pass, and offered to run it down.** The conforming amendment enacted in store revision 67 removes the risk for § 51.1-162 C. **It does not remove it for the two *"notwithstanding"* displacements in subdivision G 4**, which reach § 51.1-165 C 1 and § 51.1-165.01 F and are not accompanied by any amendment to either. Say whether you want that authority hardened before the drafting request goes to Division of Legislative Services.

    **ANNOTATION, store revision 69 — THE CARD IS ANSWERED AND THREE OF THE FOUR ANSWERS ARE IN THE TEXT.** The Policy Director accepted **f1-b**, **f4-a**, **f14-move** and **f11-authority** at **18:35:16 UTC on 12 October 2026** (card `829fa6d2`). Store revision 69 enacts the three that are drafting, in five substitutions: subdivision G 4 (three) and subsections B and L (one each). Record: §0.0-69, sweep §5.46, drafter's note §6.0-69 of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8).

    - **f1-b — enacted, with the Director's words reproduced verbatim and two conforming limbs added, each recorded at §6.0-69 items 2 and 3 and each reversible in one substitution.** (i) *"that is not a qualifying retirement"*, without which the exception — confined only by *"for the purposes of this subdivision"* — reached **a member who retired in a qualifying retirement** and pulled a retiree out of § 51.1-163, which is the class [MOO-161](/MOO/issues/MOO-161)'s F1 rated fatal and the class the standing direction protects. (ii) *"and for those purposes the member shall not be treated as having retired before the date of death in such a retirement"*, because the approved words define the **noun** *"a retirement before the date of death"* while the branch's own condition is the **verb** *"the member has not retired"* — without the limb **the approved answer did not reach the class it was approved to reach.**
    - **One residual of f1-b declined with its reason, and it is the first thing the next pass is told to attack.** A disability retiree **already in payment** whose effective date the Board *re-determines* after her death is, on the words, a member whose effective date the Board determined after the death. **f1-a's limb would close it and f1-a was not selected**, so taking it now would be re-deciding the card.
    - **f4-a — enacted. The card described option (a) and did not draft it, so the words are mine and the policy is the Director's.** The greater-of now runs only where subdivision C 2 of § 51.1-165 and the § 51.1-162 determination are payable to the same person or persons; where they are not, **the C 2 benefit is paid and the benefit determined under the preceding sentence is not.** The branch is a semicolon clause and **not a sentence of its own, because that sentence now carries five references to *"the preceding sentence"* and all five mean one sentence.** Consequence, stated because it decides who is paid: where C 2's own switch to § 51.1-162 B fails, C 2 requires payment under § 51.1-163, so the family takes a **refund** where store revisions 67 and 68 would have paid an **allowance** — which is what Chapter 1 does for that family today. **No person is worse off than under present law and the act buys that class nothing.**
    - **f14-move — enacted, word for word, net zero characters.** The bar leaves subsection L and stands in subsection B after the sentence that makes an accepted election the only route to a purchase. *"Subsection L"* is cited nowhere in the act, so nothing strands, and no citation count changes.
    - **f11-authority — commissioned as [MOO-207](/MOO/issues/MOO-207)**, assigned, self-contained, and **not drafting**: the *"complete in itself"* authority under Va. Const. art. IV, § 12 for subdivision G 4's two *"notwithstanding"* displacements, which reach subdivision C 1 of § 51.1-165 and subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 and are accompanied by no amendment to either.
    - **Closed by the selection of their alternatives, and kept rather than deleted: f1-a, f1-c, f4-b and f4-c.** **Still open and still drafted word for word: (3) f12-ninety** — the § 51.1-162 C waiver floor stays at the thirtieth day after the notice — **and (4) f3-operative**, so a member who elected the straight life option under subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-165 may still have no death benefit for the subsidy to buy. **This annotation decides neither.**
    - **[MOO-200](/MOO/issues/MOO-200)'s pass landed at 00:15 UTC on 13 October 2026, after this card was answered, and three of its findings bear on these answers.** **F14** is *aggravated* by f14-move: subsection L exists to tell localities and school boards that the act does not reach them, and the subsection addressed to them now says nothing on the subject — and F14's separate point, that the bar has **no time anchor** while subdivision D 4 determines eligibility as of the filing date of the complete application, survives the move unchanged. **F6 and F7** attack the sentence f4-a amends — F7 that the greater-of comparison *"changes no amount for anyone"*, F6 that the named assumption set is not identifiable because § 51.1-124.3 defines *"actuarial equivalent"* by *"actuarial tables **adopted** by the Board"* — and **f4-a neither cures nor worsens either.** **MOO-200's eighteen findings are not disposed in store revision 69; that is the next revision.**


133. **NEW IN STORE REVISION 68, out of [MOO-195](/MOO/issues/MOO-195)'s pass 21 on the designation-review advisory (finding F7) — drafted in full and enacted nowhere. The failure sentence catches omission and misses misstatement.** Subdivision D 1's failure sentence reaches *"a **failure to state** in the Board's certification every matter this subdivision requires to be stated in it"*, and subdivision M 2's general limb reaches *"a **failure** of the Board to state in a certification or notice a matter this section requires to be stated in it."* **Both are framed on absence. Neither reaches a matter that is stated and wrong.**

    **Why it bites hardest on the advisory, which is why the pass raised it here.** The six propositions of law in D 1's series are long and interlocking and a certification template will lift them as one block from the statute; they are present or absent together. **The advisory is short, separable and in a different register, and it is exactly the line a plain-language template editor rewrites.** Rendered as *"Your beneficiary designation on file with VRS will apply to this purchase,"* it is present — so it is no omission — and it is **wrong**, because the designation on file may defeat the subsection B allowance entirely. The member is actively misled, there is no channel, and the subsection J report records the matter as stated.

    **Drafted, in D 1's failure sentence:** *"A failure to state in the Board's certification every matter this subdivision requires to be stated in it<u>, or the statement of any such matter otherwise than as this subdivision requires it to be stated,</u> is a failure of the Board to state in a certification a matter this section requires to be stated in it for the purposes of subsection M…"*

    **Not enacted, for three reasons, and the third is the one that matters.** The defect is a property of a sentence **you approved at store revision 62**, not of the 137 characters cut at store revision 65; it is outside a cut commissioned as one edit; and **it interacts with the channel question** — if you take pass 21's F3 recommendation and except the advisory from subsection M review, the advisory needs no misstatement limb either, and the clause would then reach only the six propositions. **Decide F3 first.** The whole disposition is at [`moo195-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-191#document-moo195-disposition).

134. **NEW IN STORE REVISION 68 — item 129's conservator residual, answered. A non-case on the main question, with one narrow intake residual drafted and not enacted.** Item 129 asked the next counsel pass whether it is a defect that a conservator acting for a **living** member under a disability receives the subdivision D 1 certification and appears in no class in subdivision M 2. [MOO-195](/MOO/issues/MOO-195)'s pass 21 §7 answers: **a non-case.** M 2's class is a list of **parties in interest**, not of representatives. A conservator appointed under Chapter 20 of Title 64.2 asserts no claim of their own; they exercise **the member's** standing, and *"a member"* is the first category M 2 names. The act's other fiduciary references sit in subdivision G 4 and are needed there because those provisions concern **death** benefits, where the member has no standing left to exercise and the fiduciary must be named in their own right.

    **The residual, which is narrow and real enough to card.** Subdivision M 2 opens *"A member … adversely affected by a determination"* and then requires a *"written request filed."* **If the Board reads the filing requirement as personal to the member, a conservator's filing could be refused at intake**, forcing a petition that would plainly succeed and costing the member the time the tolling provision exists to give her.

    **Drafted, as one clause added to M 2's class:** *"<u>or a fiduciary within the meaning of § 51.1-1012 acting for any of them</u>."*

    **Not enacted.** It is outside the scope of the one-edit cut at [MOO-191](/MOO/issues/MOO-191), it widens a standing class you have not been asked about, and the answer above is enough to close the residual as item 129 posed it. **Say whether you want the clause; it is one substitution and it reverses nothing.**

### 7.1 Retained record — performed; moved to the retained-record document in store revision 41

**Moved verbatim** to [`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history), every numbered item, table row and lettered label preserved, so a reference of the form **§7.1** still resolves there. Same reason and method as the sections moved in store revisions 34, 36 and 38: the file was 3,555 characters from the store's 524,288-character ceiling and store revision 41's record did not fit.

**The durable results.** It is the record of the numbers and choices that were mine rather than the Director's, moved to the end of §7 in store revision 33 on pass 9's m-6 and not amended since. **It is a retained record and it is now in the retained-record document, which is the only move in this revision that is pure housekeeping.** Its durable result is the standing principle it exists to serve: **every number this draft chose rather than received is recorded with its direction of effect**, and nothing in it is operative text, a drafted option, or an open question. A reference of the form **§7.1 item 3** still resolves there, and §7's numbered items 1 to 70 are unaffected.
