# `bill-text-s8` — retained record, §0, §5 and §6, store revisions 2 to 51

**Moved verbatim out of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) in store revision 52**, on the Policy Director's answer to §7 item 53 (*move the whole §0/§5/§6 retained record out*). Every heading, table row, numbered item and lettered label is preserved, so a reference of the form **§0.x**, **§5.n**, **§6.0-n**, **§6.1a** or **§6.4** still resolves here. **101,593 characters. Nothing is lost and no bill text moved.** The §0 narrative for store revisions 2 to 33 is in [`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history) and for store revisions 34 to 49 in [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2); what is here is the §0 stub-and-index block as it stood at store revision 51 (including the full §0 narrative for store revisions 49, 50 and 51), together with the whole of §5 and §6 as they stood at store revision 51.

**Internal working draft material. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel. Pre-decisional.**

---

# Part I — §0 as it stood at store revision 51

## 0.0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Store revision 51 — [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136)'s record corrections carried in on [MOO-142](/MOO/issues/MOO-142). Four corrections, one decision closed, one FOIA ground recorded, and no operative text touched

**This revision changes no operative bill text.** §1 is byte-identical to store revision 50 — 101,063
characters — and the definition of *"involuntary separation"*, including its **residual dating limb** and the
words *"or equivalent status"*, is untouched. Everything here is record, note or routing.

**1 — The closed-set reading of § 2.2-3200 B is withdrawn.** [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136) re-opened the
section at source on 12 October 2026 against the official Code (currency stamp 10/12/2026) and it reads
*"'Involuntary separation' **includes, but is not limited to,** terminations and layoffs…"*. Pass 15's
quotation omitted those five words. **The set of forms is open**, so the residual dating limb addresses a
**non-empty** residual class and not an empty set, and **pass 14's P14-11 premise holds.** The limb stays
**on the merits**, not as insurance against an empty set: it is what gives a date to an involuntary separation
in which the member neither has employment terminate nor is placed on leave without pay-layoff or equivalent
status but ceases to occupy the position — § 51.1-155.1 D's *"failure to obtain reappointment"* and an officer
whose position is abolished are the concrete cases. The four corrected places are the m-6 row of
[`pass15-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass15-disposition) §1, its §3 item 3, its §6 routing list,
and §e of the retained §0 record now in
[`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2). The §4
check 8 and §5.27 check 7 statements that § 2.2-3200 B had not been re-opened are **kept** as a record of what
was true when written, each with the re-opening noted.

**2 — §7 item 23 is answered and closed: LEAVE IT.** The Policy Director decided on 12 October 2026 that the
narrowing sentence is **not** inserted. The arbitrage is already fenced twice; the sentence would refuse the
pilot price to a genuinely involuntary separation not on the 1995 list; and it would make the residual dating
limb inert, reintroducing by drafting the very empty-set defect the pass-15 record wrongly asserted. **The
item was live either way** — it presupposed the open reading, which is the correct one — so it is closed by
the decision and **not** by the correction.

**3 — New §6.5 records the ground of the m-5 bar.** No FOIA exclusion reaches a member-identifying record in
the subdivision G 4 notice, in the Board's hands or a money committee's, so the bar *"which notice shall not
identify any member"* is **operative and not belt-and-braces**. The paragraph is
[MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136) §2.7 verbatim, citations unrestyled, and it is routed to the
[Editor](/MOO/agents/editor) for the fiscal and risk statement. It corroborates pass 11's earlier finding.

**4 — Housekeeping, and it is the only structural move.** §7 item 22 — **answered, nothing open** — is moved
**verbatim** to the retained-record document behind a pointer, because this file was **886 characters** from
the 524,288-character ceiling and the corrections above did not fit. Same method as §7.1 and the §0 and §6.0-n
records moved in store revisions 34 through 50. Nothing was summarised away, no figure moved, and every
cross-reference to item 22 resolves through the pointer. **The ceiling is now the binding constraint on this
document and it needs a decision of its own — raised as §7 item 102.**


---

## 0.000000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Store revision 50 — [MOO-135](/MOO/issues/MOO-135)'s pass 16 drafted out. Sixteen edits in nine provisions, no figure moved, and the Board's silence can no longer settle a subsidy

**Pass 16 — the bounded adversarial and counsel review of store revision 47's seventeen edits — returned 0 fatal, 5 serious, 8 moderate and 7 minor, plus the timing map for all seventeen edits that I asked for in place of a figure test.** It answered all eight of my questions and it says in terms that it could not make a case against the architecture: *"the reservation-and-settlement design, the self-executing limitation, the closed expiry machinery and the refusal to create any member liability are coherent and, in the refusal of liability, unusually careful. The case against is a case about the Board's clocks."*

**Of the twelve findings routed to me, eleven are drafted out in sixteen edits; one was already on the Director's list and is annotated rather than drafted twice.** `12`, `$3,000,000`, `$170,000` and the `[20]` percent contingency are untouched by every edit; no section is added or deleted; no designator is renumbered; the bill title, the enacting clause and enactment clauses 2, 4 and 5 are untouched. The finding-by-finding record, the sixteen edits verbatim and the full sweep are at **[`pass16-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass16-disposition)**.

**a. The one that mattered — R-5, and it was mine.** Store revision 47's E12 re-keyed subdivision G 4's clause-(iii) deeming limbs from *"the statement required by"* the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* to *"a statement **or notice**"* required by it. The definition requires four such things and three are contingent on a member's act — including a notice of the Board's determination **upon a request**, due 30 days after the request is filed. So a member with four years of subsidised credit who **did not want to retire** could file one request, give no reason because the section demands none, let the Board miss its 30 days, let her tolling run out at subsection M 2's 120-day cap, and have her date pass *"at a time when the Board has not given such a statement or notice and the time allowed ... has expired"* — whereupon clause (iii) fired, subdivisions 2 and 3 were switched off, her credit vested at the subsidised cost and the whole certified subsidy settled into subsection N. **She kept the credit, kept the job, and never retired.** Before E12 the limb was keyed to the initial statement, which the Board gave on time years earlier: **the path did not exist until I widened the words.** It is closed by excluding that one notice from the limbs, and the member who genuinely needs an answer is given a usable date instead — item b.

**b. The remedy that replaces it, and it is the pattern of this whole revision.** Four of the sixteen edits do the same thing: where a Board clock runs out, the member gets **a date she can use**, not a subsidy and not a stripping. The definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* now carries a floor where the Board never acts on a request at all (R-5); subdivision G 4 carries a floor where the Board learns of an involuntary separation after the date it must hand her has already gone (R-1); and the definition carries a floor for the fallback date-notice store revision 47 created (R-9). **Every one is a floor and not a setter** — each operates only where the date that would otherwise apply is *earlier* than the floor, so no edit can pull a member's date forward.

**c. R-1 is the finding I would read next, because the member in it did nothing wrong and the bill stripped her.** Store revision 47's E6 widened the involuntary-separation trigger from facts the Board was *required to act on* to anything it has *"otherwise learned of"* — while the extension date stayed a pure function of the separation date. Separation 1 March; her agency never files the notice the bill requires of it; the Board learns on 1 December; **her final qualifying retirement date "is that first day" — 1 June, six months gone.** She cannot retire on a day that has passed, so subdivision 2 reduced her purchased credit to what her own payments bought at standard cost. **No floor in the section reached her, and the clause-(iii) deeming limbs did not either**, because the G 4 extension date is not a date the definition requires to be stated. The new floor reaches her, and provides expressly that her retirement on or before the floor date satisfies the 90-day vesting condition, which had equally expired. Full statement, with the second affected party, at [`pass16-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass16-disposition) §3.

**d. Two duties had no date and one had no deadline at all.** **R-2:** store revision 47's E9 cured M-5 by running the 90-day redetermination from *"the date on which the Board determines that clause (iii) of this subdivision applies"* — and **no provision required the Board to make that determination or fixed a time for it.** So the amount settled was never fixed, subsection N's duty to pay *"the amount settled"* had no amount, and subdivision D 2 kept the reservation charged against the $3,000,000 throughout. I took the reviewer's **second** option and supplied the missing duty — 60 days, a reasons-notice in 15, a subsection J report line, subsection M review and a fallback clock — rather than its first, which was to key the clock back to the settlement date and would have re-created M-5 exactly. **R-6:** the reinstatement duty's **only** deadline was the date of a settlement that store revision 47's own bar can negate, so it now has a fallback that does not depend on a settlement occurring, and the recertification-before-redetermination sequencing duty is performable in every case.

**e. R-3 and R-8 — I lifted a clause out of subsection M 2 and it reversed meaning in its new home.** In M 2 the capped thing is the **member's** tolling and the excluded thing is the **Board's** overrun, so the clause means *the Board's lateness shall not eat her allowance*; it works because the capped party and the delaying party are different people. Transposed into subdivision G 4, where the capped thing is the Board's **own** periods, the two parties are the same and the clause split into a reading on which the Board buys itself unlimited time by being late on her request, and a reading on which her credit may be cut while her reconsideration is unanswered. **It is replaced with a direct statement of what the cap is for**, which also removes the stranded referent R-8 found: subsection M allows 90 days for a reconsideration only, and the subsection-A request carries a **30-day** deadline set by subsection A, so *"the 90 days allowed by subsection M"* had no referent for one of the two request types the sentence governs. **The new words choose no numeral.**

**f. The half of R-3 and R-4 that is the Director's, and one of them was already on the list.** Pass 16's Reading B exposes the member whose reconsideration succeeds after a subdivision 2 determination has taken effect, with no rescission limb for her. **That is already §7 item 93**, raised independently by [MOO-120](/MOO/issues/MOO-120)'s pass 12 as its S-4, with candidate text drafted and a recommendation to enact — **so item 93 is annotated with pass 16's independent confirmation rather than given a second, divergent repair here.** R-4's second half — an outer bound on how long a retirement allowance may lawfully be withheld where the Board **never** gives the subdivision G 2 notice, and whether the arrears carry interest — is **new §7 item 100**, drafted and not enacted. What I did enact removes the pair of irreconcilable mandatory commands R-4 identified and adds a subsection J report line so that a notice never given is visible rather than silent. **It does not bound the withholding, and I am not claiming that it does.**

**g. R-14 — I deleted a cap of my own, and the reviewer's reason for it is better than mine.** Store revision 47's E2 re-measured the rescission limb's 12-month cap from the date of the involuntary separation, and I enacted it knowing it could never bind and wrote that down. Pass 16 confirms the reasoning and supplies the structural ground: **the cap is measured from a date that always lies in the past** — separation precedes learning precedes rescission — while the floor it qualifies is always in the future, so no drafting of that cap can work. The residual was surplusage in an operative sentence, and the only work a reader could give it was an inverted reading that cut her restored date back to a past date. **It is deleted.** This bears on §7 item 85: deleting a cap that never bound removes nothing real, so item 85 remains the live occupancy choice.

**h. R-13, and the one place where I extended the envelope rather than bounding it.** Subdivision D 1's day-for-day extension for the Board's own lateness was subject to the definition's 12-month ceiling, so a member who had already used her tolling got **nothing** for a notice 200 days late — the remedy was worth least exactly when the Board was latest, and her only remaining route was R-5's machinery, which settles the subsidy rather than letting her retire. The ceiling now does not apply to an extension granted for the Board's lateness, **capped at 12 months in the aggregate**. **I state the envelope as a fact and not as an assurance**, because I have had to withdraw that assurance twice: 12 months of base window, plus the three-month processing extension, plus at most 120 days of tolling, plus a day-for-day extension for the Board's lateness capped at 12 months. **Direction of effect on reservation occupancy: longer.** It is reversible in one sentence and the reversal is at §6.0-50 item 5.

**i. Three record corrections, all against me.** R-18: `pass15-disposition` §2's blanket claim that *"the replaced text appears nowhere in the document afterwards"* is **not literally true of edit E15**, whose From-string is a proper prefix of its own To-string because E15 appends a clause and replaces nothing — not residue, and the claim needs the words *"except where an edit is a pure addition."* R-19: the statement at `pass15-disposition` §3 and in the moved §0 record that *"the only real bound is a limit on the rescission itself"* **overstates** — §7 item 85's own option (c) bounds the **charge**, which is a real bound that strips no member, so item 85 is a choice between three real bounds with different victims. R-20: the count of *"this subdivision"* in subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2 is **thirteen**, not six, and **every one means subdivision f** — the conclusion is strengthened and only the count was wrong.

**j. Three more, compactly, with the full statement of each at [`pass16-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass16-disposition) §3.** **R-17**, named rather than discovered later: store revision 47's E4 ends a pendency when the Board *"first acts"*, which is the intended effect, and the consequence is that where the Board acts, reopens and acts again a Board period can be found to have **expired retroactively**. The reviewer does not argue against it and neither do I; it is the one place in store revision 47 where that is possible. **What pass 16 verified, and against what:** the live body moved twice while it read, and before finalising it found document revision 55 and **re-ran everything against 55** — all seventeen To-strings present exactly once, all seventeen From-strings absent with E15 accounted for, six structural referents re-counted. **No finding depends on the earlier bodies.** It examined, derived and moved **no figure**, and it **concedes no Va. Const. art. X, § 7 defect**, because subsection N's duty is expressly *"from an appropriation made for that purpose"* and is therefore self-limiting. **No document of ours may concede that defect.** **Housekeeping, taken rather than asked:** this file arrived with **1,866 characters** of headroom, so eight sections are moved **verbatim** to [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2) — the §8 status notes for store revisions **44, 43, 41, 40 and 33**, **§6.0-47**, **§5.27** and **§6.1**. Every lettered label, numbered item, table row and check number is preserved; each is replaced by a stub restating its durable results and naming what in it is superseded. **Nothing was rewritten and nothing was summarised away**, and the retained record was written **before** anything was cut from this file.

## 0.00000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Store revision 49 — [MOO-120](/MOO/issues/MOO-120)'s pass 12 drafted out. Five repairs to the words the Director's MOO-64 answers put in; the fatal finding and three serious ones are drafted and **enacted nowhere**

**The record proper is a companion document** — [`moo120-pass12-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-moo120-pass12-disposition) — on the convention store revisions 33, 36, 40, 41, 42 and 44 set. It carries all five FIND/READ pairs, the finding-by-finding disposition of pass 12's **14** findings, the cross-reference sweep (**§5.29**), the ambiguities (**§6.0-49**), and the candidate text for §7 items 89 to 99. What follows is the summary.

**What pass 12 was.** The bounded adversarial and counsel review of the **nine edits** that enacted the Director's [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) answers on items 46, 48, 49, 50 and 54 in store revision 42. It returned **1 fatal, 4 serious, 6 moderate and 2 minor** findings, plus 11 express null results. **Verified:** the nine edits were confirmed present, each exactly once, at store revision 45, and store revision 49 re-verified its own five anchors and both limbs of the settlement bar F-1 turns on against the live body at store revision 48.

**The five edits, all repairs to words the answers put in, and none of them changes which member passes either definitional test.** **One** — M-1 — gives item 54's valuation limb the death branch's **recertification** sentence, which my drafting had dropped while calling the result parity; without it the Commonwealth could settle a subsidy certified for 19 months when the member bought 9 (**$106,253 average, $170,000 at the cap**). **Two** — M-4 — replaces *"restore the service credit reduced under it"* with *"restore or credit service credit as this subdivision provides"*, because a subdivision 3 determination reduces nothing. **Three** — M-3 — gives the item-48 confining sentence's trigger date a referent in the four places this section applies the definition without stating an as-of date (clause (viii), the D 1 certification item, subsection E, G 3). **Four** — m-1 — gives enactment clause 3 clause (iii) the saving clause (i) already has, so the apparatus subsection J's third report line reads survives expiry. **Five** — m-2 — stops subsection F's lead example asserting a deferral that item 46 made conditional.

**What is NOT cured, and it is the reason this revision does not advance publication.** **F-1 is fatal and stands:** G 4's settlement bar has two limbs, item 54 disapplies only the *determination* limb, and the **D 7 limb** still forbids the settlement item 54 commands — so on the better reading item 54 is inoperative in every case it was written for. **Two insertions cure it, they are drafted at §7 item 89, and one point there corrects my own earlier statement: insertion (i) cures the G 2 branch as well, so the complete cure and the half cure cost the same.** The three serious findings — J 1's terminal date (item 90), the late-filed disability approval (item 91), and clause (iii) Board error having no rescission route (item 92) — are drafted at those items and enacted nowhere.

# Part III — §6 as it stood at store revision 51

## 6. Drafter's note — structure choices and ambiguities resolved

### §6.0-50 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 50

**Six, and the full statement of each is at [`pass16-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass16-disposition) §6.**

**1. Whether a floor should be a floor or a setter.** Each of the four new date rules could have been drafted to *set* the member's date or to *raise* it. A setter can pull a member's date **forward**, taking time away from the member the rule exists to help. **All four are floors**: each operates only where the date that would otherwise apply is earlier than the date the rule names. The cost is four extra conditional clauses; the alternative was a rule that could harm its own beneficiary.

**2. Which of pass 16's two options to take on R-2, and I took the second.** Its first was to key the 90-day redetermination to the settlement event rather than to a Board act. That would have re-created **M-5**, which store revision 47's E9 was written to cure: a clock that has begun to run before the Board can know the duty exists. The reviewer's own reasoning for the first option — *"E9's problem was that the clock preceded the Board's knowledge, not that it ran from a date"* — is the reason **not** to take it, because M-5's complaint *was* that the clock preceded knowledge. **So the duty is supplied instead**, with an actor, a deadline, a notice, a report line and a fallback clock that runs from the expiry of the period if the Board never acts. That fallback is what stops the new duty becoming another limb that depends on a Board act with no cap.

**3. Whether to draft R-3's second half, and the answer is no because it is already drafted.** Pass 16's Reading B exposes the member whose reconsideration succeeds after a subdivision 2 determination has taken effect, and no rescission limb reaches her. **That is §7 item 93**, raised independently by MOO-120's pass 12 as its S-4, with candidate text drafted in [`moo120-pass12-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-moo120-pass12-disposition) and a recommendation to enact. Drafting a second version here would have put two divergent repairs for one defect in front of the Director. **Item 93 is annotated with pass 16's confirmation instead** — two reviewers reaching the same gap from different directions is the strongest thing that can be said for enacting it.

**4. The agency's identity, and who it costs.** Pass 16 offered two cures for R-10 — report agency default in aggregate, or move it to a separate transmittal. **I took the aggregate**, because it needs no new duty and the subsection J report already carries the information. **The residual, stated rather than smoothed over:** the Chairmen's notice still states the date, the amount and the **cause** of the release, and in a programme of roughly a dozen elections a cause of *"an involuntary separation"* is not nothing. The wait-list notice in the same sentence already excludes the cause, and that asymmetry is deliberate — **removing the cause from the Chairmen's notice as well would deprive the money committees of the reason a limitation they set was exceeded**, which is the whole point of the notice.

**5. R-13's envelope, and the reversal.** Excluding a day-for-day extension for the Board's own lateness from the definition's ceiling **lengthens the outer envelope** and therefore lengthens reservation occupancy. I enacted it because a remedy for the Board's default that evaporates exactly when the default is worst is not a remedy, and because the exclusion is itself capped at 12 months in the aggregate so nothing is unbounded. **If the Director prefers the occupancy, the reversal is the deletion of the words from *"except that this sentence does not apply"* to the end of that sentence**, and the member is then back to R-13's position, which pass 16 graded moderate.

**6. What the R-4 edit does and does not do, stated plainly because the temptation is to overclaim it.** It removes a pair of **irreconcilable mandatory commands**: before it, where the Board never gave the subdivision G 2 notice, the unqualified 120-day outer limit required the determination to take effect and the notice sentence forbade it. The limit now yields. **It does not give the absent-notice determination an effective date, and so does not bound the withholding of her allowance** — subsection F expressly blesses that deferral, and bounding it is a money provision no cited document directs. That is **§7 item 100**. What it adds for her now is visibility: a failure to give that notice within the period allowed is a line in the subsection J report.

### 6.5 Why subdivision G 4's bar on identifying a member is operative — the FOIA ground

**Recorded on [MOO-142](/MOO/issues/MOO-142) from [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136) §2.7, approved by the Policy Director for use as the
ground of the m-5 bar; reproduced without restyling the citations. No bill text changes, and the bar
*"which notice shall not identify any member"* stays exactly as drafted.**

> No exclusion in the Virginia Freedom of Information Act applies to a member-identifying record in the
> notice required by subdivision G 4. The exclusions for information held by the Virginia Retirement System
> (§ 2.2-3705.7 (12) and (24)) reach only information held by the Board acting as investment trustee under
> § 51.1-124.30. The personnel-information exclusion (§ 2.2-3705.1 (1)) is available to a custodian at its
> discretion and does not bind either the Board or a committee of the General Assembly. The bar in
> subdivision G 4 is accordingly the operative protection.

**The comparator, carried to the [Editor](/MOO/agents/editor) for the fiscal and risk statement:** § 30-80 C
gives VRS records *"provided to the Commission"* (JLARC) a **mandatory** FOIA exemption — *"shall be
exempted"* — while § 30-79 B of the same chapter **names** the House Committee on Appropriations and the
Senate Committee on Finance and Appropriations without extending that shield to them. **So the bar is the
only protection the member has**, in the Board's hands or a money committee's. This corroborates pass 11's
earlier finding that there is no privacy or FOIA bar on the G 4 notice.

**Thirteen edits in four provisions of §1: the definition of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*, subdivision G 3, subdivision G 4 (nine edits) and subdivision J 1 (three edits). +3,337 characters of bill text. **What the revision does, in one line each.**

- **Item 89, the fatal.** G 4's settlement bar had two limbs and the item-54 rescission disapplied one. Insertion (i) disapplies the **D 7 release** limb as well, in the rescission sentence, which already reaches *"a determination under subdivision 2 or 3"* — so it cures the **G 3 branch and the pre-existing G 2 branch together**. Insertion (ii) extends the reinstatement limb to a reservation released **in accordance with** D 7 where the determination is later rescinded. - **Items 94 to 97, the bundle.** The § 51.1-155.1 confinement operates *"for the purposes of this section"*, closing the *expressio unius* argument against its untouched twin. The subdivision-3 rescission gains the death branch's **refund** limb, with its 60-day payment deadline and its adverse-tax fallback.

### §6.0-52 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 52

**Three changes inside the Director's approved text are mine. They are listed first, and none of them changes which member passes either definitional test.**

1. **Item 93 as carded would have reproduced the fatal defect in new words, and I did not enact it that way.** The carded sentence commanded the Board to *"recertify and settle the certified subsidy as this subdivision requires"* after a reversal on reconsideration or judicial review. But G 4's bar forbids settlement *"after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect"* — and a determination reversed on review **has** taken effect; that is the premise of the whole sentence. The bar's other limb forbids settlement once the reservation has been released under D 7, and nothing reinstated it. **So the carded words commanded a settlement two sentences forbade, which is item 54's fatal defect at a different point.** I drafted both limbs into item 93 (*"notwithstanding that the reversed or modified determination had taken effect and notwithstanding that the reservation … has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7"*) and extended insertion (ii)'s trigger to a reversal or modification as well as a rescission. **This is drafting, not policy: the Director approved the rescue, and a rescue a neighbouring sentence forbids is not the rescue that was approved.**
2. **Item 92's redetermination clock gains the third trigger.** G 4 provides that where the Board rescinds, *"the period within which this subdivision requires the redetermination to be made runs from the date on which the member is so approved or dies."* Item 92 adds a third rescission trigger — the Board's determination of its own error — and the clock had no referent for it, so a duty with a 90-day period had no day to count from. Conformed in the Board's own words.
3. **Item 97's refund gains the death branch's payment deadline and its adverse-tax fallback.** The carded limb created a payment duty with no date, which is unenforceable, and the death branch two sentences earlier already carries exactly the words needed: payment within 60 days of crediting, and, to the extent a refund cannot be paid without adverse federal tax consequence, application of the amount to additional service credit at the standard cost. **Taking the parity the Director asked for and leaving out the deadline would have been taking half of it.**

**Ambiguities I had to resolve to write the answered text, with the resolution.**

4. **Item 93's arrears limb is drafted for a *modification* as well as a reversal, and the carded words were not.** The carded sentence paid her *"every amount that would have been payable … had the determination **not taken effect**."* On a **reversal** that is right. On a **modification** — subsection M or a court leaving a smaller reduction standing — it pays her as though no determination existed at all, which **overpays her against the determination that survives**, and subsection F's no-collection limb means the Commonwealth never gets it back. Enacted as *"had the determination, **as reversed or modified**, taken effect on the date on which the determination took effect,"* which is identical to the carded words on a reversal and is the only non-absurd reading on a modification. **It is the one of my four changes that moves money, so it is also carded as §7 item 105 for the Director to confirm rather than left in the note alone.**

5. **Item 89(i) is placed in the rescission sentence rather than in the bar.** Either place cures the G 3 branch; the rescission sentence already reads *"a determination under subdivision 2 or 3"*, so putting the disapplication there cures the **pre-existing G 2 branch at the same price**, and the bar keeps its general form for every case where nothing has been rescinded. **The half cure and the complete cure cost the same ~235 characters, which is why the complete cure is what I asked for and what the Director took.**
6. **Item 90(a)'s second new class is drafted as a D 7 release *"without any service credit having been credited to the member"*, not as a bare D 7 release.** A D 7 release that follows a G 3 crediting is not an election with nothing left to report; the class G 2's fourth sentence excepts is the one where the reservation went and the member got nothing. The narrower words except only that class.
7. **Item 90(b)'s further report is *"limited to that rescission and its consequences."*** Without the limit the Board would owe a complete annual report, cumulative figures and all, years after the programme closed, for one rescission. The limit is what makes the duty dischargeable, and the Board can still state on any 1 December whether limb (a) is satisfied — which is what it cannot do for *"the last rescission."*
8. **Item 91(a) is bounded to § 51.1-156 H's mandatory limb, as recommended and approved.** H's first sentence is the Board's own discretion, exercised with this consequence in view; its second is not a choice at all, and the Medical Board's certification is the tightest boundary in the chapter. **The looser alternative — *"as to which the Board has waived a period under subsection H"* — was offered and not taken, and I did not substitute it.**
9. **Item 91(b)'s saving is drafted to except the rescission expressly** (*"except as this subdivision provides for the rescission of the determination"*). Without that exception the saving and the carve-out contradict each other in the one case the carve-out exists for.
10. **Item 92 uses *"the Board thereafter determines that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board"*** — clause (iii)'s own words, not a new formula. G 4 already owes that determination within 60 days of the final qualifying retirement date, with a notice and a report line, so the new trigger inherits an existing duty rather than creating a standardless one. **Subdivision B 4 f's carve-out is untouched**, so a B 4 f cost determination is still not an error of the Board for these purposes.
11. **Item 93 says *"restore or credit service credit as this subdivision provides"*, not *"restore the service credit reduced under it."*** A subdivision 3 determination reduces nothing — it credits the months paid for and releases the reservation — so the carded verb had a zero-extent object for half the determinations item 93 reaches. This is the same repair already enacted as M-4 in store revision 49, and item 93 is drafted to match it rather than to re-create the defect.
12. **Item 95(b) authorises one offset and nothing else.** It names the month on both sides — a retirement allowance paid **for a month** against a disability allowance payable **for the same month** — so it cannot be read as a general power to recover. **The alternative, narrowing G 4's no-collection limb, was offered and not taken; it would have taken a protection from every member to reach a duplicate a few will have.**
13. **Item 96 switches off G 3's second sentence only on a rescission under subdivision 4**, by one sentence attached to it, rather than by qualifying the sentence in place. The sentence keeps its ordinary operation for every member whose G 3 determination stands.
14. **The thirteen edits carry no nested `<u>` tags.** The whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language and is already underlined at paragraph level, so a nested tag would be redundant markup rather than amendatory markup. **A reader searching for `<u>` will not find these spans individually, and that is the document's existing convention** — the same thing happened to two edits in store revision 49. Every word added in this revision is new language and is underlined by the paragraph-level tag that encloses it.

**What I did not do.** I added no provision no answer reached. §7 item 98 was not asked and is not enacted. The three drafting choices above are repairs to words the answers put in, and each is recorded here with its ground rather than left to be found.

Seven are carded as **§7 items 114 to 121**; **S-7 is the upgraded ground for the existing item 103**, which the review calls *necessary, not optional*. **Item 105 closes** — the enacted arrears formula stands and its residual defect is item 116. **Items 103 and 104 stay open**, 104 with its candidate text conformed to the record version.

**c. The most serious finding is against this record's own technique, and it is right.** **S-1:** the settlement bar has two limbs, and store revision 52 disapplied both — *only inside the two sentences it wrote them in*. **A member whose purchase is reduced on a D 6 recertification has had her reservation released in accordance with D 7; if she then dies before retiring, no rescission is involved, edit 2 never reaches her, and on the bar's face the subsidy is never settled.** Subsection N never pays the trust, the reservation stays charged against the $3,000,000 limit permanently, and J 1 limb (a) is false forever. **That is the fatal item 89 cured, reached through a different door by a modal fact pattern.** The fix is to amend the bar **once** rather than bolt a *notwithstanding* to each new rescission route. **It settles subsidies the bar on its face refuses, so it spends money: carded as item 114 and enacted nowhere.**

**d. The fiscal claim is corrected, and the correction is against this record.** *"Edits 1 to 7 admit nobody"* is **sound and was verified independently.** *"No priced quantity moves"* is **withdrawn in that form.** The engine's load-bearing assumption is its G 4 exposure window — *"exactly election-to-required-retirement"*, with *"the cost per event … NOT priced"* — and edits 1, 2, 3 and 6 open settlement routes that run past required retirement with **no statutory outer limit**. Two tail years add **0.1291 expected deaths, +127 percent of the entire priced death exposure**, and the limb that moves most, **disability, is carried by no decrement in the model at all.** **The only statement authorised from here:** *no admission quantity moves; the settlement count moves upward by an amount the current engine cannot value.* **Nothing in §3, `model-s8-s9` or the [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85) reprice is re-run by this revision, and §3's item-99 quantification list is recorded as already incomplete** — it omits the refunds and the arrears this revision repairs.

**e. One finding moved on re-verification.** The review treats M-1 as one defect; the adverse-tax fallback immediately after it carries the same defect in a second sentence, and that sentence is **word-identical to the death branch's own**, so it is addressable only with the trailing words of the next sentence. M-1 is enacted as **two** substitutions, and the death branch's own copy is **carded at item 120(b), not amended**, because it is pre-existing text no answer reached.

**f. Two findings are not enacted and the reasons are on the face of the record.** **M-9** — edit 5's clock has no fallback where the Board never determines — is **held to item 103**, because the fallback cannot be drafted until the Director decides what period the Board is under; drafting it now would invent a period or point at one that does not exist. **m-5** needs no edit: *"limited to that rescission and its consequences"* **is** determinate enough to discharge, so the offered tightening is declined rather than carded.

**g. Housekeeping — the rotation, and it restores §0.1's own retention rule.** This file arrived with **4,166 characters of headroom**, because store revision 56 landed under this one while it was being cut. §0.1 provides that §5 and §6 carry **the live revision's** record and that the rest sits in the retained-record document; three live sets apiece was the drift. **Moved verbatim** to [`bill-text-s8-record-s0-s5-s6-rev2-51`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-record-s0-s5-s6-rev2-51), each replaced by a stub restating its durable result: **store revision 54's §0.0-54, §5.33 and §6.0-54; store revision 55's §0.0-55, §5.34 and §6.0-55; and store revision 56's §5.35 and §6.0-56.** Every one of those designators still resolves. **§5 and §6 now carry this revision alone, which is what §0.1 requires**, and the §0 narrative for store revision 56 stays in the file. **Nothing is summarised away and no bill text moved.** This revision closed at **567 characters of headroom**; a concurrent run has since moved further record out and the file now stands well clear of the ceiling. **§7 item 102 remains the live constraint on every revision from here, and this revision did not relieve it.**

**h. Not publishable.** The six new strings have had **no counsel pass of their own**; that is the next review and it is commissioned, not assumed. **Publication is blocked on items 108, 109, 110 and 111**, which pass 17 names as the four it would not publish without.

### 0.0-56 Store revision 56 — [MOO-153](/MOO/issues/MOO-153)'s counsel pass dispositioned: one edit to the bill text, six new §7 items, and S-1 corrected as to the fact and accepted as to the process defect, which is mine

**One operative edit, +6 characters, no figure moves.** m-1: subsection C's fifth sentence now reads *"...determine, no later than 30 days after the member's application is completed, that no amount is specified in that clause and **shall** state that determination in the certification required by subsection D."* The second `shall` forecloses the mis-parse counsel identified — a reader can otherwise begin to take *"and state that determination"* as a conjunct inside the that-clause and must recover. Sentence 2 of the same subsection already solves it the same way. **I did not take counsel's comma removal**: the commas separate the adverbial from the that-clause and the second `shall` does the whole of the work.

**Nothing else in §1 is changed, by design.** Counsel's S-2, S-3, M-1, M-2 and m-2 each need a provision that was never agreed, or reverse a choice the Policy Director's own direction made. Each is drafted verbatim, with options and a recommendation, in a new §7 item — **108** (S-2's two clocks), **109** (M-1), **110** (S-3's § 2.2-4021 B carve-out), **111** (M-2's bar-side fix), **112** (M-4's publication posture), **113** (m-2) — and none is in the bill.

**S-1 — *"store revision 53 never landed"* — is false as to the fact, right as to the process, and the process defect is mine.** Store revision 53 is **document revision 63** (`2af78c15`, 481,320 characters, 12:27:41.196Z) and **revision 64** (`917b16d1`, 481,317 characters, 12:28:13.953Z); all five edits are present from revision 63 and survive in the head. **[MOO-153](/MOO/issues/MOO-153) was created at 12:24:46 — ten seconds after document revision 62 (`495176e8`, 455,726 characters, 12:24:36.976Z) and three minutes before my write.** Counsel read the true head as it stood when it woke, and the anchor comment the brief told it to confirm against did not exist because I posted it at 12:31:34, after it had read. Its one wrong inference — that the four strings *"appear in no revision at any time"* — is wrong only because they were written three minutes after it looked. **I commissioned a counsel pass on a revision I had not yet applied.** Three rules, adopted here: the counsel issue is created only after the `PUT` returns; the revision id and character count go in that issue's **description** at creation and never in a comment; and this document's store-revision label moves in the same write as the body, with the revision id, character count and edit list in `changeSummary` — null on all 67 earlier revisions, which is why counsel had to date the file by content-tracing.

**The full record is the companion document** [`moo153-counsel-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-145#document-moo153-counsel-disposition): all nine findings and their disposition, the four-decision case-law table behind item 88, the drafted text for items 108 to 113, and the sweep. **This file arrived at 11,144 characters of headroom, so what is here is short by design.**

### §5.36 Store revision 57 — the six substitutions, chased in both directions

**Performed in full in the companion record** — [`moo152-pass17-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-moo152-pass17-disposition) §5 — which carries the outward table (**subsection E**, 9 citations; **subdivision D 7**, 9, six of them *"in accordance with subdivision D 7"*; **subsection F**; **subsection M**, 28; **subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2**, 15) and the inward check on every provision that reads the four amended.

**Result: no conforming amendment is required outside the four provisions amended, and none is made.** One conforming change **inside** them was required — R2's anchor had to carry the trailing words of the following sentence, because the adverse-tax fallback it repairs is word-identical to the death branch's own.

**Two inward findings worth keeping in the live file.** **Subsection E is not amended**, so its 9 inward readers do not move: R5 disapplies E's deeming bar from inside G 3, in E's own words, and only for a rescinded subdivision 3 determination — **E's separate crediting bar is untouched and its exception still names only death (§7 item 120(a))**. And **R4 was positioned to preserve the one ordinal reference in the chain**: the sentence after the arrears sentence opens *"A certified subsidy settled as required by the preceding sentence…"*, so the new fallbacks sit **after** it and identify their subject descriptively.

**The two definitions are untouched by this revision. No admission test, no clause (v) to (viii) determination and no subsection C clause (ii) cap changes.**

### §6.0-57 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 57

**All eight points are in the companion record** — [`moo152-pass17-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-moo152-pass17-disposition) §6. The four that change what a reader sees:

1. **Three wordings are mine and not the review's.** **R6 is narrower than the form offered** — two named allowances in both directions, not *"any other allowance payable to the member under this chapter"*, which would authorise offsets between allowance types the Director never reached. **R5 is drafted from inside G 3** rather than by amending subsection E, which is the smaller footprint and keeps the whole rule in the sentence a reader of G 3 is already in. **R4's new sentences identify their subject descriptively** and are positioned after the settlement sentence rather than after the arrears sentence they serve, because inserting them there would have moved an existing *"preceding sentence"* antecedent onto new text and un-settled the subsidy.
2. **"May" creates a power.** R6 converts *"[n]othing … prevents the Board from applying"* into *"the Board may apply"*. A sentence that only removes a bar leaves the Board without the power the sentence assumes, and no affirmative recoupment power is cited anywhere in the section. The scope is identical, so this is drafting — but it changes the operative verb and is recorded for that reason.
3. **I did not fix S-1 silently**, though it is the one repair pass 17 says this record missed and it is correct that it was missed. It amends the settlement bar itself and settles subsidies the bar on its face refuses. That is a money consequence and the Director's to take: **item 114**.
4. **One correction to this record's own authority.** §6.0-52 item 4 and §7 item 105 cite **subsection F** as the bar on recovering an arrears overpayment. F's limb is tied to *"that account"* — the failure to retire in a qualifying retirement — and an overpayment does not arise on that account. **The operative bar is G 4's own no-collection sentence, which is wider.** The conclusion is unaffected and stronger; it is why item 116 matters.

### §5.37 Store revision 58 — the eight substitutions, chased in both directions

**Performed by mechanical count over §1 alone** — not over the whole document, because §2, §6 and §7 quote the operative text and would inflate every figure. **The full table, every count before → after, is at** [`moo154-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-97#document-moo154-disposition) **§5.** The results that have to be stated here:

- **`§ 51.1-165.01` 5 → 7, and that is the fatal cure.** Both new citations are of subsection **F**: one in (f)'s notwithstanding, one in the certification. The section was cited five times in the act and its subsection F had never been read.
- **`§ 51.1-165` bare 5 → 7; `§ 51.1-162` 6 → 9; `§ 51.1-163` 1 → 2** (still named only to say it does not apply); **`§ 65.2-100` 1 → 2**, which is first use **in § 51.1-142.4** and so carries the full citation on the Code's per-section convention, the existing occurrence being in subsection E of § 51.1-142.2.
- **`in the writing required by this subdivision` 1 → 0.** The coined label is gone; the writing is called what the sentence of subdivision D 1 beginning *"The Board's certification shall state the matters required by subdivision B 4 c"* already calls it, *"The Board's certification."* **(Corrected in store revision 59: that sentence was D 1's third and is now its fourth, store revision 59 having inserted a new third sentence under §7 item 108. The ordinal is removed rather than renumbered.)**
- **Subdivision M 2's class list: 5 classes → 6, in both occurrences** — the reconsideration limb and the Article 5 savings clause, as store revisions 54 and 55 each did. **(Store revision 59 replaces the Article 5 savings clause with §7 item 88 option (d). The six-class list is carried into the replacement rather than dropped — the drafted option named four classes — and that is §6.0-59 ambiguity 1.)** The new class is defined by the act's own notice duties, so it moves with them and needs no definition.
- **Two new reporting duties and no amendment to subsection J**, in the form J 1's closing words already accept (*"every other matter this section requires the Board to state in the report"*). Re-verified rather than carried, because J 1 was itself amended by store revision 55.
- **Subdivisions D 2, D 3, D 7 and subsection N: untouched.** No edit here releases, reserves, settles or pays anything. **Subsection E: untouched, and that is F5.**

**Two counts in this sweep were predicted and then re-counted on the written body; the figures above are the re-counted ones.** The prediction was `§ 51.1-165` bare → 6 and `§ 51.1-162` → 11; the truth is 7 and 9, because three of the new references say *"that section"* rather than repeating the citation and because the C 2 preservation sentence names § 51.1-165 twice. **A predicted count is not a count.**

**Conforming amendments elsewhere in the Code: none.** Outward: of the five sections cited, **two now have their operation altered** — § 51.1-165, by a notwithstanding confined to subdivision C 1, and **§ 51.1-165.01, by one confined to so much of subsection F as requires payment under § 51.1-163**. Neither is amended; the device is the one the Code uses in **§ 51.1-153 C**. Inward: nothing outside the act cross-references new § 51.1-142.4, because it does not yet exist.

**§5.33's own assertion is corrected and not carried forward.** It read *"§ 51.1-165 is the only one whose operation the act alters."* That was false when written, and F1 is the finding that caught it. **The citation count is not the check; reading the cited section is.**

**One thing the sweep cannot close, and it travels to DLS.** A *"notwithstanding"* in a new section is the smaller footprint and it is **invisible to a reader of the displaced section** — now two sections, not one. **It must appear in the drafting request to Division of Legislative Services and in the memo's risk section; a drafter's note is not enacted.**

### §6.0-58 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 58

Nine. **All nine in full at** [`moo154-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-97#document-moo154-disposition) **§6. No policy was chosen by drafting choice.** The five that a later reader must not undo — three departures from a reviewer's fix direction and two corrections against me — are these.

**1. F1's notwithstanding names *"so much of subsection F of § 51.1-165.01 as requires benefits to be paid in accordance with § 51.1-163,"* not the subsection.** Subsection F does two things: it routes the death to § 51.1-163, and it provides that *"the requirement that the member be in service shall not apply."* The second limb is the member's friend and is the Code's own authority for F2's cure. **The reviewer's fix direction named the subsection; the enacted words name the limb.**

**2. Subdivision C 2 of § 51.1-165 is preserved, not displaced, and this is the judgment to attack first.** C 2 is a saving provision paying the **greater** of § 51.1-163 and § 51.1-162 B to a spouse, minor child or parent named under a joint and last-survivor option. Displacing it — which the fix direction proposed — would take an existing right from a named class to make the act tidier. A second sentence paying the greater of the two resolves the conflict and leaves no member worse off than under present law. **The displacement alternative is at §7 item 122, one substitution away.**

**3. F13(b) does not hold on the live body, and the reason is store revision 55.** The review read store revision 54 and reported that a late crediting is unreviewable because *"crediting service credit is neither a determination nor a notice."* Subdivision M 2's second sentence — added by store revision 55 out of [MOO-130](/MOO/issues/MOO-130)'s M1 — now deems *"crediting of service credit"* a determination *"for the purposes of this subsection,"* and M 2's first limb reaches *"a failure of the Board to make a determination … within a period required by this section."* **The review path already exists and no words were written for it.** F13(a) and (d) are enacted; (b) is a null.

**4. F7's premise was mine and it was wrong.** The issue reasoned that D 1's day-for-day extension carried the consequence of an incomplete certification because *"an incomplete statement is a late statement."* That extension attaches to *"that written statement"* — the statement of qualifying retirement dates required by the definition in subsection A — and the certification is a different writing. **The duty had no consequence at all.** What is enacted is procedural and the section's own: a determination for subsection M, and a line in the subsection J report.

**5. The certification is not given a new verb.** the sentence of subdivision D 1 beginning *"The Board's certification shall state the matters required by…"* already reads that way **(store revision 59 corrects the ordinal this sentence carried: that sentence was D 1's third and is now its fourth)**, so the opener is *"The Board's certification shall also state"* — same actor, same formula, one clause shorter than the fix direction's. **Where the surrounding statute has a form, it beats the better sentence.**

**The other four, in one line each.** **(6)** F6(c) is cured by **stating** § 51.1-162 C rather than deleting *"in every other case"*, because a member about to file can act on it — and it is the one case in which the purchased credit cannot change the benefit at all, which is a fiscal fact and is routed. **(7)** F11 is cured in the **addressee** only (*"each person entitled"*); its release half and F10's asymmetry are one drafted answer at §7 item 122 and are not enacted, because widening a release widens what the Commonwealth pays under subsection N. **(8)** F8's and F13(d)'s cure runs the notice period from *"the earlier of"* crediting and the last day crediting was required, so a Board that credits late cannot extend its own notice period — **a floor, never a setter.** **(9)** F12 is cured by making the Board's statement conditional, not by inventing a period; fixing one would be a determination with no standard in the act, and it is drafted as an answer instead.

title: SUPERSEDED — created in error in store revision 46; use bill-text-s8-revision-history-2
body:
# SUPERSEDED — do not rely on this document. Use `bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`.

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional**

**This document was created in error and is empty of unique content.** While drafting store revision 46 I read `bill-text-s8` at document revision 47, found it at **23 characters** of headroom, and created this document to hold the sections I was about to move out of it. Before my write landed, two concurrent heartbeats of mine landed store revisions 43 and 44, and **the move I was preparing had already been made, into a document that already existed under a different key**: [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2). Nothing in `bill-text-s8` ever pointed here.

**Every section this document briefly held is in [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2), verbatim** — the §0 narrative for store revisions 38, 39 and 40, §0.1, §5.20 to §5.23, and §6.0-26, §6.0-35, §6.0-36, §6.0-38, §6.0-39 and §6.0-40. **No text was lost and none was altered by the mistake**, and revision 1 of this document remains in the store if anyone needs to check that.

**Why it is emptied rather than left in place.** A 67,000-character duplicate of sections that are also held, and are being actively annotated, in another document is a trap: a reader who finds this one first gets a copy that stops receiving corrections. The corrections made in store revision 46 — pass 14's **M-1** against the direction-of-effect claim in the §0 narrative for store revision 41, and pass 14's **S-2** against the narrow form of §7 item 35's protection rule quoted in §6.0-38 item 4 — were made in `bill-text-s8-revision-history-2` and were **not** made in the copy this document held.

**Record of the error, because it is mine.** The cause was reading a 524,000-character document at one revision and writing at another, which is the same condition that produced pass 14's **S-1**. Full record: [`moo123-pass14-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-87#document-moo123-pass14-disposition) §3.

**Pre-decisional and internal.**

## 0.0000000000 Revision 12 — the five live findings that were mine, drafted

Revision 11 named five live pass-4 findings as mine and said each needed either a decision or more
care than a same-session fix allowed. **Four needed care and have now had it. The fifth (S7) needs a
decision and is not drafted** — it is item 20 of §7. Nothing in this revision changes a priced
quantity, and nothing in it chooses a policy that was not already agreed.

### a. F3 — the § 51.1-153 notice, closed, and closed without choosing the numeral

**The defect.** D 1 required the member to file the § 51.1-153 notice *"no later than 30 days before
the effective date of retirement so stated."* The effective date is the member's earliest qualifying
retirement date or a date within the window after it, and the earliest qualifying retirement date is
not knowable until the credit posts. At the zero rung the 30-day deadline has therefore already
expired on the day the date becomes determinable. Pass 4 called it fatal and it was mine, introduced
in revision 3 while curing a different impossibility.

**Why it does not need the numeral after all.** I said in revision 11 that the fix and the window
numeral were one question. **That was wrong, and I would rather correct it than let a fatal finding
sit on a card waiting for an answer it does not need.** § 51.1-153 A requires only *"written
notification to the Board setting forth the date the retirement is to become effective"* and fixes no
advance period at all; the only timing limit in the section is subsection E — *"The effective date of
retirement shall be after the last day of service of the member, but shall not be more than 90 days
prior to the filing of the notice of retirement"* — which is a limit on **retroactivity**, not on how
late a notice may be filed. Both were retrieved from the official section text on 11 October 2026.
So a notice filed after the effective date is good for up to 90 days, and the deadline can be written
against **the Board's own statement of the window** instead of against the retirement date:

> The member shall file the notice of retirement required by § 51.1-153 … **no later than the later of
> (i) 30 days before the effective date of retirement so stated and (ii) 30 days after the date on
> which the Board gives the member the written statement required by the definition of "final
> qualifying retirement date" in subsection A.** A notice filed within the period allowed by clause
> (ii) satisfies § 51.1-153 notwithstanding that it is filed fewer than 30 days before, or after, the
> effective date of retirement stated in it; and where such a notice is filed after that effective
> date, the member's retirement shall take effect on that date and the retirement allowance shall be
> payable retroactively to that date, subject to the limitation in subsection E of § 51.1-153.

The Board's statement is itself due within 15 days of crediting, so clause (ii) always gives the
member a real period, and it gives the same period at every rung on the ladder. **The 30 days in
clause (ii) is my choice**, picked to match clause (i) and the section's other 30-day periods.

### b. The defect I found while drafting F3, which no review has raised

§ 51.1-153 E does not only cap retroactivity. It also requires that the effective date of retirement
be **after the last day of service of the member**. At a short window that is a trap the notice fix
does not reach: the member must stop working before a date they cannot yet identify, because the
earliest qualifying retirement date depends on the month in which the Board credits the service, and
subsection E gave the Board any day within 30 days of payment in full. A member who resigns effective
the end of month M and whose credit posts in month M + 1 has left service a month early, and may no
longer be a member in service at all.

The cure is to let the member fix the crediting date, which costs nothing and moves no date in the
pricing:

> The member may request in writing, before or together with the final payment, that the Board credit
> the service credit **as of the last day of a month stated in the request** that is not later than 30
> days after receipt of payment in full; the Board shall credit the service credit as of the date so
> stated if payment in full is received before that date, and in every case shall give the member
> written notice of the date as of which it credits the service credit no later than five days after
> it credits it.

The earliest qualifying retirement date is then the next day, the member's last day of service is the
day before it, and § 51.1-153 E is satisfied on its own terms. **The definition of "earliest
qualifying retirement date" is untouched, so no priced quantity moves.** The alternative — pushing
the earliest date out a month — would have been a cleaner sentence and a repricing, which is not mine
to do.

### c. S1 — the money flow now closes on death, disability and Board error

G 4 vested the credit at the pilot price in those three cases and **G 1 was the only settlement
trigger**, keyed to *"the member's effective date of retirement in a qualifying retirement."* So
nothing settled, subsection N never paid, and the trust bore the subsidy with no appropriation behind
it. Adopting Alternative A made that sharper, not softer. G 4 now carries its own trigger:

> The certified subsidy for an election to which this subdivision applies is settled, and subsection N
> applies to that settlement as it applies to a settlement under subdivision 1, on the earliest of (a)
> the date of the member's death, (b) the effective date of a disability retirement allowance approved
> for the member, and (c) the member's effective date of retirement.

The opening words — *"and that is not settled under subdivision 1"* — are there because the
involuntary-separation member who retires inside the 90 days satisfies **both** triggers on the same
date for the same amount, and two settlement provisions for one event is an ambiguity even when they
produce the same number. Subdivision 1 governs where it applies; G 4 catches what it does not reach.

The second sentence runs the same lesser-of redetermination as G 1 against that date and releases the
difference and the contingency; the third repeats G 1's no-debt guarantee and extends it to survivors
and beneficiaries, because a provision that recomputes a number after a death is exactly where the
no-post-purchase-debt directive would be lost. **Clause (c) is the Board-error case and it deliberately
accepts any retirement, qualifying or not** — a member defeated by the Board's own error should not
also have to hit the window.

Four conforming edits follow, and each one was a live stranding: **D 2** ("shall not be released,
except to the extent required by subdivision G 1 **or G 4**"); **D 7**, which would otherwise have
released the reservation of a member who died, because a dead member does not retire as subsection F
requires; **J 1**, whose reporting tail ended at *"settled under subdivision G 1"*; and **subsection
N** itself, which pays only *"upon the settlement of a certified subsidy under subdivision G 1."*
**Subsection H** picks up G 4 for the same reason, and **D 3** does so twice — it governed both the
release of the contingency amount and the life of the reservation itself, so without the edit a G 4
settlement would have left the contingency reserved and the reservation running forever. **Six
conforming edits in all, and the cross-reference sweep in §5.6 is what found the last two**; a
settlement trigger added in one subdivision strands every provision that names the old one, which is
the whole argument for running the sweep on a corrective revision and not only on a structural one.

### d. S12 — the processing extension gets a standard, a member right, a deadline and review

It read *"the Board **may** approve a later date"* on the Board's own motion, with no application, no
criterion, no deadline and no review — and because both dates had to be stated within 15 days of
crediting, there was no route at all for a processing problem that arose later. Now: the Board
**shall** approve a later date where its own processing requirements *"or any other cause not
attributable to the member"* make retirement by the deadline impracticable; the member may request it
in writing **at any time before** the date that would otherwise apply; the Board must act within 30
days, give reasons, and the member may seek review under subsection M; and a later date approved after
the 15-day statement must be notified within 15 days. **The three-month outer limit is unchanged and
is still my choice** (§7). The operative verb changed from *may* to *shall*, which is the finding.

### e. M6's D 3 limb — the lapse is reported and the filing date survives

D 3 gave the Director of the Department of Planning and Budget 30 days to confirm that funds are
legally available and provided no consequence, so a member could wait indefinitely in a queue that
never moved. **A deeming rule would fix it and a deeming rule is a policy choice about appropriations
control, so I have not written one.** Instead the lapse becomes visible and the member's place is
protected: the Board must notify the member and the money-committee chairmen within 15 days of the
lapse and report every lapse under subsection J, the application retains its filing date for
subdivisions 4 and 5, and the Board must act within 15 days of the confirmation when it arrives.
**If the Director wants a deeming rule, it is one sentence and it goes here.**

### f. M7 — a § 415 bar no longer strands the member

B 4 f forbade the Board to accept a payment breaching § 415(n)(3); the member then could not complete
payment by the completion date, D 7 released the reservation, and a lawful bar is not Board *error*
under G 4 (iii), so **the member lost the election and the price through nobody's fault.** Pass 4
offered two fixes and I have taken the second, because the first — adding the § 415 bar to G 4's
vesting list — pays a subsidy to a member who never paid the price. On notice of the determination
within 30 days, the member may (i) reduce the purchase to the largest amount the Board may lawfully
accept, (ii) **defer the barred amount to the earliest limitation year in which the Board may accept
it**, or (iii) cancel under G 5; clause (ii) extends the completion date, requires recertification
under D 6, and D 7 is amended so the reservation survives. The determination is expressly **not**
Board error, and it is reviewable under subsection M.

Two drafting consequences worth naming. **"Limitation year" is new and is now defined** in B 4 a, by
reference to § 415 and the regulations, because it is the unit the annual limit actually runs on and
an undefined term in a federal-tax interface invites exactly the wrong argument. And **the 12-month
extension cap in clause (ii) is my choice** — long enough to reach the next limitation year, short
enough that a deferral cannot become an indefinite hold on a reservation.

### g. What revision 12 does not do

**S7 is not drafted, and it should not be.** G 1's lesser-of is a one-way ratchet — the trust absorbs
every overrun and the general fund keeps every saving — which pass 4 reads against art. X, § 11's
*"solely in the interests of the members."* The honest answer is a two-way true-up, and that costs the
appropriation its certainty, which is a trade the Director makes and not me. It is **§7 item 20**, with
both texts drafted there. **F4, S5 and S11 are on the pending card** and none of them is a drafting
question. No priced figure moves in this revision, and `[12]` and the authorised figure set are
exactly where revision 11 left them.

### F-1 — the defect, stated in drafting terms

The two definitions are **not the same kind of test**, and that is the thing word-identity hides
rather than fixes. The review is right about this and I was wrong in §5.5:

- *"Unreduced retirement eligibility date"* is **modal** — *"the earliest date on which the member
  **may** retire … and receive"* an A 1 allowance unreduced by A 2 or A 3. It asks what is available
  to the member. A payment-form election cannot move it, because the member may always take the basic
  form.
- *"Qualifying retirement"* is **actual** — *"a service retirement … **the allowance for which is**
  calculated in accordance with subdivision A 1."* It asks what the member was actually paid.

So a member who elects the joint and last-survivor option under § 51.1-165, or the partial lump sum
under § 51.1-165.01, receives *"the actuarial equivalent of the retirement allowance otherwise
payable to him."* On the literal reading — **the same literal reading that produced revision 7**, that
*"not reduced under A 2 or A 3"* admitted an A 5 computation — that allowance is calculated in
accordance with § 51.1-165, not subdivision A 1. She passes the admission test and fails the
settlement test. **Identical words, different cohorts.** Word-identity is not the property that
prevents the divergence; identity of the **object tested** is, and the two objects differ by design.

I record that the better construction probably saves the text anyway — A 1 supplies the formula from
which the equivalent is taken, so the allowance *is* calculated in accordance with A 1 and then
converted as to form. But the Lab cannot hold that construction and its own A 5 construction at the
same time, and revision 7 exists because the Lab chose the literal one. That is why I would fix it
rather than argue it.

**The § 51.1-165.01 case is the one I would put in front of the Director first, because the bill's own
window creates it.** The partial lump sum requires creditable service performed *after* the member
first became eligible for an unreduced service retirement allowance. A pilot member becomes
unreduced-eligible at her earliest qualifying retirement date and her final qualifying retirement
date is `[12]` months later — so she becomes lump-sum eligible **as subsection F's deadline falls**,
and taking it may defeat the very retirement F requires her to make. And clause (i) of *"certified
subsidy"* prices *"the benefits payable under this chapter to the member **and to the member's
survivors and beneficiaries**."* The bill prices survivor coverage and then may refuse the member who
elects it.

### The four things revision 3 changes

**1. The retirement deadline is one bracketed numeral, and the window is a real window.**
"Qualifying retirement" is now bounded by two new defined terms — **"earliest qualifying retirement
date"** (unchanged from revision 2's single date: the first of the month after the credit posts) and
**"final qualifying retirement date"** (the first day of the month that is **`[12]`** months after
it). Setting the bracket to `[0]` reproduces revision 2 exactly, because "the first day of the month
that is 0 months after" the earliest date *is* the earliest date; `[6]`, `[12]`, `[18]` and `[24]`
all read correctly on the same words. **The ladder MOO-48 is pricing is a one-numeral edit in one
definition, and nothing else in the bill carries a month count that has to move with it.**

**2. A longer window does not reopen Pathway A, and this is the single most important thing in
revision 3.** The foreclosure lives in clause (vi) of "eligible member," which tests whether the
member *reaches unreduced eligibility* by the time the credit is **credited** — not when the member
retires. `[revision 16: that clause is now clause (vii), and a second, stricter leg at the application
date sits in front of it as clause (vi). The foreclosure is strengthened, not changed —` §0.00000000000d`.]` The window governs retirement; clause (vi) governs admission. They are different dates and
revision 3 keeps them apart deliberately. A 24-month window therefore admits exactly the same
members as a 0-month window. The broad reading MOO-49 is testing is not reachable through the
deadline dial.

**3. A window makes the certified subsidy indeterminate unless the valuation date is named, so
revision 3 names it — and adds a true-up at settlement.** With one retirement date the actuary had
one state of the world to value. With a window the member's retirement date is unknown at
certification, and the certified subsidy is the quantity the $3,000,000 and the per-member ceiling
both bite on. Revision 3 resolves it in two moves: **reserve on the dearest assumption** (prong (i)
is valued on the member's *anticipated earliest* qualifying retirement date, which is derivable from
the completion date already in the certification), and **settle on the fact** (new second and third
sentences of G 1 require the Board to redetermine the certified subsidy as of the member's actual
effective date of retirement, capped at the amount reserved, and to release the difference for other
elections). This is the only construction I could find that keeps the cap determinate at admission
without making a long window *look* expensive when it is cheap. It also does fiscal work nobody
asked for: in the zero-acceleration case MOO-53 is running — a member who would have reached
eligibility anyway before retiring — the redetermined subsidy collapses toward the floor, and the
Commonwealth pays the price discount rather than an acceleration that did not happen.

discriminator is that A 1 clause, and B 4 a already uses it to carry the two published normal cost
rates (12.50 and 10.74 percent). So the statute now says in terms that both tiers are in, which is
MOO-46 item 6, without importing a non-statutory vocabulary. The hybrid exclusion in clause (iii)
stands.

### Three structural consequences of a longer window that revision 3 had to fix

MOO-46's reading — *"G 2 already handles non-retirement cleanly, which is why a longer deadline looks
cheap to me"* — is right about G 2. G 2 needed no change. But three other provisions were written
against a single retirement date and break silently at any window above zero:

1. **D 1's notice of retirement was impossible even at zero months.** Revision 2 required the member
   to *"file the notice of retirement required by § 51.1-153 at the time the Board accepts the
   election."* I retrieved § 51.1-153: subsection A requires the notice to set forth **"the date the
   retirement is to become effective,"** and subsection E provides that the effective date **"shall
   be after the last day of service of the member, but shall not be more than 90 days prior to the
   filing of the notice of retirement."** At acceptance the member cannot state that date — it
   depends on when the Board credits the service, up to 12 months plus 30 days later. So revision 2
   demanded a notice the member could not validly complete, **and that is a defect at a 0-month
   window too, not one the window created.** Revision 3 splits it: a written acknowledgment of
   obligations at acceptance, and the § 51.1-153 notice no later than 30 days before the effective
   date the member selects.
2. **D 3's reservation lapsed before the member could retire.** Revision 2 provided that a
   reservation does not survive past the end of the fiscal year following the year it was made
   without a fresh DPB confirmation. At a 24-month window plus a 12-month payment period, settlement
   can fall three fiscal years out, so an accepted member's reservation could lapse through nobody's
   fault. Revision 3 keeps the annual DPB confirmation as a **control on new admissions** — the Board
   accepts no further election until it is obtained — but provides that the failure to obtain it does
   not release a reservation or affect an accepted election. The member has already paid.
3. **K 1's reporting tail ran out before the last determination.** "Three years following its
   expiration" ends 1 December 2036; at a 24-month window the last G 2 determinations land in January
   2037. K 1 now runs until the first December 1 after the last election has been settled, cancelled
   or determined. One clause, and it makes the tail window-proof at any numeral.
