## 0.000000000000 Revision 17 — clause (vi) is bounded by what the member can actually buy

**Revision 17 adds one sentence to the definition of "eligible member" and changes nothing else in
the bill.** It answers revision 16's **own** reviewer question 2 — *"can clause (vi) and clause (vii)
now select different members?"* — which revision 16 stated as an argument rather than a certification
and expressly invited someone to break. **They can, and the sentence closes it.**

### a. The break

Revision 16's clause (vi) tests the member against *"the service credit the member applies to
purchase under that application"*. **Nothing bounded that amount.** Clause (vii) tests the member
against the service credit actually **purchased**, which is bounded three ways: by the member's real
entitlement under subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2, by clause (i) of subsection C (four years, less
prior purchases) and by clause (iii) of subsection C (the member's years of state service). Those
three bounds operate on clause (vii) and did not operate on clause (vi).

So a member could be admitted on an amount he could never buy, pay, be credited less, and **fail at
crediting** — the "admitted and then stranded" failure mode §0.00000000000e says it closed. It closed
it on the C (ii) side and left it open on the entitlement side.

**Worked example.** A member 36 months short of his unreduced retirement eligibility date who has
**12** months of qualifying active duty service. He applies to purchase 36 months. Clause (vi) is
satisfied on its face: 36 months credited on the application date closes a 36-month gap. Subsection C
then limits the purchase to the 12 months he actually has. At crediting he is 12 months bought plus
whatever he has earned — on a one-month completion date, 13 of the 36 months he needed. **Clause (vii)
fails.** He has paid, and subdivision G 3 re-values his money at ordinary prices.

**And the count consequence, which is why this is not merely tidy.** The admission screen the
published figures rest on is a snapshot of members who *can* reach the unreduced date on the service
they *have*. A screen that runs on an unbounded applied-for number is wider than that snapshot — not
by the ~13 months of deferral the Director identified, but by over-application. Revision 16 made the
statute say what the model priced on one axis and left a second axis open. `[Note for`
[MOO-71](/MOO/issues/MOO-71)`: this axis is closed in the text as of revision 17, so the`
**`entitlement-bounded application-date snapshot`** `is the basis to count. It is the narrower of the
two and I believe it is the basis already modelled; it needs confirming, not re-running.]`

### b. Why it had to be said expressly, and why one sentence does two jobs

There is an argument that *"applies to purchase"* already implies *"lawfully applies"*, so subsection
C bounds it without being told to. **That argument is fatal to revision 16's own cure**, because if
subsection C bounds the assumed amount by implication then **clause (ii)** of subsection C bounds it
too — and §0.00000000000e demonstrates that clause (ii) empties the pilot. The implication cannot be
accepted for clauses (i) and (iii) and refused for clause (ii) by silence. **The text has to say which
parts of subsection C bound the assumed amount.** The new sentence names the two that do and excludes
the one that does not, in those words:

> <u>For the purposes of clause (vi), the amount of service credit assumed to be credited to the
> member shall not exceed the amount of service credit the member is then eligible to purchase under
> subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2 or the amounts that clauses (i) and (iii) of subsection C would
> then permit, and shall not be limited by clause (ii) of subsection C.</u>

Clauses (i) and (iii) are in because each is a true ceiling on what a member may **ever** buy. Clause
(ii) is out because it is the only one of the three that is a function of the completion date, which
is the whole of §0.00000000000e. **Revision 16's clause (vi) is left word for word as drafted**, so
the referent it chose — and the reviewer question it posed about that referent — are untouched.

### c. What this does and does not do

It **does** make clause (vi) an entitlement test rather than a self-declaration, make the two legs
incapable of selecting different members on the entitlement axis, and secure revision 16's C (ii)
cure against the implied-limit argument that would otherwise undo it. It **does not** change the
figure, the definition of "certified subsidy", the `[12]` numeral, the `[20]` percentage, clause (v),
clause (vii) or any other provision; it adds no citation that the bill does not already carry
(subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2 is cited in clause (iv) of the same definition, and subsection C is
cited throughout); and it strands no cross-reference, because the only provisions that cite a clause
of "eligible member" by number are inside the definition itself.

**Revision 16's reviewer question 1 is untouched and still open** — whether *"the service credit the
member applies to purchase under that application"* has exactly one referent where an application
states a range or is amended inside subdivision D 4's 60-day cure period. Revision 17 bounds the
amount; it does not identify it. That is still a question for pass 5.

### d. What the leg does to the admitted cohort, in drafting terms

Clause (v) and clause (vi) now bracket the member on **one date** — the date of the complete
application:

- **(v)** without the purchased credit, the member has **not** reached the unreduced date;
- **(vi)** with the credit the member applies for, deemed in hand on that same date, the member
  **has** reached it (allowing the one-month administrative roll that clause (vii) also allows).

So the admitted set is exactly *"members whom a purchase of four years or less carries over the
unreduced line as of the day they apply."* That is the **application-date snapshot**, and it is the
basis the priced record is built on: [MOO-48](/MOO/issues/MOO-48) runs the bill's cohort with
`PATHWAY_A_SCOPE = "immediate"`, which admits a member only where the purchasable credit brings the
months-to-unreduced-eligibility to zero **at the election month** — `18.9` participants central, the
`snapshot_participants` column of `out_moo48_addendum_window.csv`. Before revision 16 the text
admitted the `31.3` column instead. **The statute now says what the model priced**, which is the
whole content of the direction.

Three things about that match, so nobody has to re-derive them:

- **The one-month roll is not a leak.** Clause (vi) permits the unreduced date to fall on the first
  of the month after application; the model works in whole months. The slack is at most one month and
  it is the same administrative roll clause (vii) carries.
- **The leg costs an excluded member nothing permanent.** A member four months short today applies in
  four months. This is the Director's second reason and the text delivers it: nothing in the section
  limits the number of applications a member may file before one is accepted, and subsection H bars a
  second **election**, not a second application.
- **The 12-month payment window in subsection E is untouched**, as directed. The leg and the window
  now do different jobs on different dates and neither constrains the other.

### e. The C (ii) interaction the Director asked about. **There is one, and it is real.**

The Director asked me to check "that C(ii)'s quantity measurement (as of the completion date) does
not now contradict the application-date leg. If it does, say so." **On the Director's literal
wording it does, and it is not a small contradiction — it would have emptied the pilot.** Here is the
arithmetic.

Write **Q_app** for the months the member needs at the application date and **Q_comp** for the months
the member needs at the completion date. Subsection C (ii) caps the purchase at Q_comp, measured "as
of the completion date stated in the Board's certification … and taking account of the membership
service the member will have earned by that date." The completion date is up to 12 months after
acceptance, so the member earns service in between and **Q_comp ≤ Q_app for every member**, strictly
smaller for any member who takes any time at all to pay.

Now read the Director's words — "determined **with the service credit to be purchased** and as though
that service credit were credited on the date the member files a complete application". Everywhere
else in this section, "the service credit to be purchased" is the **certified** quantity: all ten of
its other uses sit in B 4, in "certified subsidy", or in D 1, D 6 and D 7, and every one of them
speaks after the Board has certified (§5.7). On that referent clause (vi) would test Q_app against
Q_comp and require **Q_comp ≥ Q_app**, which with Q_comp ≤ Q_app forces **Q_comp = Q_app** — no
service earned between application and completion, i.e. only a member who completes payment inside
the application month. **That admits essentially nobody**, and it would have done so quietly, because
each provision reads correctly on its own.

**The cure is in the leg, not in subsection C.** Clause (vi) now refers to *"the service credit the
member applies to purchase under that application"*, which is the only quantity that exists on the
date clause (vi) speaks about. Two phrases, because there are genuinely two quantities — the amount
applied for, which is what the admission test can see, and the amount to be purchased, which is what
the Board certifies and what every money provision consumes. With that referent:

- **(vi) admits** on the applied-for amount at the application date — the snapshot cohort;
- **C (ii) then trims** the purchase to the minimum necessary at the completion date;
- **(vii) re-tests** at crediting on the trimmed amount, and **passes by construction**, because
  Q_comp is defined as the months needed as of the completion date and crediting follows completion.

**No member is admitted and then stranded**, which was the failure mode worth checking. I did not
amend subsection C and it needs no amendment.

### g. Item 2, answered: **the defined term in subsection A yields the corrected measure.** CS_corrected.

The Director asked for a straight statement quoted from the drafted text, and the answer is that the
definition in subsection A **is** MOO-46 Decision 2(d)'s single-basis measure. **No change is needed
to the definition or to the figure, and I have changed neither.** The reason the question arises is a
real one — `CS_drafted` is a live column in the model — but it was computed against the **revision-1
and revision-2 era** definition, which no longer exists. `moo48_inputs.py` says so in terms, quoting
the definition it priced:

> *"§ 51.1-142.4 A, 'certified subsidy', as drafted: 'the full actuarial equivalent cost, determined
> under subdivision B 3 of § 51.1-142.2, of the service credit to be purchased, **PLUS** the actuarial
> cost to the retirement system of the earlier commencement of the retirement allowance that the
> Board determines will result from the election, **LESS** the amount payable by the member and by any
> employer under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2.'"*

That is an **additive two-term** formula, and the double count is the eligibility-acceleration term
that the § 51.1-142.2 B 3 actuarial-equivalent quote already contains and the second term then adds
again. **The current definition is not additive and contains neither term.** It is a single
difference of two present values. Mapped clause by clause onto the model's ledger:

| The drafted text, subsection A, "certified subsidy" | What it is |
|---|---|
| "**(i)** the actuarial present value, determined as of the valuation date …, of the benefits payable under this chapter to the member and to the member's survivors and beneficiaries, **taking account of the service credit to be purchased and of the member's retirement on the member's anticipated earliest qualifying retirement date**" | `PV(benefit \| the election)` — the with-election world, retirement at the earliest qualifying date |
| "exceeds **(ii)** the **expected value, taken over the distribution of the member's date of retirement projected as required by this definition**, of the actuarial present value … **without the service credit to be purchased**" | `PV(benefit \| VRS's own decrements, no election)` — and the projection sentence that follows names the method: "applying, as annual probabilities over the member's remaining working lifetime, the rates of retirement in those actuarial assumptions, together with the rates of mortality in those assumptions and no other decrement" |
| "**less (iii)** the amounts payable by the member and by any employer under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2" | `− member_payment − employer_payment` (and `employer_payment = 0` in S8 by construction) |

(i) − (ii) − (iii) is
`gross_liability_increase − member_payment − employer_payment`, and that string is the model's
**definition of `CS_corrected`** (`moo48_main.py` line 176, `moo48_inputs.py`
`CERTIFIED_SUBSIDY_BASIS`). The two are the same quantity, not two measures that happen to agree.

Three features of the current text make the identification tight rather than approximate, and each
was drafted to do exactly that:

- **There is no reference to subdivision B 3 anywhere in the definition** and no "actuarial
  equivalent cost" term. The B 3 quote — the component that carries the acceleration twice — is
  structurally absent. Its only appearance in the section is as the **floor**, below.
- **There is no additive early-commencement term.** The acceleration is inside the *difference*,
  because clause (i) values retirement on the earliest qualifying date and clause (ii) values
  retirement on VRS's own projected distribution. One counterfactual, measured once.
- **Clause (ii) expressly forbids the zero-acceleration construction** — "shall not be determined by
  reference to any date on which the member first becomes eligible for a service retirement
  allowance, whether reduced or unreduced" — which is what stops a reader collapsing (ii) back onto
  (i) and recovering the drafted measure by another route. That limb is revision 5's and it is
  load-bearing here.

**So the $170,000 ceiling operates on the measure it was chosen off.** The Director set it off
"that 90th percentile", the corrected p90 of **$160,468**, and the measure the Code text yields is
the corrected one. The ceiling is as intrusive as it was meant to be: `out_moo48_ceiling_sweep.csv`
at central take-up refuses **1.94** members at $160,000 and **0.62** at $175,000, so $170,000 sits
near the top of the distribution and refuses on the order of a member — the corrected p95 is
**$170,755** and the max **$208,905**. The five-times-more-intrusive case the Director was right to
test for **does not arise**. I have changed nothing, and nothing needs changing.

**One caveat on the measure, which is mine to flag and Fiscal's to screen.** The defined term is not
`CS_corrected` alone; it is **the greater of** `CS_corrected` and a **floor**: "The certified subsidy
shall not be less than the amount by which the standard cost of the service credit to be purchased …
exceeds the amounts payable by the member and by any employer under subdivision B 4 of
§ 51.1-142.2." For a member whose acceleration is small the floor is what the Board certifies, and
the refusal screen must be run on `max(CS_corrected, floor)`, not on `CS_corrected`. On the only
measurement of the floor in the record — [MOO-53](/MOO/issues/MOO-53)'s
`out_moo53_floor_binding.csv`, on the `CS_ledger_published` basis, which is the corrected basis — the
floor binds on **5.0 percent** of members and lifts the aggregate by **$8,891** on **$4.93M**, about
**0.18 percent**. It is very unlikely to carry anyone over $170,000, but it has not been measured on
MOO-48's own cohort and I am not going to assert that it does not. **That is the one thing the
addendum should confirm**, and it is a screen on an existing column, not a new driver.

rather than preventing it, and insisting on it is what left the payment-form sections untested:

### b. The three edits that change what the bill does

**1. A member whose election the Board itself cancelled could have her entire pension withheld — and
revision 24 created her.** This is pass 9's S-1 and it is the finding with the worst
headline-to-cost ratio in the package. G 2's bar stops *any* allowance to a member whose election *"has
not been settled"* until the Board makes a determination. Revision 24 added the exclusion for a member
credited under G 3 or G 5 — and revision 24 also added **D 6's to-zero branch**, which cancels an
election, refunds everything and releases the reservation. That member is credited with nothing under
G 3 or G 5, so the exclusion did not name her; she has no final qualifying retirement date, because that
date runs from the month the Board credits *all* the purchased credit and the Board never credits any;
and G 2's trigger therefore fires on clause (b) — the day she retires in a retirement that is not a
qualifying retirement, **which is every retirement available to her**. On the review's scenario a member
whose election the Board cancelled in 2030 retires in 2041 and the Board must withhold **every dollar**
of her allowance for up to four months to make a determination that reduces nothing and refunds nothing.
The second member in the class is the G 5 canceller credited with **zero**, whom *"has been credited with
service credit"* does not naturally describe. One clause reaches both, and the review confirmed — and I
re-checked — that it strands no determination the Board still needs: releases run through D 7's own
limbs, G 5 carries its own refund, and G 3's *"full or partial months"* valuation leaves no residue.

**2. The 30-day notice period and the 120-day backstop could command incompatible dates, and the
cheapest escape restored the defect pass 8 found.** Pass 9's S-3. Three constraints, two anchors: the
Board must *make* the determination within 60 days of the trigger; effect must be at least 30 days after
notice, at most 60 days after notice, and at most 120 days after the trigger — and **nothing said when
the notice must be given.** Notice after trigger + 90 makes the floor and the backstop inconsistent on
their face, and the member's whole first allowance payment waits on effect. The Board's cheapest path was
to treat the backstop as directory, which is the unbounded deferral pass 8's F-2 was about; the
member-adverse path was to cut her notice period to 14 days and destroy the response window the 30 days
exists to give her. The cure is a deadline for the **notice**, not a qualification of the backstop:
60 + 30 = 90 ≤ 120 in every case. **And the anchor itself was missing in one branch** — for a member who
was involuntarily separated, let the 90 days lapse and has not retired, the governing 60-day period is
in G 4 and not in G 2's first sentence, so *"the 60-day period in the first sentence of this
subdivision"* had no referent at all. The new defined term names both sources.

**3. The pilot's price could expire out from under a member mid-contract.** Pass 9's S-5, and it
re-creates pass 8's F-10 in a cleaner form. Enactment 3 expires *"the amendments made by this act to
subdivision B 2"* — which is the **second** sentence, the one routing the member's price to subdivision
4. Clause (i) then preserved *"the first sentence"*, which the act does not amend and which therefore
cannot expire: a null operation, with the sentence that actually does the work expired and unpreserved.
Meanwhile revision 24's new clause (iv) restored the concluding pricing paragraph *in its pre-act form* —
which has no *"Except as provided in subdivision 4"* carve-out — so a member still paying instalments
after 1 July 2033 faced two contrary commands: priced under B 4 by clause (i), priced at the **actuarial
equivalent cost** by the restored paragraph, which on our own figures is roughly twice the pilot price.
Three words and two cross-references fix it. Clause (iv) is otherwise right and I have not touched its
substance: without it a reviser would publish *"for each year…"* with a lowercase opening mid-sentence.

### c. S-2, and the assurance I gave the Director that was not true

Pass 9's S-2 is the finding that most directly contradicts something I wrote to you. **§6.0-24's
restatement said the retirement window has "four bounded components, each bounded on the face of the
text."** Three were. The fourth — D 1's extension *"by the number of days by which the statement or
notice is late"* — had **no cap at all**: if the Board gave the 15-day statement 400 days late the window
was 400 days longer, and **if the Board never gave it the window never closed.** The member then can
never be a member who *"does not retire in a qualifying retirement"*, so he retires six years later and
his retirement is a **qualifying** retirement: his credit vests at the pilot price, the Commonwealth
settles the subsidy, and the acceleration it paid for is **negative**. G 1's lesser-of ratchet caps the
damage at the amount last certified, so the trust is protected and **the appropriation is not** — and the
reservation sits charged against the $3,000,000 for the whole period, which on the central branch is
about one-sixth of the remaining headroom for one member. **§6.0-24 is corrected in this revision**; it
is the same class of defect as pass 7's F-1, which §6.0-24 was itself written to cure.

**The bound I wrote is 12 months, and the numeral is mine rather than yours — which is why it is also
§7 item 39.** I chose it because it is **your own window length**, so the Code gains no new figure, and
because capping the component rather than the total leaves the other three components reading exactly as
you decided them. The honest outer envelope the text now delivers is **12 months, plus the three-month
processing extension, plus at most 120 days of tolling, plus at most 12 months of Board lateness.** The
review's own preference was an absolute bound of 21 months from the earliest qualifying retirement date,
which is tighter and introduces a figure nobody has priced; a 90-day cap on the lateness extension is
tighter still. Both are drafted in item 39 and either is one edit. **What I would not do is leave it
unbounded, or leave the assurance standing.**

### d. The four findings I did not enact, and where each one went

1. **S-9 — I am withdrawing my own recommendation on §7 item 33.** The candidate text would have made
   M 2's reconsideration *"the proceeding required by Article 3"* — and pass 9 verified § 2.2-4021 B from
   source: where no hearing officer is used the agency must decide within 90 days, and after a named
   party's written notice, *"[i]f no decision is made within 30 days … the decision shall be deemed to be
   in favor of the named party."* So the sentence imports a **statutory default judgment against the
   Board**, and a member refused under the $170,000 ceiling could obtain a reservation by the Board's
   silence, against limitations D 2 declares *"self-executing."* Those two cannot both be true. Item 33
   now carries the **§ 51.1-124.11 formula** instead — the General Assembly's own words for a VRS benefit
   determination, in Title 51.1, for this agency, since 1998, with an express Article 5 entitlement and
   no case-decision characterisation. **It is a better answer than the one I recommended, and it came
   from the review.**
2. **M-9 — routed to §7 item 36**, above.
3. **M-10 — the parker, and it is a new rule, so it is §7 item 41.** H bars a further election by a
   member *"credited with service credit"* under G 2, G 3 or G 5; a member who pays **nothing** is
   credited with **zero**, which is not naturally that, and the D 6 to-zero branch is not in H's list at
   all. So a member may file on day one, be accepted with a $120,373 charge against the cap, pay nothing,
   take a § 415 deferral to push the completion date out, and let the reservation lapse up to 24 months
   later — owing nothing, barred by nothing, free to file again. Against **central headroom of about six
   reservations** that is a real exposure, and on the high branch one parker displaces a real applicant.
4. **m-7 — no anti-fraud provision, and it collides with subsection F, so it is §7 item 42.**

### e. Two things for the fiscal statement, and one correction against me

**Pass 9 reran the model from its own copy** and reproduced every published figure, including the
Director's rule at **$160,468** and the **5.4 percent** refusal share at $170,000. What it adds is the
cap arithmetic on the reservation basis: **38 / 76 / 126 percent** utilisation at low / central / high
take-up, so **on the published high-take-up branch the $3,000,000 is 126 percent subscribed**, and
**central headroom is $723,758 — about six reservations** at the mean reservation-basis subsidy of
$100,311 plus the mandatory 20 percent contingency. That is the number three of revision 24's branches
operate against, and §3 carries it. It also confirms independently that **the 12-month window does not
ease the $3,000,000**, because reservations are certified on the anticipated earliest qualifying
retirement date.

**One exposure that is not in any run.** B 4 b fixes the amount payable irrespective of when payment is
made and stops statutory interest at the valuation date, so B 4 f's new 24-month cap fixes, for the first
time, the outer size of an **interest-free deferral**: a member may pay as late as 36 months after
acceptance at a price struck on the original valuation date. The review sizes the foregone investment
return at of the order of **$11,000 to $13,000 per deferring member**, borne by the **trust**, outside the
certified subsidy. The cap is an improvement — before it the deferral was unbounded — and the residual
belongs in the § 30-19.1:7 statement as a quantified, one-sided omission.

**And the correction against me: §6.0-25 item 6 said the month-end repair "names all three sources of
movement."** It named three and there were **four**. G 4's involuntary-separation branch requires
retirement within 90 days of the separation and a qualifying retirement must take effect on the first of
a month, so a member separated on 2 June has **61 usable days, not 90** — and on 3 July, 59. That is
corrected in §6.0-25 and cured in the text.

### b. The edit that changes what the bill does, and it is the bill's only quantity

**Pass 10's S-1 is the finding of the pass and it is against me.** Clause (ii) asks for *"the number
of months of **creditable service** the member needs in order to have reached his unreduced
retirement eligibility date"* and then told the Board to measure that need against *"the
**membership service** the member has earned."* Those are different defined terms. § 51.1-124.3:
*"'Creditable service' means prior service as set forth in § 51.1-142.2 **plus** membership service
for which credit is allowable."* The unreduced retirement eligibility date turns on **creditable**
service, because § 51.1-153's unreduced conditions do. So the base was strictly narrower than the
measure, and the need was **overstated by every month of non-membership credit the member holds** —
prior service purchased under subdivision B 1 or B 2, sick-leave credit under subsection D of
§ 51.1-142.2, and free military credit under subsection I.

**The failure scenario, which is the reviewer's and which I have not softened.** A Plan 2 member aged
57 with **26 years** of membership service and **4 years** purchased in 2027 under subdivision B 1
(iv) has 30 years of creditable service. Her true shortfall under the Rule of 90 is 90 − 57 − 30 =
**36 months**. Clause (ii), on its own words, returned 90 − 57 − 26 = **84 months**. Clause (i) is
unaffected, because it deducts only credit *"previously purchased … under subdivision B 2"* and her
purchase was under B 1, so clause (i) stood at the full 48 months and **48 months was the least of
the three limbs**. She could buy 48 where she needed 36: **12 months of over-credit, with the
Commonwealth paying the certified subsidy on all 48.** Nothing screened it — clauses (vi), (vii) and
(viii) all ask whether the maximum purchasable amount gets her *to* the date, and 48 months got her
well past it.

**The words I wrote, and the words I replaced them with.** The membership-service phrase is **mine**,
introduced by store revision 22 when I drafted the Director's option (c); it was not in the text
before and nobody chose it. The repair is not the reviewer's one-word *"creditable"* substitution,
and the reason is one word further on: *"the creditable service the member has **earned**"* would
read naturally to exclude credit she **bought** or was **granted**, which is the whole of the
population S-1 is about, and the defect would survive in part. **"All creditable service for which
the member is entitled to credit as of that date"** reaches earned, purchased and granted credit
alike, and the words *"entitled to credit"* rather than *"credited"* close the administrative-lag
gap — a member whose service is rendered but not yet posted is not charged for her employer's
reporting delay.

**I enacted this against the reviewer's own routing, and that is the one place in this revision where
I did.** Pass 10 says the repair *"changes a quantity and therefore a figure, so it is the
Director's, not the drafter's."* My answer is in three parts and the Director can reverse it with one

### 6.0-18 Ambiguities resolved in revision 18

Eight, and each one changes who is admitted, who is paid, or who may complain.

1. **Which quantity does the admission test measure?** Revision 16 said the amount applied for;
   revision 17 capped it; revision 18 says **the maximum purchasable amount**, as a defined term. The
   three readings admit three different cohorts and only the third turns on facts the Board already
   holds. Resolved toward the model's own quantity, with the C (iii) difference flagged for Fiscal in
   §0.00000000000000b item 2 rather than smoothed over.

2. **As of what date is eligibility determined, where an application is filed incomplete and completed
   later?** Two readings, each with a real victim: the preserved filing date refuses the member who
   honestly reduces her request, and the completion date refuses the member whose eligibility the
   Board's own 30-day-plus-60-day cure consumed. Resolved to **the filing date of the complete
   application**, with D 4's retention made general so the deeming rule reaches it. The F1 fix removes
   the first victim; the choice removes the second. **If the Director prefers the other reading, D 4's
   retention must be narrowed to D 3's formula — it cannot be left to subsection M.**

3. **May an election be accepted for zero months?** Resolved **no**. On the text before revision 18 it
   could be, and the Commonwealth paid a subsidy for a purchase that did not happen. I treated this as
   a correction rather than a policy choice because a purchase programme that pays for no purchase is
   not the agreed design, and because the alternative is drafting degenerate cases for six defined
   terms. **It is one sentence and the Director can cut it** — but then §7 item 22's fix 2 or fix 3
   becomes necessary rather than optional.

4. **Does the member's own crediting-date election move the clause (vii) deadline?** It does, and
   revision 18 leaves that alone — but only because eligibility is now expressly determined once, as of
   the complete application's filing date, and is not re-tested. The S6 review was right that the
   premise was unstated. It is stated now.

5. **What happens when a member dies having paid part?** Resolved to **pro-rata vesting at the pilot
   price**: credit what was paid for, recertify the subsidy down to it, refund the excess to the estate.
   The alternatives were to credit the whole purchase (the Commonwealth pays for months nobody bought)
   or to apply G 3's ordinary-price re-valuation (which the middle treatment took out of the death
   case). This keeps the no-post-purchase-debt directive intact — nothing is demanded of the estate —
   and it is why the no-collection sentence now names survivors and the estate.

6. **Is a DPB refusal reviewable?** Resolved **no**, and expressly. The member gets the waiting list,
   the notice, the reasons and the standard cost, and the Board's **placement** is reviewable; the
   appropriation judgment is not made a Board determination. Making DPB's refusal reviewable under
   subsection M would put a court between the Board and the Department of Planning and Budget on a
   question of whether funds are legally available, which is not a defect this bill should create.

7. **Does a late Board statement cost the member the window?** Resolved **no**: the final qualifying
   retirement date moves by the days of delay and the member may pick a later date. The alternative —
   a flat duty with no consequence — is what pass 5 found, and it put the member outside § 51.1-153 E's
   90-day retroactivity cap through nobody's fault.

8. **Does tolling the window for a pending review reopen the window question?** No, and I checked it
   by substitution. M 2's tolling runs only while a request is pending and ends 30 days after the Board
   acts; the three-month processing cap is anchored to the base date and does not compound (pass 5 §4.2
   confirms this independently). So the numeral the Director picks is still the numeral, plus the three
   months §7 item 25 now names.

### 6.0-24 Ambiguities resolved in revision 24

Eleven, and the first three are the ones a reviewer should attack.

1. **Which sentence of G 2 the exclusion for G 3 and G 5 members attaches to.** Pass 8's fix direction
   was to say *"the bar in the third sentence of G 2 does not apply."* I did not draft it that way,
   because counting sentences inside a subdivision that four revisions have added sentences to is a
   fragile way to write a rule — and because the member needs **both** halves: no determination owed,
   and no allowance withheld. The sentence now states both substantively and cites neither: *"No
   determination under this subdivision is required in respect of a member who has been credited with
   service credit under subdivision 3 or 5, and no retirement allowance shall be withheld from such a
   member by reason of this subdivision."*
2. **Whether to bound the subsection F carve-out, as pass 8's F-5 asks, or to fix F-1 instead.** F-5
   says the carve-out's one unintended effect is to strip F's protection from the member for whom the
   G 2 bar is **permanent** rather than a deferral — and then says *"then fix F-1, which is the real
   cure."* I took the real cure. With F-1 drafted there is no member for whom the bar is permanent, so
   a temporal bound on the carve-out would qualify a case that no longer exists while inviting the
   argument that some **other** unbounded deferral was intended to survive. The carve-out instead names
   the three things it covers — the allowance deferral, G 2 (i)'s reduction of credited service, and the
   deferral of a refund — which is narrower in substance than *"nothing required or permitted"* alone.
3. **The outer limit on when a G 2 determination takes effect, and its two anchors.** Pass 8 proposed 30
   days after the notice. The notice sentence already requires *"no less than 30 days before the
   determination takes effect"*, so 30 days as an outer limit would fix the date to exactly the
   thirtieth day and leave the Board no room to answer a member who responds. I wrote **60 days**, with
   a **120-day** backstop from the trigger so that a late notice cannot defeat the limit. The backstop
   is keyed to *"the date from which the 60-day period in the first sentence of this subdivision runs"*
   rather than to clause (a) or (b) by name, because clause (a) is now *"if any"* and a member may have
   no final qualifying retirement date at all.
4. **Whether a Board-initiated downward recertification cancels the election or merely reduces it.**
   Pass 7's F-4 asked for cancellation, a full refund and release where C (ii) collapses to zero. I
   drafted that, and added the case F-4 did not reach: a recertification downward that is **not** to
   zero. There the election survives and *"the service credit to be purchased **is reduced** to the
   amount the member may purchase as recertified"* — a duty, not the member's option, because the
   quantity she may lawfully buy has fallen and an option would leave her contracted for service the
   section forbids her to purchase. D 6's existing option menu is untouched, so the member who faces an
   **increase** still chooses.
5. **Three days for mailing.** Pass 7's F-15 observes that deeming a notice *"given"* on the date the
   Board mails it, with no allowance for transit, puts the whole risk of postal delay on the member — on
   a 30-day period whose miss can cost her the pilot price. Virginia's ordinary practice is to allow for
   mailing or to key the period to receipt. I added three days rather than keying to receipt, because
   receipt is a fact the Board cannot determine and the whole point of the deeming sentence is to give
   the Board a date it can act on. **The three days are my choice and are one edit.**
6. **Where the month-end repair goes.** Pass 8's F-13 found that D 1's extension-by-days-of-lateness and
   M 2's tolling can both land mid-month, where no permissible effective date exists — so the statute's
   compensation for the Board's own lateness delivers a member nothing whenever the lateness is less
   than a month. The repair is written **once**, in the definition of *"final qualifying retirement
   date"*, and names all three sources of movement, rather than three times in three provisions. It
   rounds **forward**, to the first day of the next month, which is the member-favourable direction and
   the only one that gives the remedy content. **Corrected in store revision 33 on pass 9's M-2: there
   were four places, not three.** G 4's involuntary-separation branch requires the member to retire
   within 90 days of the separation, and a qualifying retirement must take effect on the first day of a
   month, so a member separated on 2 June has **61 usable days and not 90** — and on 3 July, 59 — while
   she is also working through the § 2.2-3201 placement process. The fourth place is cured by its own
   clause in G 4 rather than by widening the rounding sentence, because the remedy there is a permission
   to retire on the first day of the next month and not a re-dating of a deadline.
7. **Naming a medium for the subsection M procedures without answering §7 item 32.** The procedures fix
   the content of a complete application, which fixes the filing date, which decides who reaches the
   $3,000,000 before it closes — and *"adopt and publish"* named no medium. The new duty is to publish on
   the Board's website and to supply a copy on request. It is deliberately **silent on Article 2**,
   because whether the act should say expressly that Article 2 governs is the Director's (item 32) and a
   publication duty should not decide it by implication.
8. **The employer-policy ordering rule.** Pass 7's O-3 found that B 4 e's *"and the order in which the
   employer will apply that amount"* is the cheapest technical compliance path with the uniformity
   requirement: a facially universal policy, a modest annual cap, applied *"in the order in which
   employees file requests with the agency"*, and an agency that mentions the Program to one senior
   employee first has defeated subsection B's *"no employer shall require, request, or induce"* without
   requesting anything. The order must now be **stated in the policy, fixed in advance, and be either
   the order of complete applications filed with the Board or an order determined by lot**, and the
   policy must be published. This is an anti-circumvention repair to an agreed rule rather than a new
   rule, which is why I drafted it; **it is one clause if the Director disagrees.**
9. **Reinstating an unlawfully released reservation over the cap.** §5.12 records the choice and the
   reason. The alternative is a member holding vested below-cost credit with no appropriation behind it,
   which is worse for the trust, worse constitutionally, and the thing the architecture exists to
   prevent.
10. **Not adding statutory interest to the G 2 arrears.** §0.x item b 2 records it. The outer limit does
    the work; interest is a money provision no document directs.
11. **Not touching D 6's option (ii).** Pass 7 notes that *"pay the amount of the increase"* means the
    member funds the Commonwealth's own subsidy, and that it *"reads badly out of context."* It is the
    member's least-bad option where the contingency is short — the alternatives are to buy less or to
    cancel, both of which she already has — so it stays, and it belongs in the memo rather than in a
    redraft.

**Withdrawn from §6.0-18.** Item 8 told the Director that *"the numeral the Director picks is still the
numeral, plus the three months §7 item 25 now names,"* citing pass 5 §4.2. Pass 7's F-1 is right that
pass 5 verified store revision 15 and the compounding risk was created by revision 18's own additions,
so **the assurance and the text it described were not the same text.** The corrected statement:
**12 months, plus the three-month processing extension, plus at most 120 days of tolling, plus any days

### 6.1a Ambiguities resolved in revision 7, and the choices inside the Director's text

Revision 7 drafts a phrase the Director wrote. Four things still had to be decided to write it into
the section, and each is recorded here rather than left for a reviewer to discover. **Revision 8
corrects the stated ground of items 2 and 3 and the cohort description in item 4**, per
[MOO-65](/MOO/issues/MOO-65) F-5, F-6 and F-3. In all three the **conclusion survives** and the
**reason did not**; I record the corrections at length rather than quietly swapping them, because a
later reader who relied on the wrong reason in another provision would get a Plan 2 member's reduction
wrong.

1. **Limb order: positive first, negative second.** I put *"is calculated in accordance with
   subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155"* ahead of *"and is not reduced under subdivision A 2 or A 3."*
   The reason is not style. Taken in that order the sentence states the computation and then the
   qualification on it, which is how § 51.1-155.1 and § 51.1-155.2 both state the same idea; taken in
   the other order the reader meets a negative qualification before knowing what is being qualified.
   The two orders are semantically identical and the order in "qualifying retirement" is the same, so
   the two tests remain word-identical, which is the property MOO-49 §4.3 requires.
2. **"Whichever applies to the member" comes out, and nothing replaces it.** In revision 6's
   definition that phrase chose between A 2 and A 3. It is surplus against a disjunctive negative
   limb: an allowance that is *"not reduced under subdivision A 2 or A 3"* is unreduced whichever of
   the two provisions governs the member. **The ground revision 7 gave for that was wrong and
   revision 8 replaces it.** Revision 7 said *"the member's tier already selects between them by the
   terms of A 2 and A 3 themselves."* It does not. A 2's applicability sentence reads *"The provisions
   of this subdivision shall apply to teachers and state employees"* with **no tier limit**, and A 3's
   caption reaches *"any person who becomes a member on or after July 1, 2010"* while its operative
   applicability paragraph reaches political-subdivision employees *"and any other employees as
   provided by law"* — so a **post-1-July-2010 state employee is facially within both**. What resolves
   the overlap is **§ 51.1-153 B 1**, which pins that member's benefit to *"subdivision A 3 of
   § 51.1-155"* ([MOO-65](/MOO/issues/MOO-65) F-5). **The removal is still harmless, for a better
   reason than the one revision 7 gave:** the limb tests the allowance **as computed**, not which
   provision abstractly governs the member, and the disjunctive form requires that the allowance be
   unreduced under **either** — which is the safe direction, because it cannot admit an allowance that
   one of the two has reduced. Keeping the phrase would also have required a third reference to the same
   Plan 1 / Plan 2 discriminator that A 1's clauses (i) and (ii) and clause (ii) of "eligible member"
   already carry, which invites the argument that the three references mean different things. **I did
   not substitute a tier test**, per the Director's express instruction. The consequence for the
   verification record is in §5.2: *"whichever applies"* is no longer a pin this bill makes.
3. **"Of that section" rather than a second full citation.** Both definitions now cite § 51.1-155
   once and refer to *"subdivision A 2 or A 3 of that section."* The alternative — repeating
   *"of § 51.1-155"* — is not wrong, but Chapter 1 uses the short back-reference where the antecedent
   is the immediately preceding citation, and the shorter form is what keeps the added phrase to
   eleven words. **Revision 8 corrects the ground.** Revision 7 said *"both definitions now cite
   § 51.1-155 once"* and *"there is no intervening section citation in either definition."* Both are
   imprecise: **each definition cites two sections** — § 51.1-153 first, then § 51.1-155, then *"that
   section"* — and the accurate claim is the narrower one, that no citation intervenes **between the
   antecedent and the back-reference** ([MOO-65](/MOO/issues/MOO-65) F-6). **The decisive
   disambiguator, which revision 7 did not state, is that § 51.1-153 A has no numbered subdivisions at
   all**, so *"subdivision A 2 or A 3"* has no possible referent in § 51.1-153 and can only reach
   § 51.1-155. I verified that on the official section page. The conclusion is unchanged: the
   antecedent is unambiguous in both definitions as enacted. If DLS prefers to spend four words and
   write *"of § 51.1-155"* twice, nothing turns on it.
4. **The zero-reduction member: noted, not drafted against.** A member who retires on or after the
   date the A 2 or A 3 reduction factor falls to zero receives an allowance that is *"determined in
   the same manner as for normal retirement"* and is **not** reduced, so that allowance passes both
   limbs. That is the right result, not a leak: a zero reduction factor means the member has reached
   the unreduced threshold, which puts her in the same **unreduced subdivision A 1 cohort** every
   figure in the package is priced on. **Revision 8 corrects the description** — revision 7 called it
   *"the § 51.1-153 B normal-retirement cohort,"* and subsection B is captioned *Early retirement*
   ([MOO-65](/MOO/issues/MOO-65) F-3). The arithmetic is unchanged and the review verified it for both
   tiers: A 2's zero-reduction point is 30 years of service, which for a member over 50 **is**
   § 51.1-153 B 2; A 3's is service of 30 or more years with age plus service of at least 90, which
   **is** § 51.1-153 B 3. Both land inside the priced cohort, which is why letting the route pass is
   the right result. Trying to exclude the route by name — "other than under subdivision A 2
   or A 3" — would exclude a member whose allowance is identical to a normal-retirement allowance and
   would turn the test from a test on the **allowance** into a test on the **route**, which is the
   thing MOO-52 showed the Code does not do consistently. **Both limbs test the allowance. I left it
   that way on purpose.**

**What I did not do, and would need an instruction to do.** I did not touch clause (vi) of "eligible
member," `[the clause that was clause (vi) when this was written is now clause (vii); the present clause (vi) did not exist until revision 16 —` [MOO-77](/MOO/issues/MOO-77) `F10.]` subsection C clause (ii), or clause (ii) of "certified subsidy," all of which consume the
revised term and all of which §5.5 shows work correctly on it. I did not add a definition of
"service retirement allowance" — the phrase is used in Chapter 1 without definition and the positive
limb now makes the computation explicit, so a definition would be surplus and would reach provisions
outside this pilot. And I did not record the § 51.1-155 A 5 question as open; per the Director's
decision on [MOO-62](/MOO/issues/MOO-62) it is closed because it changes no operative text against
the combined phrase (§0.0000, §7 item 17). The review agreed with that on independent grounds and
would not open an issue on it either.

**Revision 8's own choices, and the one I am most likely to be wrong about.** Revision 8 enacts no
text, so its only choices are about where the four candidate repairs sit and what I declined to decide
for the Director.

5. **I did not enact any of the four repairs**, including the two the review assigned to me outright
   (F-4's G 4 clause and F-8's D 1 category error). Each moves text **outside the two definitions**
   [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) commissioned, and F-8 in particular is so nearly cost-free that
   enacting it would have been defensible. I did not, for one reason: the Director's commission said
   in terms that *"no other section moves,"* and a drafter who treats that as advisory the moment he
   thinks a change is harmless is the drafter who later enacts something that is not. All four are
   written out ready to paste, so the answer converts to text in one pass.
6. **On F-1 I recommend Candidate B over the review's Candidate A**, which is a disagreement with the
   reviewer worth recording. The reviewer's point — that word-identity is not the property that
   prevents cohort divergence — is **correct**, and I accept it against my own §5.5. But it does not
   follow that word-identity should be abandoned once it is shown not to be load-bearing: a reader who
   finds the payment-form words in one definition and not the other will argue the omission was
   deliberate, and in the modal definition the words are declaratory rather than operative, so they
   cost six words of surplusage and buy symmetry. **Candidate C is the better drafting and I did not
   recommend it**, because a non-definition sentence inside a definitions subsection is the kind of
   structure a DLS drafter will move, and I would rather the Director choose that deliberately than
   inherit it from me.
7. **I declined to draft the F-2 fix in the form the review suggested** — *"one sentence in G 2"* — and
   drafted **two** independent repairs instead, because the single sentence the review had in mind
   cures either the delay or the loss but not both. Candidate (a) removes the delay in the ordinary
   case and leaves it where the Board learns late; candidate (b) cannot fail, because it makes the
   member financially indifferent to a delay of any length. The reason I would enact both is that
   subsection F makes the member a **promise** — *"no other consequence shall attach"* — and a promise
   half kept is the sentence a member advocate reads aloud.

### 6.0-20 Ambiguities resolved in revision 20

Four edits, three ambiguities. Each one is a choice I made that the commission did not decide, and each
is stated so the Director can overturn it.

1. **Is the zero-refused person "the member" or "the applicant"?** The three notices around her in
   subdivisions D 3, D 4 and D 5 all say *"the applicant"*; R3's sentence says *"the member"*. **Resolved
   to "the member", and the reason is that the sentence sits in subsection C**, whose own vocabulary is
   *"[a]n eligible member may purchase"*, *"[t]he member may complete payment"*. She has already passed
   D 4's eligibility determination — that is the whole point of R3 — so she is a member and an eligible
   member, and calling her an applicant in the one provision that has established she is more than one
   would be the inconsistency the chapter's drafting rules exist to prevent. **Never two words for one
   concept**: "applicant" is the person whose eligibility is undetermined or refused, "member" is the
   person whose is established. The draft now uses each consistently.

   this draft's and this chapter's own idiom (D 2's *"first sentence of this subdivision"*, G 4's
   *"[n]otwithstanding the preceding sentence"*) and that R3's sentence is placed last in subsection C.

   under clause (ii) of this subsection is zero"* — which is more robust to a later insertion but
   duplicates the bar's own words, and duplicated operative language is the defect that creates two
   provisions to amend where there should be one. §5.10 Check 5 records the residual fragility.
3. **Does a defined term keyed to a "member" bear being applied to an applicant who is not one?**
   Resolved yes, because every limb yields a determinate figure for such a person and limb (a) yields

   re-key only D 3 and D 5**, which would have kept an applicant-supplied referent in the one notice

until the Board made a determination that reduced, refunded and released nothing. That is verbatim the

**elections** and carries a fourth limb for a reservation released under D 7 with nothing credited.

### b. Eight more edits, each a real failure

- **The three-day mailing allowance did not reach the periods it was made for** (finding 5). Its sentence
  carried **no scoping phrase**, so its scope was § 51.1-142.4 alone and it missed B 4 f's 30-day § 415
  election period — the period whose loss costs the member the pilot price on the whole purchase. It also
  reached only *"the member"*, and the bill uses **"applicant"** as a distinct term in D 2 to D 5,
  including D 4's 60-day completeness cure, whose miss costs her filing date and her place against the
  $3,000,000. Scoped and widened, with sentence 1 conformed. **§5.15's *"all ten are now reached"* is
  withdrawn.**
- **B 4 g is deleted** (finding 6). I created it in store revision 34, and pass 11 re-opened **26 C.F.R.
  § 1.415(j)-1** at source: a limitation year is a **per-plan** attribute, the calendar year is the federal
  **default** absent plan terms, and *"[o]nce established, the limitation year may be changed only by
  amending the plan."* So the designation is surplusage or an impermissible statutory change, and in
  neither case can it be confined to a subset of a plan's participants — the narrowing achieved nothing. It
  also reached teachers and local employees in a bill whose subsection L tells localities it imposes no
  duty on them, and it expired **mid-limitation-year**. Pass 11 confirms **B 4 f is not stranded**:
  *"limitation year"* stays defined in B 4 a under *"As used in this subdivision."* Nothing cited the
  designation. The plan-document question is routed to Statutory Researcher at
  [MOO-115](/MOO/issues/MOO-115), because the bill cannot answer it.
- **G 2's 30-day notice floor now tracks the member's own review period** (finding 9) — the three-day
  allowance made her M 2 request period 33 days while a determination could take effect on day 30.
- **Subsection F's carve-out names four provisions, not three** (finding 10). Store revision 33 created a
  fourth refund conversion, in **D 6**, in the revision in which it stated the list as complete.
- **The agency notice duty now has a consequence, and the Board's clock no longer runs from its own
  ignorance** (finding 11). **J 1's list is closed** and did not reach an agency's failure; every failure
  of which the Board becomes aware is now reportable, on D 1's and D 3's model, and the Board's 15 days run
  from the earlier of receipt and knowledge.
- **The over-cap reinstatement must now seek the appropriation it spends** (finding 13). D 3's annual
  re-confirmation is what keeps the architecture inside **Va. Const. art. X, § 7**, and reinstating is not
  reserving, so it bypassed it; store revision 33's four safeguards notified four audiences and **obliged
  nobody**.
- **That notice is split, specified and reviewable** (finding 14). Pass 11 looked for a privacy or FOIA bar
  and **found none**, so compelling disclosure of *"the cause of the release"* to every wait-listed
  applicant was lawful — which was the problem, because in a cohort of nineteen it identifies a member who
  had no forum to contest the Board's characterisation of her own file. Applicants now get the **fact,
  amount and date** and may not be told the cause or the identity; the Chairmen get the cause; and a
  reinstatement **is a determination for subsection M**, on D 3's own model.
- **Enactment 3 preserves the member's rights, not only the Board's verbs** (finding 15), and **two
  cosmetic repairs travel with them**: D 6 refunds the member who **elects** to reduce under D 6 (i) or
  B 4 f (i), whose overpayment the refund duty missed because it was keyed to what she *may* purchase
  (finding 18); and G 4's determination clock runs from *"the last day on which the member may retire in a
  qualifying retirement under this subdivision"* (finding 19).

### c. For the Director, and the record corrections

**§7 items 55 to 58**, each drafted and none enacted: finding 12's privacy choice (the separating agency
may never have known the election exists); finding 1's tighter alternatives, which **item 39 now carries in
repaired form**; finding 6's residual if a designation is to be kept rather than deleted; and pass 11's
attacks on the candidates at items 33, 41 and 42, each seriously defective **as drafted** — most
consequentially that item 41(a) as written **releases the reservation and leaves the election accepted**,
creating the art. X, § 7 exposure item 40 is about.

**Four statements of mine did not hold**: §5.15's *"all ten are now reached"*; §0.x's M-4 and §5.15's M-4
row on the completeness of F's list; §0.x's M-5 claim that the protective limb *"matches the prohibition it
qualifies"* (three terms differ each way — harmless, but not accurate); and §0.x a's location of the S-1
exclusion at *"G 2, 5th sentence"*, which is the **4th of nine** on a mechanical count. The corrections are
in [`pass11-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass11-disposition) §4.

### d. One fiscal fact that moves no figure and is more adverse than the record's own statement

Pass 11 accepted §7 item 41's premise that a parked reservation's charge comes back — D 3 releases the
contingency, D 2 keeps only **settled** amounts charged — so the exposure is a **timing** exposure. **Then
it found the timing does not come back inside the pilot.** A parker's maximum hold is 12 months under
subsection E plus the 24 months B 4 f permits: **36 months from acceptance.** Acceptances run 1 July 2029
to 1 July 2033, so **a reservation parked by a member accepted on or after 1 July 2030 does not lapse until
at or after the last date the Board may accept any election, and the returned headroom can never be used.**
The honest statement is not *"six parkers close the programme"* but *"a parker accepted in three of the
programme's four acceptance years permanently removes her charge from it, and six such parkers close it."*
It moves no figure and it strengthens item 41. Two lines are with Fiscal & Impact Modeler at
[MOO-116](/MOO/issues/MOO-116).

### e. Housekeeping

**Nine sections are moved** verbatim to
[`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history) — the **store
revision 34 §0 record**, the five remaining cross-reference sweeps **§5.3, §5.4, §5.6, §5.7 and §5.8**
(consolidated behind one stub with §5.5, which went out in store revision 34), **§6.0-18** and **§6.0-21** —
every lettered label and every check number preserved, and the durable results restated in the stubs.
**Nothing was summarised away**, and each survives verbatim in the store revisions of this file that carried
it. The file had about **9,800 characters** of headroom and this record alone exceeds that, which is why the
disposition is a companion document and why these went out. **It now stands at about 515,300 characters,
with roughly 9,000 of headroom** — still less than one revision's record costs, so the next revision also
needs a companion document from the start, and the remaining candidates for moving are §6.0-20 and
§6.0-22.

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel.
Pre-decisional.**

## 0.000000000000000000000000000 Store revision 35 — §7 items 27 to 30 drafted out, with pass 10's repairs folded into the same words

> **Store-revision note.** Labelled **34** because store revision 33 is the record below. **The number is
> the store's**; if the store assigns a higher one, this record is still the one that revision means.

**The Director answered all four of store revision 32's open items on 12 October 2026**
([MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64)): **item 28 both clauses, item 29 enact, item 27 candidate (a), item 30 the
gateway open for subsections A and C of § 51.1-155.1 only** — **and [MOO-99](/MOO/issues/MOO-99), pass 10's
adversarial review of those very edits, returned 6 serious, 10 moderate and 3 minor before this write
landed.** So the answers are **enacted as repaired rather than enacted and then repaired: six edits in three
provisions**, five of them the answers and one a pass-10 repair, with **nine more pass-10 repairs folded into
the wording of the answers themselves**. **Item 29 needed no edit** — its substance was already in the text
as store revision 21's conforming edit — and nothing was re-enacted.

**The repair that mattered most was one word.** The draft read *"the certified subsidy **may be settled**"*,
where every neighbouring operator in G 1 and G 4 is automatic; against that background *"may"* confers a
**discretion**, making the Commonwealth's payment of a named member's subsidy standardless (*Ames v. Town of
Painter*, 239 Va. 343 (1990)). **Enacted: *"is settled."*** The tolling now reaches **every period** in
subdivision 2 or G 4, of both kinds; the rescission carries **notice and subsection M review**; *"pending"*
is **defined**; a determination in contravention of the bar is **of no effect**; the bar reaches the
**notice**; the redetermination runs from the approval rather than a date the Board picks; the reinstatement
gets a **deadline**; and D 1's notice must state the **outer bound**, the **rounding-forward** rule and the
**three-day mailing** rule, with the earliest-date floor stated as the **permission** it is.

**Two findings needed no edit because store revision 33 had already cured them — verified, not assumed:**
**M13** (G 2's 120-day bound had no referent for the subdivision 4 cohort; its new term *"the determination
date"* supplies one) and most of **M15**. **Six findings are policy and are on the card as items 48 to 52 and
54**, with candidate text for every one and none of it in the bill.

**No figure moves on the enacted text, no section is added, no definition is added or removed, and the bill
title does not grow.** Two new citations — **§ 51.1-155.1 A and C**, **§ 51.1-156 A and H** — are checked in
**§5.17**; ambiguities at **§6.0-35**; **the whole record, including the redline, the use-by-use trace, all
19 findings and the candidate text, is in
[`moo64-record`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-moo64-record)**. **Store revision 33's §0 record is moved out below, and ten
older pointer stubs are consolidated into the single table at §0.1** — about 14,700 characters of stubs for
records that were already moved. **Nothing is lost**, every one being verbatim in the history document, and
**the remaining question is §7 item 53**.

### 6.0-37 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 37

1. **I withdrew the clause I had drafted rather than repairing it.** [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) gave
   me a repair for each of its three serious findings on that clause — widen the antecedent to reach the
   certified subsidy, add a *notwithstanding* to G 4's settlement sentence so the deeming does not
   displace its own machinery, and add *"by reason of his death."* Taking all three would have produced a
   fourth draft of a cure for a problem **the live text does not have**: the live sentence creates no
   deeming, so G 1 is not triggered and the subsidy calculation is not reached. **The smallest change that
   achieves the agreed policy was to keep the sentence and add the one disapplication MOO-96 asked for.**
   Rewriting a provision you do not need to touch creates opposition for free.
2. **I did not choose between the review's option (a) and option (b), and I did not draft a third and
   enact it.** S10-F1 is *"a policy choice, not a drafting choice"*, in the reviewer's own words, and
   §7 item 60 puts it with the text for each answer written out. What I did do is correct both of its
   premises — the survivor half is narrower than stated and the fiscal half runs through the
   *"certified subsidy"* floor rather than through the deeming — because a Director choosing between two
   options should not be choosing on a mechanism that is not the operative one.
3. **I repeated *"for that purpose"* and I know it is surplusage.** The sentence already carries the
   adverbial once. Omitting it the second time would have left *"no other requirement … shall apply"*
   arguable as a general disapplication of § 51.1-153 for all purposes of the section, which is a bigger
   defect than a repeated three-word phrase. A DLS attorney who deletes the second one will be right on
   style and will need to re-scope the clause another way.
4. **"No other requirement," not "no requirement."** *"No other"* signals that the three express date
   disapplications in the same sentence are handled expressly and are not left to the residual. The
   review tested whether the residual subsumes them and found it does not, so without *"other"* the
   sentence would read as though it might.
5. **"That a member cannot satisfy by reason of his death," not "that a deceased member cannot
   satisfy."** S10-F9. The second form bears an individual reading — a requirement *this* member cannot
   satisfy — under which a member who died at 46 with 11 years of service would be assumed into a service
   retirement for which she was never eligible. The five added words foreclose that without an
   enumeration. *"His"* follows the chapter's own convention, which this section matches elsewhere.
6. **I re-anchored a pointer in a sentence nobody commissioned me to touch, and the reason is that my
   own commission changed the sentence it points at.** Subdivision G 4's death sentence is this revision's
   commission; the pointer in the next sentence reads onto it. The re-anchor removes an argument and
   changes no outcome on the better reading.
7. **I did not enact S10-F14's *"personal representative"* for *"estate."*** The reviewer verified that
   § 51.1-162 A's fourth person in the order of precedence is the **executor or administrator** and that
   an estate is not a person capable of being paid, and rated it minor and *"fix, if it is cheap."* **It
   is not cheap.** *"Estate"* appears **four** times in subdivision G 4 and once in subdivision G 2, in
   two different senses: as a payee and notice recipient, where *"personal representative"* is the better
   word; and in the protective sentence *"[n]o amount shall be collected, offset, or withheld from any
   member, retiree, survivor, beneficiary, or estate of a member"*, where narrowing to a named person
   would **shrink a protection**. And a refund of the order of $4,400 under G 4 may have no personal
   representative at all, because § 64.2-601 lets a successor collect a small asset without
   administration. Changing one occurrence and not the others would use two words for one concept.
   **Recorded as a declined minor with the reason, not as an oversight.**
8. **I did not enact S10-F10's widening of M 2's class.** It is the same amendment to the same sentence
   as §7 item 34 item 2, which has been waiting on an extension of commission since store revision 30.
   Two agents have now found two classes missing from one sentence; one amendment should carry both.
   §7 item 61.
9. **I did not treat the review's S10-F6 as open.** Store revision 33 capped subdivision D 1's extension
   at 12 months while [MOO-104](/MOO/issues/MOO-104) was running, so the uncapped-lateness half of that
   finding is already closed in the text. What survives is the **absolute** bound the reviewer says he
   would insist on, which is §7 item 39's existing question, and his figure is a third alternative to the
   two already drafted there. §7 item 61.

### 7.1 Retained record — numbers and choices that were mine, recorded rather than fixed

*Moved to the end of §7 in store revision 33 on pass 9's m-6, so that items 1 to 54 read in order. No word of it changed.*

**Items MOO-44 §6 found I had resolved silently and that are now recorded rather than fixed**, so you
know they were chosen: the 12-month payment period in E; the contingency percentage in D 3 (**now
derived rather than chosen — MOO-53 §7 and item 15 above**); the
exclusion of hybrid retirement program participants in A clause (iii) — sensible on the merits
because hybrid members are far from any threshold, but a scope decision that Pathway B's removal did
not dictate; and the whole of subsection I, whose trigger and remedy I chose with no cited authority
in revision 1 and which MOO-44 calls the most litigable clause in the bill. Subsection I is now
drafted with notice, a response period and a determination, but the **12-month window** and the
**Employee Work Profile** test are still my choices.

**Revision 3's own chosen numbers, recorded on the same principle.** Four, all procedural, none of
them directed by any cited document: the Board must state both ends of the window **within 15 days**
of posting the credit (chosen to land before any member would plausibly resign); the member's
§ 51.1-153 notice is due **30 days** before the date they select (the shortest period that lets VRS
set up a payment, and it matches the 30-day periods already used throughout the section); the
settlement redetermination is due **within 90 days** of retirement (an actuarial determination, so
longer than the administrative 30- and 60-day periods); and the Board's three-month processing
extension carries over from revision 2 unchanged, now attached to the final date rather than to the
member's chosen date. Any of the four can move on instruction without touching anything else.

**Revision 12's own chosen numbers, recorded on the same principle.** Four again, all procedural, none
of them directed by any cited document, and each one a single edit: the member's § 51.1-153 notice is
due within **30 days** of the Board's statement of the window (chosen to match the 30 days in the
other limb and the section's other 30-day periods); the member may fix the crediting date to the last
day of a month and the Board must notify the date it credits within **five days** (short because
everything the member does next is measured from it); the Board must act on a processing-extension
request within **30 days** and notify a late-approved date within **15 days** (matching D 3 and the
15-day window statement); and a § 415 deferral may extend the completion date by no more than **12
months** after the start of the limitation year (long enough to reach the next year's limit, short
enough that a deferral cannot hold a reservation open indefinitely). **Two of revision 11's
recorded choices are also now live rather than latent**, because revision 12 attached consequences to
them: D 3's 30 days for the Director of the Department of Planning and Budget now has a reporting
duty behind it, and the **three-month** outer limit on the processing extension is now the only
remaining limit on a duty rather than a cap on a discretion.

# bill-text-s8 — retained record, second volume: the §0 narrative for store revisions 38 to 41, the sweeps §5.20 to §5.23, and §6.0-26, §6.0-35, §6.0-36 and §6.0-38, and §3

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · opened at store revision 43, 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional, not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by counsel or DLS. Nothing here is cleared for external use.**

**Why a second volume.** [`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history) stands at 523,352 characters against the document store's 524,288-character ceiling and **cannot absorb another move**. `bill-text-s8` arrived at store revision 43 with **23 characters** of headroom, and pass 14's record would not fit. The sections below are moved here **verbatim**, with every lettered label, numbered item, table row and check number preserved, so a `§0.0000000000000000d`- or `§5.21`-style reference still resolves. **Nothing was rewritten and nothing was summarised away.** Each one is replaced in `bill-text-s8` by a stub restating its durable results and naming anything in it that is superseded.

**Three warnings for a reader who arrives here first.**

1. **Three rows of §5.21's sweep are corrected by pass 14 and must not be relied on as written** — the ordinal-reference row (P14-17), the *"limitation year"* count (P14-18), and the count of provisions that move with the final qualifying retirement date, which is six and not five (N14-2). The corrections are at `bill-text-s8` §5.24.
2. **§5.20's Checks 2, 3 and 4 carry corrections already recorded in their own text**, from [MOO-119](/MOO/issues/MOO-119)'s pass 13.
3. **§3's cap-utilisation range — low 38, central 76, high 126 percent — is §3's own reservation-basis arithmetic and is superseded for every external use** by MOO-32 v6's authorised **78.1872** percent central and **130.31** percent high on **18.3965** participants. §3's reasoning about the cap is unaffected. The stub in `bill-text-s8` says the same, so nobody has to come here to find it out.
4. **§6.0-36 item 1 is the record of the second withdrawal of the window-envelope assurance.** Store revision 43 states the envelope as a statement of the text and not as a warranty, and two residuals are in front of the Policy Director at §7 items 68 and 71.

## 0.000000000000000000000000000000000 Store revision 41 — [MOO-119](/MOO/issues/MOO-119)'s pass 13 drafted out. Two edits, 484 characters, and the first gives subsection C's quantity limit a value it did not have for a measured, admitted class

**The record proper is a companion document from the start** —
[`pass13-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-87#document-pass13-disposition) — on the convention store
revisions 33, 36 and 40 set. It carries the finding-by-finding disposition of all twelve findings, the
redline, the measured class, and the record corrections in full. What follows is the summary.

**Pass 13 returned 12 findings — 0 fatal, 4 serious, 4 moderate, 4 minor — and does not recommend
reversing store revision 38's deletion.** It found what neither the deletion nor any of §7 item 35's
three checks reached: a class for whom clause (ii) of subsection C has **no value at all**.

**Edit 1 — subsection C's new third sentence says what clause (ii) does where no quantity of service can
answer it.** For a Plan 1 member under age 50 at the filing date, § 51.1-153 B 2 requires age 50 **and**
30 years of creditable service, so no number of months of creditable service causes her to have reached
her unreduced retirement eligibility date as of that date: the solution set is **empty**, and the bill
did not say whether that yields a cap of **zero** — on which the deleted bar would have refused her,
with notice — or **no binding limb**. Clause **(vi)** admits her at the boundary, one month short of 50.
**0.0826 participants in the class, 0.0259 admitted, at $145,396 to $166,226 of certified subsidy
each** against subdivision D 2's $170,000 ceiling: de minimis in aggregate, **not** de minimis per
member, and resolved before this revision by whoever at the Board wrote the spreadsheet.

**It enacts the reading the authorised basis is measured on, which is why no figure moves.**
`moo32_v6_engine.py`'s `need_months_at` returns `INF`, not 0, for that class, so **18.3965 admitted**
and [MOO-71](/MOO/issues/MOO-71)'s **18 (range 9 to 30)** already stand on the reading now in the text;
the other reading is **18.3706**, about $4,000 of the $3,000,000 lower. **Direction of effect: nil
against the authorised count, upward against the alternative**, and the ground for choosing is the
Director's own — a count may not travel on a basis the statute does not require. The sentence also makes
the choice a **determination stated in the certification**, which subdivision M 2 reaches; before it
there was nothing stated and nothing to review.

**Edit 2 — clause (v) of *"eligible member"* now carries clause (ii)'s entitlement base, verbatim.**
Store revision 34 gave clause (ii) the words *"taking account of all creditable service for which the
member is entitled to credit as of that date"* and §6.0-38 item 4 records that clause (v) was
deliberately left alone, which invited the inference that the instruction does not reach the limb that
is now the **sole** screen for the same fact (F-11, F-12). **Direction of effect: ~~it can only exclude,
never admit~~ <u>[Store revision 46, on pass 14's **M-1**: no quantity of creditable service can postpone
an unreduced retirement eligibility date, but the direction of effect of the base specification itself
is not determinate on the face of the statute. Corrected here and in §8's status note for store
revision 41; the text question is §7 item 82 and [MOO-124](/MOO/issues/MOO-124) has answered the
research question it turns on.]</u>**, because more creditable service cannot postpone an unreduced date; on the authorised
basis it moves nothing, the engine carrying one service variable per member so that the split-base case
is not representable.

**One serious finding is live and not enacted: F-3, at §7 item 70.** An accepted election with nothing
to buy has no defined downstream operation. Edit 1 closes the **pre-acceptance** route to it. **Two
