## 2. MOO-101 section A — §7 item 34's five repairs

All five are enacted. Three of them are enacted in words that differ from the drafted words, each
difference a repair MOO-121 found **before** the string landed, and each reversible in one substitution.

**Item 1 (MOO-84's F3) — E1.** The filing-date retention sentence, enacted **without** its durational
limit *"until 30 days after the Board acts upon the request."* MOO-121's **M3**: a filing date is a fact,
nothing in the bill ever takes one away, and a retention rule with an expiry invites the negative
implication that the date is **lost** when the retention lapses — which would hand the later-filing
applicant an argument about queue order that the text does not answer. Placement is between M 2's tolling
sentence and its savings sentence, which MOO-121 confirms, and the reference form *"subdivisions D 4 and
D 5"* is correct from subsection M. **Depends on item 2:** without the class amendment an applicant cannot
request reconsideration at all and this sentence is hollow for the class that needs it.

**Item 2 (F4) — E2, with E3 and E4 conforming.** M 2 now reads *"A member, retiree, beneficiary, or
applicant."* **Reversible in one word**, as recorded. Three things went with it:

- **E3, MOO-121's M4.** M 2's tolling sentence tolled only *"any period within which **the member** must
  act"*, and D 4's 60-day completion window is an **applicant's** period — *"the applicant shall have 60
  days from that notice to supply the missing items."* So the applicant who won the right to seek
  reconsideration would have got no tolling of the one period she needs tolled. Subsection A's own final
  paragraph already says *"every period within which a member **or an applicant** may or must act"*, so
  this was an inconsistency and not a choice.
- **E4, my own residue, which MOO-121 confirms and endorses.** M 2's judicial-review savings sentence
  still named three classes. Leaving it would have displaced the F4 argument by exactly one sentence.
- **E2's second limb is wider than MOO-98's finding and it is mine.** See §4 and §10 item 2.

**Item 3 (F8) — E5.** D 7 releases a reserved certified subsidy and its contingency amount on the giving
of subsection C's or subdivision D 2's refusal notice, as drafted. **Fiscal's measurement of it
([MOO-102](/MOO/issues/MOO-102)) changes what the sentence *is* rather than what it says:** MOO-32 v6's
published cap row charges **nothing** against the $3,000,000 for a ceiling-refused election, which is this
rule and not the as-drafted twelve-month hold — so **the sentence is what makes the published 78.19
percent true rather than an improvement on it.** Worth **$65,473** of peak charge, **+2.18** points of the
cap and about **one** point of take-up headroom; the gross convention would have shown 8.86 points and
overstated it by 4.1x. **Under-inclusive in four further cases (MOO-121's M2) — §7 item 75.**

**Item 4 (the F1 clone in D 2) — E6 and E7. The priority of the five, and the one MOO-121 attacked
hardest.**

- **E6 re-keys the trigger to the fact** — *"Where the certified subsidy determined for an election
  exceeds $170,000"* — so the notice duty no longer waits on a determination the Board may never make.
  That is the Director's string.
- **The repair.** Re-keying stranded the next six words. *"The determination"* had an antecedent: the
  Board's determination *"that it may not accept an election"*, named in the clause E6 strikes. Without a
  repair the notice's required content would have included **no statement that the election is refused**
  — a dollar figure, the subsection B rights and a price list — *"the reasons for it"* would have become
  the actuarial reasons for the **amount**, and the review right would have moved from the refusal to the
  subsidy computation. It now reads *"written notice of the Board's determination that it may not accept
  the election, of the reasons for that determination."* **This notice is the only statutory exit for the
  refused cohort**: 1.2339 expected refusals, **6.29 percent** of the live applicant set of 19.6304, with
  no waiting-list route (D 5 is keyed to insufficient **headroom**, not to the per-election ceiling).
- **E7 is the Director's parity answer**, and it closes the half of MOO-121's **S1** that §7 item 59
  already stated: the clock read *"30 days after the Board determines the certified subsidy"* and
  **nothing in the bill gives the Board a deadline for determining a certified subsidy** — subsection C's
  30 days reach the three clause amounts, D 4's reach eligibility, D 3's reach the Director of Planning
  and Budget. It now reads *"no later than 30 days after the member's application is completed"*, which
  is the clock subsection C's own refusal notice uses, so **both refusal notices run on one clock keyed to
  a fact.** One word is deliberately unconformed — the sentence otherwise names *"the applicant"* — and
  that is **§7 item 77**.

**Item 5 (D 6's cancellation notice) — E8, enacted in full, and my narrowing of it was wrong.** I had
enacted the standard-cost limb only, on the stated premise that D 6's third sentence already supplied the
30 days and the review route. MOO-121's **S3** re-read that sentence and the premise fails twice: the 30
days bound the **recertification** notice, which is a different notice with different content (the amounts
as recertified and the reasons for the recertification), and the review route runs to *"the
recertification"*, not to the cancellation — which operates *"by force of statute"* (*"the member's
election **is cancelled**"*) and so is doubtfully *"a determination of the Board"* at M 2's gateway at
all. The directed words did real work: they deemed the cancellation reviewable and gave the notice a
deadline. **Both are enacted in the Director's own words.** The one premise of mine that held is the
refund limb: store revision 36's words reach *"a refund required by this subdivision"*, which includes
sentence 4's refund, at 60 days with the adverse-tax fallback. **The *expressio unius* worry I recorded
against the review limb is answered by E2**, which now reaches a failure as well as a determination, so
the express grant in D 6 is no longer the only one of its kind in the section.

## 3. MOO-101 section B — clause (vii), and the edit that is not there

**E9 enacts the Director's answer (B).** Clause (vii) now tests *"the least of the member's maximum
purchasable amount and the amount specified in clause (ii) of subsection C, each determined as of the date
the member files that application"*. Three things are worth recording about it.

1. **The premise of the commission did not hold, and the Director was told so before answering.** Section
   B was commissioned because clause (vii) tested a quantity the member may not purchase, and so would
   admit the sub-month purchase MOO-87 option (c) barred. **It would not.** The advance clause (vii)
   measures is capped by the member's remaining shortfall and does **not** scale with the quantity
   credited: crediting four years to a member who is ten days short moves her unreduced date by ten days.
   **Clause (vii) as it stood already refused her.** Fiscal turned that into a proof — *0 of 5,552 cells
   differ, maximum difference 0.000000000000 months, 0.0000 expected elections* — with advance-to-shortfall
   ratios of 1.0 for Plan 1 and exactly 0.5 for Plan 2, which is the Rule-of-90 halving. **So E9 is a
   clarity edit, not a cure**, and the Director took it on that basis.
2. **Why (B) and not the commissioned form (A).** Option (A) — the least of clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) —
   drops limb (a) of the defined term, the member's own § 51.1-142.2 entitlement. Fiscal measured both:
   option (A) tests a **different** amount in **224 of 5,552 cells** (0.7245 live, 0.5167 admitted
   expected elections), exceeding what the member may buy by up to **12 months**, and changes **no**
   clause (vii) decision in any cell, the band where the forms differ and the band where the one-month bar
   bites being disjoint. **Option (A) costs nothing and is simply the text that computes an advance off
   credit the member cannot buy — in 224 places — which is the defect section B exists to cure.**
3. **Clause (vi) is unchanged, and the question was answered expressly: no.** Three reasons. The bill
   contains exactly **three** lowercase uses of *"maximum purchasable amount"* — its definition's final
   sentence, clause (vi), and clause (vii) — so after E9 clause (vi) is the term's only unqualified
   operative consumer and re-keying it too would leave the definition and the *"does not limit"* sentence
   with nothing to govern. Re-keying clause (vi) would also make it **self-satisfying**, because crediting
   clause (ii) brings the member to her unreduced date by definition, so the window test would screen
   nobody. MOO-121's null result 4 verifies the asymmetry admits nobody: where clause (ii) ≤ the maximum
   amount, clause (ii) reaches the unreduced date as of the **filing** date, which is on or before the
   first day of the following month, so clause (vi) passes on clause (ii) wherever it passes on the
   maximum; and where clause (ii) exceeds it the two are the same number.

**Section B edit 2 is withdrawn on the Director's answer (A), and the record is corrected.** Edit 2 would
have had clause (ii) *"expressed in months and portions of months"* — **keep** the fraction — against
store revision 32's enacted *"any fraction of a month … being counted as a whole month"* — round **up**.
Opposite instructions to the same words, and edit 2's stated reason (*"the draft states no rounding
convention"*) was not accurate against the live text. Store revision 33 then re-expressed the rule as
*"any fraction of a month **in the number so determined** being counted as a whole month"* — the same rule
with its referent named — so the answer is unaffected by the rebase. **Price of the choice: zero on the
authorised cohort**, because the engine advances age and service in exact twelfths, so every shortfall it
produces is already a whole number of months and the round-up never bites on a single cell. The round-up
is paid only by a day-exact member the model never produces, bounded above by one month of credit.

**MOO-98's M2 string is withdrawn** — see §1.

## 4. MOO-98's M1, enacted in form (B), and the amendment that makes it work

**The finding was right.** Subsection C imposes **two** 30-day duties — to determine the three clause
amounts, and (with the restoration) to give the refusal notice — and neither carried a consequence for
breach, where **D 1, D 3, D 4 and G 4 each carry one in the same words**: *"shall state every such delay
in the report required by subsection J."* And because M 2's window runs *"within 30 days after **the
notice** of the determination"*, a Board that sent nothing left no window open at all.

**Form (B) is enacted because the Director answered item 35 (a)**, which puts the second duty back and
gives form (B)'s second limb a referent. **E14**, at the end of subsection C:

> The Board shall state in the report required by subsection J every failure to make a determination, or
> to give a notice, required by this subsection within the period this subsection allows for it. Where the
> Board does not give the notice required by this subsection within that period, the member may seek
> review under subsection M of the Board's failure to give it at any time before the Board gives it, and
> the period within which the member may seek review of a determination under this subsection runs from
> the date the Board gives that notice.

**Two departures from the drafted and reviewed words, both recorded.**

1. **MOO-121's m1 is cured in the sentence rather than left.** Both held forms read *"shall state every
   failure to determine the amounts required by this subsection **within the period required by this
   subsection** in the report required by subsection J"*, where *"within the period"* can attach to
   *"state"* instead of to *"failure to determine"* — and in form (B) *"the"* period was singular against
   two different periods. The report phrase is moved to the front and the period is keyed distributively
   (*"the period this subsection allows for it"*), which is the structure the four provisions it is
   modelled on achieve with *"every **such** delay."*
2. **MOO-121's M5 is cured by an amendment to M 2 that is wider than MOO-98's finding — E2's second
   limb — and it is mine.** Form (B) confers review of a **failure to act**, and M 2's gateway ran only to
   *"a determination of the Board under this section."* A failure is not a determination, so the right
   would have run into a gateway that excludes it: the F4 defect displaced from the class to the subject
   matter. M 2's first sentence now reaches *"a failure of the Board to make a determination or to give a
   notice within a period required by this section"*, **and supplies the window for it** — *"in the case
   of such a failure, at any time before the Board makes the determination or gives the notice"* — because
   a right whose 30 days run from a notice nobody sent is not a right. **This reaches every period in the
   section, not only subsection C's.** That is deliberate: the narrow form would leave the identical hole
   next door, and D 1, D 3, D 4 and G 4's report lines have the same gap in their own remedy. It is
   **§7 item 76** so that the Director can narrow it, and it is one clause out.

**Red Team's own words for the second limb are not taken**, in either pass. They drafted *"the notice
shall be treated as given on the last day of that period for the purposes of subsection M"*, which opens
M 2's window and **starts its 30 days running against a member who has received nothing**, so the remedy
can expire before she knows it exists. Form (B) gives her review of the **failure** at any time and her
window on the determination from **actual** notice. A one-sentence substitution if the Director prefers
the deeming.

**Who / what / by when / or else, on the enacted form.** Actor: the Board. Object: the subsection J report
line, which already carries D 1's, D 3's, D 4's and G 4's delays in the same form, so this adds a row and
no machinery. Deadline: the subsection J report date. Or else: reconsideration under subsection M,
unbounded until the notice is given, and judicial review preserved by M 2's savings sentence as conformed.

## 5. MOO-101 section C — items 35 and 26

**Item 35 is answered (a) and the restoration is E13.** The conflict was real and I did not resolve it by
drafting choice: MOO-101's commission directs *"[d]o not delete subsection C's zero bar in this
revision"*, store revision 38 deleted it on the Director's later routing on MOO-87 (*"the call is
yours"*), the routing was later and the commission more specific, and MOO-101's card of 12 October did not
re-ask the item. **I left store revision 38's enactment undisturbed and restored nothing until the
Director answered**, because restoring deleted operative text is as much a policy act as deleting it.

**What went back, and in what form.** The two sentences are restored **verbatim as they stood in store
revision 37**, immediately before the deletion, in their original position as subsection C's third and
fourth sentences — which is to say with store revision 24's standard-cost limb and store revision 30's
**fact-keyed** trigger and *"30 days after the member's application is completed"* clock, not with
revision 22's original *"Where the Board determines…"* trigger. Because § 51.1-142.4 is a wholly new
section the restoration carries **no markup**: the words are simply present again, exactly as their
deletion carried none. A reader comparing store revisions 42 and 43 must read this record.

**It does not collide with store revision 41's third sentence.** The bar fires where the clause (ii)
amount **is zero**; revision 41's sentence governs where clause (ii) **has no value at all** and does not
limit. No member is in both classes, neither sentence refers to the other, and nothing of revision 41 is
reversed or renumbered. The corrected proposition is in §7 item 35: **for every person subsection C
addresses, clause (ii) either exceeds zero or does not limit her, and the Board must say which in
writing.**

**What the restoration does not do, stated plainly.** It does not make the bar reachable. Clause (v) of
*"eligible member"* screens out the member whose clause (ii) is zero before subsection C opens *"An
eligible member may purchase"*, which is store revision 38's paragraph b and §5.20's Check 2, and MOO-32
measured the bar as refusing **0.0000 of 19.6304**. **The restored bar is a belt beside a brace.** What
the restoration does buy is a **named, reviewable notice** for a case the rest of the section reaches only
through subdivision D 4, a referent for E5's cross-reference (MOO-121's **S2**: before it, D 7 would have
pointed at a notice subsection C did not require — the word *"notice"* appearing **zero** times in its 954
characters), and the second of the two duties form (B) reports on.

**Item 26 re-opens and closes in the same revision**, in the form it already carried, as the answer
directed. Its first half is answered on MOO-101 — keep both halves of revision 30's cure, the two §6.0-25
deletions are **not** taken — and its second half (the further-application statement) stays out. **No
edit.** E10 and E11 restore the consistency ground that answer relied on: after them every surviving
applicant notice in the section states the subsection B right **and** its price, which is what MOO-84's F6
classified as a consistency defect rather than a policy choice.

## 6. MOO-101 section D and MOO-98's S3 — the sunset

**E15, one word.** Enactment 3 clause (i) continues *"every refund, payment, **notice**, determination,
rescission, restoration, and reinstatement required by § 51.1-142.4."* It removes the argument that the
notice duties revision 30 repaired expire with the section while the elections they protect do not, and it
does real work on subdivision I 2, whose notice and determination are now expressly continued.

**E16 and E17 — MOO-98's S3 on the Director's answer, Red Team's variant 1.** The gap S3 found is real:
clause (i)'s leading limb is keyed to *"every election **accepted** before that date"*, and subsection M
expires regardless, so the applicant who files 1 May 2033, is told on 31 May that two certifications are
missing and cures on 10 July is owed a determination whose notice falls due five weeks after the section
expired, with no reconsideration route and no waiting-list notice. **Variant 2 was not taken and the
Director was told why:** it closes intake on 1 January 2033, which solves the problem by taking six months
of intake away from members, and it leaves D 3's annual-reconfirmation tail running. The new clause (v):

> …and (v) every duty of the Board to determine and to give notice under § 51.1-142.4 in respect of an
> application filed before that date, and subsection M of that section as it applies to such a
> determination, shall continue in effect until discharged, the application is withdrawn, or the applicant
> dies, and for the purposes of every such determination and notice subdivision B 4 a of § 51.1-142.2 as
> amended by this act shall continue in effect as though it had not expired.

**Two additions to the reviewed string, both MOO-121's and both taken.**

- **M1.** The notices D 2, D 3, D 4, D 5 and D 6 require each state *"the standard cost … of the service
  credit … the applicant is eligible to purchase"*, *"standard cost"* is defined in subsection A by
  reference to **subdivision B 4 a of § 51.1-142.2**, and enactment 3's lead-in expires subdivision B 4.
  Clause (i) solves exactly this for accepted elections — *"in each case as though those provisions had
  not expired"* — and clause (v) had no equivalent, which under *expressio unius* would say the omission
  was deliberate. The savings limb is added. The underlying **amount** was always computable, which is why
  MOO-121 rated it moderate; the dangling definition is closed anyway, because a Board that omits the
  figure breaches a duty clause (v) keeps alive.
- **Null result 2's outer bound.** Clauses (ii) and (iii) are self-terminating; clause (v) terminated only
  on performance, which leaves the Board a duty it can never discharge if the applicant withdraws (D 3
  expressly contemplates *"the applicant withdraws it"*) or dies after expiry. *"the application is
  withdrawn, or the applicant dies"* is added. **A calendar outer bound is deliberately not added**: it
  would cut off the very applicant the clause exists to protect.

**E16 conforms the series connector**, moving *"and"* from clause (iv) to clause (v). MOO-121's null
result 9 confirms the semicolon keeps clause (v) parallel to clauses (i) to (iv) rather than making it a
sub-part of clause (iv). **Null result 2 also disposes of the overlap I had ranked first for attack:**
clause (v) is **not** surplusage against clause (i), because clause (i)'s rights-and-periods limb is keyed
to *"a member"* and its duty limbs to accepted elections, so neither reaches an applicant whose election
was never accepted; and on the competing reading the negative implication is harmless, because no refund
and no payment is owed on an unaccepted application.

## 11. Ambiguities resolved in store revision 44 — what would otherwise be §6.0-43

1. ***"The determination"* in subdivision D 2 now has an express antecedent.** Before E6 the phrase relied

   determination it is about. The review limb at the end of the sentence takes the same antecedent, which
   is what keeps the review right attached to the **refusal** rather than drifting to the subsidy
   computation.
2. **Two refusal notices, one clock, one fact.** Subsection C's notice and subdivision D 2's both run 30
   days from the completion of the application, which is the only date in the section that is fixed by the
   applicant's own act and recorded in the certification. **No notice duty in subsection C or D now waits
   on an act for which the bill sets no deadline.**
3. **A failure to act is reviewable, and the window for reviewing it does not run from silence.** E2
   answers both halves: the gateway reaches the failure, and the 30 days do not begin until the Board
   cures it. E14 says the same thing for subsection C specifically and adds the report line, so the
   member's remedy and the General Assembly's metric point at the same event.
4. **The restored bar and store revision 41's third sentence are complementary, not alternative.** *Is
   zero* and *has no value* are different states of the same limb; a member cannot be in both; and the
   Board must state in the certification which one applies.
5. **The standard cost of an amount is the aggregate of the standard cost of its parts** (E12), scoped to
   § 51.1-142.4 only, so the unit rate subdivision B 4 b needs is untouched. **What this does not say** is
   that the cost of a portion of a year is proportionate; that is MOO-121's m2 and the chapter's *"each
   year or portion thereof"* idiom governs it (§7 item 80).
6. **A filing date, once retained, is not divested.** E1 states the retention without an expiry, so the
   negative implication MOO-121's M3 identified does not arise, and D 3's overlapping retention and this
   one are a union rather than a conflict.
7. **The sunset's surviving duties terminate on performance, withdrawal or death** — and the definition
   they depend on survives with them. Clause (v) carries both, so there is no case in which the Board owes
   a notice it cannot compute or a duty it cannot discharge.

### 12.1 The correction to this record's own headline, and it is the one to read

This record says at §1 and §10 that **this revision carries no fiscal event** and that **no figure moves.**
That is true **on the model's reading of clause (vii) and false on the other**, and the reviewer measured
the other. The load-bearing proposition is that subsection C's *"clause (ii) does not limit"* savings
**carries into clause (vii) of *"eligible member"***. The statute does not say so; the model reaches it by
arithmetic (`need_months_at` returns `INF` and `min(cap, INF) == cap`). If the savings does not carry,
clause (vii) cannot be applied to the no-value class at all and D 4 refuses them:

| figure | published | alternate, class excluded | move |
|---|---|---|---|
| participants, central | 18.3965 | **18.3706** | −0.0259 |
| cap utilisation, central | 78.1872 % | **78.0258 %** | −0.1614 pp |
| net trust cost, rung 12, PV | $1,321,112 | **$1,318,273** | −$2,838 |

**All three move by more than the published precision**, and the move is a quarter of one admitted member.
**So the correct form of the claim is conditional, not absolute:** *no figure moves on the model's reading
of clause (vii), and the reading is an assumption the statute does not state.* That is a reason to state
the assumption, not to restate the package — and the drafting cure is MOO-130's **S3**, which gives clause
(vii) the no-value savings the other two consumers of clause (ii) already have.

**Fiscal's cellwise proof is sound for what it tests and silent on this.** It compares form A with form B
of clause (vii), and both sides were computed with `min(cap, INF) == cap`, so on exactly the 24 cells at
issue the two forms agree trivially. The reviewer verified `flips.sum() == 0` and says so.

**The count answer MOO-101 required of me does not change:** section B moves the participating count by
**zero members on both edits**, and edit 2 was withdrawn so the per-member quantity does not move either.
What changes is the width of the sentence that sits beside it.

## 13. A stranded-designator sweep of §0's record apparatus — reported, not cured, and not operative text

Run against the live body (`bd703cd6`, store revision 48/49) while confirming that this cut's edits had
survived three rebases. **It found nothing wrong with the bill's operative text and nothing wrong with any
cross-reference in §9.** It is recorded here because §0's designator apparatus is a by-product of the §0 and
§3 moves that MOO-101's own section E directed, and because the next run to hold the file should see it.

**First, a hypothesis of mine that was wrong, and I am recording it as wrong.** On first reading I took
designators of the form `§0.0000000000000000e` to be numeric corruption — a float coercion that had eaten a
label. **They are not.** §0's scheme is deliberate: a designator is `§0.` followed by *N* zeros, one zero
added per store revision, so that newest sorts first and the designators are unique and strictly descending.
A lettered suffix marks a sub-point. `§0.x` is the scheme's own placeholder for "this revision's designator"
and is used 30 times in the bill and 61 times in the two companions as a deliberate convention. **Nothing is
corrupted and nothing should be renumbered.**

**What the sweep does find.** The bill cites **25** distinct §0 designators. Nineteen of them resolve to a
banner in the bill or in one of the two revision-history companions. **Five resolve to nothing in any of the
three documents:**

| designator | how it is cited in the bill |
|---|---|
| `§0.00000000000` | the § 51.1-155 reference sweep — *"thirty references in Chapter 1 of Title 51.1"* |
| `§0.00000000000a` | *"says so plainly and names the process fix"* — the dropped-direction process note |
| `§0.0000000000b` | the crediting-date point — *"but the cure is administration the member has to get right"* |
| `§0.000000000000000` | *"alone would have been a defect"* |
| `§0.000000000000000000` | a bare trailing citation |

A sixth candidate, `§0.00000000000000000000000000a`, is **not a defect**: it appears inside backticks as an
illustrative example of the citation form, not as a citation.

**Why this is not a defect in the bill and is not cured here.** None of the five is a reference to operative
text, to an amended section, or to anything this cut changed; §9's thirteen checks covered every operative
cross-reference and stand as reported. These five are internal pointers between record banners, and the most
likely cause is that the banners they name were moved to a companion and re-designated, or folded into a stub,
by one of the moves §0 records. **Curing them means reading the two companions against the bill and either
restoring the designator or re-pointing the citation — a record repair, not an amendment.** It is routed to
[MOO-148](/MOO/issues/MOO-148) as housekeeping for a run that holds MOO-42, and it should become a §7 item
rather than an edit to the operative text. **Nothing in the bill's operative text turns on it, no figure turns
on it, and it is below the threshold at which it should delay anything.**

## 1. The five edits, verbatim — drafted and PARKED, enacted nowhere

All five are repairs to words the Director's five answers put into the text. **None changes which member passes either definitional test, which member is admitted, or which member is refused.** One changes an amount the Commonwealth pays, in the Commonwealth's favour, and that is E1 — the one the answer's own words required and my drafting did not deliver.

### E1 — M-1. Item 54's valuation limb gains the death branch's recertification limb

FIND (unique in the live body):

> `valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2. Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made`

READ:

> `valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2, and shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase. Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made`

**Why this is drafting and not policy.** The Director's answer was *"extend to subdivision 3, for parity with G 4's own death branch."* The death branch does three things in one sentence: credits the months fully paid for at pilot cost; **recertifies the certified subsidy to reflect that credit**; and refunds the excess. **I enacted the first limb only, and called the result parity.** It was not parity. Without the recertification the amount settled stays at `min(redetermined, the amount last certified and reserved)` — a figure keyed to the whole certification — so the Commonwealth could settle a subsidy for 19 months of credit when the member bought 9. Importing the recertification limb is what makes the enacted text do what the answer said.

**What it does to the money.** It scales the settlement down to the credit actually credited. Pass 12's worked case was **$106,253 average on the authorised basis and $170,000 at the statutory per-election cap** paid for a fraction of the credit; E1 removes that. **It also reduces, without eliminating, the cap exposure pass 12 identified** — see §8.

**The refund limb is deliberately NOT imported.** The death branch also refunds the excess of amounts paid over the cost of the credit credited. In the rescission case that would be a payment to the member or her employer that no answer authorised, and subsection G 4's own refund machinery and item 50's buy-back already occupy that ground. **Drafted in §7 as item 92 with a recommendation, enacted nowhere.**

### E2 — M-4. The rescission sentence's operative verb gets an object that exists

FIND:

> `shall restore the service credit reduced under it, to the extent this subdivision provides, no later than 60 days`

READ:

> `shall restore or credit service credit as this subdivision provides, no later than 60 days`

**A subdivision 3 determination reduces nothing** — G 3 credits the months paid for and releases the reservation; it never had more to take away. So for half the determinations item 54 brought within the rescission sentence, *"restore the service credit reduced under it"* commanded the Board to restore a quantity of zero. *"To the extent this subdivision provides"* does find item 54's valuation limb, so the machinery functioned; the defect was in the verb and its object, not in the result. **This is the reviewer's own fix text, and it is 24 characters shorter than what it replaces.**

### E3 — M-3. The confining sentence's trigger date gets a referent everywhere the definition is applied

FIND:

> `on or before the date as of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined.`

READ (the FIND text, then a new sentence):

> `on or before the date as of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined. Where this section does not state a date as of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined, that date is, for the purposes of the preceding sentence, the date on which the Board makes the certification, recertification, determination, statement, or other decision in which that date is applied.`

**The trigger date was mine**, substituted for the candidate text's *"the date as of which the determination is made"* because *"the determination"* in a subsection A definition would most naturally have been read as the determination under subdivision G 2 and so imported G 2 into a definition. Pass 12 agrees that was an improvement and shows that **it relocated the indeterminacy rather than removing it**: four of the places the definition is applied state no as-of date — clause (viii) of *"eligible member"*, the D 1 certification item, subsection E's last limb, and G 3's second sentence. E3 names the date in those four and names the actor who fixes it. **It is not vagueness and pass 12 says so** — this is benefit-eligibility administration, not a penal or speech provision, so *Grayned v. City of Rockford*, 408 U.S. 104 (1972) has no purchase. It was a construction gap with no stated standard, which is a drafting defect at moderate severity, and it is closed.

## 6.0-47 Ambiguities resolved in the five edits

1. **E1: *"recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited"* — which credit?** The credit E1's own sentence directs, i.e. the months fully paid for, valued at pilot cost. Resolved by using the death branch's words *"so credited"* unaltered so that the referent is the immediately preceding limb in the same sentence, which is how the death branch itself reads.
2. **E1: does the imported recertification run before or after the 90-day redetermination?** G 4 already provides that *"the Board shall make every recertification required by this subdivision before making the redetermination required by the following sentence."* **E1 needs no ordering words because that sentence already supplies them**, and it is the reason E1 is drafted as a recertification rather than as a direct cap on the amount settled.
3. **E2: does *"restore or credit"* widen the Board's duty?** No. The extent is fixed by *"as this subdivision provides"*, which is the same limiter the words it replaces carried. The change is from a verb with a zero-extent object to a verb with the object the subdivision actually provides.
4. **E3: which decision fixes the date where the section states none?** The decision in which the date is applied, made by the Board. The alternative — the date of the application for which the decision is made — was rejected because the member's own filing date would let her fix her eligibility by the timing of a form.
5. **Residue, not cured.** The rescission notice sentence requires notice *"of the service credit restored"*. After E2 the Board may *credit* rather than restore, and the notice sentence does not say *"or credited"*. **Four words would cure it and they are not enacted**, because the notice sentence is not one the Director's answers reached and because the notice duty is discharged in substance either way — the Board must state the credit it has given. Recorded so that it is found deliberately rather than later.
6. **E5: *"that subdivision G 2 requires"* — does it exclude a deferral G 2 permits?** Yes, deliberately. G 2 does not permit a discretionary deferral; it requires one in the ordinary case and item 46 disapplies the requirement in the pendency case. A deeming list that reached a deferral the section does not authorise would deem away a collection the section never allowed.

## 4. Two findings that do not hold as the reviewer states them — with verbatim authority

**I re-opened both sources rather than accepting a correction to my own record.** One correction runs against the reviewer. The other runs against the reviewer **and restores a claim of mine the reviewer had withdrawn for me**, which is the more important of the two because the Director's item 49(i) answer rests on it.

### 4.1 S-4's mechanism does not operate, because G 4's own tolling sentence reaches the 120-day bound

S-4's engine is that *"M 2's tolling reaches only 'the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date and of any period within which the member must act' — it does not toll the Board's 120 days,"* so the determination is **forced** to take effect at day 120 while the Board still has 90 days to decide the reconsideration.

**That is right about subsection M 2 and wrong about the bill, because the tolling the Director enacted as part of item 28 is in G 4 and is wider.** Verbatim from the live body:

> *"No period stated in subdivision 2 or in this subdivision, **whether it is a period within which the Board is required to act or a period within which a determination is required to take effect**, runs while such an application is pending or **while a request the filing of which tolls the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date under subsection M is pending**."*

A request for reconsideration under subsection M 2 is such a request — M 2 provides in terms that its filing *"tolls the running of the member's final qualifying retirement date"* — and G 4 defines when it is pending (*"from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board acts upon it"*). **So the 120-day bound does not run while her reconsideration is pending.** Run the reviewer's own clocks: determination date 1 February, notice mailed 1 April, request filed 4 April — 62 days of the 120 have run, and they stop. **Nothing forces the determination to take effect, and on the reviewer's facts the Board reverses before it ever does.**

**What survives, and it is still worth fixing.** Two classes are untouched by the tolling: the member who requests reconsideration **after** the determination has already taken effect, and the member whose determination the Board takes effect during the pendency because tolling extends a deadline without prohibiting earlier action. In both, she has drawn a reduced allowance, she wins, and **no provision requires the Board to restore the credit, states a deadline for doing so, or pays her the difference** — the rescission machinery items 49 and 54 built runs on disability approval and death only. **Confirmed in part, re-stated narrowly, and carded at item 88.**

### 4.2 § 51.1-156 H is mandatory in exactly the class item 49(i) excludes — the reviewer quoted its first sentence only

Pass 12 corrects the objective's claim that H *requires* the Board to waive, quoting: *"For good cause shown, the Board **may** waive the ninety-day notification periods set forth in subsections A and B."* **That sentence is quoted accurately. It is the first of two.** Re-read on `law.lis.virginia.gov` on 12 October 2026, § 51.1-156 H reads in full:

> *"H. For good cause shown, the Board may waive the ninety-day notification periods set forth in subsections A and B. For purposes of this section, good cause **shall** exist and the Board **shall waive** such ninety-day notification periods if (i) the member would otherwise qualify for disability retirement but for failing to comply with the requirements of subsection A or B and (ii) the Medical Board, acting solely in its own discretion after reviewing objective medical evidence of the disability and its cause, certifies that: (a) the disability and its cause existed on the date the member's employment was terminated, (b) the member had no knowledge of the existence of the disability and its cause at any time within ninety days after the date the member's employment was terminated, and (c) the member could not, with reasonable inquiry, have ascertained the existence of the disability and its cause within ninety days after the date the member's employment was terminated."*

**The second sentence is mandatory and it is bounded by the Medical Board's own certification.** So the class is not one the Code *lets* the Board admit; it is the class the Code **commands** the Board to admit — and it is defined by the member having had **no knowledge** of her disability and being **unable with reasonable inquiry** to have found it.

**Three consequences.**

1. **M-6 is not a cheap optional carve-out and is not moderate.** Item 49(i), as the Director answered it, denies the rescission remedy to a member whose late application the Board had **no discretion to refuse**. On the better reading the bill takes the remedy away in the one class where the member is, by statutory definition, blameless. I would rate it serious.
2. **S-2 is sharper, not softer.** Its failure scenario is built on the H waiver, and the waiver in that scenario is compelled. The member's plea — that clause (ii) disapplied subdivision 2 to her election by operation of law, so the determination was made without authority — is made against a statute that required the Board to let her application in.
3. **My own earlier record was right and the reviewer's correction of it is withdrawn.** The store revision 42 record said H *requires* the Board to waive for a disability the member could not have known of. **That is what the second sentence says.** I accepted the correction in a comment before re-opening the source; this is the re-opening, and the citation is quoted in full above so that nobody has to take either of us on trust.

**Neither correction changes an enacted word.** Both change what the Director is choosing between, which is why they are here and in the card's own text rather than in a footnote.

## 8. The money, and what is routed rather than asserted

**No priced quantity moves on the five enacted edits.** No admission test, no clause (v) to (viii) determination and no subsection C clause (ii) cap changes; E2, E3, E4 and E5 touch the form, the referent and the savings of duties the trust and the appropriation already carry.

**E1 moves an amount, in the Commonwealth's favour, and the figure is not mine to state.** Pass 12's fiscal challenge is that item 54 added a **second, disjoint exposed population** — the E-failure, non-completion member who reaches G 3 — to a mechanism the model prices only for the F-failure population, and that **the model contains no non-completion parameter at all**. On the reviewer's own per-member arithmetic the charge per recalled member with the 20 percent contingency is **$117,392** against **$114,482** of headroom to the $3,000,000 limitation — so a **5.3 percent** non-completion share takes worst-case cap utilisation from 96.2 percent to 100.0 percent, 10 percent takes it to 103.4, and 25 percent to 114.2, while **expected cost stays trivial, about $1,800.**

**E1 reduces the per-member charge in that arithmetic**, because the amount settled is now recertified down to the credit actually bought rather than left at the full certification. **It does not follow that the cap no longer binds, and I am not going to assert that it does** — the per-member figure, the share, and the utilisation are Fiscal's to compute. **Routed to [@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50)**, with the non-completion parameter named as the thing the model does not contain. **No figure in the package is retracted, and no re-run is claimed to have happened.**

**Pass 12's own statement bears repeating because it is the honest form of *"no figure moves"*:** that claim is true only as against a model that cannot represent the case. **It is the cap that moves, not the cost.**

plus a new sentence at the end of subdivision J 1:

> <u>Where a rescission under subdivision G 4 occurs after the Board has made the last report required by this subdivision, the Board shall make one further report, limited to that rescission and its consequences, no later than the first December 1 following the rescission.</u>

**Recommend both.** (a) alone leaves the duty perpetual through limb (b); (b) alone leaves it perpetual through limb (a). **The death limb is why limb (b) has no outer bound** — a parker who never retires stays inside clause (i) until she dies, and a member aged 52 in 2033 may die in 2075. The one-further-report form is the only shape I could find that keeps the information and lets the duty end: the Board can state on any 1 December whether limb (a) is satisfied, which it cannot do for *"the last rescission."*

### Item 86 — S-2 with M-6. The late-filed approval, and the class the Code COMPELS the Board to admit

**(a) The carve-out, bounded to § 51.1-156 H's mandatory limb** — in the rescission sentence:

> … upon an application filed no later than the date on which the determination took effect<u>, or upon an application as to which the Board was required by subsection H of § 51.1-156 to waive the period allowed by subsection A or B of that section</u>, …

**(b) The express saving**, as a new sentence after the rescission sentence:

> <u>A determination under subdivision 2 or 3 that has taken effect is not affected by an approval of the member for a disability retirement allowance upon an application filed after the date on which the determination took effect, except as this subdivision provides for the rescission of the determination.</u>

**Recommend (a) and (b) together.** (b) alone resolves the contradiction S-2 found by cutting clause (ii) down — which is defensible drafting and **leaves the blameless member with nothing.** (a) alone leaves clause (ii) unqualified for every other late filing. **Together they say what I believe the Director's item 49(i) answer meant: bound the remedy by the filing date, except where the Code took the filing date out of the member's hands.**

**Why (a) is bounded to the second sentence of H rather than to any waiver.** The discretionary first sentence is the Board's own choice, which it can make with this consequence in view; the second sentence is not a choice at all, and the Medical Board's certification — no knowledge, and no ability with reasonable inquiry to find out — is the tightest boundary available anywhere in the chapter. The alternative drafting, *"as to which the Board has waived a period under subsection H of § 51.1-156,"* reaches both limbs and is one line shorter; **it is the option to take if the Director would rather not distinguish.**

### Item 87 — S-3. Clause (iii), Board error, gets the rescission route the other two clauses have

In the rescission sentence:

> Where a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect and the member is thereafter approved … or thereafter dies in a case to which clause (i) of this subdivision applies<u>, or the Board thereafter determines that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board</u>, the Board shall rescind … no later than 60 days after the date on which the member is so approved<u>,</u> or dies<u>, or the Board makes that determination</u>, …

**Recommend enacting.** This is the one of the three clause-events where the equities run hardest against the Board — it concedes its own error and the member keeps the reduction — and it is the only one the nine edits left out. **Subdivision B 4 f's carve-out is untouched** (*"A determination under this subdivision is not an error of the Board for the purposes of subdivision G 4"*), so this cannot be turned into a challenge to a B 4 f cost determination.

### Item 88 — S-4 as corrected. The member who wins on reconsideration after the determination has taken effect

New sentence in G 4:

> <u>Where a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 that has taken effect is reversed or modified on reconsideration under subsection M or on judicial review, the Board shall restore the service credit reduced under it, and shall recertify and settle the certified subsidy as this subdivision requires, no later than 60 days after the reversal or modification, and the next payment of the member's retirement allowance shall include every amount that would have been payable to the member had the determination not taken effect.</u>

**Recommend enacting.** **Read §4.1 first**: the reviewer's forced-effect mechanism does not operate, because the tolling the Director enacted as item 28 stops the 120-day bound while her reconsideration is pending. What survives is the member who asks **after** effect, or whose determination the Board takes effect during the pendency anyway. For her there is today **no duty to restore, no deadline, and no arrears** — and the arrears limb above is the same device subsection G 2's third sentence already uses, so it introduces no new mechanism.

### Item 89 — M-2. One word: *"this definition"* → *"this section"*

> <u>For the purposes of this section</u> the member may retire under subsection A or C of § 51.1-155.1 only where …

**Recommend enacting.** On my reading it is operatively inert — the confinement has nothing to bite on in *"qualifying retirement"*, which asks about a retirement that has actually happened. **But that reading is exactly what a reader who sees the sentence in one definition and not its twin will argue against**, by *expressio unius*, and it is cheaper to spend a word than to defend the asymmetry. **It is carded and not enacted because the asymmetry is the ground I gave the Director for the text they approved**, and reversing my own stated ground is not a drafting repair.

### Item 90 — M-5. The offset bar, and the duplicate item 46 creates

**(a) Narrow the limb:**

> … on account of an involuntary separation, of a rescission or restoration under this subdivision, or of <u>a failure of the member to retire in a qualifying retirement</u> …

**(b) Or, better, authorise the one offset that is needed and leave the limb alone:**

> <u>Nothing in this subdivision or in subsection F prevents the Board from applying a retirement allowance paid to the member for a month against a disability retirement allowance payable to the member for the same month.</u>

**Recommend (b) alone.** § 51.1-156 D allows a disability effective date up to 90 days before the notice is filed, so a member paid a service allowance during pendency and then approved retroactively has been paid twice for the same months; G 4's limb bars the Board from offsetting it, and subsection F's deeming list makes deferrals and refund-applications not-collections without authorising an offset. **(a) does the job by taking a protection away from every member to reach a duplicate a few will have; (b) reaches only the duplicate.** The money is small — pass 12 puts it at $1,300 to $2,500 per affected member on a headcount well under 0.1 expected — **and it falls on the trust fund, is reimbursed by nothing, and appears in no line of J 1.**

### Item 91 — G 3's second sentence still withholds the premise item 54's rescue runs on

> A member credited under this subdivision shall not be treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of the election. <u>This sentence does not apply where a determination under this subdivision is rescinded under subdivision 4.</u>

**Recommend enacting.** Pass 12 says the defect is a genuine ambiguity rather than a certainty — on rescission she is credited afresh *in G 4*, so she is arguably no longer *"a member credited under this subdivision"* — **and that it does not reach the certified-subsidy floor or the subsection C clause (ii) cap by the route I asked about.** It costs nothing: every member it reaches has already been approved for disability or has died.

### Item 92 — the refund limb E1 did not import

> … and <u>shall refund, to the member and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited</u>.

**Recommend enacting, as the other half of the parity the Director's item-54 answer asked for.** The death branch has this limb; E1's rescission limb now has the crediting and the recertification but not the refund, so a member who paid for 9.4 months and is credited with 9 keeps nothing back for the part-month. **It is a payment out and no answer authorised it, which is why it is here.**

### Item 93 — should G 4's bar and tolling follow the rescission to subdivision 3?

**Recommend leaving it.** The bar stops the Board making a **subdivision 2** determination while a disability application is pending. A subdivision 3 crediting is not a determination the Board chooses to make at a time of its choosing; it follows non-completion by the completion date. Carried from the store revision 42 card unanswered.

### Item 94 — should the § 30-19.1:7 statement quantify the two one-sided costs?

**Recommend yes.** Item 46 pays an allowance during pendency that the later determination may show was too large, and subsection F's no-collection limb means it is never recovered; item 50 makes the clause (ii) refund irrecoverable even where she buys her credit back. **Both were argued to the Director on exactly that basis and taken, so nothing here reopens either answer** — the only question is whether the fiscal statement names the amounts rather than leaving them to be found. Quantification is **[@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50)**'s, not mine. Carried from the store revision 42 card unanswered.

title: Pass 17 (MOO-152) disposition — the record for store revision 57: six repairs enacted, eight serious findings carded as §7 items 114 to 121
body:
# Pass 17 (MOO-152) disposition — the record for store revision 57 of `bill-text-s8`

**Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel. Pre-decisional.**

[MOO-152](/MOO/issues/MOO-152)'s pass 17 reviewed **store revision 52's thirteen edits** — the thirteen that enacted [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64)'s seven answers — and returned **0 fatal, 8 serious, 9 moderate, 5 minor**. This document is the record of what store revision 57 does with them.

**Store revision 57 enacts five repairs and no policy.** Every one of the five is a repair to words the Director's own answers put in, and **none changes which member passes either definitional test**. The eight serious findings are **policy and are carded, not drafted into the text** — seven of them as new §7 items 114 to 121, and S-7 as the upgraded ground for the existing item 103. **Four minor findings are record repairs and are applied.** One moderate (M-9) is held, with its reason. One moderate (M-8) and the whole of the fiscal challenge (S-8 / §4 of the review) are routed outside this lane.

**The review's own address for what it read:** `bill-text-s8` store revision 52, document revision `495176e8`. **This revision is written against store revision 56**, document revision `e81147bd` as first read and re-read at store revision 56 before the write, 520,122 characters — four store revisions later. Store revisions 53, 54, 55 and 56 **disturbed none of the six anchors**, each of which occurred exactly once in the live body. **Every anchor was re-verified against the live body before anything was written** (§6 below records the one finding that moved as a result).

---

## 1. The five repairs, verbatim

Each is a single-occurrence substitution in §1. The FIND string occurred exactly once in the live body and the ENACTED string zero times.

### R1 — M-1. The refund payee in the subdivision-3 rescission branch

The branch's three triggers include the member's **death**, and the death branch two sentences upstream — the sentence R1's own words were copied from in store revision 52 — pays *"the member's estate."*

**FIND**

> and shall refund, to the member and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited

**ENACTED**

> and shall refund, <u>to the member or, where the member has died, to the member's estate,</u> and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited

### R2 — M-1, second limb. The adverse-tax fallback had to yield to the death case

The fallback applies an unpayable refund *"to the purchase of additional service credit **for the member**."* Where the trigger is death there is no member to buy credit for, and a purchase of credit for a decedent is a § 401(a) / § 415(n) problem in its own right.

**FIND**

> The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost. Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made or took effect before the Board learned of an involuntary separation

**ENACTED**

> The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, <u>except that where the member has died the Board shall pay the whole of the refund to the member's estate and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid and shall apply no amount of it to the purchase of service credit, and except that in every other case,</u> to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence<u>,</u> the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost. Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made or took effect before the Board learned of an involuntary separation

**The anchor needed the trailing sentence.** This fallback sentence is **word-identical** to the death branch's own fallback in the same subdivision; it occurs twice, and the trailing words of the next sentence are what make the second occurrence addressable. **The death branch's own copy carries the same defect and I have not amended it** — it is pre-existing text no answer of the Director's reached. It is §7 item 120(b).

### R3 — M-2. The reinstatement deadline for a release made in accordance with D 7

Store revision 52's edit 7 extended reinstatement to a reservation *released in accordance with D 7* where a determination is later rescinded, reversed or modified. **The deadline was not extended with it.** Its fallback limb — *"60 days after the Board learns of the release"* — was written for an **erroneous** release the Board did not know about; for a release the Board itself made in accordance with D 7 it has always known, so the duty was breached on the day it arose. On the review's worked facts the deadline fell **two years before** the event that created the duty.

**FIND**

> no later than the date on which the certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision or, where no certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision, no later than 60 days after the Board learns of the release

**ENACTED**

> no later than the date on which the certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision or, where no certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision, <u>no later than 60 days after the rescission, reversal, or modification or, where the reservation was released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7 and no determination is rescinded, reversed, or modified,</u> no later than 60 days after the Board learns of the release

Both cases now have their own deadline and the two conditions are mutually exclusive on their face, so no reader has to choose between them.

### R4 — M-3. The arrears on a reversal had no vehicle in two of its own branches

Edit 6's arrears attach to *"the next payment of the member's retirement allowance."* Where the subdivision 2 determination followed the passing of the final qualifying retirement date and the member never retired, and in the whole subdivision 3 branch, there is no allowance and no next payment; and where the member dies between the determination and the reversal there is no *"member's retirement allowance"* at all. **Subdivision 2 has an express fallback for each case and edit 6 had neither.** Both are borrowed, in subdivision 2's own words.

**FIND**

> A certified subsidy settled as required by the preceding sentence is settled notwithstanding that the reversed or modified determination had taken effect and notwithstanding that the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7.

**ENACTED**

> A certified subsidy settled as required by the preceding sentence is settled notwithstanding that the reversed or modified determination had taken effect and notwithstanding that the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7. <u>Where no payment of a retirement allowance has become payable to the member when the determination is reversed or modified, the Board shall include the amount that this subdivision requires to be included in the next payment of the member's retirement allowance on a reversal or modification in the first payment of a retirement allowance to the member; and where the member has died, the Board shall pay that amount to the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death or, if there is none, to the member's estate, no later than 60 days after the reversal or modification.</u>

**Why the insertion sits after this sentence and not after the arrears sentence it serves.** The next sentence in the subdivision opens *"A certified subsidy settled as required by **the preceding sentence**…"* — inserting after the arrears sentence would have moved that antecedent onto my new text and un-settled the subsidy. The new sentences identify their subject **descriptively** rather than by ordinal (*"the amount that this subdivision requires to be included in the next payment … on a reversal or modification"*) so that no future insertion can strand them in turn.

### R5 — M-5. Edit 9 was inoperative, because subsection E carries the same bar independently

Store revision 52's edit 9 switched off G 3's deeming sentence on a rescission, so that the rescued member is treated as having reached her unreduced retirement eligibility date — the premise the *"certified subsidy"* definition and the subsection C clause (ii) cap both read. **Subsection E carries a materially identical bar of its own**, and on a rescinded G 3 determination the Board credits only the months fully paid for, so *"payment in full"* has still not been received and E's bar still bites. **Edit 9 therefore changed nothing.**

**FIND**

> This sentence does not apply where a determination under this subdivision is rescinded under subdivision 4.

**ENACTED**

> <u>Neither this sentence nor the provision of subsection E that no member shall be treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of an election before payment in full is received applies where a determination under this subdivision is rescinded under subdivision 4.</u>

**The repair is made from inside G 3 rather than by amending subsection E.** It is the smaller footprint, it keeps the whole rule in the sentence a reader of G 3 is already in, and it leaves E's bar in force for every other case. **It does not touch E's separate *crediting* bar**, whose exception names only death — that gap is pre-existing, is made newly load-bearing by the new clause (iii) population, and is §7 item 120(a).

### R6 — M-6. The offset was one-directional, and "nothing prevents" is not a grant

The mirror duplicate is one **edit 6 itself creates**: the member is approved for disability and paid, and a reversal then makes a service retirement allowance payable retroactively for the same months, with no offset authorised and the no-collection limb barring one. Separately, *"[n]othing … prevents"* removes a bar; it does not confer the power, and no affirmative recoupment power is cited anywhere in the section. **"May" creates a power** — that is the rule this record applies everywhere else.

**FIND**

> Nothing in this subdivision or in subsection F prevents the Board from applying a retirement allowance paid to the member for a month against a disability retirement allowance payable to the member for the same month.

**ENACTED**

> <u>Notwithstanding the prohibition stated in this subdivision on the collection, offset, or withholding of any amount, and notwithstanding subsection F, the Board may apply a retirement allowance paid to the member for a month against a disability retirement allowance payable to the member for the same month, and may apply a disability retirement allowance paid to the member for a month against a retirement allowance payable to the member for the same month.</u>

**I did not enact the review's wider form.** Its suggested words — *"any other allowance payable to the member under this chapter for the same month"* — reach allowance types the Director never authorised an offset between. The enacted form names the same two allowances in both directions and nothing else, so it **cannot leave the member worse off than zero for the month**, which is the ground on which the narrow offset was approved. The prohibition is identified **descriptively** rather than as *"the preceding sentence"*, so a later insertion cannot strand it.

---

## 2. The eight serious findings — carded, not drafted into the text

Candidate text for every one is below and **none of it is in the bill.** §7 item numbers are the live ones: the review suggested 106 and 107 for S-1 and S-5, and **106 and 107 were taken by store revisions 54 and 55, and 108 to 113 by store revision 56, while this pass was running.**

### §7 item 114 — S-1. Amend the settlement bar once, instead of a *notwithstanding* for every rescission route

The bar has two limbs. Store revision 52's edits 2 and 6 disapply both — **but only inside the two sentences they are written in.** Two routes still reach the release limb, and the first is ordinary:

- **(a)** A member whose purchase is reduced on a **D 6 recertification** has had her reservation released *"to the extent of any reduction"* **in accordance with D 7**. She pays in full, is credited, and dies before retiring. Clause (i) applies and the Board credits the service and pays the death benefit — but **no rescission is involved, so edit 2 never reaches her**, and on the bar's face the certified subsidy is never settled. Subsection N never pays the trust; the remaining reservation stays charged against the $3,000,000 limit permanently under D 3; and her election is in none of J 1 limb (a)'s classes, so the reporting duty is perpetual. **That is the fatal item 89 cured, reached through a different door by a modal fact pattern.**
- **(b)** The **involuntary-separation rescission** is a fourth rescission route in its own sentence with no *notwithstanding*; its deeming defeats the determination limb and says nothing about the release.

**The ground is this record's own.** §6.0-52 item 1 and both edits are premised on the strict historical-fact reading of the bar — *"a determination reversed on review **has** taken effect."* A drafter who legislates twice on the strict reading cannot then rely on a purposive reading for the branches he did not touch. **Candidate text, one amendment to the bar:**

> No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the reservation for the election has been released <u>in full</u> in accordance with subdivision D 7 <u>and has not been reinstated under this subdivision</u>, or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect <u>and has not been rescinded, reversed, or modified</u>, and no certified subsidy is settled more than once under this subdivision or under subdivision 1.

**Recommend enacting.** It cures both surviving routes, it makes edits 2 and 6's *notwithstanding* clauses surplusage rather than load-bearing, and it is the only form that does not need a new clause for the next rescission route anyone adds. **It spends money** — it settles subsidies the bar on its face refuses — which is why it is carded and not fixed silently.

### §7 item 115 — S-2. Edit 6 commands settlement on *any* reversal or modification, including where none is due

This is the Director's own question, asked on [MOO-152](/MOO/issues/MOO-152), and the answer is the one the question feared. Edit 6's duty is unconditioned: it does not ask whether clause (i), (ii) or (iii) applies. A member who seeks reconsideration and **loses** — the Board modifies the determination to a **larger** reduction — satisfies it on its face, so the Board must *"recertify and settle the certified subsidy"* within 60 days and subsection N pays it. **Subdivision 2 is the non-settlement outcome; edit 6 now pays the subsidy anyway.**

The charitable reading is that *"as this subdivision requires"* is a manner qualifier and the duty is empty where nothing is due. **But then edit 6's second sentence has nothing to operate on and §6.0-52 item 1's premise collapses.** Either it is a null duty and the repair was unnecessary, or it is an unpriced money command. **Candidate text**, which also corrects the referent (on a reversal because she *did* retire in a qualifying retirement, settlement is under **subdivision 1**):

> … the Board shall restore or credit service credit as this subdivision provides, and<u>, where the determination as reversed or modified is such that the certified subsidy falls to be settled under subdivision 1 or under this subdivision,</u> shall recertify and settle <u>it</u> ~~the certified subsidy~~ <u>accordingly</u>, no later than 60 days after the reversal or modification …

**Recommend enacting.**

### §7 item 116 — S-3. The arrears formula is gross, not net — and the excess is irrecoverable

**The repair the Director confirmed as item 105 is right and does not underpay her. The defect runs the other way and it is larger.** The words were lifted from subdivision 2's arrears sentence, which is safe **because subdivision 2 forbids any payment before its determination takes effect** — nothing had been paid, so gross equalled net. Edit 6 transplants the formula into a context where payments **have been running throughout**. On the review's worked facts: shortfall **$8,280**, amount the sentence commands **$64,080**, excess **$55,800** — and G 4's own no-collection sentence bars recovery.

**One correction to this record's own authority.** §6.0-52 item 4 and §7 item 105 cite **subsection F** as the no-collection bar. F's limb is tied to *"that account"* — the failure to retire in a qualifying retirement — and an arrears overpayment does not arise on that account. **The operative bar is G 4's own sentence, which is wider.** The conclusion is unaffected and stronger. **Candidate text, both limbs:**

> … shall include every amount <u>by which the amounts paid to the member fall short of the amounts that</u> would have been payable to the member had the determination, as reversed or modified, taken effect on the date on which the determination took effect<u>, or, where the determination is reversed in its entirety, had no determination been made</u>.

**Recommend enacting.** The second limb answers the argument that a determination reversed in its entirety cannot "take effect", which would leave the clause without a referent and the arrears at zero. **Item 105 closes with this**: the enacted form stands and the residual defect is this item.

### §7 item 117 — S-4. The carve-out rescues the *late* filer and excludes the *timely* one

Four classes of disability approval after a determination has taken effect: **(1)** filed on or before the effective date — rescission, pre-existing; **(2)** filed after, § 51.1-156 H's **mandatory** waiver required — rescission, the Director's item-91 answer; **(3)** filed after, waived under H's **permissive** first sentence — nothing, by the Director's choice; **(4)** filed after the determination took effect **but inside § 51.1-156 A or B's own ninety days, so no waiver is needed at all** — **nothing, and nobody decided that.**

Class 4 is a member who complied with the Code's own deadline and is treated worse than a member who missed it by eight months. **That inversion is also the equal-protection surface** (Va. Const. art. I, § 11; U.S. Const. amend. XIV), pleaded alongside an Article 5 petition; the Commonwealth would probably win on rational basis and **has no answer in the record**. **Second defect in the same words:** the trigger is *"as to which the Board **was required** … to waive"* — a counterfactual about the Board's legal obligation, which the section nowhere assigns, times or requires notice of. **Candidate text, two clauses:**

> (a) … or upon an application filed <u>within a period set forth in subsection A or B of § 51.1-156</u>, or …
>
> (b) … or upon an application as to which <u>the Medical Board has made a certification described in clause (ii) of subsection H of § 51.1-156</u> ~~the Board was required by subsection H of § 51.1-156 to waive the ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of that section~~ …

**Recommend both.** Whether to close **class 3** as well is a policy choice the Director already made the other way, and it should be re-made knowing class 4 exists; closing class 4 alone leaves class 3 the only excluded class and the line then runs on *"the Board had a discretion and exercised it"*, which is at least a reason.

### §7 item 118 — S-5. Disability-application pendency is uncapped, and J 1 limb (a) can still be false forever

The 120-day aggregate caps **subsection M requests** and nothing else. **Application pendency is uncapped and uncounted** — so while any application is on file the Board is forbidden to make the subdivision 2 determination and no period runs. A member who files, is denied, and files again indefinitely is never reduced; D 7's second sentence withholds release while vesting is undetermined, so the reservation stays charged against the $3,000,000 limit, a fresh Director of Planning and Budget confirmation is required *"for each fiscal year in which any reservation remains in effect"*, **and until it is obtained the Board may accept no further election.** J 1 limb (a) is false forever and the annual report never ends. **Candidate text, two parts:**

> (a) … except that the aggregate of all such non-running by reason of such requests <u>and by reason of applications for a disability retirement allowance filed after the first such application</u> shall not exceed 120 days …
>
> (b) … and in no event shall the Board be required to report under this subdivision after the first December 1 following the <u>twentieth</u> anniversary of the expiration of this section.

**Recommend both.** (a) is the one that touches a member's credit and the waiting list's access to the cap; (b) is a long-stop that costs nothing and makes the duty terminable whatever happens.

### §7 item 119 — S-6. Edit 10 may have disabled the only unreduced retirement the hardship branch requires

The confinement's **substance** is declaratory of § 51.1-155.1's own conditions and admits nobody — that part of this record holds and the review verified it. But it carries a **temporal** condition § 51.1-155.1 does not contain (*"on or before the date as of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined"*), and the Director's item-94 answer pushed that condition out of one definition and into **the whole section**.

A member certified at 48 and involuntarily separated at 50 is told by G 4's hardship branch to retire in a **qualifying retirement** within 90 days. Her only unreduced route is § 51.1-155.1 A. The residual sentence resolves the operative date to the decision *"in which that date is applied"* — her 2030 certification, when she had not been separated. **On that reading her retirement is not one she "may" take for the purposes of the section, she fails subsection F, and subdivision 2 reduces her credit.** Before edit 10 this could not happen. **Candidate text:**

> … only where the member has incurred an involuntary separation or the lawful abolition of the member's office, position, or employment on or before the date as of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined <u>or, where this sentence is applied otherwise than in the determination of the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date, on or before the member's effective date of retirement</u>.

**Recommend enacting.** The alternative — revert to *"this definition"* and amend the twin expressly — is the option §6.0-52 declined, and **the ground given for declining it does not survive this scenario.** See also M-4: the same residual sentence yields no date at all in a G 1 settlement, a qualifying-retirement determination or the hardship branch, so the candidate above is the general cure as well as the cure for this case.

### §7 item 120 — M-5's second limb and R2's twin. Two pre-existing gaps the new population makes load-bearing

**(a)** Subsection E's **crediting** bar is excepted only *"as subdivision G 4 provides in the case of the member's **death**"*, yet G 4's vesting sentence credits the whole purchased credit on **clause (ii)** and **clause (iii)** too, where payment may be incomplete. The Director's items 91 and 92 bring a new population into clause (iii), which is what makes this live. **Candidate:** *"except as subdivision G 4 provides in the case of the member's death, of the member's approval for a disability retirement allowance, or of an error of the Board."*
**(b)** The **death branch's own** adverse-tax fallback carries the defect R2 cured in the rescission branch — it applies an unpayable refund *"to the purchase of additional service credit for the member"* where the member is dead. **Candidate:** the same words R2 enacted.

**Recommend both.** Neither is a repair to an answered item, which is why neither is enacted.

### §7 item 121 — M-7. Four 60-day payment duties with no remedy, no interest and no report line

Edit 4's deadline, and D 6's, subdivision 2's, G 5's and the death branch's, are each a bare *"shall pay … within 60 days."* Subsection M 2 reaches *"a determination of the Board"* and *"a failure of the Board to make a determination or to give a notice within a period required by this section"* — **a failure to pay is neither**, and no J 1 line records it. This is the money-side twin of item 100. **Candidate:** add *"or to make a payment"* to M 2's failure clause, or interest at the rate subdivision B 4 a already defines, or both. **Recommend the M 2 limb**, which costs nothing and gives the duty an *"or else"*; the interest limb is a money decision.

### §7 item 103 — S-7, with its ground upgraded. The clause (iii) trigger is unenforceable without it

**The review's verdict is that item 103 is necessary, not optional**, and the reason is sharper than the one this record gave. After a subdivision 2 determination has taken effect there is **no period** within which the Board must determine its own error, **no route** by which the member may ask, and **no notice duty**.
