Subsection M 2 reaches a failure to determine only *"within a period required by this section"* — and no period is required for this determination. **The cheapest path to nominal compliance is silence, and silence is complete.** The candidate text drafted at `moo64-rev52-record` §4 is unchanged and reads through to the clause (iii) trigger and to the redetermination clock without further conforming. **Recommend enacting.** **M-9 is held to it** (§3 below).

### §7 item 104 — conformed, and still carded

The review directs the **record** version, which catches the restored service credit and the word *"refunded"*; §7's version missed both. §7 item 104's candidate text is conformed to it in this revision (m-3). **Recommend enacting** — unchanged.

---

## 3. What is not enacted and why — the two held findings

**M-9 is held to item 103, deliberately.** Edit 5's clock has no fallback where the Board never makes the error determination, unlike its own neighbour. The gap is **self-consistent** — no determination, no rescission, nothing to count — so it is not live on its own, and **the fallback cannot be drafted until item 103 decides what period the Board is under.** Drafting one now would either invent a period the Director has not approved or point at a period that does not exist. It is drafted together with item 103 or not at all.

**m-5 needs no edit.** The review answers the Director's question 5 in the affirmative: *"limited to that rescission and its consequences"* **is** determinate enough to discharge, because G 4 enumerates the consequences of a rescission exhaustively. The offered tightening is optional and buys nothing, so it is declined rather than carded.

---

## 4. The fiscal claim — corrected, and the correction is against this record

**Split in two.** *"Edits 1 to 7 admit nobody"* — **sound, and verified independently by the review** against the clause (v) to (viii) tests, the subsection C clause (ii) cap and the definition of *"eligible member"*. *"No priced quantity moves"* — **not supportable as written, and it is withdrawn in that form.**

The engine's load-bearing assumption is its **G 4 exposure window**, stated in its own prose as *"exactly election-to-required-retirement"*, with *"the cost per event … **NOT** priced."* Store revision 52's edits 1, 2, 3 and 6 open settlement routes that run **past** required retirement **with no statutory outer limit**: § 51.1-156 H has no time limit at all by its own premise, the clause (iii) trigger has no period, and judicial review under Article 5 ordinarily takes two to four years. The review replicated `g4_exposure` on the model's own cells and **reproduced the published baseline to the digit** before testing the alternate: two tail years add **0.1291 expected deaths, +127 percent of the entire priced death exposure**, and the limb that moves most — **disability** — is carried by **no decrement in the model at all**.

**The statement this record now authorises, and the only one the memo may use:** *no admission quantity moves; the settlement count moves upward by an amount the current engine cannot value, because per-event G 4 cost was never priced and disability was never a decrement.* The numbers above are the death limb only and are a floor; they are the reviewer's arithmetic on an assumption, not a figure of Fiscal's, and they are **not** a dollar figure. **Also recorded: §3's item-99 quantification list is already incomplete** — it names item 46's pendency allowance and item 50's clause (ii) refund and omits **edit 4's refunds** and **edit 6's arrears**, both new payments out of the trust.

**Nothing in §3, `model-s8-s9` or the [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85) reprice is re-run by store revision 57 itself.** The five repairs touch a payee, two deadlines, a payment vehicle, a deeming and the direction of one offset. **The re-run that is needed is the window and the decrement**, and it is requested, not asserted.

---

## 5. Cross-reference check — §5.36, chased in both directions

**Outward — every citation the five repairs introduce or rely on.**

| Citation | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **subsection E** | R5 | 9 citations of *"subsection E"* in §1. R5 names E's deeming bar in E's own words rather than by paraphrase, and disapplies it only for a rescinded subdivision 3 determination. **E's separate crediting bar is untouched** — §7 item 120(a). |
| **subdivision D 7** | R3 | 9 citations, 6 of them *"in accordance with subdivision D 7"*. R3 uses the existing *"otherwise than in accordance with"* formula verbatim, so the two deadline limbs track the two release classes the subdivision already distinguishes. |
| **subdivision 4 / subdivision 3 / subdivision 2** | R3, R4, R5 | Unchanged designators; no renumbering. The *"subdivision 2 or 3"* references all continue to read on the same rescission and reversal sentences. |
| **subsection F** | R6 | R6 keeps F named, because F's deeming list is what makes the offset bar bite. **The authority for the no-collection bar is corrected in the record** from F to G 4's own sentence (§7 item 116) — the citation in the text is still right, because the offset needs both disapplied. |
| **subsection M** | R4, R5 (consequentially) | 28 citations. No repair creates or removes an M route; the rescission notice already gives the member one. |
| **subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2** | R1, R2 | 15 citations. The refund continues to value the credit at the same cost the death branch and the rescission crediting use. |

**Inward — every provision that reads the five I changed.**

- **G 3** is cited as *"subdivision G 2 or G 3"* in J 1 and as *"subdivision 3"* five times inside subsection G. R5 is confined to G 3's own second sentence plus the named limb of E, and changes no other reader of G 3.
- **G 4** is cited 8 times as *"subdivision G 4"*. Four of the five repairs sit inside it; none moves a sentence boundary that another sentence counts from, and **R4 was positioned specifically to preserve the one ordinal reference in the chain** (*"the preceding sentence"*).
- **Subsection E** has 9 inward readers; R5 does not amend E, so none of them moves.
- **J 1** has no inward citation by designator. No repair touches it.
- **The two definitions** are untouched by this revision. No admission test, no clause (v) to (viii) determination and no subsection C clause (ii) cap changes.

**Result: no conforming amendment is required outside the four provisions amended, and none is made.** One conforming change **inside** them was required and is R2's anchor disambiguation, recorded above.

---

## 6. Drafter's note — §6.0-57. Choices made, and the one finding that moved on re-verification

1. **Every repair is to words the Director's own answers put in.** R1 and R2 repair item 97's refund; R3 repairs item 89's reinstatement trigger; R4 and the carded item 116 repair item 93's arrears; R5 makes item 96 operative; R6 completes item 95's offset. **None of them decides a policy and none changes which member passes either definitional test.**
2. **Three wordings are mine and not the review's.** R6 is narrower than the form offered (two named allowances in both directions, not *"any other allowance under this chapter"*), because the wider form authorises offsets between allowance types the Director never reached. R5 is drafted from inside G 3 rather than by amending subsection E, which is the smaller footprint. R4's new sentences identify their subject descriptively rather than as *"the preceding sentence"*, and are **positioned after** the settlement sentence rather than after the arrears sentence they serve, because inserting them there would have moved an existing *"preceding sentence"* antecedent onto new text and un-settled the subsidy.
3. **"May" creates a power.** R6 converts *"[n]othing … prevents the Board from applying"* into *"the Board may apply"*. A sentence that only removes a bar leaves the Board without the power the sentence assumes, and no affirmative recoupment power is cited anywhere in the section. The scope is identical, so this is drafting; it is recorded here because it changes the operative verb.
4. **One finding moved on re-verification, and it is R2.** The review treats M-1 as a single defect in the payee. Re-reading the live body, the **adverse-tax fallback** immediately after it carries the same defect in a second sentence — and that sentence is **word-identical to the death branch's own fallback**, so it is not addressable without the trailing words of the next sentence. M-1 is therefore enacted as **two** substitutions, not one, and the death branch's own copy is carded at item 120(b) rather than amended, because it is pre-existing text no answer reached.
5. **I did not fix S-1 silently.** It is the fourth repair the review says this record missed, and it is correct that it was missed — but it amends the settlement bar itself and **settles subsidies the bar on its face refuses**, which is a money consequence and the Director's to take. Carded as item 114.
6. **The record repairs.** Four stranded internal references are corrected (m-1 to m-4) and §7 item 104's candidate text is conformed to the record version, which catches the restored service credit and the word *"refunded"* the §7 version missed. **No bill text and no figure moves on any of them.**
7. **Housekeeping.** Store revision 56 landed under this revision while it was being cut, leaving **4,166 characters of headroom** and three live sets of §5 and §6 against §0.1's rule that they carry the live revision only. **Moved verbatim** to [`bill-text-s8-record-s0-s5-s6-rev2-51`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-record-s0-s5-s6-rev2-51), each replaced by a stub restating its durable result: **store revision 54's §0.0-54, §5.33 and §6.0-54; store revision 55's §0.0-55, §5.34 and §6.0-55; and store revision 56's §5.35 and §6.0-56.** All nine designators still resolve, §5 and §6 now carry this revision alone, and the §0 narrative for store revision 56 stays in the file. **Nothing is summarised away and no bill text moved.** This revision closed at **567 characters of headroom**; a concurrent run has since moved further record out and the file now stands well clear of the ceiling. **§7 item 102 remains the live constraint on every revision from here, and this revision did not relieve it.**
8. **What the review could not re-open, recorded so it is not re-litigated.** All thirteen of store revision 52's edits were verified present in the live store as carded. Edit 11's four classes match subdivision 2's four excepted classes exactly; edit 12 creates no gap; edit 13 self-replicates for a second late rescission. **Edit 9 does not reach the certified-subsidy floor or the subsection C clause (ii) cap.** Edit 8 cannot be read as a cross-month or general recovery power. **Edit 10 admits nobody.** § 51.1-156 H, A, B and D were verified verbatim and the *notification* / *application* point is **not** a defect. **No constitutional finding** on single object, special legislation, Dillon's Rule, delegation, vagueness, takings or contract impairment — each tested fresh, each with its reason recorded; the one live surface is S-4's equal-protection inversion. **No broken `§0.x`, `§5.n` or `§6.0-n` reference** after store revision 52's record move: all 21, 12 and 16 designators resolve.

---

## 7. Status

**Store revision 57 of `bill-text-s8` carries five repairs in four provisions of §1 and four record corrections. It cures no serious finding and does not claim to.** Eight serious findings and two pre-existing gaps are with the Policy Director as §7 items 114 to 121, with 103 and 104 restated and 105 closed. **The five repairs have had no adversarial pass of their own.**

**Routed outside this lane:** Fiscal — the unbounded G 4 window and a disability decrement in `g4_exposure`, and the two omissions from the item-99 list. Statutory Researcher — M-8, whether a service retiree remains a *"member"* for § 51.1-156, on which the item-91 carve-out rests. Stakeholder Analyst — the subdivision B 4 e employer and the subdivision D 5 waiting-list applicant. Editor — S-1, S-2, S-3, S-4, S-6 and the corrected fiscal statement in the risk section.

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel. Pre-decisional.**

title: Store revision 42 (re-verified at 45) — the record for MOO-64 items 46, 48, 49, 50 and 54: ENACTED in bill-text-s8
body:
> **MERGED. This document is the canonical record for the MOO-64 items 46, 48, 49, 50 and 54 edits.**
> It replaces, in full, the earlier body of this document that was titled *"Store revision 38"* and said the
> nine edits were **not** in the bill. **They are.** The paste was blocked twice by `409 Issue run ownership
> conflict` on [MOO-42](/MOO/issues/MOO-42) and landed on a later heartbeat; the body below is unchanged from
> the one written when the edits were enacted, except for this note and the re-verification note immediately
> under it.

> **RE-VERIFIED 12 October 2026 against [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) at store
> revision 45** (document revision `91baade7`, 506,548 characters), not merely at store revision 42 where the
> edits were enacted. **All nine edits are present in the live text, each exactly once.** Concurrent store
> revisions 43, 44 and 45 reversed none of them. **Two of the nine now read without their own `<u>` tags** —
> E6, the `G 4,` in subsection F's deeming list, and E8's *"the later of (a)"* in subdivision J 1 — because
> later revisions absorbed those spans into a whole-paragraph underline (J 1 now opens
> `<u>**J. 1.** The Board shall report…`). **The operative words are identical; only the markup nesting
> changed, and the result as amended is the same.** The two file-size statements below are now historical: the
> file carried 23 characters of headroom at store revision 42 and carries about **17,700** at store revision
> 45, because later revisions moved retained record out into
> [`bill-text-s8-retained-record-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-retained-record-2). **Card item
> 53 is therefore eased but not answered** — the fatal fix in §9 below is now writable.

# Store revision 42 — the Director's five answers on [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) items 46, 48, 49, 50 and 54, ENACTED

**Internal working draft material. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel.
Pre-decisional.**

**READ THIS FIRST: the nine edits are now IN [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), at
store revision 42** (document revision `41a3bbd9-2c54-4b21-b3d1-e0e4b6b3c946`, 524,265 characters). Verified
after the write, against the live body: **all nine edits present, each exactly once; exactly six paragraphs of
§1 differ from the body immediately before the write; §1's paragraph count unchanged at 92.** Earlier versions
of this document said the edits were *not* in the bill and were numbered for store revisions 38 and 39. **Both
statements are superseded by this one.**

**This document is the ENTIRE record for store revision 42**, including the parts that are normally in the bill
file: the cross-reference sweep (normally §5.x), the ambiguities (normally §6.0-x), the new open items
(normally §7) and the status block (normally §8). **None of them is in `bill-text-s8`, and the reason is that
the file is full.** Store revision 42 left **23 characters** of headroom against the server's
524,288-character limit; the bill's §0 carries a one-paragraph pointer to this document and nothing else.
**That is below the output bar for a drafting deliverable and it is stated here rather than worked around.**

**Why the numbering is 42.** These nine edits were drafted against store revision 37 and waited through five
concurrent publications for a write. **Store revisions 38, 39, 40 and 41 landed underneath them** — pass 12
([MOO-117](/MOO/issues/MOO-117)) took revision 39, §5.21, §6.0-39 and §7 items 62 to 69; pass 13
([MOO-118](/MOO/issues/MOO-118)) took revision 40, §5.22 and §6.0-40; a further run took revision 41, §5.23,
§6.0-41 and §7 item 70. **Every one of them touched none of the six provisions these edits change**, and all
nine anchors were verified present and unique in the live body in the same operation that wrote it. **Nothing
in revisions 38 to 41 is reversed, re-opened or renumbered.**

**A correction to my own record: nine edits in SIX provisions, not seven.** Earlier comments and earlier
versions of this document said seven. The paragraph-level diff says six: the definition of *"unreduced
retirement eligibility date"*, **subsection F**, **subdivision G 2**, **subdivision G 4** (three edits),
**subdivision J 1** (two edits) and **enactment clause 3**. No edit is added or dropped by the correction;
the count was simply wrong.

Answers taken as given, from the [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) question card resolved 12 October 2026:
**item 46 enact · item 48 candidate (a), confine · item 49 all four fixes · item 50 both limbs ·
item 54 extend to subdivision 3.**

## 1. The nine edits

**Nine edits in six provisions, +2,176 characters of bill text.** Verified mechanically against the live text
as at store revision 42: **exactly six paragraphs of §1 differ**, and §1's paragraph count is unchanged
at 92. The six are the definition of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*, subsection F, subdivision
G 2, subdivision G 4, subdivision J 1, and enactment clause 3.

| # | Item | Provision | Characters |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | 48 | `A`, *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*, new final sentence | +332 |
| E2 | 46 | `G 2`, new fourth sentence | +371 |
| E3 | 49(i), 54 | `G 4`, rescission sentence rewritten; new sentence after it | +544 |
| E4 | 54 | `G 4`, redetermination-clock sentence | +5 |
| E5 | 50 | `G 4`, new sentence after the notice-of-rescission sentence | +582 |
| E6 | 50 | `F`, the deeming list | +5 |
| E7 | 49(ii) | `J 1`, report contents | +218 |
| E8 | 49(iii) | `J 1`, reporting tail | +79 |
| E9 | 49(iv) | Enactment clause 3, clause (i) | +40 |

### E1 — item 48 (a), the modal definition confined

Appended to the definition:

> <u>For the purposes of this definition the member may retire under subsection A or C of § 51.1-155.1 only
> where the member has incurred an involuntary separation, or the member's office has been lawfully
> abolished, as the case may be, on or before the date as of which the member's unreduced retirement
> eligibility date is determined.</u>

**Note what is deliberately *not* symmetric here.** The sentence goes into *"unreduced retirement
eligibility date"* and **not** into *"qualifying retirement"*, and that is the answer's own logic rather than
an omission. The distinction established in revision 8 governs: the modal definition asks the earliest date
the member **may** retire, so a reader can project a separation she has not incurred; *"qualifying
retirement"* asks about a retirement that has actually happened, so the contingent reading has nothing to
bite on. **Word-identity between the two definitions is not the test** — that claim was withdrawn in
revision 22 — and forcing it here would have put a sentence with no work to do into the actual-facts test.

### E2 — item 46, the allowance during pendency

Inserted in G 2 immediately after the arrears sentence:

> <u>Nothing in this subdivision prevents the payment of a retirement allowance to a member while an
> application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter is pending, and the
> determination required by this subdivision shall take effect notwithstanding that a retirement allowance
> has been paid to the member while such an application was pending.</u>

Both limbs are necessary and they answer the two halves of G 2's third sentence: the first lifts the bar on
payment, the second lifts the requirement that the determination take effect *"before the first payment of
any retirement allowance."*

### E3 — item 49(i) and item 54, the rescission sentence

As enacted (the two insertions underlined in the bill's markup; shown here in **bold**):

> <u>Where a determination under subdivision 2 **or 3** has taken effect and the member is thereafter
> approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter **upon an application filed no later
> than the date on which the determination took effect**, or thereafter dies in a case to which clause (i)
> of this subdivision applies, the Board shall rescind the determination and shall restore the service
> credit reduced under it**, to the extent this subdivision provides,** no later than 60 days after the date
> on which the member is so approved or dies, and the certified subsidy for the election is settled under
> this subdivision notwithstanding that the rescinded determination had taken effect. **Where the rescinded
> determination is a determination under subdivision 3, the Board shall credit the member with the largest
> number of full or partial months of service credit for which full payment has been made, determined in the
> manner provided in subsection F of § 51.1-142.2 and without regard to the method by which payment was
> made, valued at the cost determined under subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2.**</u>

**The filing cut-off attaches to the approval limb only, not to the death limb.** That is item 49(i) as
asked: it bounds the disability route and leaves the death route alone.

### E5 — item 50, the refund, the characterisation, and the buy-back

> <u>For the avoidance of doubt, an amount refunded under clause (ii) of subdivision 2 is not recoverable
> from any person; where a determination under subdivision 2 is rescinded under this subdivision the Board
> shall restore service credit to the extent of the amounts paid under the election and not refunded; and
> the member, or any employer that paid on the member's behalf, may pay to the Board the amount refunded no
> later than 90 days after the Board gives notice of the rescission, whereupon the Board shall restore the
> whole of the service credit reduced under the determination.</u>

### E6 — item 50, subsection F

> Nothing required or permitted by subdivision G 2, G 3, <u>G 4,</u> or G 5 …

### E7 and E8 — item 49(ii) and (iii), subsection J 1

Report contents, inserted before the variance item:

> <u>the number of determinations rescinded and the service credit restored under subdivision G 4; every
> amount by which a reservation reinstated under subdivision G 4 caused a limitation in subdivision D 2 to
> be exceeded;</u>

Reporting tail, as enacted:

> … until the first December 1 following <u>the later of (a)</u> the date on which every election … has been
> settled under subdivision G 1 or G 4, cancelled under subdivision G 5, or determined under subdivision
> G 2 or G 3 <u>and (b) the date of the last rescission under subdivision G 4</u>, …

### E9 — item 49(iv), enactment clause 3 clause (i)

> … and to make every refund, payment, <u>determination, rescission, restoration, and reinstatement</u>
> required by § 51.1-142.4, …

## a. The answers, and what each one now does

**Item 46.** The member with a non-qualifying retirement and a pending disability application is paid while
it is pending. Pass 10's worked case was 14 months with no cheque; the arrears sentence made her whole in
money and not in time, and this makes her whole in time.

**Item 48.** The contingent reading is shut. This is the only one of the five that could have moved a priced
quantity, and confining the route is what stops it: on the contingent reading the admission rule moved in
**both** directions — a Plan 1 division director of 53 with 24 years excluded under clause (v), and a member
of 51 with 18 years in the same position class admitted who was never priced. **Enacted, neither happens.**

**Item 49.** The rescission acquires an outer bound (the application must predate the determination's taking
effect), the reporting acquires the rescission line and the over-cap excess line, the reporting tail runs to
the last rescission, and the expiry clause names the three duties that generate all of it.

**Item 50.** The refund is characterised — not recoverable from anyone — restoration follows the money
actually retained, and the member or her employer may buy the rest back inside 90 days. Subsection F's
deeming list gains **G 4**, which cures a stranding: F promised *"no other consequence shall attach"* while
G 4's refund-application machinery sat outside the list that makes that true.

**Item 54.** The partial payer reaches parity with the death branch. A subdivision 3 determination is
rescindable on the same terms, and the credit she gets back is valued on the death branch's own formula.

## b. The wording inside the approved text that is mine. All of it, flagged.

**Three changes. None of them chooses a policy, and each is recorded because the next reader should be able
to see that the Director's words and the enacted words are not identical.**

1. **Item 46 — *"the preceding sentence"* was not enacted.** The candidate began *"The preceding sentence
   does not prevent…"*. G 2's third sentence is **compound**: it bars payment of any allowance **and**
   guarantees that the first payment carries everything accrued from the effective date of retirement. A
   reference to *"the preceding sentence"* reaches both limbs, so the cure would have disapplied the
   **arrears** limb the Director enacted for this same member as F-2(b) one revision earlier — taking with
   one hand what it gave with the other. Enacted as *"Nothing in this subdivision prevents the payment…"*,
   which reaches the prohibition and leaves the arrears limb standing.
2. **Item 48 — *"the date as of which the determination is made"* was not enacted.** Inside a definition
   there is no determination, so the phrase had no antecedent; the same definition is applied at
   certification, at every recertification, and on every clause (v) to (viii) test. Enacted as *"the date as
   of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined"* — self-referential, but it
   has exactly one meaning wherever the definition is applied.
3. **The rescission sentence gained *"to the extent this subdivision provides."*** G 4 commanded the Board
   to restore *"the service credit reduced under"* the determination. Item 50 provides that restoration
   follows the amounts **paid and not refunded**, with a buy-back for the balance. Without the added words
   the Board has two contradictory commands and the member's entitlement turns on which sentence a reader
   reaches first. **The Director's answer decides the extent; these six words only stop the two sentences
   fighting.**

## c. The ambiguity item 54 forced, and how it was resolved

**Subdivision 3 does not reduce service credit.** It credits the largest number of months fully paid for, at
the **standard cost**, and releases the reservation. So *"restore the service credit reduced under it"* —
the operative words of the rescission sentence — had **no referent** for a subdivision 3 determination, and
the answer as written would have produced a rescission that restored nothing.

Resolved with the death branch's own formula, in its own words, valued at the **subdivision B 4** cost. That
is the parity the answer asked for, and it is the only formula in the section built for a partial payer.
**It is worth being explicit that this is slightly better for her than the determination it replaces:** the
same months, revalued from the standard cost to the pilot cost. That follows from "parity with the death
branch" and is not a separate choice of mine, but it is a money consequence and it is stated rather than
assumed.

## d. The money, stated rather than netted away

**No priced quantity moves, and item 48 is the reason.** Every figure in the package prices the admitted
cohort — the unreduced subdivision A 1 cohort reached through § 51.1-153 A, B 2 or B 3 — as settling, on the
actual-facts reading of the gateway. Item 48 (a) puts that reading in the text. **Nothing in §3,
`model-s8-s9` or the [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85) reprice needs re-running**, and no admission test, no
clause (v) to (viii) determination and no subsection C clause (ii) cap changes.

**Two of the five answers nonetheless spend money, one-sidedly, and neither amount is in any model.**

- **Item 46** pays an allowance during pendency which the later determination may show was too large, and
  **subsection F's no-collection limb means it is never recovered.**
- **Item 50** provides that the clause (ii) refund is not recoverable from any person, including where the
  member later buys her credit back.

Both were put to the Director on exactly that basis — the Commonwealth bears it either way, so paying her is
strictly better — and both were taken, so **nothing here reopens either answer.** What is open is whether
the § 30-19.1:7 statement should **quantify** them. The population is the one
[MOO-108](/MOO/issues/MOO-108) has now sized at **0.11 expected rescissions and $8,600 PV**, so the figure
is small; *small and stated* is a different posture from *absent*. **Open decision C** below, routed to
[@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50).

## 5. Cross-reference check — performed in full, both directions

**Result: no conforming amendment is required outside the nine provisions, and none is made.**

### Outward — every citation the nine edits introduce or touch

| Citation | Where introduced | Target verified |
|---|---|---|
| `subsection A or C of § 51.1-155.1` | E1 | Already cited in both definitions; E1 adds no new section, it narrows an existing route. |
| `subdivision 3` (of G) | E3, E4 | Exists; the partial-payment crediting rule. |
| `subsection F of § 51.1-142.2` | E3 | The partial-month rule, cited in the same words the death branch already uses. |
| `subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2` | E3 | The pilot cost; same citation the death branch uses. |
| `clause (ii) of subdivision 2` | E5 | Exists; the refund limb. |
| `subdivision G 4` | E6, E7 | Exists. |
| `subdivision D 2` | E7 | Exists; the two limitations. |
| `§ 51.1-142.4` | E9 | Already cited in that clause. |

### Inward — every provision that reads what the nine edits changed

- **Every use of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* re-chased**, because E1 narrows a definition that
  the clause (v) to (viii) tests, the subsection C clause (ii) cap, the *"certified subsidy"* projection and
  subdivision G 3's second sentence all read. **No use breaks**, and the reason is the same reason the
  confinement is safe at all: § 51.1-155.1 A and C are open only to a member who has **already** been
  involuntarily separated or whose office has been abolished, while *"eligible member"* requires a **member
  in service**. The route E1 confines was never reachable by a member the pilot can admit.
- **Subsection F re-read against its new G 4 limb.** The added `G 4` extends F's *"is not a collection,
  offset, or withholding"* conclusion to G 4's refund-application machinery. Nothing else in F changes
  meaning, and the no-collection sentence that precedes the list was already wider than the list.
- **Subdivision G 2 re-read against E2.** The new sentence disapplies the bar and the taking-effect
  requirement, and nothing else in G 2 is conditioned on either. **G 4's bar on making the determination
  while an application is pending is unaffected** — that bar stops the *determination*, and E2 stops the
  *non-payment* that the bar was producing as a side effect. The two now work together, which was the point.
- **Subdivision J 1's tail checked against enactment clause 3 clause (iii)**, which keeps subsection J alive
  *"until the last report and evaluation required by that subsection has been submitted."* The extended tail
  is therefore carried past expiry **without a further amendment**, and E9 names the duties that generate it.
- **Subsection M** reaches the rescission already: G 4 provides that the person *"may seek review of the
  rescission under subsection M"* and that a reinstatement is a determination for M's purposes. E3's and
  E5's additions change what is restored, not who may contest it. **No amendment needed.**
- **Subsection N** settles on the earliest of the three dates in G 4 and is unaffected by a rescission that
  settles *"under this subdivision"*. **No amendment needed.**

### One inward result is adverse and is NOT cured here

**Subdivision G 3's second sentence.** It provides that *"[a] member credited under this subdivision shall
not be treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of the election."*
Item 54 now rescinds a subdivision 3 determination and settles the subsidy — but on G 3's own words the
member is **still** not treated as having reached that date by reason of the election, and that date is the
fact the *"certified subsidy"* definition and the subsection C clause (ii) cap both read. **The rescue is
granted and the premise it runs on is withheld.** It moves text in G 3, which the answer did not reach, so it
is **Open decision A** below, with candidate text and a recommendation to enact, not a change made here.

## 6. The ambiguities resolved

The four that bear on the enacted words are in the bill at **§6.0-38** and are not repeated here. The six
remaining, each resolved and none by policy choice:

5. **Where E2 goes inside G 2.** After the arrears sentence rather than at the end, so that the three
   sentences about payment sit together and *"this subdivision"* in E2 is read against the bar it lifts.
6. **Whether E2 should name G 4's bar.** It does not. E2 is drafted to work whatever the reason the
   determination has not been made — the G 4 bar, the tolling, or ordinary delay — because the harm is the
   non-payment and not its cause.
7. **Whether the E3 filing cut-off reaches the death limb.** It does not, as placed. Item 49(i) bounded the
   disability route; death needs no bound.
8. **Whether E5's buy-back survives expiry.** It does: enactment clause 3 clause (i) preserves *"every right
   of a member under those provisions and every period allowed to a member by those provisions"*, and E9
   now names restoration expressly.
9. **The order of the two new J 1 report items.** Placed immediately before the variance item, which is the
   list's existing last-and-widest entry, so the `; and` that introduces it still reads correctly.
10. **Whether E8 needed lettering.** It did. *"The later of the date on which … and the date of …"* across a
    three-branch disposition clause is unreadable without `(a)` and `(b)`; the lettering carries no meaning
    of its own.

## 7. What is open — three new decisions, and one of them is adverse

**These three could not be written into the bill's §7 at all**, the file having 23 characters of headroom.
They were to be §7 items 71, 72 and 73. **They are decisions for Policy Director and none of them was
resolved by drafting choice.** Candidate text for each is verbatim below.

### Open decision A (intended §7 item 71) — ADVERSE, and not cured

**G 3's second sentence is not disapplied when a subdivision 3 determination is rescinded.** Found by the
inward sweep on item 54. G 3 provides that *"[a] member credited under this subdivision shall not be treated
as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of the election."* Item 54 now rescinds
that determination and settles the subsidy — but on G 3's own words she is **still** not treated as having
reached that date by reason of the election, and that date is the fact the *"certified subsidy"* definition
and the subsection C clause (ii) cap both read. **The rescue is granted and the premise it runs on is
withheld.**

Nineteen words cure it, at the end of that sentence:

> *"<u>, except where a determination under this subdivision is rescinded under subdivision 4, in which case
> this sentence does not apply</u>."*

**I recommend enacting it.** It is the only finding of this revision that leaves a member worse off than the
answer intended; it costs nothing, every member it reaches having already been approved for a disability
retirement allowance or died; and it is out only because it moves text in **G 3**, which the answer did not
reach.

### Open decision B (intended §7 item 72) — should G 4's bar and tolling follow the rescission to subdivision 3?

Item 54 extended the **rescission** and I extended nothing else, the bar being a different duty and not in the
answer. The result is asymmetric but not unsafe: a G 3 determination may still take effect during pendency,
and item 54's rescission then undoes it. **I recommend leaving it** — G 3 is triggered by the member's own
partial payment rather than by her failure to retire, so there is no race for the Board to win. Eleven words
in two places would change it.

### Open decision C (intended §7 item 73) — should the § 30-19.1:7 statement quantify the two one-sided costs?

A disclosure question, not a drafting one, for Policy Director and
[@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50). Item 46 pays an allowance during
pendency that the later determination may show was too large, and **subsection F's no-collection limb never
recovers it**; item 50 makes the clause (ii) refund irrecoverable even where the member buys her credit back.
**Both were argued on exactly that basis and taken, so nothing here reopens either answer.** Open only:
whether the statement should **quantify** them. **I recommend that it should.**

### Still open from earlier rounds

**Items 45, 47, 51 and 52**, each with a recommendation already on the card.

**Item 53 — the size ceiling — is no longer a constraint to work around; it is blocking.** Store revision 42
left **23 characters** of headroom in `bill-text-s8`, and
[`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history), the document
every previous revision moved its record into, is itself within about **a thousand characters** of the same
limit. **De-duplication is exhausted** — a concurrent run took the last of it in store revision 41, and a
sweep run during this write found **zero** remaining byte-identical duplicates. So:

- **No further revision can record itself in `bill-text-s8`**, and the retained-record document cannot absorb
  much more either.
- **The next edit of any size will fail the write outright**, as this revision's first attempt did, with
  `too_big`.

**This is a structural decision for Policy Director, not a drafting choice, and I am not taking it by
default.** My recommendation is to move the whole §0, §5 and §6 retained record out of `bill-text-s8` into
one or more new documents keyed by revision range, leaving §1 (the bill text), §2, §3, §4, §7 and §8 in the
file. That is roughly 90,000 characters and would restore working room for the remaining passes.

## 8. Status

**Store revision 42 IS in `bill-text-s8`.** Nine edits, six provisions, +2,176 characters, verified after the
write. **No priced quantity moves and nothing needs re-running** — item 48's confinement puts into the text
the actual-facts reading every figure in the package is already priced on.

**Pass 12 ([MOO-120](/MOO/issues/MOO-120)) has now landed, with a FATAL finding against the enacted item-54 text. See §9 below — it is the most important thing in this document.**

**One adverse finding is open and not cured (Open decision A) and two further decisions are on the card (B
and C), plus item 53, which is blocking.**

**The ceiling, stated accurately because I got it wrong once in this heartbeat.** The 524,288-character limit
is **real and enforced by the server** — the first write of this revision was rejected with
`too_big`/`maximum: 524288`. It is **not published in the API schema**, so it cannot be discovered by reading
the spec; I checked the spec mid-heartbeat, found no limit, and was wrong to doubt the figure. Earlier
revisions' records had it right.

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel.
Pre-decisional.**

## 9. Pass 12 ([MOO-120](/MOO/issues/MOO-120)) landed after this revision was written, and it has a FATAL finding against the enacted text

**This section supersedes the statement above that these nine edits "have had no adversarial pass of their
own." They have. [MOO-120](/MOO/issues/MOO-120) completed on 12 October 2026 and is `done`.**

**14 findings: 1 fatal, 4 serious, 6 moderate, 2 minor**, plus 11 express null results and 3 citation
re-checks of which 2 did not hold as the reviewer had them. **My three wording changes all survive** —
though the reviewer gives a different and better reason for the first, and says my ground for item 48 was
wrong even though the conclusion holds (the correct ground is that the confinement *can only ever exclude*,
and the excluded class is not in the priced population; `member in service` covers only the admission-time
uses, and the definition is applied again at D 1, on every D 6 recertification, and in G 3).

### F-1, fatal — and I have confirmed it verbatim against the live text

**Item 54, as enacted, is inoperative in every case it was written for.** G 4's settlement bar reads:

> *"No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the reservation for the election has been
> released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken
> effect."*

Item 54's rescission sentence disapplies **only the second limb** — *"notwithstanding that the rescinded
determination had taken effect."* **The D 7 limb is untouched.** And G 3 *commands* release of the
reservation, which for a G 3 member is squarely in accordance with D 7 (D 7's first sentence releases where
*"the member has not completed payment by the completion date stated in the certification"* — the exact G 3
trigger). The reinstatement limb is then confined to a reservation *"released **otherwise than** in
accordance with subdivision D 7,"* so there is nothing the Board may reinstate. **The survivor gets the
crediting and no subsidy.**

**All four of those quotations were re-read against store revision 42 before this was written, and each
appears in the live text as the reviewer gives it.** The reviewer's textual clincher also checks out: the
reinstatement limb's own notice duty requires the Board to state *"whether the release was in accordance
with subdivision D 7, **of the nature of any error**, and of the cause of the release"* — that limb was
written for erroneous releases, not commanded ones, which is why the rescuing construction is the weaker
reading. **The defect is pre-existing in the G 2 branch and item 54 doubles its reach rather than creating
it.**

### The fix, drafted, and enacted nowhere

Two insertions, my text, on the reviewer's direction:

**(i) In G 4's rescission sentence**, after *"notwithstanding that the rescinded determination had taken
effect"*:

> *"<u> and notwithstanding that the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with
> subdivision D 7</u>"*

**(ii) In G 4's reinstatement limb**, extending the trigger:

> *"…in the case of a reservation released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7<u>, or
> released in accordance with that subdivision where a determination is thereafter rescinded under this
> subdivision</u>…"*

**Together about 225 characters. `bill-text-s8` has 23.** So this fix, and every other fix pass 12 asks
for, is **physically unenactable until §7 item 53 is decided.** That is no longer a tidiness question about
where the record lives; it is the thing standing between a fatal finding and its cure. **It is the first
question on the card.**

**I have not enacted either insertion.** They move text in the settlement bar and the reinstatement limb,
neither of which the Director's item-54 answer reached, and the G 2 branch would need the same treatment to
cure the defect completely rather than halfway.

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel.
Pre-decisional.**

title: Store revision 35 — the full record (copied from MOO-64)
body:
# Store revision 35 — the full record: the Director's four answers, and pass 10 dispositioned in the same write

**Owner: Drafting Specialist. Commissioned by [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64).** Two things landed together.
The Director answered all four of store revision 32's open items on 12 October 2026 — **item 28 both
clauses, item 29 enact, item 27 candidate (a), item 30 open the gateway for subsections A and C of
§ 51.1-155.1 only** — and [MOO-99](/MOO/issues/MOO-99), pass 10's adversarial review **of those very
edits**, returned **6 serious, 10 moderate and 3 minor** before the write landed. **So the answers are
enacted as repaired rather than enacted and then repaired:** six edits in three provisions, five of them the
answers and four of them pass-10 repairs to the words the answers put in. **This record lives outside
`bill-text-s8` because that file is at the platform's character ceiling.**

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel.
Pre-decisional.**

---

## 1. The redline, all six edits

**All of §1 is new language, so the whole section is underlined in the source and these inserts appear as
plain text inside it. §1 diff against the live text immediately before this write: exactly four paragraphs
differ** — the two definitions in subsection A, subdivision D 1, and subdivision G 4. **Six edits, three
provisions.**

> **A note on the numbering, because it churned while this was drafted.** Concurrent runs of this agent
> published store revisions 33 and 34 of `bill-text-s8` while these edits waited for the canonical write,
> each taking the §0 designator, the §5 and §6 section numbers and the §7 item numbers I had reserved. This
> record and the enacted text are therefore **store revision 35**, with **§5.17**, **§6.0-35** and **card
> items 45 to 54**, chosen against the live document at the moment of the write. **This document's key is
> deliberately not revision-numbered** — the bill text points at `moo64-record` so that a further
> renumbering does not strand the pointer.

**E1 — § 51.1-142.4 A, "unreduced retirement eligibility date" (item 30).**

> <u>"Unreduced retirement eligibility date" means the earliest date on which the member may retire under
> § 51.1-153**, or under subsection A or C of § 51.1-155.1,** and receive a service retirement allowance
> that is calculated in accordance with subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155 and is not reduced under subdivision
> A 2 or A 3 of that section, in each case determined as though no option had been elected under
> § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 and no lump-sum distribution had been paid under § 51.1-165.01.</u>

**E2 — § 51.1-142.4 A, "qualifying retirement" (item 30).**

> <u>"Qualifying retirement" means a service retirement under § 51.1-153**, or under subsection A or C of
> § 51.1-155.1,** with an effective date of retirement that is the first day of a month, is no earlier than
> the member's earliest qualifying retirement date, and is no later than the member's final qualifying
> retirement date, the allowance for which retirement is calculated in accordance with subdivision A 1 of
> § 51.1-155 … </u>

**E3 — subdivision D 1, new final sentence (item 27 candidate (a), with pass 10's M9 and M10 accuracy
repairs folded in).** It follows the existing sentence that extends the final qualifying retirement date
where the Board's statement is late.

> <u>**The Board shall state, in the written statement required by that definition and in every notice of a
> later approved date required by that definition, (i) that where the Board gives the statement or notice
> later than the time required by that definition the member's final qualifying retirement date is extended
> by the number of days by which the statement or notice is late and, where the date so extended is not the
> first day of a month, is the first day of the next month; (ii) that the member may state as the effective
> date of retirement a date no earlier than the first day of the month following the month in which the
> Board gives the statement or notice, and that nothing in this subdivision prevents the member from stating
> an earlier effective date of retirement to which the member is otherwise entitled, subject to the
> limitation in subsection E of § 51.1-153; and (iii) that where the Board mails the statement or notice,
> every period that runs from the giving of it is extended by three days.**</u>

**E4 — subdivision G 4, four new sentences (item 28 both clauses, with pass 10's S1, S2, S3, M8, M12, m18
and m19 repairs folded in).** Inserted immediately after *"No certified subsidy is settled under this
subdivision after the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or
after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect,"* and immediately before the sentence
requiring the Board to reinstate a reservation released otherwise than under D 7.

> <u>**The Board shall not make a determination under subdivision 2, and shall not give the notice required
> by subdivision 2, while an application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this
> chapter is pending, and a determination made in contravention of this sentence is of no effect. No period
> stated in subdivision 2 or in this subdivision, whether it is a period within which the Board is required
> to act or a period within which a determination is required to take effect, runs while such an application
> is pending. For the purposes of this subdivision an application for a disability retirement allowance is
> pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it.
> Where a determination under subdivision 2 has taken effect and the member is thereafter approved for a
> disability retirement allowance under this chapter, or thereafter dies in a case to which clause (i) of
> this subdivision applies, the Board shall rescind the determination and shall restore the service credit
> reduced under it no later than 60 days after the date on which the member is so approved or dies, and the
> certified subsidy for the election is settled under this subdivision notwithstanding that the rescinded
> determination had taken effect. Where the Board rescinds a determination under subdivision 2 as this
> subdivision requires, the period within which this subdivision requires the redetermination to be made
> runs from the date on which the member is so approved or dies. The Board shall give the member, or the
> person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, written notice of a rescission under this
> subdivision, of the service credit restored, of the amount settled, and of the reasons for the rescission,
> no later than 30 days after the rescission, and that person may seek review of the rescission under
> subsection M.**</u>

**E5 — subdivision G 4's final sentence, seven words (item 28, the no-recovery limb).**

> <u>No amount shall be collected, offset, or withheld from any member, retiree, survivor, beneficiary, or
> estate of a member on account of an involuntary separation**, of a rescission or restoration under this
> subdivision,** or of any other event to which this subdivision applies …</u>

**E6 — subdivision G 4's reinstatement sentence (pass 10's M16).** A duty with no deadline, newly reachable
on the path item 28 opens, and the step it must precede is settlement. Re-cut onto store revision 33's version
of the sentence, which reinstates the contingency amount with the reservation.

> <u>Where a reservation has been released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7, the Board shall
> reinstate it, together with the contingency amount released with it, **no later than the date on which the
> certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision**, and the reinstated reservation and contingency amount
> shall be charged against the limitations in subdivision D 2 …</u>

**M13 needed no edit, and I verified that rather than assuming it.** Pass 10 found that G 2's 120-day outer
bound was keyed to *"the 60-day period in the first sentence of this subdivision"*, which does not run at all
for the member item 29 is about, because subdivision 4 displaces it. **Store revision 33 had already cured
it** with a new subdivision-scoped term — *"'the determination date' means the date from which the 60-day
period within which the Board must make the determination required by this subdivision runs, whether that
period runs under the first sentence of this subdivision or under subdivision 4"* — and the effect sentence
now reads *"in no event later than 120 days after the determination date."* Read on the live text. **No edit
made.**

**The record edits.** §0 gains store revision 35's change note; **§5.17** the cross-reference check;
**§6.0-35** the ambiguities; **§7** the disposition of items 27 to 30 and new items 45 to 54; **§8** the
status. Two mislabels in §7 item 8 are corrected and two duplicate headings (§5.11, §6.0-21) are renumbered.
**§5.5's false *"G 4 (iii)"* claim needed no edit either** — a concurrent revision corrected it and moved
§5.5 to the companion record before this write; verified absent from the live text. **Store revision 33's §0
record is moved verbatim to
[`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history) and ten §0
pointer stubs are replaced by the single table at §0.1** — about 34,000 characters in all, because the file
had **5,606 characters of headroom** when these edits landed. Nothing was summarised away: the stubs are in
the history document too. **That is §7 item 53**, and it is the part of the ceiling problem I had to act on
rather than ask about.

**Item 29 — no edit, because the text already carries it.** G 4's involuntary-separation sentence reads
*"within 60 days after the earliest of the expiration of that 90-day period, the member's final qualifying
retirement date, if any, and the date on which the member retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying
retirement"* — store revision 21's conforming edit — and G 2's duty is expressly *"except as subdivision 4
provides."* **One duty, one deadline, whose limbs are a superset of G 2's.** My card had recorded this as
drafted and not enacted; **the card was wrong and the text was right.** Pass 10 confirms it and found the
one residual, which is E7.

---

## a. The wording that is mine rather than the Director's. All of it, flagged.

**Four changes inside the approved text.**

**1. Item 28's death limb, narrowed to a case to which clause (i) of G 4 applies.** As approved the clause
operated where the member *"is thereafter approved for a disability retirement allowance … or dies."* G 4's
second sentence provides that *"[c]lause (i) of this subdivision does not apply where the member has retired
in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement before the date of death"* — the line settled on
[MOO-44](/MOO/issues/MOO-44). **Enacted verbatim, the approved words would have reversed that line.** The
narrowing keeps it and still cures the gap: the member who **never retired at all**, whose determination
took effect when her final qualifying retirement date passed, and who then dies. **Pass 10 agrees the
narrowing is right.** The policy question it leaves is §7 item 45 and I did not take it.

**2. A tolling sentence, because the approved clause is otherwise unperformable** — G 2 commands a
determination while the approved clause forbids making it.

**3. A 60-day deadline on the rescission.** *"Shall rescind"* with no time limit is a duty with no deadline.

**4. The no-recovery limb enacted inside G 4's existing prohibition** rather than as a second overlapping
sentence; that sentence's own list of protected persons is wider than the approved words. **Pass 10 calls
this the right structural choice** and still finds a defect in it, which is §7 item 50.

**Five more are pass-10 repairs to those same words, and they are mine too.**

**5. S1 — the settlement operator is automatic, and this is the repair I would least want left undone.**
The draft read *"and the certified subsidy **may be settled** under this subdivision notwithstanding that
the determination had taken effect."* Every neighbouring operator is automatic — G 1's *"is settled… on the
member's effective date of retirement"* and G 4's own *"is settled… on the earliest of (a)… (b)… and (c)"* —
so against that background *"may"* reads as conferring a **discretion**, not as lifting a bar: the
Commonwealth's payment of a named member's subsidy, standardless, with the trust carrying the unfunded
difference where the Board declines. *Ames v. Town of Painter*, 239 Va. 343, 389 S.E.2d 702 (1990), is the
delegation authority and I accept it. **Enacted:** *"and the certified subsidy for the election **is**
settled under this subdivision notwithstanding that the rescinded determination had taken effect."* I did
not use *"shall be settled"*, because the subdivision already fixes the settlement **date** in its automatic
operator and a second mandatory operator with no date would compete with it.

**6. S2 and S3 — the tolling reaches every period, of both kinds.** The draft tolled *"no period within
which subdivision 2 requires the Board **to act**."* G 2's hard stops are not periods for the Board to act;
they are periods within which a determination must **take effect**. And G 4's own 60-day deadline is imposed
by **subdivision 4**, not subdivision 2. Both kept running against a prohibition. **§ 51.1-156 A makes the
second collision concrete** — a disability application may be filed *"within ninety days after termination
of service"*, which is **the same 90 days** G 4 gives the separated member to retire. **Enacted:** *"No
period stated in subdivision 2 **or in this subdivision**, whether it is a period within which the Board is
required to act **or a period within which a determination is required to take effect**, runs while such an
application is pending."*

**7. M8 — the rescission carries notice and subsection M review.** Every other Board act in this section
does: G 2 (30 days' notice plus M), subsection C, D 4, D 6, I 2, and G 4's own death branch. A rescission
restoring 29 of 36 months with no notice leaves the member nothing to seek review of. **Enacted** for the
member and for the person entitled to a benefit on her death.

**8. m19 — the redetermination period runs from the approval or the death, not from the rescission.** The
rescission date is one the Board chooses inside its 60-day window, so measuring the 90 days from it allowed
150 days from approval. And **the bar now reaches the notice** as well as the determination, so a member
cannot be handed a notice of credit reduction, and spend her M 2 window answering it, while the application
that makes it void is pending.

**9. M12, m18, M13, M16, M9, M10 — the smaller ones.** *"Pending"* is **defined** — from filing until the
Board first acts — which bounds the gaming surface without a numeric cap (the cap is item 52). A
determination made in contravention of the bar is **of no effect**. G 2's 120-day outer bound gets a
referent for the subdivision 4 cohort. The reinstatement duty gets a deadline. And D 1's new notice must
state the **rounding-forward** rule and the **three-day mailing** rule, and must state the earliest-date
floor as the **permission** it is: as first drafted it would have told a member whose statement was 20 days
late that her earliest effective date was 1 March when 1 February was hers by right and within § 51.1-153
E's retroactivity window. **That one would have cost a real member a month, through a notice this bill
requires the Board to give.**

---

## b. Corrections to my own record

**1. §5.5's statement that no member is harmed if the § 51.1-155.1 gateway stays closed was wrong, and it
stood from revision 8 to store revision 32.** It rested on *"G 4 (iii) vest[ing] the purchased credit on the
involuntary separation itself."* **There is no such clause.** Clause (iii) is an **error of the Board**. The
involuntary-separation route is G 4's own later sentence and it protects the member only *"if the member
retires in a qualifying retirement no later than 90 days after the date of the involuntary separation."* So
on the closed reading the member separated at 50 with 20 years, retiring by the only route open to her,
failed that condition and subdivision 2 clawed her credit back. **Pass 10 found the same error
independently (M7).** Corrected in §5.5 and in the two §7 item 8 mislabels.

**2. §5.5's claim that word-identity prevents the two definitions selecting different cohorts** was
withdrawn in store revision 22 and stays withdrawn: one test is **modal** and the other **actual**.

**3. The counts in my own cross-reference checks have been wrong twice** (twelve uses where there were
fifteen; five where there were nine). They are now taken mechanically and restated each revision: **10
occurrences of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* (one definitional, nine uses)** and **21 bare
occurrences of *"qualifying retirement"* (one definitional, twenty uses)**.

---

## 2. Pass 10 — every one of the 19 findings, and what happened to it

| # | Rating | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** | serious | *"May be settled"* makes settlement discretionary and standardless | **Enacted** — *"is settled"*. §a item 5 |
| **S2** | serious | Tolling misses the periods for a determination to **take effect**, including G 2's 120-day bound | **Enacted** — §a item 6 |
| **S3** | serious | Tolling misses G 4's own 60-day deadline, which subdivision 4 imposes; § 51.1-156 A makes the collision real | **Enacted** — §a item 6 |
| **S4** | serious | The contingent reading of *"may retire"* moves the admission rule in both directions; the gateway in the modal definition is surplusage | **NOT enacted — §7 item 48, with three ways to take it.** The only open item in this revision that can move a priced quantity |
| **S5** | serious | No outer time limit on the rescission; § 51.1-156 H lets approval land years later; J's reporting duty has closed by then | **NOT enacted — §7 item 49**, four fixes drafted |
| **S6** | serious | The allowance bar now runs for an uncapped period: no cheque at all while the application is pending | **NOT enacted — §7 item 46**, which I had opened before the review for the same reason |
| **M7** | moderate | §5.5's *"G 4 (iii)"* reason is wrong on the bill's own text | **Corrected upstream before this write**, by a concurrent revision that also moved §5.5 to the companion record. Verified. The error and its consequence are at §b item 1 |
| **M8** | moderate | No notice and no review right for the rescission | **Enacted** — §a item 7 |
| **M9** | moderate | D 1's notice omits the rounding-forward rule and states a permission as a prohibition | **Enacted** — §a item 9 |
| **M10** | moderate | The D 1 notice duty has no consequence; the three-day mailing rule is unstated | **Three-day rule enacted; the consequence is §7 item 51**, because it has operative bite |
| **M11** | moderate | *"On account of a rescission"* imports a causation element the absolute bar did not have; the G 2 (ii) refund is undecided | **NOT enacted — §7 item 50**, with the F deeming-list stranding |
| **M12** | moderate | *"Pending"* undefined and the tolling uncapped against M 2's 120-day cap | ***"Pending"* defined and enacted; the cap is §7 item 52**, where I recommend against it and show the trade |
| **M13** | moderate | G 2's 120-day outer bound has no referent for the subdivision 4 cohort | **No edit needed — cured by store revision 33's new term *"the determination date"***, verified on the live text, not assumed |
| **M14** | moderate | The notwithstanding clause lifts the bar for subdivision 2 only, so the partial payer under G 3 is not rescued | **NOT enacted — §7 item 54** |
| **M15** | moderate | Over-cap reinstatement is newly reachable and unbounded in number | **Mostly cured upstream:** store revision 33's S-8 gave reinstatement notice to the money-committee Chairmen and every waiting-list applicant within 15 days, the amount and cause of the excess, a J-report line, and a bar on further elections. **The residue — no bound on the number, no time limit — is §7 item 49** |
| **M16** | moderate | The reinstatement duty has no deadline | **Enacted** — E6 |
| **m17** | minor | The rescission is silent on the G 2 (ii) refund; de minimis | **Recorded; disposed of by item 50's candidate text** |
| **m18** | minor | The prohibition on determining has no stated consequence | **Enacted** — *"of no effect"* |
| **m19** | minor | The rescission date is the Board's own choosing; the prohibition does not reach the notice | **Enacted both limbs** — §a item 8 |

**Eleven enacted, three needing no edit because they were cured upstream — M7, M13 and most of M15, each verified on the live text rather than assumed — and six on the card.** **Every one of the six is policy**: it
either takes something from a member (S5's outer limit), gives the member something the Director has not
agreed (S6, M14), decides who bears money (M11), moves the admission rule (S4), or chooses between two
harms (M12's cap). None was resolved by drafting choice.

**What pass 10 could not re-open.** Both allowance limbs survive, and subsections A and C of § 51.1-155.1
pass both expressly. **Edit 2 is confirmed load-bearing**: a § 51.1-155.1 A retirement is not *"a service
retirement under § 51.1-153"* — those words appear nowhere in A or C — so without the gateway in
*"qualifying retirement"* the separated member's G 4 protection failed on its own terms. The reinstatement
path works; a G 2 (iii) release is not a D 7 release, so G 4's reinstatement sentence applies on its own
terms. The settlement date and the redetermination valuation date stay coherent. There is **no large refund
windfall**. And **no constitutional finding** beyond S1's delegation point: no single-object problem, no
special legislation, no Dillon's Rule problem, no takings, no retroactivity, no vagueness, no preemption.

---

## 5. Cross-reference check — performed in full

**Sources read on `law.lis.virginia.gov` for this revision:** § 51.1-155.1 (all four subsections) and
**§ 51.1-156 A and H**, the second pair because pass 10 found them load-bearing for item 28 and absent from
every check in this document. Both quotations in §5.17 of the bill document are verbatim from that reading,
including H's two-sentence structure — a discretionary waiver in the first sentence and a **mandatory** one
in the second, *"good cause **shall** exist and the Board **shall** waive,"* on the Medical Board's
certification of a disability the member could not have known of. **That is why the rescission trigger is
open-ended in time, and why item 49 exists.**

| Citation | What it says | Checked |
|---|---|---|
| **§ 51.1-155.1 A** | A member in one of the listed § 2.2-2905 positions, involuntarily separated with 20 or more years *"at the date of separation"*, *"may retire with the retirement allowance as provided in subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155" "upon attaining age 50"* (or 60 for the later-hired) | **Passes both allowance limbs expressly.** The split timing — service at separation, entitlement on a later birthday — is what makes pass 10's contingent reading available (item 48) |
| **§ 51.1-155.1 C** | The constitutional officer whose office is lawfully abolished, same terms | **Same reading, and probably inoperative here** — a constitutional officer is not a *"state employee"* under clause (i) of *"eligible member"*. Deliberate surplusage; § 51.1-124.3's definition is with Statutory Researcher |
| **§ 51.1-155.1 B** | The chief executive of an interstate commission, who *"may retire without the reduction … required by subdivision A 2"* | **Excluded by the answer; consequence recorded, not cured** (item 47) |
| **§ 51.1-156 A** | *"Any member in service **or within ninety days after termination of service** … may retire for disability"* | **New citation.** The disability window and G 4's 90-day retirement window are the same window — S3 |
| **§ 51.1-156 H** | Mandatory waiver of the 90-day period on Medical Board certification of an unknowable disability | **New citation.** Approval can land years after separation — item 49 |
| **§ 51.1-153 E** | *"not … more than 90 days prior to the filing of the notice of retirement"* | **Holds.** D 1's new notice preserves it expressly, and the floor is protective in the long-delay case and was harmful in the short-delay case until M9 was folded in |

**Counts and the use-by-use trace are in §5.17 of the bill document.** **Result: no conforming amendment is
required outside the two definitions and the four provisions this revision moves, and none is made.**
Nothing outside this act cross-references either defined term, because § 51.1-142.4 is a new section. **One
stranding found and left standing, on the card: subsection F's deeming sentence lists G 2, G 3 and G 5 and
not G 4** (item 50).

**No priced quantity moves on the enacted text, and there are three independent reasons.** **(1)** Admission
cannot move on the actual-facts reading: § 51.1-155.1 A and C are open only to a member already
involuntarily separated, and *"eligible member"* requires a **member in service**. **(2)** Settlement moves
**toward** the priced basis: every figure prices the admitted cohort as settling, and the closed reading
refused settlement to the separated member and released her reservation. **(3)** G 1 caps it: *"the amount
settled shall be the amount so redetermined or the amount last certified and reserved for the election,
whichever is less."* **Nothing in §3, `model-s8-s9` or the [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85) re-price needs
re-running for this revision.**

**But two things pass 10 raises are live fiscal questions and I am not going to soften them.** **Item 48**:
on the contingent reading the admission rule itself moves, and the model's own sensitivity table ranks the
eligibility horizon as its second-largest driver. **Item 49**: the rescission makes a released reservation
**recallable, over the cap, with no time limit and no report**, which the model books as permanently
released at zero cost; pass 10's bound, on its own stated assumption of a 25% subsection F failure share, is
**up to roughly $803,000 recallable, about +49% on D0's trust cost**, and about +20% at a 10% share. **That
is an assumption of the reviewer's, not a figure of Fiscal's** — which is exactly why the rerun is asked for
rather than quoted.

---

## 6. The ambiguities resolved

Nine, each stated in §a above and summarised in §6.0-35 of the bill document. The ones worth restating:

1. **The settlement operator** — automatic, not *"may"*. §a item 5.
2. **The tolling's reach** — every period, of both kinds, in subdivision 2 and in G 4. §a item 6.
3. **"Pending"** — from filing until the Board first acts. Not *"until finally determined"*, which would
   have carried reconsideration, a § 51.1-156 H waiver request and judicial review and made the tolling
   indefinite.
4. **The redetermination clock** — from the approval or the death, not from the rescission.
5. **The deeming form for lifting the settlement bar** — *"notwithstanding that the rescinded determination
   had taken effect"*, inside the sentence that commands the rescission, rather than an amendment to the bar
   sentence itself. The bar still reads naturally for every other case.
6. **D 1's notice content stated, not cross-referenced.** The whole point of candidate (a) is that the
   member learns the extension is the safer route; a pointer to another sentence does not achieve that.
7. **One consequence stated rather than cured:** the G 2 (ii) refund already paid is not recovered on a
   restoration. Bounded by **less than one month of credit at standard cost**, because G 2 (i) credits whole
   months. Item 50.
8. **Item 30's placement** — the citation sits in the gateway, ahead of the allowance limbs, so *"in each
   case"* still governs both limbs and does not reach the gateway. Form is *"subsection A or C of
   § 51.1-155.1"*, the Code's own style.
9. **Subsection B excluded on instruction**, against my recommendation. Recorded, not cured. Item 47.

---

## 7. Candidate text for every open item. None of it is in the bill.

**Item 45 — rescuing the estate of a member who retired in a non-qualifying retirement and then died.** To
**G 4's second sentence**, nine words:

> <u>Clause (i) of this subdivision does not apply where the member has retired in a retirement that is not
> a qualifying retirement before the date of death**, except where a determination under subdivision 2 has
> taken effect**.</u>

**I recommend against it.** A member who retired reduced made a choice the program told her would cost her
the subsidy, and dying afterwards does not change the choice. Pass 10 notes the question and does not press
it.

**Item 46 — the allowance bar during a pending disability application (pass 10's S6).** One sentence in
**G 2**, after its third sentence:

> <u>The preceding sentence does not prevent the payment of a retirement allowance to a member while an
> application of the member for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter is pending, and where a
> retirement allowance is paid under this sentence the determination required by this subdivision shall take
> effect notwithstanding that payment.</u>

**I recommend enacting it.** Pass 10's worked case is 14 months with no allowance at all, and the no-recovery
limb absorbs any overpayment, so the Commonwealth bears the cost either way and paying her is strictly
better. The second limb is necessary because G 2's third sentence also requires the determination to take
effect *"before the first payment of any retirement allowance."*

**Item 47 — the expressio unius consequence of naming A and C.** One sentence in each definition:

> <u>The naming of a provision in this definition does not imply that a retirement under any other provision
> of this chapter is not a service retirement under § 51.1-153.</u>

**I recommend enacting it** rather than reopening subsection B.

**Item 48 — the contingent reading (pass 10's S4). Three ways, and they are mutually exclusive.**

**(a) My recommendation — confine the route, keep the answer.** One sentence at the end of *"unreduced
retirement eligibility date"*:

> <u>For the purposes of this definition the member may retire under subsection A or C of § 51.1-155.1 only
> where the member has incurred an involuntary separation, or the member's office has been lawfully
> abolished, as the case may be, on or before the date as of which the determination is made.</u>

It keeps the Director's answer intact, confirms in text the actual-facts reading on which every figure in
the package is priced, and costs one sentence.

**(b) Pass 10's preference — delete the gateway from the modal definition and keep it only in *"qualifying
retirement."*** The reviewer traced the deletion through clauses (v) to (viii), subsection C clause (ii),
D 1's certification, subsection E and G 3 and found nothing breaks, and I agree with that trace: on the
actual-facts reading the modal gateway does no work. **The cost is that it reads as a retreat from the
answer**, and anyone who later takes the contingent reading of the remaining words gets no help from the
section.

**(c) Leave it as enacted.** **I do not recommend this.** The ambiguity sits on the admission rule, which the
model ranks as its second-largest driver.

**Item 49 — the rescission's time limit and the reporting hole (pass 10's S5 and M15). Four fixes.**

> **(i)** <u>… and the member is thereafter approved for a disability retirement allowance under this chapter
> **upon an application filed no later than the date on which the determination took effect** …</u>
>
> **(ii)** to J 1's list: <u>the number of determinations rescinded and the service credit restored under
> subdivision G 4, and every amount by which a reservation reinstated under subdivision G 4 caused a
> limitation in subdivision D 2 to be exceeded</u>
>
> **(iii)** J's tail: <u>… until the first December 1 following **the later of that date and the date of the
> last rescission under subdivision G 4**</u>
>
> **(iv)** enactment clause 3 clause (i): add the rescission and the reinstatement expressly.

**Store revision 33 has since closed most of the over-cap half of M15** — reinstatement now carries notice
to the money-committee Chairmen and to every waiting-list applicant within 15 days, the amount and cause of
the excess, a J-report line, and a bar on further elections until the excess is eliminated — so what these
four fixes add is **time and tail**, not the over-cap notice. **I recommend all four, and (i) is the only one
with policy content** — it takes from the member the
§ 51.1-156 H case, the unknowable disability certified years later, which is precisely the case H exists to
protect. If you want only one, take (ii), (iii) and (iv): the reporting is what makes the $3,000,000 limit a
real control.

**Item 50 — the refund, the clawback characterisation, and F's deeming list (pass 10's M11 and m17).**

> <u>For the avoidance of doubt, an amount refunded under clause (ii) of subdivision 2 is not recoverable
> from any person; where a determination under subdivision 2 is rescinded under this subdivision the Board
> shall restore service credit to the extent of the amounts paid under the election and not refunded; and the
> member, or any employer that paid on the member's behalf, may pay to the Board the amount refunded no later
> than 90 days after the Board gives notice of the rescission, whereupon the Board shall restore the whole of
> the service credit reduced under the determination.</u>

And in **subsection F**: *"Nothing required or permitted by subdivision G 2, G 3**, G 4** or G 5 …"*

**I recommend both.** The first decides a contested amount without coercing anyone; the second is a one-word
cure for a stranding.

**Item 51 — a consequence for the D 1 notice duty (pass 10's M10).**

> <u>Where the Board gives a statement or notice that does not state the matters required by this
> subdivision, the statement or notice is not given for the purposes of this subdivision until the Board
> gives the member those matters in writing.</u>

**I recommend it, with the bite stated:** the periods that run from the giving of the statement, and the
extension of her final qualifying retirement date, would then run from the complete one.

**Item 52 — a cap on the tolling (pass 10's M12).**

> <u>… and the aggregate of all tolling under this subdivision shall not exceed 180 days.</u>

**I recommend no cap.** It closes pass 10's free-option path — a member who expects to fail subsection F
filing an application she expects to lose, because death during pendency vests the whole election at the
pilot price — but it re-creates for the member with a genuine 14-month application the exact contradiction
the tolling was enacted to cure: the Board commanded to determine while forbidden to determine. **The
definition of *"pending"* already bounds the abuse**; the cap trades a real member's credit for a
hypothetical member's option.

**Item 54 — the partial payer (pass 10's M14).** The notwithstanding limb lifts the bar for a **subdivision
2** determination only, so the member who completed payment in part, was credited pro rata under G 3, and is
then approved for disability gets **no rescission and no settlement** — while the full payer who merely
