missed her window gets everything restored. **G 4's own death branch expressly rescues the partial payer.**
The fix is *"a determination under subdivision 2 **or 3**"* in both places, with restoration on the death
branch's formula. **I recommend it, for parity with the death branch**, and I flag that it is a money
decision: it settles a subsidy for a member who never completed payment, at the pro-rata credit.

---

## 8. Status

**Six edits, three provisions, four paragraphs of §1 changed, item 29 already in the text, no figure moved
on the enacted text, two new citations checked.** Eleven pass-10 findings enacted and three cured upstream
and verified; **six are on the card as items 48, 49, 50, 51, 52 and 54**, with items 45, 46, 47 and 53 also
open. **The six edits of this revision have had no adversarial pass of their own.**

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel.
Pre-decisional.**

---

## 9. [MOO-89](/MOO/issues/MOO-89)'s F-7 research, and what it does to this drafting

**It supports the answer on item 30, for better reasons than mine.** § 51.1-155.1 has **no retirement
machinery of its own** — no notification clause, no effective-date rule — while the General Assembly
demonstrably builds free-standing authorities when it means to (§ 51.1-156 A and D, § 51.1-138 C each have
both); `Va. Code § 1-217` forecloses the catchline argument, catchlines being *"mere catchwords"* that *"do
not constitute part of the act"*; and VRS administers § 51.1-155.1 as an ordinary service retirement with a
certified special waiver on form VRS-8 on top of the ordinary VRS-5. **But it is the better reading and not
a safe harbour**, which is why putting it in text was worth doing, at zero conforming amendments.

**It contradicts the reason I gave for excluding subsection B, and that error is mine.** I told the Director
the B member *"fails the positive limb"* because her allowance is computed under A 2 with the reduction
waived. **The research concludes she passes**: A 2's own first sentence provides that *"[t]he allowance shall
be determined in the same manner as for normal retirement,"* so A 2 **is** the A 1 computation plus a
reduction B waives — and **§ 51.1-153 A, ordinary normal retirement, names subdivision A 1 nowhere at all**,
so the reading I relied on would also exclude the 65-year-old with five years of service. The asymmetry was
left in place by **SB 87 (2014)**, Chapter 356, on block votes, with no record noticing it. **Hence item
41.**

**One thing recorded because it is inert here and will not be inert forever.** **§ 51.1-169 D 1** gives a
hybrid member's allowance as *"one percent"* of average final compensation, so it is **not computed under
§ 51.1-155 A 1 at all** — a direct hit on the positive limb for everyone hired on or after 1 January 2014.
Clause (iii) of *"eligible member"* excludes hybrid participants, so nothing in this act turns on it, and §7
item 8's overlap population should be checked against it.

# Store revision 52 — the full record for [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64)'s seven answers

**Companion record to [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) store revision 52.** The bill's §0.0, §5.31, §6.0-52, §7 and §8 point here. **Thirteen edits in four provisions of §1** — the definition of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*, subdivision G 3, subdivision G 4 (nine edits) and subdivision J 1 (three edits). **+3,337 characters of bill text.** Verified after the write against the live body: every one of the thirteen present exactly once, the text each replaced gone, **exactly four paragraphs of §1 different** and §1's paragraph count unchanged at **92**.

## 1. The seven answers, and where each one is

| Question | Answer taken as given | Enacted |
|---|---|---|
| **F-1** (fatal) | cure in full | Edits 2 and 7 — both insertions |
| **S-1** | both repairs | Edits 11, 12 and 13 |
| **S-2 with M-6** | the carve-out **and** the saving | Edits 1 and 3 |
| **S-3** | extend to clause (iii) | Edits 1, 2 and 5 |
| **S-4** | the restoration-and-arrears duty | Edit 6 |
| **Bundle** | m2 + m5 + g3 + refund + quantify | Edits 10, 8, 9, 4, and §3 |
| **§7 item 53** | move the record out | 101,593 characters moved; §0.1 is the index |

**§7 items 89 to 97 and 99 are CLOSED. Item 98 was not asked and stays open. Three new items — 103, 104 and 105 — are open and none is enacted.**

## 2. The redline — all thirteen edits, FIND and ENACTED verbatim

### Edit 1 — Items 91(a) and 92. G 4, the rescission sentence — the carve-out for the application § 51.1-156 H compelled the Board to admit, and clause (iii)'s new rescission trigger

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> took effect, or thereafter dies in a case to which clause (i) of this subdivision applies, the Board shall rescind

**ENACTED:**

> took effect, or upon an application as to which the Board was required by subsection H of § 51.1-156 to waive the ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of that section, or thereafter dies in a case to which clause (i) of this subdivision applies, or the Board thereafter determines that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board, the Board shall rescind

*(+315 characters)*

### Edit 2 — Items 92 and 89(i). G 4, the rescission sentence — the 60-day deadline gains the third trigger, and the FATAL cure: the D 7 release limb of the settlement bar is disapplied

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> no later than 60 days after the date on which the member is so approved or dies, and the certified subsidy for the election is settled under this subdivision notwithstanding that the rescinded determination had taken effect.

**ENACTED:**

> no later than 60 days after the date on which the member is so approved, or dies, or the Board makes that determination, and the certified subsidy for the election is settled under this subdivision notwithstanding that the rescinded determination had taken effect, and notwithstanding that the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7.

*(+152 characters)*

### Edit 3 — Item 91(b). G 4, new sentence — the express saving for every other late-filed approval

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> Where the rescinded determination is a determination under subdivision 3, the Board shall credit the member

**ENACTED:**

> A determination under subdivision 2 or 3 that has taken effect is not affected by an approval of the member for a disability retirement allowance upon an application filed after the date on which the determination took effect, except as this subdivision provides for the rescission of the determination. Where the rescinded determination is a determination under subdivision 3, the Board shall credit the member

*(+304 characters)*

### Edit 4 — Item 97. G 4, the subdivision-3 rescission — the refund limb, with the death branch's own 60-day deadline and adverse-tax fallback

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> and shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase. Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made or took effect before the Board learned of an involuntary separation

**ENACTED:**

> and shall recertify the certified subsidy to reflect the service credit so credited, and subdivision D 6 applies to that recertification only so far as it provides for the reservation of an increase; and shall refund, to the member and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid, any amount paid that exceeds the cost of the service credit so credited. The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost. Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made or took effect before the Board learned of an involuntary separation

*(+523 characters)*

### Edit 5 — Item 92, conforming. G 4 — the redetermination clock gains the third trigger

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> Where the Board rescinds a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 as this subdivision requires, the period within which this subdivision requires the redetermination to be made runs from the date on which the member is so approved or dies.

**ENACTED:**

> Where the Board rescinds a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 as this subdivision requires, the period within which this subdivision requires the redetermination to be made runs from the date on which the member is so approved, or dies, or the Board makes the determination stated in this subdivision that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board.

*(+165 characters)*

### Edit 6 — Item 93. G 4, new sentences — restoration, recertification, settlement, 60 days and arrears on a reversal or modification, with both bar limbs disapplied

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

**ENACTED:**

A certified subsidy settled as required by the preceding sentence is settled notwithstanding that the reversed or modified determination had taken effect and notwithstanding that the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7. The Board shall give the member, or the person entitled to any benefit payable on the member's death, written notice of a rescission under this subdivision,

*(+881 characters)*

### Edit 7 — Item 89(ii). G 4, the reinstatement limb — extended to a reservation released IN ACCORDANCE WITH D 7 where the determination is later rescinded, reversed or modified

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> Where a reservation has been released otherwise than in accordance with subdivision D 7, the Board shall reinstate it,

### Edit 8 — Item 95(b). G 4 — the one authorised offset, month for month

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> or of the member's estate to the retirement system, to an employer, or to the Commonwealth.</u>

**ENACTED:**

Nothing in this subdivision or in subsection F prevents the Board from applying a retirement allowance paid to the member for a month against a disability retirement allowance payable to the member for the same month.</u>

*(+218 characters)*

### Edit 9 — Item 96. G 3, second sentence — yields where a G 3 determination is rescinded under subdivision 4

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> A member credited under this subdivision shall not be treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of the election.</u>

**ENACTED:**

> A member credited under this subdivision shall not be treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date by reason of the election. This sentence does not apply where a determination under this subdivision is rescinded under subdivision 4.</u>

*(+108 characters)*

### Edit 10 — Item 94. "Unreduced retirement eligibility date" — the confinement operates for the purposes of the SECTION

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> For the purposes of this definition the member may retire under subsection A or C of § 51.1-155.1 only where

**ENACTED:**

> For the purposes of this section the member may retire under subsection A or C of § 51.1-155.1 only where

*(+-3 characters)*

### Edit 11 — Item 90(a). J 1, limb (a) — the two classes G 2 excepts from any determination

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> has been settled under subdivision G 1 or G 4, cancelled under subdivision G 5, or determined under subdivision G 2 or G 3 and (b)

**ENACTED:**

> has been settled under subdivision G 1 or G 4, cancelled under subdivision D 6 or G 5, or determined under subdivision G 2 or G 3, or has had its reservation released under subdivision D 7 without any service credit having been credited to the member, and (b)

*(+129 characters)*

### Edit 12 — Item 90(b). J 1, limb (b) — bounded to rescissions already occurred

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> and (b) the date of the last rescission under subdivision G 4, to the Governor,

**ENACTED:**

> and (b) the date of the last rescission under subdivision G 4 that has occurred on or before the date stated in clause (a), to the Governor,

*(+61 characters)*

### Edit 13 — Item 90(b). J 1, new final sentence — one further report for a later rescission

**FIND (one occurrence in §1, verified before and after the write):**

> and every other matter this section requires the Board to state in the report.</u>

**ENACTED:**

> and every other matter this section requires the Board to state in the report. Where a rescission under subdivision G 4 occurs after the Board has made the last report required by this subdivision, the Board shall make one further report, limited to that rescission and its consequences, no later than the first December 1 following the rescission.</u>

*(+270 characters)*

## 3. The four changes inside the approved text that are mine

Reproduced from §6.0-52 items 1 to 4, which is the authoritative copy in the bill.

1. **Item 93 as carded would have reproduced the fatal defect in new words.** A determination reversed on review **has** taken effect, so G 4's bar forbade the settlement item 93 commanded, and the released reservation was reinstated by nothing. Both limbs are drafted into edit 6 and into edit 7's trigger. **This is drafting, not policy: a rescue a neighbouring sentence forbids is not the rescue that was approved.**
2. **The redetermination clock gains item 92's third trigger** (edit 5). Otherwise a 90-day duty had no day to count from.
3. **Item 97's refund gains the death branch's 60-day payment deadline and its adverse-tax fallback** (edit 4). A payment duty with no date is unenforceable, and the words are the death branch's own, two sentences earlier.
4. **Item 93's arrears limb reaches a *modification* as well as a reversal** (edit 6). As carded it paid her as though no determination existed, which **overpays her against a modified determination that survives** and which subsection F makes irrecoverable. **This one moves money, so it is carded as §7 item 105 as well as recorded here.**

## 4. Candidate text for the three new open items — drafted, enacted nowhere

### Item 103 — a member-initiated route to a clause (iii) determination

> <u>A member may file with the Board written evidence that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. The Board shall determine whether the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board and shall give the member written notice of the determination and of the reasons for it no later than 30 days after the member files that evidence, and a determination under this sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M.</u>

Modelled word for word on G 4's own involuntary-separation route, which is the only member-initiated determination the subdivision already has. **Recommend enacting.**

### Item 104 — the subsection J lines the new provisions do not reach

In subdivision J 1's list of report contents, after *"the number of determinations rescinded and the service credit restored under subdivision G 4"*:

> <u>; the number of determinations reversed or modified on reconsideration or on judicial review and the service credit restored or credited on account of them; and every amount paid or refunded under subdivision G 4 on account of a rescission, reversal, or modification</u>

**Recommend enacting.** Item 97's refunds are a payment out of the trust that appears in no line of J 1, and item 93's reversals are not rescissions and so are counted nowhere. Item 99's quantification will be read against these lines.

### Item 105 — confirmation of the arrears formula

The enacted words are *"every amount that would have been payable to the member had the determination, **as reversed or modified**, taken effect on the date on which the determination took effect."* The carded words were *"had the determination **not taken effect**."* **Recommend the enacted form stand.** To revert, delete *", as reversed or modified,"* and restore *"not taken effect"* — one sentence, and it is the Director's call because it decides what the member is paid where a smaller reduction survives.

## 5. The cross-reference check

### §5.31 Store revision 52 — the thirteen edits, chased in both directions

**Outward — every citation the new words introduce or rely on, each opened and checked.**

| Citation | Where I put it | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **subsection H of § 51.1-156** | item 91(a), the carve-out | **The only citation of § 51.1-156 anywhere in §1, so it is wholly new and was verified on `law.lis.virginia.gov` today.** H's first sentence is permissive (*"the Board **may** waive the ninety-day notification periods set forth in subsections A and B"*); its second is mandatory (*"good cause **shall** exist and the Board **shall waive** such ninety-day notification periods"*) on the Medical Board's certification of (a) disability existing at termination, (b) no knowledge within 90 days, (c) no ability with reasonable inquiry to ascertain. **The carve-out is bounded to the mandatory limb and uses H's own words — *"the ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of that section."*** |
| **subsection A or B of § 51.1-156** | item 91(a) | Both exist and both carry a ninety-day notification period running from termination of service. Cited by designator and not paraphrased. |
| **subdivision D 7** | items 89(i), 89(ii), 90(a) | 9 citations in §1, 6 of them *"in accordance with subdivision D 7"*. The release limb of the G 4 bar and the *"otherwise than"* trigger of the reinstatement limb both read on it, which is the mechanism item 89 cures. |
| **subdivision D 6** | item 90(a) | 7 citations. D 6 is the cancellation route G 2's fourth sentence excepts from any determination, which is the first of limb (a)'s two new classes. |
| **subdivision D 2** | item 89(ii), consequentially | 6 citations. The reinstatement limb charges a reinstated reservation against D 2's limitations notwithstanding that the amount available is exceeded, so insertion (ii) enlarges the over-cap route the Director accepted at §7 item 40. **All four safeguards enacted there apply to it unchanged** — money-committee notice, waiting-list notice, J reporting, no further elections — and I confirmed each is in the same sentence chain the new trigger feeds. |
| **subdivision G 5, subdivision G 2 or G 3** | item 90(a) | Present and unchanged; limb (a)'s existing clauses are preserved word for word and only added to. |
| **subsection M** | items 93, 89(ii) | 28 citations. M is the reconsideration and review route item 93 reads on, and the rescission notice already gives the member an M route. |
| **subsection F** | item 95(b) | F's deeming list is what makes the offset bar bite, so the authorisation names F as well as G 4. |
| **subsection J** | item 90 | 12 citations, 10 of them *"required by subsection J"*. No other provision states J 1's terminal date, so limb (a) and limb (b) are the only places it is set. |
| **subdivision B 4 of § 51.1-142.2** | item 97 | 15 citations. The refund limb values the credit at the same cost the death branch and the rescission crediting already use. |
| **subdivision 4** | item 96 | 12 citations. G 3's new second sentence cites subdivision 4 by designator rather than describing the rescission. |

**Inward — every provision that reads the four I changed.**

- **The definition of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*** is used 12 times in §1. Item 94 changes *"this definition"* to *"this section"* in the confining sentence, which **widens** the confinement's reach from one definition to every use in the section. I chased all 12: the confinement can only ever **exclude** a § 51.1-155.1 A or C route for a member who has not actually incurred the separation, and in each of the 12 the direction is exclusion or no effect. **The twin definition *"qualifying retirement"* carries the same gateway and is untouched** — that asymmetry is the ground item 94 exists to remove, and it is now removed without amending the twin.
- **G 3** is cited as *"subdivision G 2 or G 3"* in J 1 and as *"subdivision 3"* five times inside subsection G. Item 96's new sentence is confined to G 3's own second sentence and switches it off only on a rescission under subdivision 4; it changes no other reader of G 3.
- **G 4** is cited 8 times as *"subdivision G 4"* and is the subdivision nine of the thirteen edits sit in. The five *"subdivision 2 or 3"* references are all inside G 4 and all now read on the same rescission sentence.
- **J 1** has no inward citation by designator — it is reached as *"the report required by subsection J"* — so the three J 1 edits strand nothing. The one further report required by item 90(b) is a duty of the Board with a named actor, a stated content limit, and a 1 December deadline.

**Result: no conforming amendment is required outside the four provisions amended, and none is made.** Two conforming changes **inside** them were required and are made: the redetermination clock in G 4 gains item 92's third trigger, and insertion (ii) gains item 93's reversal, each because the answered text would otherwise command a duty with no referent. Both are at §6.0-52.


### §6.0-52 Ambiguities resolved in store revision 52

**Three changes inside the Director's approved text are mine. They are listed first, and none of them changes which member passes either definitional test.**

1. **Item 93 as carded would have reproduced the fatal defect in new words, and I did not enact it that way.** The carded sentence commanded the Board to *"recertify and settle the certified subsidy as this subdivision requires"* after a reversal on reconsideration or judicial review. But G 4's bar forbids settlement *"after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect"* — and a determination reversed on review **has** taken effect; that is the premise of the whole sentence. The bar's other limb forbids settlement once the reservation has been released under D 7, and nothing reinstated it. **So the carded words commanded a settlement two sentences forbade, which is item 54's fatal defect at a different point.** I drafted both limbs into item 93 (*"notwithstanding that the reversed or modified determination had taken effect and notwithstanding that the reservation … has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7"*) and extended insertion (ii)'s trigger to a reversal or modification as well as a rescission. **This is drafting, not policy: the Director approved the rescue, and a rescue a neighbouring sentence forbids is not the rescue that was approved.**
2. **Item 92's redetermination clock gains the third trigger.** G 4 provides that where the Board rescinds, *"the period within which this subdivision requires the redetermination to be made runs from the date on which the member is so approved or dies."* Item 92 adds a third rescission trigger — the Board's determination of its own error — and the clock had no referent for it, so a duty with a 90-day period had no day to count from. Conformed in the Board's own words.
3. **Item 97's refund gains the death branch's payment deadline and its adverse-tax fallback.** The carded limb created a payment duty with no date, which is unenforceable, and the death branch two sentences earlier already carries exactly the words needed: payment within 60 days of crediting, and, to the extent a refund cannot be paid without adverse federal tax consequence, application of the amount to additional service credit at the standard cost. **Taking the parity the Director asked for and leaving out the deadline would have been taking half of it.**

**Ambiguities I had to resolve to write the answered text, with the resolution.**

4. **Item 93's arrears limb is drafted for a *modification* as well as a reversal, and the carded words were not.** The carded sentence paid her *"every amount that would have been payable … had the determination **not taken effect**."* On a **reversal** that is right. On a **modification** — subsection M or a court leaving a smaller reduction standing — it pays her as though no determination existed at all, which **overpays her against the determination that survives**, and subsection F's no-collection limb means the Commonwealth never gets it back. Enacted as *"had the determination, **as reversed or modified**, taken effect on the date on which the determination took effect,"* which is identical to the carded words on a reversal and is the only non-absurd reading on a modification. **It is the one of my four changes that moves money, so it is also carded as §7 item 105 for the Director to confirm rather than left in the note alone.**

5. **Item 89(i) is placed in the rescission sentence rather than in the bar.** Either place cures the G 3 branch; the rescission sentence already reads *"a determination under subdivision 2 or 3"*, so putting the disapplication there cures the **pre-existing G 2 branch at the same price**, and the bar keeps its general form for every case where nothing has been rescinded. **The half cure and the complete cure cost the same ~235 characters, which is why the complete cure is what I asked for and what the Director took.**
6. **Item 90(a)'s second new class is drafted as a D 7 release *"without any service credit having been credited to the member"*, not as a bare D 7 release.** A D 7 release that follows a G 3 crediting is not an election with nothing left to report; the class G 2's fourth sentence excepts is the one where the reservation went and the member got nothing. The narrower words except only that class.
7. **Item 90(b)'s further report is *"limited to that rescission and its consequences."*** Without the limit the Board would owe a complete annual report, cumulative figures and all, years after the programme closed, for one rescission. The limit is what makes the duty dischargeable, and the Board can still state on any 1 December whether limb (a) is satisfied — which is what it cannot do for *"the last rescission."*
8. **Item 91(a) is bounded to § 51.1-156 H's mandatory limb, as recommended and approved.** H's first sentence is the Board's own discretion, exercised with this consequence in view; its second is not a choice at all, and the Medical Board's certification is the tightest boundary in the chapter. **The looser alternative — *"as to which the Board has waived a period under subsection H"* — was offered and not taken, and I did not substitute it.**
9. **Item 91(b)'s saving is drafted to except the rescission expressly** (*"except as this subdivision provides for the rescission of the determination"*). Without that exception the saving and the carve-out contradict each other in the one case the carve-out exists for.
10. **Item 92 uses *"the Board thereafter determines that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board"*** — clause (iii)'s own words, not a new formula. G 4 already owes that determination within 60 days of the final qualifying retirement date, with a notice and a report line, so the new trigger inherits an existing duty rather than creating a standardless one. **Subdivision B 4 f's carve-out is untouched**, so a B 4 f cost determination is still not an error of the Board for these purposes.
11. **Item 93 says *"restore or credit service credit as this subdivision provides"*, not *"restore the service credit reduced under it."*** A subdivision 3 determination reduces nothing — it credits the months paid for and releases the reservation — so the carded verb had a zero-extent object for half the determinations item 93 reaches. This is the same repair already enacted as M-4 in store revision 49, and item 93 is drafted to match it rather than to re-create the defect.
12. **Item 95(b) authorises one offset and nothing else.** It names the month on both sides — a retirement allowance paid **for a month** against a disability allowance payable **for the same month** — so it cannot be read as a general power to recover. **The alternative, narrowing G 4's no-collection limb, was offered and not taken; it would have taken a protection from every member to reach a duplicate a few will have.**
13. **Item 96 switches off G 3's second sentence only on a rescission under subdivision 4**, by one sentence attached to it, rather than by qualifying the sentence in place. The sentence keeps its ordinary operation for every member whose G 3 determination stands.
14. **The thirteen edits carry no nested `<u>` tags.** The whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language and is already underlined at paragraph level, so a nested tag would be redundant markup rather than amendatory markup. **A reader searching for `<u>` will not find these spans individually, and that is the document's existing convention** — the same thing happened to two edits in store revision 49. Every word added in this revision is new language and is underlined by the paragraph-level tag that encloses it.

**What I did not do.** I added no provision no answer reached. §7 item 98 was not asked and is not enacted. The three drafting choices above are repairs to words the answers put in, and each is recorded here with its ground rather than left to be found.


## 6. No figure moves

Every figure in the package prices the admitted cohort — the unreduced subdivision A 1 cohort reached through § 51.1-153 A, B 2 or B 3 — **as settling**. Edits 1 to 7 and the refund limb move **settlement** toward that basis by removing bars and gaps that refused it; the J 1, definition, offset and G 3 edits touch a reporting date, a scope phrase, an offset and a deeming sentence. **No admission test, no clause (v) to (viii) determination and no subsection C clause (ii) cap changes, and nothing in §3, `model-s8-s9` or the [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85) reprice needs re-running.**

**Two of the thirteen spend money one-sidedly**, both on answers the Director took on exactly that footing: item 46's pendency allowance, now net of the one offset item 95 authorises, and item 50's irrecoverable clause (ii) refund. **Neither answer is reopened.** §3 now requires the § 30-19.1:7 statement to quantify both; the amounts are Fiscal's and are requested at [MOO-151](/MOO/issues/MOO-151), not asserted.

## 7. Status

**Store revision 52 is in the canonical document** (document revision `35b45851`, 455,652 characters, 68,636 characters of headroom). **The thirteen edits have had no adversarial pass of their own** — that is **pass 17**, sent as [MOO-152](/MOO/issues/MOO-152). **Publication is no longer blocked on F-1.**

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel. Pre-decisional.**

title: Store revision 60 — the full record for MOO-64's eight answers (redline, cross-reference check, drafter's note, pass-18 triage)
body:
# Store revision 60 — the record for [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64)'s eight answers of 12 October 2026

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by counsel, pre-decisional.**

**Thirteen substitutions, five provisions, and they are in [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) at store revision 60** (document revision `6b1e227f`, 250,229 characters). Verified **after** the write against the live body: each of the thirteen ENACTED strings present exactly once, each replaced string gone, **exactly five paragraphs of §1 different from store revision 59** — the definition of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* in subsection A, subsection E, subdivision G 4, subdivision J 1 and subdivision M 2 — and **§1's paragraph count unchanged at 93**.

## 1. The eight answers, and where each one is

| Question | Answer | Where it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Item 114** — amend the settlement bar once? | **Enact** | Edit 1, G 4 |
| **Item 115** — condition the reversal sentence's settlement duty? | **Enact** | Edit 2, G 4 |
| **Item 116** — net rather than gross arrears? | **Both limbs** | Edit 3, G 4 |
| **Item 117** — close the class the carve-out misses? | **Both clauses** | Edit 4, G 4 |
| **Item 118** — cap pendency and give J 1 a long-stop? | **Both** | Edits 5 and 6, G 4 and J 1 |
| **Item 119** — the missing temporal rule? | **Enact** | Edit 7, the definition |
| **Items 103 and 104** | **Both** | Edits 8 and 9, G 4 and J 1 |
| **Items 120 and 121** — the cheap bundle | **120(a), 120(b), 121's M 2 limb. NOT the interest limb.** | Edits 10 to 13, subsection E, G 4 and M 2 |

**Every answer is taken as given.** Four wordings inside those answers are mine and are at §4 below. **The interest limb of item 121 was not selected and is drafted nowhere.** Class 3 of item 117 — the discretionary waiver — remains excluded, which is the line the Director drew on item 91.

**Numbering.** This is **store revision 60, not 59**, and the new items are **126 and 127, not 123 and 124**: a concurrent run published store revision 59 under this cut, which answered items 88 and 108 to 113, opened items 123 to 125, and moved §7's item list out to [`bill-text-s8-item-list`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-item-list). **Item 113's enactment changed one of this revision's own anchors** — J 1's further-report sentence gained an independent trigger — so edit 6 was re-anchored to the amended sentence before it was applied. **Store revision 59 touched none of the other twelve anchors and nothing in it is reversed, re-opened or renumbered here.**

## 2. The redline — all thirteen edits, FIND and ENACTED verbatim

Every edit is inside the whole-paragraph underline that marks § 51.1-142.4 as new language, so no inner `<u>` markup is used; the amendments to subsection E and the definition sit inside the same device.

### Edit 1 · Item 114 — G 4, the settlement bar (one amendment, both limbs)

**FIND:**

> released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect, and no certified subsidy is settled more than once

**ENACTED:**

> released in full in accordance with subdivision D 7 and has not been reinstated under this subdivision, or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect and has not been rescinded, reversed, or modified, and no certified subsidy is settled more than once

### Edit 2 · Item 115 — G 4, the reversal sentence's settlement duty, conditioned

**FIND:**

> and shall recertify and settle the certified subsidy as this subdivision requires, no later than 60 days after the reversal or modification

**ENACTED:**

> and, where the determination as reversed or modified is such that the certified subsidy falls to be settled under subdivision 1 or under this subdivision, shall recertify and settle it accordingly, no later than 60 days after the reversal or modification

### Edit 3 · Item 116 — G 4, the arrears formula, net and with the total-reversal limb

**FIND:**

> shall include every amount that would have been payable to the member had the determination, as reversed or modified, taken effect on the date on which the determination took effect.

**ENACTED:**

> shall include every amount by which the amounts paid to the member fall short of the amounts that would have been payable to the member had the determination, as reversed or modified, taken effect on the date on which the determination took effect, or, where the determination is reversed in its entirety, had no determination been made.

### Edit 4 · Item 117 — G 4, the rescission sentence's disability carve-out, both clauses

**FIND:**

> upon an application filed no later than the date on which the determination took effect, or upon an application as to which the Board was required by subsection H of § 51.1-156 to waive the ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of that section,

**ENACTED:**

> upon an application filed no later than the date on which the determination took effect, or upon an application the filing of which did not require a waiver of a ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of § 51.1-156, or upon an application as to which the Medical Board has made a certification described in clause (ii) of subsection H of § 51.1-156,

### Edit 5 · Item 118(a) — G 4, the 120-day aggregate

**FIND:**

> except that the aggregate of all such non-running by reason of such requests shall not exceed 120 days

**ENACTED:**

> except that the aggregate of all such non-running by reason of such requests and by reason of applications for a disability retirement allowance filed after the first such application shall not exceed 120 days

### Edit 6 · Item 118(b) — J 1, the reporting long-stop (re-anchored to store revision 59's amended sentence)

**FIND:**

> the Board shall make one further report, limited to that rescission or matter and its consequences, no later than the first December 1 following that rescission or the date on which that matter arises, as the case may be.

**ENACTED:**

> the Board shall make one further report, limited to that rescission or matter and its consequences, no later than the first December 1 following that rescission or the date on which that matter arises, as the case may be. In no event shall the Board be required to report under this subdivision after the first December 1 following the twentieth anniversary of the expiration of this section.

### Edit 7 · Item 119 — subsection A, the definition of "unreduced retirement eligibility date"

**FIND:**

> as the case may be, on or before the date as of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined.

**ENACTED:**

> as the case may be, on or before the date as of which the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date is determined or, where this sentence is applied otherwise than in the determination of the member's unreduced retirement eligibility date, on or before the member's effective date of retirement.

### Edit 8 · Item 103 — G 4, the member-initiated route to an error determination

**FIND:**

> A determination under the preceding sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M.

**ENACTED:**

> A determination under the preceding sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M. Where a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect, a member may file with the Board written evidence that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. The Board shall determine whether the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board and shall give the member written notice of the determination and of the reasons for it no later than 30 days after the member files that evidence, and a determination under this sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M.

### Edit 9 · Item 104 — J 1, the report contents

**FIND:**

> the number of determinations rescinded and the service credit restored under subdivision G 4;

**ENACTED:**

> the number of determinations rescinded and the service credit restored under subdivision G 4; the number of determinations reversed or modified on reconsideration or on judicial review and the service credit restored or credited on account of them; every amount paid or refunded under subdivision G 4 on account of a rescission, reversal, or modification;

### Edit 10 · Item 120(a) — subsection E, the crediting-bar exception

**FIND:**

> except as subdivision G 4 provides in the case of the member's death, and, except for the purposes of the definition

**ENACTED:**

> except as subdivision G 4 provides in the case of the member's death, of the member's approval for a disability retirement allowance, or of an error of the Board, and, except for the purposes of the definition

### Edit 11 · Item 120(b) — G 4, the death branch's refund

**FIND:**

> The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, except that to the extent the refund may not be paid without adverse federal tax consequence the Board shall apply that amount to the purchase of additional service credit for the member at the standard cost.

**ENACTED:**

> The Board shall pay a refund required by the preceding sentence within 60 days after it credits the service credit, and shall pay the whole of that refund to the member's estate and to any employer that paid on the member's behalf in proportion to the amounts each paid and shall apply no amount of it to the purchase of service credit.

### Edit 12 · Item 121 — M 2, the failure clause

**FIND:**

> or by a failure of the Board to make a determination or to give a notice within a period required by this section, may obtain

**ENACTED:**

> or by a failure of the Board to make a determination, to give a notice, or to make a payment within a period required by this section, may obtain

### Edit 13 · Item 121, conforming — M 2, the reconsideration-timing limb

**FIND:**

> in the case of such a failure, at any time before the Board makes the determination or gives the notice

**ENACTED:**

> in the case of such a failure, at any time before the Board makes the determination, gives the notice, or makes the payment

## 3. The cross-reference check — §5.39 of the bill, reproduced

**Result: no conforming amendment is required outside the six provisions amended, and none is made.** Every citation the thirteen substitutions create was opened and read before it was enacted; every provision that cites an amended sentence was read against the amended text.

**Outward — the citations the new words make.**

| New citation | Read where | Holds? |
|---|---|---|
| § 51.1-156 **A** and **B** (item 117(a), *"a ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B"*) | `law.lis.virginia.gov`, 12 October 2026 | Yes. Each permits a member *"in service or within ninety days after termination of service"* to retire for disability. The clause reaches **both** the member still in service, for whom neither subsection sets any period, and the member inside the ninety days — see §6.0-60 item 1. |
| § 51.1-156 **H**, clause (ii) (item 117(b)) | Same | Yes, and verbatim. H's second sentence: good cause *"**shall** exist and the Board **shall waive** such ninety-day notification periods if (i) the member would otherwise qualify … and (ii) the **Medical Board** … certifies that: (a) … (b) … (c) …"*. Clause (ii) **is** the Medical Board's certification, which is the fact the Board can see; clause (i) is supplied by the approval itself, since a member approved for a disability retirement allowance has *"otherwise qualif[ied]."* |
| *"Medical Board"* (item 117(b)) | Va. Code **§ 51.1-124.3** | Defined chapter-wide — *"the boards composed of physicians or other health care professionals as provided by this chapter"* — so the term is the chapter's own and needs no definition in subsection A. **First use of it in §1**, which is why it was checked. |
| *"subdivision 1"* (item 115) | § 51.1-142.4 **G 1**; subsection **N** | Yes. N applies *"[u]pon the settlement of a certified subsidy under subdivision G 1 or G 4"*, so both referents the conditioned limb now names carry the Commonwealth's payment duty. |
| *"released **in full** in accordance with subdivision D 7"* (item 114) | § 51.1-142.4 **D 7**, first sentence | **This is what makes the amendment work.** D 7 releases *"to the extent of any reduction, if the member reduces the service credit … or if a recertification under subdivision 6 reduces the certified subsidy"* — so the **D 6 partial release is a release in accordance with D 7**, and before this revision it engaged the bar. *"In full"* confines the bar to the whole-reservation releases in D 7's other five limbs. |

**Inward — every provision that reads an amended sentence.**

1. **The two existing *notwithstanding* clauses in G 4** (the rescission sentence and the reversal-settlement sentence) now disapply a bar that no longer catches their cases. **They are left standing and are not deleted**: they are surplusage, not contradiction, and deleting them would re-open the strict-reading argument item 114 exists to close. §6.0-60 item 5.
2. **D 2 and D 3** — the limitation and the contingency amount. Item 114 settles subsidies the bar refused, so an amount that previously stayed charged against the first-sentence limitation of D 2 **permanently** is now settled and remains charged as that subdivision provides for a settled amount. **No amendment to D 2 or D 3 is required**; the reinstatement machinery and its over-cap safeguards (money-committee notice, waiting-list notice, J reporting, no further elections) are reached through G 4's reinstatement limb unchanged.
3. **Subsection N** — unamended, and it now pays on the settlements items 114, 115 and 117 produce, which is the intended effect.
4. **Subdivision G 1** — unamended; item 115's conditioned limb cites it as the settlement provision for the member who **did** retire in a qualifying retirement.
5. **The sentence after item 116's** — *"the amount that this subdivision requires to be included in the next payment of the member's retirement allowance on a reversal or modification"* — reads the amended formula by reference and needs no conforming words.
6. **G 4's notice-of-rescission sentence** and **subsection M 2's deeming sentence** both reach item 103's new determination: the first is unamended because the new determination is not a rescission (it is the trigger for one), and the second because the new sentence says so expressly in the chapter's established form.
7. **J 1's general failure line** — *"every failure of the Board to make a determination, or to give a notice, within a period required by this section, stated separately for each provision"* — already reports a failure to make item 103's determination or to give its notice. **No express report line was drafted for item 103**, which is the minimal footprint. §6.0-60 item 3.
8. **J 2 and J 3** — item 118(b)'s long-stop is confined to a report *"under this subdivision"*, so the Department of Human Resource Management and Department of Accounts report under J 2 and the Director of the Department of Planning and Budget's submission under J 3 are untouched.
9. **Enactment clause 3** — **read clause by clause and no amendment is required.** Clause (i) continues the whole of § 51.1-142.4 for every election accepted before expiry, naming *"every refund, payment, notice, determination, rescission, restoration, and reinstatement required by § 51.1-142.4"* and preserving *"every right of a member under those provisions"* — which carries item 103's determination, item 116's arrears payment and item 120(b)'s refund past 1 July 2033. Clause (iii) continues subsection J *"until the last report and evaluation required by that subsection has been submitted"*, which is now a terminable duty because of item 118(b). **Clause (v)'s saving of subsection M names determinations and notices and not payments**, and that is **not** a gap: clause (v) is the saving for *applications*, and a failure to make a payment can arise only on an accepted election, which clause (i) carries.
10. **Subsection E's second limb** — *"except for the purposes of the definition of 'eligible member' in subsection A, no member shall be treated as having reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date"* — is **not** touched by item 120(a), which amends the **crediting** bar in the same sentence only. **G 3's third sentence**, which disapplies E's second limb on a rescission, therefore reads unchanged.
11. **The third sentence of the definition of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"*** — the residual date rule — is not displaced by item 119. The new limb is **disjunctive**: the condition is satisfied if the separation or abolition occurred on or before **either** the date the section states (or the third sentence supplies) **or** the member's effective date of retirement. Two rules do not compete for one question.
12. **Subsection F, subsections H, I, K, L and subdivision M 1** — read against all thirteen substitutions; none cites an amended sentence by ordinal or by paraphrase.
13. **Sentence-ordinal citations.** No citation anywhere in §1 points to a sentence of G 4, J 1, M 2, subsection E or the definition by ordinal position, so the two new sentences in G 4 and the one new sentence in J 1 renumber nothing. Checked by searching §1 for *"sentence of"* and for *"preceding sentence"* and reading every occurrence in the amended paragraphs: each *"preceding sentence"* in G 4 still has the same antecedent after the insertion, because item 103's two sentences are inserted **after** a sentence no later sentence points back to, and item 118(b)'s sentence is the **last** of J 1.
14. **The retained record and the §7 split.** Store revision 59's and this revision's §5 and §6 are live in the file; §0.0-57, §0.0-56, §5.36, §5.37, §6.0-57 and §6.0-58 are moved to [`bill-text-s8-record-s0-s5-s6-rev2-51`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-record-s0-s5-s6-rev2-51), and the §8 notes for store revisions 54, 53 and 52 to [`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2), each behind a stub. **Every §0.x, §5.n, §6.0-n and §8 designator still resolves**, and **every §7 item n reference resolves in [`bill-text-s8-item-list`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-item-list)**, where store revision 59 moved the list and where this revision's closures and new items 126 and 127 are written.

## 4. The drafter's note — §6.0-60 of the bill, reproduced

**Every one of the Director's eight answers is enacted as given. Four things inside those answers are mine, and they are listed first.**

1. **Item 117(a) is wider than the carded words, deliberately.** The card read *"an application filed **within a period set forth in** subsection A or B of § 51.1-156."* Enacted: *"an application **the filing of which did not require a waiver of** a ninety-day notification period set forth in subsection A or B of § 51.1-156."* The carded form reaches only the member inside the ninety days after termination. **It misses the purest class-4 case of all:** a member whose final qualifying retirement date passes while she is **still in service** — she has not retired at all, which is why subdivision 2 reduced her — and who then applies for a disability retirement allowance as *"[a]ny member in service"* under § 51.1-156 A, for whom **that subsection sets no period**. She needs no waiver, she broke no deadline, and on the carded words she was excluded while a member who filed eight months late was rescued. The enacted form is defined by the thing the class has in common — that no waiver was needed — and reaches both.

2. **Item 117(b) anchors on clause (ii) alone and not on the whole of subsection H.** § 51.1-156 H's mandatory limb has two conditions: (i) the member *"would otherwise qualify for disability retirement but for failing to comply"*, and (ii) the Medical Board's certification of three facts. **Clause (i) is supplied by the approval itself** — the trigger operates only where the member *"is thereafter approved for a disability retirement allowance"*, and a member who is approved has otherwise qualified. Anchoring on both would have made the Board prove a condition its own approval had already decided. **This is the point of the finding:** the enacted trigger is a **fact the Board can see in its file**, not a legal conclusion about what the Board *"was required"* to do.

3. **No express subsection J report line was drafted for item 103's determination, and no fallback was drafted for pass 17's M-9 — and the second of those is a decision, not an omission.** J 1 already reports *"every failure of the Board to make a determination, or to give a notice, within a period required by this section, stated separately for each provision"*, so an express line would be surplusage. **M-9 is CLOSED and needs no text.** It was held to item 103 on the ground that the redetermination clock has no fallback where the Board never makes the error determination. With item 103 enacted the gap is **self-consistent and remediable**: the clock sentence opens *"Where the Board rescinds a determination"*, and the rescission cannot occur without the determination, so a fallback date would start a clock that never runs. What the member needed was a **remedy for the absent determination**, and item 103 gives her one — a 30-day period, a notice duty, review under subsection M 2's failure limb, judicial review under Article 5, and a line in the J report. **Drafting a deemed determination instead would have been a policy choice nobody made.**

4. **Item 120(b) is enacted as a conjunctive duty, not as an exception.** The carded repair was *"the same words R2 enacted in the rescission branch"* — an *"except that where the member has died"* clause. **In the death branch the member has always died**, so the condition is always true and the exception form is nonsense. Enacted: *"and shall pay the whole of that refund to the member's estate … and shall apply no amount of it to the purchase of service credit."* The form also cures **pass 18's M18-3** as a by-product: as an exception restating the verb without a period, the death refund could be read to carry away the main clause's **60-day deadline**; as a conjunctive duty it cannot, and the estate keeps the deadline.

**Five further choices, none of which changes which member passes either definitional test.**

5. **Item 114's amendment leaves the two existing *notwithstanding* clauses standing.** They become surplusage. Deleting them would be tidier and would re-open the argument the amendment exists to foreclose — that the bar was never meant to catch these cases at all — and store revision 52 legislated twice on the strict historical-fact reading. **Surplusage is the cheaper of the two risks.** The record states it so a reader does not take the redundancy for a drafting slip.

6. **Item 114's *"in full"* is confined to the whole-reservation release and that is what makes it operative.** D 7 releases *"to the extent of any reduction"* on a D 6 recertification and releases the whole reserved amount in its other five limbs. Had the amendment read *"released in accordance with subdivision D 7 and has not been reinstated"* it would have cured nothing for the D 6 member, because her partial release is never reinstated — it was correct.

7. **Item 118(b)'s long-stop is the last sentence of J 1 and reads on *"report under this subdivision."*** The card attached it to limb (a) of the first sentence. Placed there it would not have reached the **third** sentence's further report, which has its own trigger, and the duty would still have been interminable on the facts item 118 describes. As the closing sentence it bounds **every** report J 1 requires, which is what the card's stated purpose — *"makes the duty terminable whatever happens"* — asks for. It is confined to *"this subdivision"*, so J 2 and J 3 are untouched.

8. **Item 103's route is confined to the period after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect.** Before that moment the Board is already under a **60-day** duty to determine whether clause (iii) applies, with a 15-day notice duty, a J report line and review under subsection M; an unconditioned member-filing route would have put a **second clock on one determination**, which is pass 18's M18-9. The gap the Director's answer was aimed at is the **later** determination in the rescission sentence — the one with no period, no route and no notice — and the enacted sentence reaches exactly that. **No conforming limb is needed to connect it to the rescission:** the rescission trigger reads *"or the Board thereafter determines that the member was unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board"*, which the new determination satisfies on its own words, and the redetermination clock already runs *"from the date on which … the Board makes the determination stated in this subdivision."*

9. **Item 120(a) is enacted although pass 18 shows its stated premise is false, and the part that would actually fix the problem is carded.** The card's ground was that *"G 4 credits the whole purchase on clauses (ii) and (iii) too."* It does not: G 4's crediting duties are confined to **death** and to the **rescission** branch, and clause (ii) switches off G 3's partial-crediting duty along with subdivisions 2 and 3. So for a member approved for a disability retirement allowance **before** completing payment, with no prior determination, there is **no crediting duty to lift a bar in front of**. The amendment is still right on its own terms — E's death-only exception conflicted on its face with G 4's unqualified *"Subsection E does not prevent the crediting of service credit required by this subdivision"* — and it is enacted on that narrower ground. **The crediting duty is §7 item 126**, drafted in full, enacted nowhere, and recommended: it decides what a partial payer is credited with and what she is refunded, which is a money question and the Director's.

## 5. No figure moves

Every figure in the package prices the admitted cohort — the unreduced subdivision A 1 cohort reached through § 51.1-153 A, B 2 or B 3 — **as settling**.

- **No admission quantity moves.** Nothing in the thirteen touches *"eligible member"*, the subsection C clause (ii) cap, or the clauses (v) to (viii) determinations. **Item 119 can only ever restore a retirement route the section had disabled**, and it restores it for a member already inside the program: a member certified at 48 and involuntarily separated at 50. It admits nobody to the program.
- **Settlement moves toward the priced basis, not past it.** Items 114 and 117 settle subsidies that were refused by a bar and by a gap, which is what the figures already assume. Item 115 **withdraws** a settlement the basis never assumed — the member who loses on reconsideration. Item 116 moves the arrears to the correct quantum and **in the Commonwealth's favour**, since the sentence previously commanded a gross amount the Commonwealth could not recover.
- **Items 103, 104, 118, 120 and 121 touch a route, two report lines, two periods, a crediting bar and a remedy.** None of them changes an amount.
- **Nothing in §3, `model-s8-s9` or the [MOO-85](/MOO/issues/MOO-85) reprice needs re-running**, and no figure in the package is restated here.

**Two of the answers spend money one-sidedly and the Director took them on exactly that footing** — item 114 settles subsidies the bar refused, and item 103's route will produce rescissions that would otherwise never have been asked for. **§7 item 99's quantification is with [@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50) at [MOO-151](/MOO/issues/MOO-151) and no figure of Fiscal's is asserted or retracted here.** The standing qualification from store revision 57 is unchanged and is repeated so it is not lost: **no admission quantity moves; the settlement count moves upward by an amount the current `g4_exposure` engine cannot value**, which is [MOO-157](/MOO/issues/MOO-157).

## 6. [MOO-156](/MOO/issues/MOO-156)'s pass 18 — triage, not disposition

**Pass 18 returned 0 fatal, 6 serious, 11 moderate, 3 minor, plus 2 adjacent, on store revision 57's six repairs. It is NOT dispositioned in this revision and nothing here claims otherwise.** It is read, and this triage records what this revision did to it so the next cut does not have to re-derive it. **Every finding not marked *acted on* below is live and unanswered.**

| Finding | What this revision did |
|---|---|
| **S18-1** — R5 enacts the Form-A side of F5 for one population, and that side costs money | **Untouched and live.** It reaches §7 item 122(1), which is the Director's open choice between Form A and Form B. Not mine to resolve. |
| **S18-2** — R5's *"this sentence"* refers to itself, so the repair may be self-nullifying | **Untouched and live, and it is serious:** on the self-referential reading item 96 and R5 both do nothing in the one case they were written for. Drafting, and the next cut's first repair. |
| **S18-3** — R4's death limb is nested inside a condition that excludes the commonest death case | **Untouched and live.** Drafting. |
| **S18-4** — R2 commands payment of the whole refund notwithstanding adverse federal tax consequence, with no residual | **MADE WIDER BY THIS REVISION, and I am not burying it.** Item 120(b), as the Director approved it, gives the **death branch** the same treatment R2 gave the rescission branch — so the absent residual now sits in **both** branches. The answer is enacted as given and the enactment is right; **S18-4's cure must now be applied twice.** Pass 18's own direction — a *"to the extent permitted"* valve rather than an absolute command — is drafting, not policy, and it is the next cut's. |
| **S18-5** — R6 is an enlargement, not a repair; § 51.1-124.9 A already imposes the duty | **Untouched and live.** It bears on a wording change that was mine in store revision 57, and the authority (§ 51.1-124.9 A, same chapter) is one I did not have. Drafting. |
| **S18-6** — item 120(a)'s candidate text will not work, because outside death G 4 imposes no crediting duty at all | **ACTED ON.** Item 120(a) is enacted on a **narrower ground** (§6.0-60 item 9) and the missing crediting duty is carded as **§7 item 126** with text, recommended. The review is right and this item's stated premise was wrong. |
| **M18-1, M18-2** — R3's limbs are not mutually exclusive, and the primary limb has the same pathology R3 repaired | **Untouched and live.** Drafting. |
| **M18-3** — R2's death exception may carry away the 60-day deadline | **CURED, as a by-product.** Item 120(b) is enacted as a **conjunctive duty** rather than as an exception, so the main clause's 60 days cannot be carried away (§6.0-60 item 4). **In the death branch only** — the rescission branch's R2 keeps the exception form and M18-3 is live there. |
| **M18-4, M18-5** — R6's *"retirement allowance"* is the chapter-wide genus, and R6 lifted less than the sentence it replaced | **Untouched and live.** |
| **M18-6, M18-7, M18-8** — R5's trigger, its identification of subsection E's provision, and its placement | **Untouched and live.** |
| **M18-9** — item 103's stated ground is too broad | **ACTED ON.** The route is **confined to the period after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect**, which is what re-grounds it on the later determination and avoids two clocks for one determination (§6.0-60 item 8). **Pass 17's M-9 is closed with no text** and the review's hold of it to item 103 is respected. |
| **M18-10, M18-11** — no notice duty on a reversal; two payee rules for one death | **Untouched and live.** M18-11 is partly a policy question — whether the refund should follow R4's payee hierarchy — and will be carded rather than fixed. |
| **m18-1, m18-2, m18-3** | **Untouched and live.** m18-2 is a correction to a ground of mine and will be taken. |
| **Adjacent 1** — G 4's reversal sentence routes to a restoration mechanic that does not exist for a reversal | **Untouched and live, and item 115 does not cure it.** Item 115 conditions the **settlement** limb; the **restoration** limb still says *"as this subdivision provides"* and G 4's two restoration provisions both name a rescission. The next cut must card it. |
| **Adjacent 2** — the settlement bar is contradicted by two of its own sentences | **ACTED ON by item 114**, which makes those two *notwithstanding* clauses surplusage rather than contradictory (§6.0-60 item 5). |

## 7. Status

- **Store revision 60 is in the canonical document and verified after the write.**
- **§7 items 114, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 103 and 104 are CLOSED**, and items 120 and 121 are closed as to the limbs selected. The closures are in [`bill-text-s8-item-list`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-item-list).
- **Two new items are open and enacted nowhere: 126** (the crediting duty for the clause (ii) and clause (iii) partial payer, which is a money question) **and 127** (subdivision J 1's failure line, nine words, conforming to item 121).
- **Pass 19 is [MOO-167](/MOO/issues/MOO-167)**, scoped to these thirteen substitutions, with every FIND and ENACTED string reproduced in its description. **These thirteen have had no adversarial pass of their own.**
- **Pass 18 is not dispositioned.** Eighteen of its twenty findings are live; §6 above is a triage, not an answer.

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel or by DLS. Pre-decisional. Nothing here is cleared to leave Paperclip.**

title: Pass 11 disposition — MOO-106's 19 findings on the enacted text and 3 on the candidates: 13 drafted out in eleven edits, 3 corrected, 4 to the Director (store revision 36 companion record)
body:
# Pass 11 disposition — MOO-106's 19 findings on the enacted text and 3 on the candidates, finding by finding

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · companion record to store revision 36 of
[`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8) · 12 October 2026**

**INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT. Pre-decisional. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by
counsel or DLS, and nothing here states or implies that the draft is legally sufficient for introduction.
Pass 11 is our own adversarial review and is expressly not legal advice.**

**Target of the review:** the 24 changed places of store revision 33 of `bill-text-s8` —
[MOO-95](/MOO/issues/MOO-95)'s pass 9 drafted out. **Review:** [MOO-106](/MOO/issues/MOO-106),
[`pass11-review`](/MOO/issues/MOO-106#document-pass11-review).

**Result: 19 findings on the enacted text (0 fatal, 6 serious, 9 moderate, 4 minor) and 3 serious defects
in candidate texts that are not in the bill. 13 are drafted out in eleven edits; 3 are corrected in the
record; 2 statements of mine are withdrawn; 4 go to the Director at §7 items 55 to 58.** No figure moved.
One definition paragraph deleted. Bill title unchanged.

**One thing to record before the table.** Pass 11 reviewed store revision 33, and store revisions 34 and
35 landed while it ran — four edits and six edits respectively. **I re-read every one of its 22 quoted
strings against the live body before editing**, and every one was present as quoted, so no finding in the
pass is addressed to text that had already changed. Where a finding touched a provision store revision 34
or 35 had edited, the edit and the finding are in different sentences.

---

## 1. Disposition of all 22

| # | Rank | Finding in one line | Disposition | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | serious | The S-2 outer bound reaches only D 1's lateness; **subsection M's tolling is unbounded and S-6 unbounded it**, so an unanswered reconsideration letter holds the window open indefinitely and the Commonwealth settles a subsidy for a negative acceleration | **DRAFTED.** The bound reaches tolling; M 2's protection survives as a **deeming rule**; no new figure. Tighter alternatives are **§7 item 39**, repaired | Definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* |
| **2** | serious | G 4's 90-day involuntary-separation protection is **capped by the final qualifying retirement date and can deliver zero usable days** | **DRAFTED, by the reviewer's alternative and not its first fix** — disapplying the final-date limb would have stranded settlement. The member's **final date is extended** to the first of the month after day 90 | G 4 |
| **3** | serious | The S-1 exclusion is keyed to **the member, not the election**, so a member with one cancelled and one failed election keeps the credit at the pilot price | **DRAFTED.** Keyed to the election | G 2, 4th sentence |
| **4** | serious | S-1 **still does not reach the member who pays nothing** — the very failure it was written to cure | **DRAFTED**, in the same sentence: a fourth limb for a reservation released under D 7 with nothing credited | G 2, 4th sentence |
| **5** | serious | The three-day mailing allowance **does not reach B 4 f's 30-day § 415 election period** and reaches no period of an *"applicant"* | **DRAFTED.** Both sentences scoped; actor widened; sentence 1 conformed. **§5.15's claim withdrawn** | Subsection A, concluding paragraph |
| **6** | serious | **New B 4 g cannot do what M-6 said**: a § 415 limitation year is a per-plan attribute changeable only by plan amendment and cannot be designated for a subset of participants | **DRAFTED — B 4 g deleted.** Residual, if a designation is wanted, is **§7 item 57**; the plan-document fact is [MOO-115](/MOO/issues/MOO-115) | B 4 |
| **7** | moderate | *"the first two sentences of this definition"* has **two available readings three months apart** | **DRAFTED** with finding 1: the anchor names the first sentence or the approved later date | Definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* |
| **8** | moderate | The new bound **closes the window on a member the Board never told her dates** | **DRAFTED** with finding 1: a floor at the first of the second month after the statement | Same definition |
| **9** | moderate | The three-day allowance makes the member's M 2 request period 33 days while a G 2 determination may take effect on day 30 | **DRAFTED.** The notice floor tracks the member's period, minimum 30 days | G 2 |
| **10** | moderate | F's carve-out names G 2, G 4 and G 5 and **omits the D 6 conversion S-7 created in the same revision** | **DRAFTED.** One word. **§0.x's M-4 entry and §5.15's M-4 row corrected** | Subsection F |
| **11** | moderate | M-3's agency duty **has no consequence** and the Board's 15 days run from the date it *"learns"* | **DRAFTED.** J-report line; 15 days re-keyed to the earlier of receipt and knowledge | G 4 |
| **12** | moderate | M-3's duty is **triggered by a fact the agency may not have**, and G 4 contemplates transfer | **TO THE DIRECTOR — §7 item 55.** Both cures drafted; it is a privacy choice. Pass 11 also routes the separating agency to Stakeholder Analyst | — |
| **13** | moderate | S-8's safeguards **notify four audiences and oblige no one to cure the excess**, bypassing the D 3 confirmation that keeps the architecture inside art. X, § 7 | **DRAFTED.** The Board must request a D 3 confirmation for the excess within 15 days and certify the amount to the Governor and the Chairmen. The structural alternative is **§7 item 40** and is the Director's | G 4 |
| **14** | moderate | *"The cause of the release"* has **no specified content, no review route and no confidentiality bar** | **DRAFTED.** Notice split; content specified; **a reinstatement is a determination for subsection M** | G 4 |
| **15** | moderate | Enactment 3 (i) preserves **the Board's verbs and not the member's rights and periods** | **DRAFTED.** One phrase | Enactment 3 |
| **16** | minor | §0.x a locates the S-1 exclusion at *"G 2, 5th sentence"*; it is the **4th of nine** | **CORRECTED IN THE RECORD** (§4 below) | — |
| **17** | minor | §0.x's M-5 entry says the protective limb *"matches the prohibition it qualifies"*; **three terms differ in each direction** | **CORRECTED IN THE RECORD** (§4). Harmless in operation | — |
| **18** | minor | D 6 contains a **reduction route that refunds nothing** — the member who *elects* to reduce has overpaid and D 6's duty is keyed to what she *may* purchase | **DRAFTED**, and widened to reach B 4 f clause (i) as well | D 6 |
| **19** | minor | In the G 4 branch the determination date **can precede the last date the text permits the member to retire** | **DRAFTED.** The clock runs from *"the last day on which the member may retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision"* | G 4 |
| **C-1** | serious (candidate) | **§7 item 41(a) as drafted releases the reservation and leaves the election accepted** — creating the art. X, § 7 exposure item 40 is about; plus two different five percents, and it releases the member B 4 e was written for | **TO THE DIRECTOR — §7 item 56.** Three repairs drafted; **not enacted** | — |
| **C-2** | serious (candidate) | **§7 item 42's premise is half wrong** — § 51.1-124.11 already reaches the inflated allowance — and the carve-out reaches further than "fraud-only" | **TO THE DIRECTOR — §7 item 56.** My implicit recommendation **withdrawn**; pass 11 and I both lean to **no bespoke provision** | — |
| **C-3** | serious (candidate) | **§7 item 33's substitute imposes a pre-determination hearing on every determination** in a section whose notice architecture is post-determination, and still engages § 2.2-4021 B | **TO THE DIRECTOR — §7 item 56.** My substitute **withdrawn**; the repair is drafted | — |

---

## 2. The eleven edits, verbatim

New language in **bold** within the quoted provision; nothing else in the quoted sentence changes.

**1. Definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* — the last sentence is replaced and two are added.**

> In no event shall a member's final qualifying retirement date, as extended under subdivision D 1 **or as
> tolled under subsection M,** be later than 12 months after the date **that applies under the first
> sentence of this definition or, where a later date has been approved under this definition, after that
> later date. Where the running of a period has been tolled under subsection M and the member is prevented
> by the preceding sentence from retiring in a qualifying retirement after that tolling ends, a retirement
> that satisfies every requirement of the definition of "qualifying retirement" in this subsection other
> than the requirement that its effective date of retirement be no later than the member's final qualifying
> retirement date, and that takes effect no later than the first day of the second month following the
> month in which the Board acts upon the request the filing of which tolled that period, is a qualifying
> retirement. Notwithstanding the two preceding sentences, a member's final qualifying retirement date
> shall be no earlier than the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board gives
> the statement required by this definition.**

**2. G 4 — the involuntary separation branch gains one sentence.**

> **Where the involuntary separation occurs on or before the date that would otherwise be the member's
> final qualifying retirement date and the first day of the month next following the ninetieth day after
> the date of the involuntary separation is later than that date, the member's final qualifying retirement
> date is that first day.**

**3. G 2 — the exclusion sentence is replaced.**

> No determination under this subdivision is required in respect of **an election that** has been cancelled
> under subdivision D 6 or under subdivision 5 of this subsection, **in respect of an election under which
> the member** has been credited with service credit under subdivision 3 or 5 **of this subsection, or in
> respect of an election under which the reservation has been released under subdivision D 7 without any
> service credit having been credited to the member**, and no retirement allowance shall be withheld **by
> reason of this subdivision on account of any such election.**

**4. Subsection A — the giving rule and the three-day allowance.**

> For the purposes of this section and of subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, a written statement or notice
> required of the Board is given on the date the Board mails it to the member **or applicant to whom it is
> required to be given** or transmits it electronically to an address **that member or applicant** has
> provided to the Board for that purpose, except that an electronic transmission completed after 5:00 p.m.
> is given on the following day. **For the purposes of this section and of subdivision B 4 f of
> § 51.1-142.2, where** the Board mails a written statement or notice, every period within which **a member
> or an applicant** may or must act that runs from the giving of that statement or notice is extended by
> three days.

**5. Subdivision B 4 g — deleted in its entirety.** It read: *"For the purposes of § 415 of the Internal
Revenue Code and the regulations thereunder, the limitation year of the defined benefit plan under which a
member described in subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155 is covered is the calendar year."* **"Limitation year"
remains defined in B 4 a under *"As used in this subdivision,"* which reaches B 4 f.**

**6. G 2 — the notice floor.**

> The Board shall give the member written notice of the determination, of the service credit retained, and
> of the reasons for the determination, no less than 30 days, **and in no case less than the period allowed
> to the member by subsection M within which to request reconsideration of the determination,** before the
> determination takes effect…

**7. Subsection F — one word.**

> …and nothing required by subdivision **D 6,** G 2, G 4, or G 5 by way of the application of a refund…

**8. G 4 — the Board's 15 days and the agency-failure report.**

> The Board shall give the member written notice, no later than 15 days after **the earlier of the date on
> which the Board receives the notice required by this subdivision and the date on which the Board
> otherwise learns of** the involuntary separation, of the date by which the member must retire… A state
> agency shall notify the Board of the involuntary separation of any member whose election the Board has
> accepted no later than 15 days after the separation, **and the Board shall state every failure of a state
> agency to give that notice of which the Board becomes aware in the report required by subsection J.**

**9 and 10. G 4 — the reinstatement notice, the appropriation duty, and the subsection M characterisation.**

> The Board shall give written notice of every reinstatement under this subdivision, **of the date of the
> release, of whether the release was in accordance with subdivision D 7, of the nature of any error,** of
> the amount of any resulting excess, and of the cause of the release, to the Chairmen of the House
> Committee on Appropriations and the Senate Committee on Finance and Appropriations no later than 15 days
> after the reinstatement; **shall give written notice of the fact, the amount, and the date of any
> resulting excess to each applicant then on the waiting list maintained under subdivision D 5 no later
> than 15 days after the reinstatement, which notice shall not state the cause of the release and shall not
> identify any member; shall request a confirmation under subdivision D 3 in respect of the amount of any
> resulting excess no later than 15 days after the reinstatement, and shall certify the amount of the
> excess to the Governor and to those Chairmen as an amount necessary to fund the purposes of this
> section;** shall state every reinstatement and every such excess in the report required by subsection J;
> and shall accept no further election until the excess is eliminated. **A reinstatement under this
