> subdivision is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M.**

**11. Enactment 3 clause (i) — the member's rights and periods.**

> …in each case as though those provisions had not expired and notwithstanding clause (iv) of this
> enactment, **and every right of a member under those provisions and every period allowed to a member by
> those provisions shall continue in effect and continue to run as though those provisions had not
> expired**;

**Plus two within the above:** D 6 gains *"Where the member reduces the amount of service credit to be
purchased under clause (i) of this subdivision or under clause (i) of subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2,
the service credit to be purchased is reduced to the amount to which the member reduces it, the Board shall
recertify the certified subsidy and the amount payable to reflect the reduction, and the Board shall refund
any amount paid that exceeds the amount payable as so recertified"* (finding 18); and G 4's determination
clock now runs from *"the last day on which the member may retire in a qualifying retirement under this
subdivision"* in place of *"the expiration of that 90-day period"* (finding 19).

**Cross-reference check:** performed in both directions for all eleven, provision by provision, at **§5.18**
of `bill-text-s8`. **One citation leaves the bill** (the § 51.1-155 A 1 reference inside the deleted B 4 g,
which is cited elsewhere in both sections and so is not lost); **two internal references are added**; and
**nothing is stranded** — nothing cited B 4 g, and §5.15's own M-6 row had already recorded that.

---

## 3. The candidate texts — what pass 11 did to them, and what I now recommend

The full attack is at [`pass11-review`](/MOO/issues/MOO-106#document-pass11-review) §4 and the drafted
repairs are in `bill-text-s8` §7 item 56. In short:

- **Item 41(a)** — the minimum first payment — **must not be adopted as drafted.** It releases the
  reservation and leaves the election accepted, so the member may pay in full in month 11 against no
  reservation and the Commonwealth is obliged to pay out of nothing. Three repairs; with them I still
  prefer (a) to (b), and so does pass 11.
- **Item 42** — the fraud carve-out — **I withdraw my implicit recommendation.** § 51.1-124.11 already
  reaches the inflated allowance once the member retires, so the gap is narrower than the item states; and
  the carve-out as drafted lifts subsection F for setoff, exposes an innocent estate, and sits badly on a
  prediction. Pass 11 leans to no bespoke provision and so do I.
- **Item 33** — the § 51.1-124.11 substitute — **I withdraw my own substitute.** *"Reasonable prior written
  notice"* in § 51.1-124.11 is prior to a fraud-recovery determination; adapted to *"a determination under
  this section"* it imposes a pre-determination hearing on nine determinations the Board must make inside
  30 days, and *"in accordance with the Administrative Process Act"* still engages § 2.2-4021 B. The
  repair — notice **of** a determination, a hearing **on reconsideration**, and the Article 5 formula — is
  drafted and is what I recommend if review is to be in the bill.

---

## 4. Statements of mine that did not hold

| Statement | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| *"every component of it is now bounded in the text"* | §6.0-24, as corrected in store revision 33 | **Withdrawn a second time.** The unbounded component moved from D 1 to subsection M's tolling, and store revision 33's own S-6 edit put it there. §6.0-36 item 1 states the envelope once and does not restate the assurance |
| *"all ten are now reached"* (the giving rule) | §5.15, S-4 row | **Withdrawn.** It did not reach B 4 f's 30-day period, nor any period of an *"applicant"* |
| *"which G 2, G 4 and G 5 each require"* (F's carve-out list) | §0.x M-4 and §5.15 M-4 row | **Corrected to four.** S-7 created a fourth conversion, in D 6, in the same revision |
| *"matching the prohibition it qualifies"* (the protective limb) | §0.x M-5 | **Corrected.** The prohibition says *"member, retiree, or beneficiary"*; the limb says *"member … survivor, beneficiary, or estate."* Harmless in operation, because G 2 uses *"member"* throughout for the retired member — but the claim was not accurate |
| *"G 2, 5th sentence"* (location of the S-1 edit) | §0.x a | **Corrected to the 4th of nine**, on pass 11's mechanical count: (1) the determination duty, (2) the notice, (3) the allowance bar, (4) the exclusion, (5) *"the determination date"*, (6) the notice deadline, (7) the effect limits, (8) death before first payment, (9) the refund |
| *"the designation … should not reach the § 51.1-169 hybrid program"* | §5.15, M-6 row | **Second half withdrawn.** 26 C.F.R. § 1.415(j)-1 does not permit a limitation year to be designated for a subset of a plan's participants at all, so the narrowing achieved nothing — which is why B 4 g is deleted rather than confined |
| *"61 usable days and not 90"* | §6.0-25 item 6 | **Corrected: it can be zero**, and for a member separated after her final date the branch gave nothing at all. Cured by edit 2 |

---

## 5. What pass 11 certified sound, expressly

Seventeen null results, which are findings. The ones that matter most to the architecture: **the new term
*"the determination date"* has exactly one referent in every branch where an allowance is payable** and the
old anchor had none in the G 4 branch; **the 30-day notice floor has room in every branch** (60 + 30 ≤ 120);
**enactment 3's sentence count is right** and clause (i) now preserves the only sentence the act amends;
**the two enactment-3 carve-outs do not loop** and no member's price is ambiguous on 2 July 2033; **the
B 4 f pointer is reciprocal rather than circular**, so the rule-of-construction-across-sections device
works; **nothing is stranded for the members the S-1 exclusion names**; ***"cancelled under subdivision
D 6"* has exactly one referent**; **notifying every wait-listed applicant is performable**; **M-2 does not
disapply the final-date requirement** — which is the premise of finding 2; **B 4 f is not stranded by the
B 4 a / B 4 g split**; and **§ 51.1-153 E and B 2 and the biennium reading all hold, verified at source.**

---

## 6. Routing out of this disposition

- **[MOO-117](/MOO/issues/MOO-117)** — Red Team / Counsel Reviewer, **pass 12**, bounded to the eleven
  changed places. None of this language has been attacked by anyone.
- **[MOO-115](/MOO/issues/MOO-115)** — Statutory Researcher. Does VRS's plan document designate a § 415
  limitation year, and are Plan 1, Plan 2 and the § 51.1-169 hybrid defined benefit component one plan or
  more for § 415 purposes? Finding 6 turns on it and the bill cannot answer it.
- **[MOO-116](/MOO/issues/MOO-116)** — Fiscal & Impact Modeler. The **1 July 2030 parker cliff**, and the
  cap-utilisation question if the Director takes §7 item 39 option (a).
- **Policy Director** — §7 items **55 to 58**, and §7 item **39** in its repaired form.
- **Editor** — pass 11 names five items for the memo's risk section; four are now answered in the text and
  the fifth, the interest-free deferral residual, is §7 item 58.
- **Stakeholder Analyst** — two unmapped parties bearing a real cost: the **wait-listed applicant** and the
  **separating state agency**. Edits 9, 10 and 8 reduce but do not remove either.

**Standing caveat, repeated: internal working draft, pre-decisional, not a Division of Legislative Services
bill, not reviewed by counsel or DLS, and nothing in it is cleared for external use. Saving a file is not
sending it.**

title: Pass 12 disposition — store revision 39 of bill-text-s8: 26 findings dispositioned, 17 edits, no figure moved (internal working draft)
body:
# Pass 12 disposition — store revision 39 of `bill-text-s8`

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional, not a
Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by counsel or DLS, not cleared for external use.**

> **What this is.** The companion record for **store revision 39** of
> [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), which drafts out
> [MOO-117](/MOO/issues/MOO-117)'s **pass 12** — the bounded adversarial and counsel review of store
> revision 36's eleven edits. Written as its own document from the start, on the convention set by
> `rev21-record`, `rev22-record`, `pass9-disposition`, `pass10-disposition` and `pass11-disposition`,
> because the main file has no room for a record of this size.
>
> Pass 12 returned **26 findings — 0 fatal, 8 serious, 13 moderate, 5 minor — plus 20 express null
> results.** It says in terms that no edit in store revision 36 prevents the bill from operating,
> creates a facial constitutional defect, or defeats the enactment.

---

## 0. Verification performed before any edit

Store revision 36 landed at 03:24:36Z and store revisions 37 and 38 landed after it, so the first job
was to confirm that pass 12 is not addressed to superseded text.

**All 26 findings quote text that is present in the live body as quoted.** I re-read every quoted string
against store revision 38's body (document revision 43, `f71f225b`) before editing. Pass 12 did the same
thing from its own side and recorded it: it worked from the live body rather than from a revision label,
and it says so at §4 of [`pass12-review`](/MOO/issues/MOO-117#document-pass12-review).

**One citation in pass 12 rests on a mirror rather than on the source.** eCFR redirected, so
26 C.F.R. § 1.415(j)-1 was read at Cornell LII. That citation is the whole ground of **F-8**, which this
revision enacts. I have not re-opened it in this heartbeat and I am not representing that I have.
[MOO-115](/MOO/issues/MOO-115) is the place to confirm (a) and (d) against eCFR or the printed CFR, and
**F-8's fix is drafted so that the answer does not matter to the bill** — which is the point of taking it.

---

## 1. Disposition of all 26 findings

**17 string edits in 12 provisions.** `12`, `$3,000,000`, `$170,000` and the `[20]` percent contingency
are untouched. No section is added or deleted. The bill title does not change. The act still amends one
section of the Code and adds one.

| # | Severity | Disposition | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-1** | serious | **Drafted out.** G 4's clock re-keyed to the **earlier of (a) the later of** the ninetieth day and the final date, **and (b)** the non-qualifying retirement | G 4 |
| **F-2** | serious | **Drafted out**, by the device pass 12 identified: the deeming sentence now **moves the date** instead of deeming the retirement | definition of "final qualifying retirement date", sentence 7 |
| **F-3** | serious | **Drafted out by F-2's fix, with no separate edit.** G 2's clock runs from *"the member's final qualifying retirement date, if any"*; once the date itself moves, the clock moves with it and cannot mature before the window closes | G 2, unamended |
| **F-4** | serious | **Drafted out.** The floor is now a **date-setter**, so Reading B is gone and the outer bound stays alive for every other purpose | definition, sentence 8 |
| **F-5** | serious | **Drafted out.** *"the outer bound stated in **that definition**"* — sentence counts rot, so the ordinal is dropped rather than corrected | D 1 clause (i) |
| **F-6** | serious | **Drafted out in two places.** The agency notice must state the date and the cause and be **certified by the agency head or his designee**; and the extension operates **only** where the Board has received such a notice or has otherwise determined that a separation occurred | G 4 |
| **F-7** | serious | **Drafted out, and largely pre-empted by F-6's condition.** With the extension conditioned on Board knowledge the date can no longer move silently; the **rescission limb** is enacted as the backstop for the case where the Board determines late, and it now also **reinstates the reservation** | G 4 |
| **F-8** | serious | **Drafted out.** *"'Limitation year' means the limitation year of the defined benefit plan under which the member is covered, determined under § 415 of the Internal Revenue Code and the regulations thereunder."* | B 4 a |
| **F-9** | moderate | **Drafted out inside F-2's replacement:** *"the month in which the Board **last acts upon a request** the filing of which tolled that period"* | definition, sentence 7 |
| **F-10** | moderate | **Not drafted. Routed to the Director — §7 item 66**, as pass 12 routed it. The widening extends the Board's duties past the sunset | enactment 3 |
| **F-11** | moderate | **Drafted out, by pass 12's preferred cure — stop enumerating.** *"the person to whom it is required to be given"*; *"every period within which **a person** may or must act"* | giving rule in subsection A |
| **F-12** | moderate | **Not drafted. Routed to the Director — §7 item 62.** Pass 12 says expressly *"this is the Director's call, not mine"* | G 4 |
| **F-13** | moderate | **Not drafted. Routed to the Director — §7 item 63.** Whether the certification engages subsection K is a whole-fiscal-year freeze question | G 4 |
| **F-14** | moderate | **Not drafted. Routed to the Director — §7 item 64** | G 4 |
| **F-15** | moderate | **Drafted out**, in G 4's own words: *"and a determination that takes effect in contravention of this sentence is of no effect"* | G 2 |
| **F-16** | moderate | **Drafted out.** The date of an involuntary separation is the termination date or, where there is a placement on leave without pay-layoff or equivalent status, the **placement** date | definition of "involuntary separation" |
| **F-17** | moderate | **Not drafted. Routed to the Director — §7 item 67.** The cure is a new quarterly reconciliation duty on the Board against DHRM data. It is a new obligation with an administrative cost and no cited document directs it | G 4, J |
| **F-18** | moderate | **Drafted out, but not by pass 12's fix.** See §3 below — its fix reopens the unbounded window. What is enacted instead puts the never-told member inside G 4 clause (iii) on the face of the text | G 4 |
| **F-19** | moderate | **Drafted out.** *"As used in this subdivision 4"* | B 4 a |
| **F-20** | moderate | **Drafted out.** The seventh adverse notice now carries the same two recitals the other six carry | G 4 |
| **F-21** | moderate | **Not drafted. Routed to the Director — §7 item 65.** Giving an employer a right of review, or saying expressly that it has none, is a choice about who may litigate | M 2 |
| **F-22** | minor | **Drafted out, but not by pass 12's fix.** See §3 — adding G 4's extension to the general outer bound would re-create F-1's harm for the member whose date already sits at the bound. The ratchet is capped directly instead: *"shall not be extended under this subdivision by reason of more than one involuntary separation"* | G 4 |
| **F-23** | minor | **Drafted out.** *"within 30 days after the notice of the determination **is given**"* | M 2 |
| **F-24** | minor | **No change, with the reason recorded.** See §4 | — |
| **F-25** | minor | **Drafted out**, by reference rather than by quoting the figure: *"an excess is eliminated when the aggregate of the amounts charged against the limitation in the first sentence of subdivision D 2 no longer exceeds that limitation"* | G 4 |
| **F-26** | minor, pre-existing | **Not drafted. Routed to the Director — §7 item 69**, with the sentence drafted. Pass 12 expressly left it out of scope and so do I; it is a real incoherence and it is not a revision-36 edit | G 4, D 6 |

**Totals: 18 drafted out (16 by express edit, F-3 by consequence), 1 no change needed, 7 with the
Director.** Two of the 18 depart from pass 12's own fix direction and both departures are at §3.

---

## 2. The seventeen edits, verbatim

New language is shown in **bold** against the surrounding words; all of § 51.1-142.4 is new language and
is reproduced underlined in the bill, so **bold here is an editorial device for this record only** and
does not appear in the text.

**Edit 1 — F-5 · subdivision D 1, clause (i) of the notice-content sentence**

> …that the date so extended is subject to the outer bound stated in **~~the last sentence of~~ that
> definition**…

**Edit 2 — F-8 · subdivision B 4 a, definition of "limitation year"**

> <u>"Limitation year" means **the limitation year of the defined benefit plan under which the member is
> covered, determined under § 415 of the Internal Revenue Code and the regulations thereunder**.</u>

**Edit 3 — F-19 · subdivision B 4 a, definitional preamble**

> <u>**4.** a. As used in this subdivision **4**:</u>

**Edit 4 — F-1 · subdivision G 4, the re-keyed determination clock**

> If the member does not so retire, subdivision 2 shall apply, and the Board shall make the determination
> required by subdivision 2 within 60 days after the **earlier of (a) the later of** the last day on which
> the member may retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision **and** the member's final
> qualifying retirement date, if any, and **(b)** the date on which the member retires in a retirement
> that is not a qualifying retirement.

**Edit 5 — F-2, F-3, F-9 · definition of "final qualifying retirement date", sentence 7**

> Where the running of a period has been tolled under subsection M and the member is prevented by the
> preceding sentence from retiring in a qualifying retirement after that tolling ends, **the member's
> final qualifying retirement date is, notwithstanding the preceding sentence, the first day of the second
> month following the month in which the Board last acts upon a request the filing of which tolled that
> period, and in no event later than 12 months after the latest date the preceding sentence permits.**

**Edit 6 — F-4 · definition of "final qualifying retirement date", sentence 8**

> Notwithstanding the two preceding sentences, **where the date that would otherwise apply under this
> definition is earlier than** the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board
> gives the statement required by this definition, **the member's final qualifying retirement date is that
> first day.**

**Edit 7 — F-18 · subdivision G 4, a new second sentence**

> **For the purposes of clause (iii) of this subdivision, a member who retires at a time when the Board
> has not given the statement required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in
> subsection A is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board.**

**Edits 8 and 9 — F-6 and F-22 · subdivision G 4, the extension sentence**

> Where the involuntary separation occurs on or before the date that would otherwise be the member's final
> qualifying retirement date and the first day of the month next following the ninetieth day after the
> date of the involuntary separation is later than that date, the member's final qualifying retirement
> date is that first day, **provided that the Board has received a notice of the separation required of a
> state agency by this subdivision or has otherwise determined that an involuntary separation occurred. A
> member's final qualifying retirement date shall not be extended under this subdivision by reason of more
> than one involuntary separation.**

**Edit 10 — F-6 · subdivision G 4, the agency-notice sentence**

> A state agency shall notify the Board of the involuntary separation of any member whose election the
> Board has accepted no later than 15 days after the separation. **A notice required of a state agency by
> this subdivision shall state the date of the involuntary separation and the cause of it and shall be
> certified by the agency head or his designee.** The Board shall state every failure of a state agency to
> give that notice of which the Board becomes aware in the report required by subsection J.

**Edit 11 — F-7 · subdivision G 4, a new sentence after the rescission sentence**

> **Where a determination under subdivision 2 was made or took effect before the Board learned of an
> involuntary separation of the member occurring on or before the date that was then the member's final
> qualifying retirement date, the Board shall rescind the determination and shall restore the service
> credit reduced under it no later than 60 days after the date on which the Board learns of the
> separation, this subdivision applies to the election as though the determination had not been made, and
> the Board shall reinstate the reservation and any contingency amount released on account of the
> determination, in the manner this subdivision requires in the case of a reservation released otherwise
> than in accordance with subdivision D 7, no later than the date of the rescission.**

**Edits 12 and 13 — F-11 · the giving rule, subsection A**

> …a written statement or notice required of the Board is given on the date the Board mails it to **the
> person** ~~the member or applicant~~ to whom it is required to be given or transmits it electronically
> to an address **that person** ~~that member or applicant~~ has provided to the Board for that purpose…
> …every period within which **a person** ~~a member or an applicant~~ may or must act that runs from the
> giving of that statement or notice is extended by three days.

**Edit 14 — F-15 · subdivision G 2, the notice floor**

> …before the determination takes effect, **and a determination that takes effect in contravention of this
> sentence is of no effect; and** the member may seek review of the determination under subsection M.

**Edit 15 — F-16 · definition of "involuntary separation"**

> …or a voluntary resignation. **The date of an involuntary separation is the date on which the member's
> employment terminates or, where the member is placed on leave without pay-layoff or equivalent status,
> the date of that placement.**

**Edit 16 — F-20 · subdivision G 4, the excess notice to wait-listed applicants**

> …shall give written notice of the fact, the amount, and the date of any resulting excess, **of the
> applicant's rights under subsection B of § 51.1-142.2, and of the standard cost, determined as of the
> date of the notice, of the service credit, if any, the applicant is eligible to purchase under
> subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2 as of that date,** to each applicant then on the waiting list…

**Edit 17 — F-23 · subdivision M 2**

> …upon written request filed within 30 days after the notice of the determination **is given**, written
> reconsideration…

**Edit 18 — F-25 · subdivision G 4, a new sentence after the reinstatement duties**

> **For the purposes of this subdivision, an excess is eliminated when the aggregate of the amounts
> charged against the limitation in the first sentence of subdivision D 2 no longer exceeds that
> limitation.**

---

## 3. Two departures from pass 12's own fix direction, with reasons

**(a) F-22 — I did not add G 4's extension to the general outer bound.**

Pass 12's fix was *"add 'or as extended under subdivision G 4' to the bound."* That closes the ratchet and
**re-creates F-1's harm in a narrower class.** A member whose final qualifying retirement date already sits
at the outer bound — because the Board's statement was late and D 1 extended her day for day — would get
**no extension at all** on an involuntary separation, so her 90 days would again be a ceiling and not a
floor. That is precisely the defect store revision 36's edit 2 was written to cure, and F-1 is the finding
that says the protective branch must never shorten the ordinary window.

The ratchet is capped directly instead: a member's date is not extended under G 4 *"by reason of more than
one involuntary separation."* It reaches the whole of pass 12's concern — a member RIF'd, rehired and RIF'd
again gains three months once rather than nine — and it costs the single-separation member nothing.

**(b) F-18 — I did not extend the window for the member who was never given her dates.**

Pass 12's fix was to add to the floor *"or, where the Board has not given that statement, the first day of
the second month following the month in which the Board gives it."* That makes a member's final qualifying
retirement date **depend on an act the Board may never perform**, with a reservation charged against the
$3,000,000 for as long as it does not. I have had to withdraw an assurance that the retirement window's
components are each bounded on the face of the text **twice** — in store revision 33 and again in store
revision 36 — and both times the cause was a limb that ran on a Board act with no cap. I am not writing a
third one.

What is enacted puts the never-told member inside **G 4 clause (iii)** expressly, which is where pass 12's
own mitigation said she probably already was, and removes the *"able but uninformed"* argument that made it
only probable: a member who **retires** at a time when the statement has not been given *is* unable to
retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board. Her credit vests at the pilot price
and the subsidy settles on her effective date of retirement. It extends no window, it adds nothing to cap
occupancy, and it cannot be engineered by the member, because she cannot cause the Board not to give the
statement.

**It does not reach the member whose statement is given very late**, because a statement exists when she
retires; she has the floor instead. The residual — that the floor is keyed to a Board act and so is the one
component of the window with no figure bounding it — is **§7 item 68**, with two candidate bounds drafted
and neither enacted. I would rather it sat on the Director's list as a known, stated residual than be cured
by a numeral nobody chose.

---

## 4. F-24 — no change needed, and why

Pass 12: an agency notice failure occurring after the last report required by J 1 is unreportable, because
J 1's obligation ends *"the first December 1 following the date on which every election … has been settled
… cancelled … or determined."*

**There is nothing left to report by that date.** The agency notice duty in G 4 attaches to the involuntary
separation of *"any member whose election the Board has accepted"*, and its only operative purpose is to
start the Board's 15-day duty to tell the member her G 4 deadline. Once every accepted election has been
settled, cancelled or determined, no member holds a live election, no G 4 deadline can run, and a late
agency notice costs nobody anything. Extending J 1's tail to catch a notice that can no longer harm a member
would lengthen a reporting duty past the point where it reports on anything.

Recorded rather than fixed. If the Director disagrees the cure is four words in J 1 and it moves no figure.

---

## 5. Cross-reference sweep — performed, both directions

**Mechanical checks on the operative text of §1 after the edits:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| *"last sentence"* anywhere in the operative text | **0 occurrences.** F-5 removed the only one, and no new ordinal reference to a sentence was introduced |
| *"the earliest of"* | **1 occurrence**, in G 4's settlement sentence, where three dates are genuinely alternatives and the earliest is correct. F-1's limb was the other one and it is gone |
| *"limitation year"* / *"Limitation year"* | **5 uses in B 4 f and 1 definition in B 4 a.** All five uses now resolve to the plan's own limitation year. Nothing is stranded by the B 4 g deletion or by F-8's redefinition |
| *"As used in this subdivision"* | **1 occurrence**, now *"this subdivision 4"*. No other provision of either section uses the bare form |
| *"member or applicant"* / *"a member or an applicant"* | **0 occurrences.** Both were in the giving rule and both are now *"person"*. The widening is strictly inclusive, so nothing that relied on the rule is narrowed |
| *"is a qualifying retirement"* (the deeming formula) | **0 occurrences.** The fiction is gone from the bill |
| *"the two preceding sentences"* | **1 occurrence**, in the floor. Its referents are now the outer bound and F-2's date-setter — both still date rules, so the phrase is still accurate |
| *"the date of the involuntary separation"* | **3 occurrences**, all in G 4, all now resolved by the new sentence in the definition |
| *"of no effect"* | **2 occurrences** — G 4's disability-application bar and F-15's new G 2 limb. Same device, same words |

**Downstream of the F-2 date-setter.** G 2's clock (limb (a)), F-1's new clock (limb (a)), subsection F's
duty to retire, D 7's release on failure to retire, and D 1's notice content all name the final qualifying
retirement date **by its defined term** and not by restating it. So moving the date moves all five
together, which is the property that makes F-2's cure also cure F-3 and dissolve the F/D 7 conflict without
a carve-out in either provision.

**Downstream of F-6's condition.** The condition is a condition on the **extension**, not on the 90-day
vesting branch, which is unchanged and still runs from the separation itself. So a member whose agency
never notifies keeps the vesting branch within her unmoved window and loses only the extension — and
F-7's rescission limb restores her position if the Board determines the fact later.

**Downstream of F-8.** B 4 f's three computations against *"limitation year"*, and its *"no limitation
year in which it may accept the amount"* branch, all now read on the plan's own year. B 4 f's completion-date
extension (*"no earlier than the first day of that limitation year"*) is the one that produced pass 12's
failure scenario and it is cured by the definition rather than by amending B 4 f.

**Title, enacting clause and enactment clauses.** Unchanged. No edit adds, deletes or renumbers a
subsection, subdivision or clause, so no enactment-clause list needed conforming.

---

## 6. For Fiscal & Impact Modeler — direction of effect, no figure derived

Pass 12 §5 is right that four of its serious findings lengthen expected reservation occupancy and that the
direction is adverse to cap turnover. **Three of the four are now closed in the text**, and the direction
of this revision is therefore the opposite of the one pass 12 measured:

- **F-3 and F-2** — the nine-month-plus hold through a Board over-run. Closed. F-2's date-setter is itself
  capped at **12 months beyond the outer bound**, so the hold is bounded on the face of the text.
- **F-6** — up to three months per election for the price of a one-day layoff-status placement. Closed by
  the evidenced trigger.
- **F-22** — ~3 months per repeat separation. Closed by the one-extension cap.
- **F-7** — the reservation consumed **twice**. Partly closed: the silent-movement path is gone, and where
  the Board does learn late the reinstatement is now express, which **is** a second charge against the
  $3,000,000 and is the thing to model. It is the same over-cap charge the existing reinstatement sentence
  already creates, so it is not a new class.

**No figure moves and I have derived none.** The one-line request pass 12 made of
[MOO-116](/MOO/issues/MOO-116) still stands and is now narrower: test the participant count against a
distribution of reservation hold times rather than a point estimate, on an envelope whose outer bound is
stated in §7 item 68 rather than open.

---

## 7. For the Editor

Four things reach the sponsor documents independently of any figure.

1. **Pass 12's four named risk-section items are now three.** **F-1** (the separated member made worse
   off), **F-6** (the separation trigger can be arranged) and **F-8** (a federal-tax statement the statute
   cannot make) are **closed in the text** and should not appear as live defects. **F-12 paired with
   N-17** is the one that stays, and pass 12 is emphatic about how: the fiscal risk is real and the
   **constitutional** version of it is wrong. Do not let the memo concede an Article X defect that does not
   exist — pass 12 opened both sections and found art. X, § 7 not breached and art. X, § 11's bite to be
   the employer contribution rate.
2. **[MOO-115](/MOO/issues/MOO-115) is no longer load-bearing for the bill text.** F-8's fix defines the
   limitation year by reference to the plan, so the answer to *"what does VRS's plan document designate"*
   no longer changes a word of the draft. It still matters to administration.
3. **A third unmapped party**, after the wait-listed applicant and the separating agency: **the employer
   that may pay up to 95 percent of a member's cost under B 4 e** and holds no right of review anywhere in
   the section. §7 item 65.
4. **The draft is still not publishable.** None of these 17 edits has been attacked by anyone.

---

**Standing caveat.** Internal working draft. Pre-decisional. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill,
not reviewed by counsel or by DLS — passes 4 to 13 are our own adversarial reviews and are expressly not
legal advice — and nothing here is an opinion that any part of the draft is legally sufficient for
introduction. Nothing is cleared for external use. Saving a file is not sending it.

title: Pass 14 disposition — store revision 43 of bill-text-s8: all 20 findings, the fourteen edits verbatim, the cross-reference check, and the four questions (internal working draft)
body:
# Pass 14 disposition — store revision 43 of `bill-text-s8`: all 20 findings, the fourteen edits verbatim, the cross-reference check, and the four questions

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional, not a
Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by counsel or by DLS. Pass 14 is our own adversarial
review and is expressly not legal advice. Nothing here is cleared for external use.**

**What this is.** [MOO-122](/MOO/issues/MOO-122)'s pass 14 — the bounded adversarial and counsel review of
store revision 39's seventeen edits — returned **20 findings: 0 fatal, 8 serious, 8 moderate, 4 minor**,
plus **12 express null results**. This document is the finding-by-finding disposition and the verbatim
operative strings. It is a companion document from the start because `bill-text-s8` arrived with **23
characters** of headroom.

**Result in one line: 14 drafted out in fourteen edits, 1 declined in part with reasons, 2 corrected in the
record, 1 routed to the Director as a choice, 1 recorded with no text defect, 1 corrected against the
reviewer's own fix direction.** No figure moves. `12`, `$3,000,000`, `$170,000` and the `[20]` percent
contingency are untouched by every edit. No section is added, deleted or renumbered. The bill title does
not change.

**Provenance.** Narrative revision 42 — the [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) items, nine edits in six
provisions — landed **after** pass 14 finished at document revision 46. **I re-read all 20 of pass 14's
quoted strings against the live body before editing** and every one was present as quoted. Revision 42's
E3 touched the **disability-and-death** rescission sentence; P14-7 and P14-12 address the
**involuntary-separation** rescission limb, which E3 did not touch. No finding in the pass is addressed to
superseded text.

---

## 1. Disposition of all 20 findings

| Finding | Grade | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **P14-1** · G 4 clause (iii) deemed a Board error on the Board's lawful silence | serious | **Drafted out — edit 1.** The deeming is confined to the case where the time allowed for giving the statement **has expired**. The reviewer's five words, taken as recommended. |
| **P14-2** · the F-3 cure is not secured; nothing suspends a Board period during subsection M tolling | serious | **Drafted out — edit 3.** G 4's existing non-running formula now reaches a pending tolling request, and the request is given the same "pending" definition the disability application has. This is the second half of pass 12's own F-3 fix, which my disposition declined. |
| **P14-3** · the tolling date-setter moves a date by force of law and nobody must tell her | serious | **Drafted out — edit 4**, in the reviewer's second (event-keyed) form, because the Board is already writing to her. |
| **P14-4** · D 1 clause (i)'s mandated recital is now false for three classes of member | serious | **Drafted out — edit 5.** *"The limits stated in that definition."* The substantive claim is dropped rather than the exceptions enumerated. |
| **P14-5** · F-18 is cured for one of its two sub-classes; the never-told member who does **not** retire is still stripped | serious | **Drafted out — edits 1 and 2**, paired with P14-15 as the reviewer advised. |
| **P14-6** · *"determined"* against *"learns"* against *"learned"*; the Board holds a finding of fact it pays for, with no deadline and no review of inaction | serious | **Drafted out in part — edits 6 and 7.** Predicates aligned and a member route with a 30-day determination, notice, reasons and subsection M review. **The deeming rule is declined and drafted at §7 item 74.** |
| **P14-7** · the rescission rescinds without curing, and freezes the Program while it does | serious | **Drafted out — edit 8.** The rescission now carries the date-setter, capped at 12 months. |
| **P14-8** · G 2's *"of no effect"* has no reconciliation machinery | serious | **Drafted out — edit 9**, on the reviewer's primary fix (cure, not nullity). **Reduces a member windfall; direction of effect stated. The nullity with its machinery is drafted at §7 item 73.** |
| **P14-9** · the 12-month cap is measured off the wrong datum | moderate | **Not enacted. §7 item 71**, three options drafted. **The reviewer's own fix direction is surplusage** and I say why. |
| **P14-10** · what *"the last day on which the member may retire … under this subdivision"* means | moderate | **To the Director — §7 item 72.** Both readings drafted; about three months of reservation occupancy per repeat separation between them. |
| **P14-11** · edit 15 dates two forms out of an **open** set | moderate | **Drafted out — edit 10.** Residual limb, as recommended. |
| **P14-12** · *"the date that was then the member's final qualifying retirement date"* has no fixed datum | moderate | **Drafted out — edit 11.** |
| **P14-13** · F-19 disambiguated one use of thirteen and the inference now runs against the member | moderate | **Drafted out — edit 12.** B 4 f's carve-out is confined to B 4 f, so a Board error in a **B 4 c** redetermination is again an error of the Board. |
| **P14-14** · the plan's limitation year collides with B 4 f's 24-month cap | moderate | **Drafted out — edit 13.** Added to the exception already there. |
| **P14-15** · clause (iii) can apply to a member who never retires and nothing settles her | moderate | **Drafted out — edit 2**, drawn to the status rather than to the statement, as the reviewer advised. |
| **P14-16** · settled amounts never leave the aggregate, so a late-Program excess does not self-cure | moderate | **No text defect. Recorded**, and the correction is routed to the Modeler at §5 below. The reviewer endorses the edit itself (N14-4). |
| **P14-17** · the sweep's ordinal-reference row does not hold | minor | **Record corrected — §5.24**, in `bill-text-s8` and in the §5.21 stub. |
| **P14-18** · the sweep's *"limitation year"* count is four, not five | minor | **Record corrected — §5.24**, with the further note that **edit 13 adds a fifth**. |
| **P14-19** · the date-setter's condition must be read counterfactually | minor | **Recorded. No edit.** No other reading is available without making the sentence self-defeating, and the reviewer recorded it only so nobody later thinks it was missed. I agree. |
| **P14-20** · the reinstatement notices are shaped like an error report about a lawful act | minor | **Drafted out — edit 14.** The agency's failure is now notice content, which also gives subsection J something to count. |

---

## 2. The fourteen edits, verbatim

The whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language and is underlined in the bill. Underlining is stripped here so
the strings can be diffed; **new words are in bold**.

**Edit 1 — subdivision G 4, the clause (iii) deeming sentence (P14-1, P14-5).**

> For the purposes of clause (iii) of this subdivision, a member who retires at a time when the Board has
> not given the statement required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection
> A**, and the time allowed by that definition for giving that statement has expired,** is unable to
> retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board**; and a member whose final
> qualifying retirement date passes at a time when the Board has not given that statement and the time
> allowed by that definition for giving it has expired is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by
> reason of an error of the Board**.

**Edit 2 — subdivision G 4, a new sentence immediately before *"No certified subsidy is settled under this
subdivision after the reservation …"* (P14-5, P14-15).**

> **Where clause (iii) of this subdivision applies and, by the member's final qualifying retirement date
> or, where the member has none, by the completion date stated in the certification, the member has
> neither died nor been approved for a disability retirement allowance nor retired, the certified subsidy
> for the election is settled on that date, and this subdivision and subsection N apply to that settlement
> as they apply to a settlement on a date stated in clause (a), (b), or (c) of this subdivision.**

**Edit 3 — subdivision G 4, the non-running sentence and the definition of "pending" (P14-2).**

> No period stated in subdivision 2 or in this subdivision, whether it is a period within which the Board
> is required to act or a period within which a determination is required to take effect, runs while such
> an application is pending **or while a request the filing of which tolls the running of the member's
> final qualifying retirement date under subsection M is pending**. For the purposes of this subdivision
> an application for a disability retirement allowance is pending from the date on which the member files
> it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it**, and such a request is pending from the date
> on which the member files it until the date on which the Board acts upon it**.

**Edit 4 — the definition of "final qualifying retirement date", a new last sentence (P14-3).**

> **Where the Board's action upon a request determines a member's final qualifying retirement date under
> this definition, the Board shall state that date in its decision upon the request.**

**Edit 5 — subdivision D 1, clause (i) of the notice-content sentence (P14-4).**

> … that the date so extended is subject to the **limits** stated in that definition …

*(for* "the outer bound stated in that definition"*)*

**Edit 6 — subdivision G 4, the extension proviso (P14-6).**

> … provided that the Board has received a notice of the separation required of a state agency by this
> subdivision**,** has otherwise determined that an involuntary separation occurred**, or has otherwise
> learned of facts from which it is required by this subdivision to determine that an involuntary
> separation occurred**.

**Edit 7 — subdivision G 4, two new sentences after the agency-certification sentence (P14-6).**

> **A member may file with the Board written evidence of an involuntary separation of the member. The
> Board shall determine whether an involuntary separation occurred and shall give the member written
> notice of the determination, of the date of the separation as determined, and of the reasons for the
> determination, no later than 30 days after the member files that evidence; and a determination under
> this sentence is a determination of the Board for the purposes of subsection M.**

**Edit 8 — subdivision G 4, the involuntary-separation rescission limb (P14-7).**

> … in the manner this subdivision requires in the case of a reservation released otherwise than in
> accordance with subdivision D 7, no later than the date of the rescission**, and the member's final
> qualifying retirement date is the first day of the second month following the month in which the Board
> rescinds the determination, and in no event later than 12 months after the date that would have applied
> under this subdivision had the Board determined the separation on the date it learned of it**.

**Edit 9 — subdivision G 2, the notice sentence (P14-8).**

> … and a determination that takes effect in contravention of this sentence **takes effect instead on the
> first day on which it may take effect under this sentence** …

*(for* "is of no effect"*)*

**Edit 10 — the definition of "involuntary separation" (P14-11).**

> … or, where the member is placed on leave without pay-layoff or equivalent status, the date of that
> placement**, or, in the case of any other involuntary separation, the date on which the member ceases to
> occupy the position from which the member is separated**.

**Edit 11 — subdivision G 4, the rescission limb's datum (P14-12).**

> … occurring on or before **the member's final qualifying retirement date as it stood immediately before
> the determination was made** …

*(for* "the date that was then the member's final qualifying retirement date"*)*

**Edit 12 — § 51.1-142.2, subdivision B 4 f (P14-13).**

> A determination under **subdivision f of this subdivision 4** is not an error of the Board for the
> purposes of subdivision G 4 of § 51.1-142.4 …

**Edit 13 — § 51.1-142.2, subdivision B 4 f, the 24-month cap's exception (P14-14).**

> … except that this sentence does not prevent the extension of a completion date to the last day of the
> period allowed by this subdivision for making an election under clause (i), (ii), or (iii)**, or to the
> first day of a limitation year under clause (ii) of this subdivision**.

**Edit 14 — subdivision G 4, the reinstatement notices sentence (P14-20).**

> … of the nature of any error, of the amount of any resulting excess, **of** the cause of the release**,
> and of whether a state agency failed to give a notice required of it by this subdivision and, if so, of
> the identity of that agency**, to the Chairmen …

---

## 3. The three that cost a real person real money

**1. An appropriation trigger that fired on the Board's lawful silence (P14-1).** Store revision 39's
F-18 cure said, in the indicative and with no discretion, that a member who retires *"at a time when the
Board has not given the statement"* is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement **by reason of an error
of the Board**. The Board has 15 days **after crediting** to give that statement, and for the whole of
that period — and for the entire period before crediting — the condition is true and the Board is in
perfect compliance. The reviewer's facts: she pays in full on 20 February 2032, has filed a § 51.1-153
notice for 1 March 2032 (which breaches nothing, because D 1's filing scheme runs *from* the statement),
the Board credits on 10 March 2032 within its 30 days, her earliest qualifying retirement date is
therefore 1 April 2032 and her statement is due 25 March 2032. Her 1 March retirement is **not** a
qualifying retirement. On the old text she went to G 2. Under edit 7 the Board was **commanded** to find
that it erred: her four years vested at the pilot price and up to **$170,000** settled on 1 March 2032 and
became payable under subsection N, for an acceleration that never occurred. **It is my defect from store
revision 39**, and the cure costs the never-told member nothing, because her statement is always overdue.

**2. The never-told member who does not retire (P14-5).** Edit 7 reached *"a member who **retires**"*.
Pass 12's F-18 member is the one who **does not** retire, and she is the modal case, because a member who
has never been told in writing that there is a date is far more likely to let it pass than to retire on
it. She is rescued nowhere else: the floor is keyed to *"the month in which the Board **gives** the
statement"*, and D 1's day-for-day extension to *"[w]here the Board **gives** that written statement …
later than the time required"*. Neither fires if it is never given. So her bare first-sentence date
matured, G 2 cut four years back to the sixteen months her payments bought at standard cost, and roughly
$30,000 of her money bought a third of what she paid for. **The second limb of edit 1 reaches her by the
passing of the date rather than by a retirement, and extends no window and adds nothing to cap
occupancy** — her date does not move; her credit vests and the subsidy settles and clears on the date it
would otherwise have been stripped.

**3. Two classes of reservation with no terminating event (P14-15, P14-7).** Clause (iii) states a
**status**, not an event. A member can occupy it without ever retiring — clearest case, she pays in full
and the Board never credits, so she has no earliest qualifying retirement date and no retirement she can
take will satisfy the definition. Her credit vests, which **bars D 7's release**; subdivisions 2 and 3 are
disapplied, so G 2 cannot determine; and the settlement sentence had only three limbs, all requiring a
death, a disability effective date or a retirement. **Her reservation and contingency were charged against
the $3,000,000 with no terminating event, for the life of the Program and beyond**, because enactment 3
clause (ii) keeps them charged after expiry. On twelve elections, one such election removes about **6
percent** of the Program's capacity permanently. Edit 2 settles her. Edit 8 closes the second class, the
member rescinded into a window that closed months before the rescission.

---

## 4. Cross-reference check

**Performed in both directions. The summary table is at `bill-text-s8` §5.24**, which also carries the
three corrections to §5.21's sweep rows (P14-17, P14-18, N14-2) and the mechanical counts: *"of no
effect"* 2 → **1**; *"the date of the involuntary separation"* **3**; *"the earliest of"* **1**; *"this
subdivision 4"* **2**; *"last sentence"* **0**; *"limitation year"* in §1 6 → **7**, of which **5** are in
B 4 f. **Title, enacting clause and every enactment clause unchanged.**

**The one inward result worth repeating here.** Edit 8 moves the final qualifying retirement date, and
that date is the carrier for **six** downstream provisions — subsection F's duty, D 7's release, G 2's
clock, G 4's clock, D 1's notice content and the **definition of *"qualifying retirement"* itself**, which
pass 14 identified as the sixth and the one that makes the whole cure work. **None needs a carve-out.**
That is the same property that made pass 12's F-2 cure work, and it is why a date-setter is the right
device for a rescission as well.

---

## 5. For the Fiscal & Impact Modeler — the assumption, narrowed, and no figure moved

**No figure is derived or moved in this revision.** Pass 14 did not derive one either; its §4 is a
challenge to an assumption, as pass 12's was.

**The correction that must be carried.** [`pass12-disposition`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-pass12-disposition)
§6 tells you *"the hold is bounded on the face of the text."* **Narrow it to: the member's retirement
window is bounded on the face of the text — at the outer bound plus 12 months under the tolling
date-setter, or plus about four months under G 4, once — but reservation occupancy was not.** Store
revision 43 closes the two classes that had no terminating event (edits 2 and 8). What remains for your
model:

1. **Settled amounts never leave the aggregate (P14-16).** D 2's second sentence keeps an amount settled
   charged against the limitation, so an excess self-cures only to the extent of the difference between
   amounts reserved and amounts settled. **Late in the Program an excess cannot be eliminated at all**,
   and G 4's *"accept no further election until the excess is eliminated"* is then permanent rather than
   temporary. Operationally close to harmless, because D 2's first sentence has already stopped acceptance
   by then — but the statement that an excess self-cures is wrong in the late-Program case.
2. **Reading (a) of §7 item 72 slides the Board's clock by about three months per repeat separation**,
   even where the member's own date has not moved. The window is bounded either way; occupancy is not.
   **Tell me which reading you want priced and I will tell the Director what it costs.**
3. **§7 item 71 option (b) adds occupancy in the tail only** — it requires the Board to breach its own
   90-day reconsideration deadline, so no central-case member reaches it.
4. **Edit 9 has a direction of effect on the trust, and it runs in the trust's favour.** The nullity it
   replaces created an unfunded liability — credit never reduced, reservation re-let, aggregate over
   $3,000,000 — flowing into the employer contribution rate at the next valuation under art. X, § 11's
   actuarial-methods clause. **Not an art. X, § 7 defect**, and no document of ours may concede one.

---

## 6. For the Editor — the risk section

**Four of pass 14's five named items are closed in the text and must not be carried as live defects:**
P14-1, P14-4, P14-5 and P14-2. **What stays**, and how to say it:

- **P14-16**, as a disclosure and not a defect: the acceptance freeze is temporary early in the Program and
  permanent late in it, because settled amounts stay charged.
- **§7 items 71 to 74**, as open drafting questions with the Director, not as findings.
- **Two things no document may concede.** The **nondelegation** challenge to *"otherwise determined"*
  fails — a delegation of the power to ascertain whether facts required by a law exist is not of itself
  arbitrary, and *"an involuntary separation occurred"* is a fact under a borrowed statutory definition
  (pass 14 N14-11, with its own caveat that *Ames v. Town of Painter* could not be opened at source and
  that no live finding rests on it). And **art. X** holds, on both pass 12's N-17 and pass 14's reading:
  P14-8's exposure is art. X, § 11's actuarial-methods clause, **not** art. X, § 7.
- **One stakeholder re-weighting, not a new party** (pass 14 N14-12): edit 11 of store revision 39 added a
  new class of event triggering the acceptance freeze, so the **wait-listed applicant** now bears the cost
  of a state agency's failure to file a notice. Edit 8 of this revision shortens that exposure; it does
  not remove it.

---

## 7. Status

**None of these fourteen edits has been attacked by anyone.** [MOO-127](/MOO/issues/MOO-127) is the bounded
pass, and the three I most want broken are **edit 2** (a new settlement sentence that pays the
Commonwealth's money on a date no retirement occurred), **edit 8** (a date-setter inside a rescission, with
a 12-month cap that is my numeral) and **edit 9** (where I took a protection out and put a cure in).

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by counsel, not legally
sufficient for introduction. Pre-decisional and internal. Saving a file is not sending it.**

title: Pass 15 disposition — store revision 47 of bill-text-s8: all 25 findings, the seventeen edits verbatim, and four questions for the Policy Director
body:
# Pass 15 disposition — store revision 47 of `bill-text-s8`: all 25 findings, the seventeen edits verbatim, and four questions for the Policy Director

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional, not a Division
of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by counsel and not reviewed by DLS. Pass 15 is our own adversarial
review and is expressly not legal advice. Nothing here is cleared for external use, and saving a file is not
sending it.**

## 0. Scope, method and the string check

[MOO-127](/MOO/issues/MOO-127)'s **pass 15** reviewed the fourteen edits of store revision 43 and returned
**25 findings — 0 fatal, 6 serious, 11 moderate, 8 minor — with 15 express null results.** It records that
the fatal count is zero and that it could not make a case against the architecture.

**Disposition of all 25: 17 drafted out in seventeen edits, 1 no change with the reason, 3 corrected in the
record, 4 routed to the Policy Director as §7 items 84 to 87 with addenda to items 71, 72 and 73.**

**Why this is its own document.** `bill-text-s8` arrived with about **6,400 characters** of headroom against
the store's 524,288-character ceiling. Seven sections were moved **verbatim** to
[`bill-text-s8-revision-history-2`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history-2) to make
room for the record alone — the §0 narrative for store revisions 43, 44 and 45, the sweeps §5.24 and §5.25,
and §6.0-43 and §6.0-45 — each replaced by a stub restating its durable results and naming what in it is
superseded.

**The string check, run before any editing.** Pass 15 verified its fourteen strings against document revision
`9cfa093e`. **Store revisions 44, 45 and 46 landed after that**, so I re-read all fourteen, and all seventeen
of my own target strings, against the live body at document revision 52 (`ac8c1de6`, 517,909 characters).
**Every one was present exactly once.** No finding in the pass is addressed to text that had already changed,
and no edit of mine was applied to a string I had not just read.

**What did not move.** `12`, `$3,000,000`, `$170,000` and the `[20]` percent contingency are untouched by
every edit. No section is added, deleted or renumbered. The bill title, the enacting clause and enactment
clauses 2, 4 and 5 are untouched; enactment clause 3 is amended once (M-4).

## 1. Every finding, and what happened to it

| Finding | Grade | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **S-1** second settlement of the same certified subsidy | serious | **Drafted out, E1.** Fix (a), widened to reach subdivision 1 as well as G 4. The structural alternative (b) is **§7 item 84**. |
| **S-2** the rescission cap has no referent | serious | **Drafted out, E2** — datum repaired and subordinated. **The bound itself is §7 item 85**, and the reviewer's own proposed wording is inert in the same way mine is. |
| **S-3** the Board's periods stop with no cap | serious | **Drafted out, E3**, in M 2's own words, confined to the tolling-request limb. |
| **S-4** the cure can breach G 2's 120-day outer limit | serious | **Drafted out, E5.** The outer limit yields where the Board's own notice is late. Falls away if §7 item 73 restores the nullity. |
| **S-5** *"required by this subdivision to determine"* has no anchoring duty | serious | **Drafted out, E6** — *"has otherwise learned of the involuntary separation."* §7 item 74's claim narrowed. |
| **S-6** no tolling on the member's filing, no case decision, no appeal | serious | **Routed, §7 item 86.** Both drafted sentences are the reviewer's and both are better than pass 14's deeming rule. Recommended, not enacted. |
| **M-1** the 15-day notice falls due before the determination | moderate | **Drafted out, E7.** |
| **M-2** the never-retiring member is valued on a retirement that never happens | moderate | **Routed to Fiscal**, [MOO-134](/MOO/issues/MOO-134). Direction indeterminate on the text; I assert none. |
| **M-3** the settlement recovers the contingency, not the reservation | moderate | **Record correction** against `pass14-disposition` §3 point 3, and **routed to Fiscal** for the restatement. No figure moved. |
| **M-4** subsection N's duty is the Commonwealth's and enactment 3 preserves the Board's | moderate | **Drafted out, E8.** |
| **M-5** the settlement date can precede the date clause (iii) applies | moderate | **Drafted out, E9** — the valuation date stays, the clock moves. |
| **M-6** the tolling date-setter's statement has no time and no consequence | moderate | **Drafted out, E10, E11, E12.** |
| **M-7** the rescission datum ignores a date her own reconsideration moved | moderate | **Drafted out, E13.** |
