## 2. The seventeen edits, verbatim

The whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language and is underlined in the bill; underlining and bold are stripped here so the substitutions can be diffed. **Every edit below was verified present exactly once before it was made, and the replaced text appears nowhere in the document afterwards.**

### E1 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the backstop sentence (S-1)

**From:**

> No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect.

**To:**

> No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the reservation for the election has been released in accordance with subdivision D 7 or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect, and no certified subsidy is settled more than once under this subdivision or under subdivision 1.

### E2 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the rescission date-setter (S-2)

**From:**

> , and in no event later than 12 months after the date that would have applied under this subdivision had the Board determined the separation on the date it learned of it.

**To:**

> , and in no event later than 12 months after the date of the involuntary separation, except that where that first day is later than 12 months after the date of the involuntary separation the member's final qualifying retirement date is that first day.

### E3 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the non-running sentence (S-3)

**From:**

> runs while such an application is pending or while a request the filing of which tolls the running of the member’s final qualifying retirement date under subsection M is pending.

**To:**

> runs while such an application is pending or while a request the filing of which tolls the running of the member’s final qualifying retirement date under subsection M is pending, except that the aggregate of all such non-running by reason of such requests shall not exceed 120 days and shall exclude any period after the expiration of the 90 days allowed by subsection M and before the Board acts upon the request.

### E4 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the "pending" definition (m-1)

**From:**

> and such a request is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board acts upon it.

**To:**

> and such a request is pending from the date on which the member files it until the date on which the Board first acts upon it.

### E5 — § 51.1-142.4 G 2 — the outer-limit sentence (S-4)

**From:**

> A determination under this subdivision shall take effect no later than 60 days after the Board gives the notice required by this subdivision, and in no event later than 120 days after the determination date.

**To:**

> A determination under this subdivision shall take effect no later than 60 days after the Board gives the notice required by this subdivision, and in no event later than 120 days after the determination date, except that where the Board gives that notice later than 60 days after the determination date the determination takes effect on the first day on which it may take effect under the sentence of this subdivision that requires notice to be given before the determination takes effect.

### E6 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the extension proviso (S-5)

**From:**

> , has otherwise determined that an involuntary separation occurred, or has otherwise learned of facts from which it is required by this subdivision to determine that an involuntary separation occurred.

**To:**

> , has otherwise determined that an involuntary separation occurred, or has otherwise learned of the involuntary separation.

### E7 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — a new sentence after the 15-day member notice (M-1)

**From:**

> of the date by which the member must retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision and of the consequences under subdivision 2 of not retiring by that date. A state agency shall notify the Board

**To:**

> of the date by which the member must retire in a qualifying retirement under this subdivision and of the consequences under subdivision 2 of not retiring by that date. Where the Board learns of the involuntary separation by written evidence filed by the member under this subdivision, the notice required by the preceding sentence shall be given no later than 15 days after the Board makes the determination required by this subdivision. A state agency shall notify the Board

### E8 — Enactment clause 3, clause (i) (M-4)

**From:**

> shall continue in effect and continue to run as though those provisions had not expired;

**To:**

> shall continue in effect and continue to run as though those provisions had not expired, and the Commonwealth shall make every payment required by subsection N of that section in respect of any settlement the Board so makes;

### E9 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the no-final-date settlement limb (M-5)

**From:**

> the certified subsidy for the election is settled on that date, and this subdivision and subsection N apply to that settlement as they apply to a settlement on a date stated in clause (a), (b), or (c) of this subdivision.

**To:**

> the certified subsidy for the election is settled on that date, and this subdivision and subsection N apply to that settlement as they apply to a settlement on a date stated in clause (a), (b), or (c) of this subdivision, except that the period within which the redetermination required by this subdivision must be made runs from the date on which the Board determines that clause (iii) of this subdivision applies.

### E10 — § 51.1-142.4 A — "final qualifying retirement date", last sentence (M-6)

**From:**

> Where the Board's action upon a request determines a member's final qualifying retirement date under this definition, the Board shall state that date in its decision upon the request.

**To:**

> Where the Board's action upon a request determines a member's final qualifying retirement date under this definition, the Board shall state that date in its decision upon the request, and where the Board does not do so it shall give the member written notice of that date no later than 15 days after it acts upon the request.

### E11 — § 51.1-142.4 D 1 — the day-for-day extension sentence (M-6)

**From:**

> Where the Board gives that written statement, or any notice of a later approved date required by that definition, later than the time required by that definition,

**To:**

> Where the Board gives that written statement, any notice of a later approved date required by that definition, or any notice of a date required by that definition upon the Board's action upon a request, later than the time required by that definition,

### E12 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the two clause (iii) deeming limbs (M-6)

**From:**

> a member who retires at a time when the Board has not given the statement required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A, and the time allowed by that definition for giving that statement has expired, is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board; and a member whose final qualifying retirement date passes at a time when the Board has not given that statement and the time allowed by that definition for giving it has expired is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board.

**To:**

> a member who retires at a time when the Board has not given a statement or notice of the member's final qualifying retirement date required by the definition of "final qualifying retirement date" in subsection A, and the time allowed by that definition for giving that statement or notice has expired, is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board; and a member whose final qualifying retirement date passes at a time when the Board has not given such a statement or notice and the time allowed by that definition for giving it has expired is unable to retire in a qualifying retirement by reason of an error of the Board.

### E13 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the rescission condition's datum (M-7)

**From:**

> occurring on or before the member's final qualifying retirement date as it stood immediately before the determination was made,

**To:**

> occurring on or before the member's final qualifying retirement date as it stood immediately before the determination was made or, if later, immediately before the determination took effect,

### E14 — § 51.1-142.2 B 4 f — the 24-month cap's exception (M-9 and m-4)

**From:**

> except that this sentence does not prevent the extension of a completion date to the last day of the period allowed by this subdivision for making an election under clause (i), (ii), or (iii), or to the first day of a limitation year under clause (ii) of this subdivision.

**To:**

> except that this sentence does not prevent the extension of a completion date to the last day of the period allowed by this subdivision for making an election under clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of this subdivision, or to a date no later than 12 months after the first day of a limitation year under clause (ii) of this subdivision.

### E15 — § 51.1-142.4 J 1 — the content of the report (M-10)

**From:**

> the number of determinations rescinded and the service credit restored under subdivision G 4;

**To:**

> the number of determinations rescinded and the service credit restored under subdivision G 4; the number of elections settled under subdivision G 4 by reason of an error of the Board and the amounts so settled;

### E16 — § 51.1-142.2 B 4 f — the error-of-the-Board carve-out (m-3)

**From:**

> A determination under subdivision f of this subdivision 4 is not an error of the Board

**To:**

> A determination under this subdivision is not an error of the Board

### E17 — § 51.1-142.4 G 4 — the Chairmen's reinstatement notice (m-5)

**From:**

> and the Senate Committee on Finance and Appropriations no later than 15 days after the reinstatement; shall give written notice of the fact,

**To:**

> and the Senate Committee on Finance and Appropriations no later than 15 days after the reinstatement, which notice shall not identify any member; shall give written notice of the fact,

## 3. Where I departed from the reviewer, and the corrections that run against me

**1. S-1: I took the cheaper fix and widened it.** The reviewer offered a bar (a) and a restructure (b) and
preferred (b). I enacted **(a)**, and added the words *"or under subdivision 1"* that (a) as offered did not
carry, so the rule is single-settlement across the whole of subsection G. **(b) is better and it is a
question, not a repair:** it rewrites a sentence passes 12 to 15 have certified, and it changes which of two
dates governs a member who retires after her date has passed. That is §7 item 84.

**2. S-2: the reviewer's own fix has the defect it found in mine, and I am saying so.** Its wording puts the
floor at the base — *"in no event earlier than the first day of the second month following the month in which
the Board rescinds"* — so the 12-month cap can **never bind**, which is precisely the inertness it
(correctly) diagnosed in my counterfactual. **Mine has the same property and I enacted it knowing that**,
because what the edit must do is remove an operative term with no referent and remove the reading that
restores a member's credit and re-strips it in the same breath. **The bound cannot sit on the retirement date
at all**: a rescission happens when the Board learns, so the only real bound is a limit on the rescission,
and that strips the member whose agency never filed. §7 item 85 puts that choice where it belongs.

**3. m-6: the residual limb of *"involuntary separation"* stays, and this is a no-change with a reason.**
**Corrected on [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136), 12 October 2026.** § 2.2-3200 B is **open** — it reads
*"'Involuntary separation' **includes, but is not limited to,** terminations and layoffs…"* — so the limb
addresses a **non-empty** residual class and not an empty set. Pass 15's quotation omitted those five words,
the closed-set reading recorded here is **withdrawn**, and **pass 14's P14-11 premise holds.** The limb stays
**on the merits**: § 2.2-3200 B is not ours to control, and the residual limb is what gives a date to an
involuntary separation in which the member neither has employment terminate nor is placed on leave without
pay-layoff or equivalent status but ceases to occupy the position — § 51.1-155.1 D's *"failure to obtain
reappointment"* and an officer whose position is abolished are the concrete cases. [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136) re-opened
the section at source, so the attribution is to it and not to pass 15, and the disposition of m-6 is unchanged.

**4. S-6 and M-11 are the reviewer's answer to a question I put to it, and I did not enact either half.**
I asked whether declining pass 14's deeming rule leaves the member without a remedy. The answer is yes, on a
ground pass 14 did not give — her date runs while the Board sits, and if the Board never determines there is
no *"case decision"* within § 2.2-4001, so § 2.2-4026 gives her nothing to appeal. **The two-sentence fix
costs the Director nothing on the fact-finding principle the deeming rule offended**, which is why it is
recommended at §7 item 86 rather than enacted: one adds a tolling trigger and the other takes a filing right
away, and both change occupancy.

**5. Three corrections in the record, two of them mine.** §6.0-43 item 2 (S-1), §7 item 74's alignment claim
(S-5), and `pass14-disposition` §3 point 3's capacity claim (M-3). **And one correction to the reviewer, from
my own sweep:** its §3 table records `$170,000` as appearing **once**; it appears **twice**, both in
subdivision D 2 — the ceiling and the refusal notice store revision 44 restored. Both are the same figure,
both untouched, and nothing in the pass turns on it.

## 4. The sweep, check by check

1. **Pre-edit string verification.** 17 target strings and 14 pass-15 strings, each present **exactly once**
   in the live body at document revision 52.
2. **Superseded strings.** Six checks — the deleted counterfactual; *"facts from which it is required by this
   subdivision to determine"*; *"subdivision f of this subdivision 4"*; the old deeming-limb formula; the old
   rescission datum; the unqualified outer limit — **zero** occurrences in the bill text, **zero** in the
   commentary. Nothing in §2 to §8 quotes a string this revision replaced.
3. **Protected figures.** `$3,000,000` ×1; `$170,000` ×2 (both subdivision D 2, both untouched); `[20]`
   percent ×1; the 12-month first sentence of *"final qualifying retirement date"* unaltered.
4. **No new sentence-ordinal citation.** `"last sentence"` **0** in the bill text; `"second sentence"` **1**,
   pre-existing in enactment 3 and about subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2. The one place that needed to point
   at the tolling date-setter's statement duty is keyed to its **content** — *"a date required by that
   definition upon the Board's action upon a request"*. This honours pass 14's P14-17 correction.
5. **S-4's descriptive reference is unique.** Only one sentence of G 2 requires notice to be given *before
   the determination takes effect*. The 60-day notice-timing sentence requires notice but not notice before
   effect; the allowance-bar sentence is about payment. **One referent.**
6. **Cross-references chased in both directions**, edit by edit: subdivision 1 and subsection N (E1);
   subsection M 2 clauses (i) and (ii) (E3); G 2's notice sentence, subsection A's mailing rule and M 2's 30
   days (E5); the two other knowledge formulas in G 4 (E6); the agency-notice sentence (E7); subsection N and
   enactment 3 clauses (ii) to (v) (E8); the redetermination sentence and subdivision D 3 (E9); D 1's clauses
   (i) to (iii) and G 4's deeming limbs (E10, E11, E12); subdivision 2's effective-date machinery (E13); B 4
   f's extension sentence and its clauses (i) to (iii) (E14); subsection J 1's terminal condition (E15); the
   wait-list limb in the same sentence (E17). **Nothing is stranded.**
7. **Diff discipline.** The bill text differs from store revision 46 in **7 lines and 17 substitutions**, and
   in nothing else. No heading is duplicated; the fifteen `§0.x` zero-tokens remain unique.
8. **Sources I did not re-open and do not represent that I did.** § 2.2-3200 B, § 2.2-4001, § 2.2-4026 and
   art. X, § 11 — all opened at source by pass 15, each attributed where used. The only one that carries a
   decision of mine is § 2.2-3200 B, and that decision is to change nothing. **[MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136) has since re-opened
   § 2.2-3200 B at source** (12 October 2026): it reads *"includes, but is not limited to"*, the set is
   **open**, and the closed-set reading is withdrawn. The three sentences above stand as a record of what was
   true when they were written. The decision is still to change nothing, and it now rests on the merits.

## 5. The four questions, drafted verbatim

### Question 1 — §7 item 84 (S-1): keep the bar, or make the date clause (d)?

**(a) Enacted.** In G 4's backstop sentence: *"…or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken
effect, **and no certified subsidy is settled more than once under this subdivision or under subdivision
1**."*

**(b) The restructure.** Delete the sentence beginning *"Where clause (iii) of this subdivision applies
and,"* and add to *"the earliest of"* a fourth limb:

> **(d) the member's final qualifying retirement date or, where the member has none, the completion date
> stated in the certification, where by that date the member has neither died nor been approved for a
> disability retirement allowance nor retired.**

On (b) a second settlement is structurally impossible rather than barred, and the condition travels with the
limb, so a clause (iii) member who later retires cannot settle on the earlier of two dates. **If (b) is
adopted, E9 (M-5's clock) must be re-pointed at clause (d) and E1 becomes unnecessary** — one further edit,
and I will make it.

### Question 2 — §7 item 85 (S-2): how long may a rescission-restored reservation sit against the $3,000,000?

**(a) Accept and disclose.** Enacted text stands; the fiscal statement says that a reservation restored on a
rescission can sit against the limitation for as long as the Board takes to learn of the separation.

**(b) Bound the rescission.** Add to G 4's rescission limb: *"**The Board shall not rescind a determination
under this sentence where the Board learns of the involuntary separation more than [24] months after the date
of it.**"* A real bound; **it strips the member whose agency never filed and who never knew the right
existed.**

**(c) Bound the charge, not the date.** Add: *"**Where the Board reinstates a reservation under this
sentence and the amount available to be reserved is insufficient for it, the Board shall reinstate it only to
the extent that amount permits and shall place the balance on the waiting list maintained under subdivision D
5 in the position the application held.**"* The cap is never exceeded; **the cost moves from the waiting list
to the member whose credit was wrongly stripped.**

I recommend **(a)**. The numeral in (b) is a placeholder and is not mine to choose.

### Question 3 — §7 item 86 (S-6 and M-11): the member's evidence filing

**(i) Tolling.** In subsection M 2, for *"and the filing of a request under the definition of 'final
qualifying retirement date' in subsection A,"* read *"**, the filing of a request under the definition of
'final qualifying retirement date' in subsection A, and the filing of written evidence of an involuntary
separation under subdivision G 4,**"*. This stops her clock and brings the filing inside M 2's own 120-day
aggregate cap and its anti-repetition clause (i).

**(ii) Repetition.** In G 4, after the filing sentence: *"**A member may file such evidence once in respect
of any one involuntary separation.**"*

I recommend **both**. (i) alone leaves M-11's workload tail open; (ii) alone leaves the member with a right
and no clock.

### Question 4 — §7 item 87 (M-8): the acceptance freeze in the success case

**(a) Exclude a settled reinstated amount from the freeze test.** In G 4, for *"an excess is eliminated when
the aggregate of the amounts charged against the limitation in the first sentence of subdivision D 2 no
longer exceeds that limitation"* read *"…**no longer exceeds that limitation, the amount of any certified
subsidy that has been settled and that was reinstated under this subdivision being left out of that
aggregate for the purposes of this sentence only**."*

**(b) Disclose it** and leave the text: the freeze lifts if the member fails to retire and is permanent if
she retires, and the party who bears it is the wait-listed applicant.

I am neutral. **(a) relaxes the one self-executing limitation in the bill; (b) is a fiscal-statement
choice.**

## 6. Routing

- **Policy Director** — §7 items **84, 85, 86, 87**, and the addenda to items **71** (same cap question),
  **72** (m-7) and **73** (m-2, and S-4's edit falls away if the nullity is restored). **Nothing in the
  seventeen edits pre-empts any answer on your list**, and items 31 to 83 are untouched.
- **Fiscal & Impact Modeler** — [MOO-134](/MOO/issues/MOO-134): **M-2** (the PV gap between the amount
  settled for a member who never retires and the trust's cost of her vested credit at her actual later
  retirement, and how many of the twelve elections can reach that state — **direction indeterminate on the
  text and I assert none**); **M-3** (which base the "about 6 percent" capacity figure used, and the
  restatement that the settlement recovers the **contingency**, not the reservation); and **M-11**'s tail
  occupancy. **No figure is moved, derived or challenged by this revision.**
- **Statutory Researcher** — [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136), **answered and accepted 12 October 2026**.
  On **m-5**, **no FOIA exclusion applies** to a member-identifying record in the subdivision G 4 notice,
  in the Board's hands or a money committee's, so the bar *"which notice shall not identify any member"* is
  **operative and not belt-and-braces**. And **§ 2.2-3200 B is open** — [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136) re-opened it at
  source and **withdrew** the closed-set reading; the no-change decision stands on the merits.
- **Red Team / Counsel Reviewer** — [MOO-135](/MOO/issues/MOO-135): **pass 16**, bounded to these seventeen
  places. **None of this language has been attacked by anyone.**
- **Editor — the risk section.** Carry **M-3** (the settlement recovers the contingency, not the
  reservation — this corrects what `pass14-disposition` §3 implies), **M-8** (the freeze is permanent in the
  success case) and **m-8** as one line (between a settlement by operation of law and the Board's
  recognition of it, nothing authorises withholding her allowance). **Do not carry S-1, S-3, S-4, S-5, M-1,
  M-4 to M-7, M-9, M-10, m-1, m-3, m-4 or m-5 as live defects** — all closed in the text. **Do not concede an
  art. X, § 7 defect:** pass 15 concedes none and frames the only constitutional exposure as art. X, § 11's
  actuarial-methods clause, quoted verbatim from source. **And carry the ground of the m-5 bar**, supplied by
  [MOO-136](/MOO/issues/MOO-136) §2.7, approved by the Policy Director and reproduced without restyling the citations
  (also at §6.5 of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8)):

  > No exclusion in the Virginia Freedom of Information Act applies to a member-identifying record in the
  > notice required by subdivision G 4. The exclusions for information held by the Virginia Retirement System
  > (§ 2.2-3705.7 (12) and (24)) reach only information held by the Board acting as investment trustee under
  > § 51.1-124.30. The personnel-information exclusion (§ 2.2-3705.1 (1)) is available to a custodian at its
  > discretion and does not bind either the Board or a committee of the General Assembly. The bar in
  > subdivision G 4 is accordingly the operative protection.

  **The comparator, if it helps:** § 30-80 C gives VRS records *"provided to the Commission"* (JLARC) a
  **mandatory** FOIA exemption — *"shall be exempted"* — and § 30-79 B of the same chapter **names** the
  House Committee on Appropriations and the Senate Committee on Finance and Appropriations without extending
  that shield to them. **This corroborates pass 11's finding that there is no privacy or FOIA bar on the G 4
  notice.** No bill text changes.
- **Stakeholder Analyst** — **M-8**, the wait-listed applicant whose exposure becomes permanent in the
  success case; and **m-5**, the separating member's own agency as a named party in a transmittal to the
  money committees.

**MOO-42 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · companion record to store revision 50 of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), document revision 57 (`012d478d`), 523,402 characters. INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT. Pre-decisional and internal. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill, not reviewed by counsel, not reviewed by DLS, not legally sufficient for introduction. Passes 4 to 16 are our own adversarial reviews and are expressly not legal advice; counsel has not cleared this proposal and nothing here states or implies that it has. Nothing is cleared for external use, and saving a file is not sending it.**

Written as its own document from the start, because `bill-text-s8` arrived at store revision 50 with **1,866 characters** of headroom against the document store's 524,288-character ceiling.

## 1. What landed, and what did not

It answered all eight of my questions.

## 3. The findings, finding by finding

### R-5 (serious, E12) — drafted out, and the defect was mine

E12 was my edit in store revision 47, written to close pass 15's M-6. It re-keyed subdivision G 4's two clause-(iii) deeming limbs from *"the statement required by"* the definition of *"final qualifying retirement date"* to *"a statement **or notice**"* required by it. **The definition requires four such things and three of them are contingent on a member's act**, including the notice of the Board's determination upon a request that the definition requires *"no later than 30 days after the request is filed."*

Pass 16's scenario, which I have not been able to break: a member with four years of subsidised credit and no intention of retiring files one request; she need give no reason because the section demands none; the Board misses its 30 days; her tolling ends at subsection M 2's 120-day cap; her date passes *"at a time when the Board has not given such a statement or notice and the time allowed by that definition for giving it has expired"*; the second deeming limb fires on its own words; subdivisions 2 and 3 are switched off; her credit vests at the subsidised cost; and the clause-(iii) settlement limb settles the whole certified subsidy, which subsection N turns into a payment by the Commonwealth. **Before E12 the limb was keyed to the initial statement, which the Board gave on time years earlier. The path did not exist until I widened the words.**

**Edit 1 excludes that one notice and nothing else.** The other two request-contingent duties are safe without being excluded, and I checked each: the notice of a later **approved** date arises from an approval, so the Board cannot be in default of it unless it has approved a later date, in which case her date is later and she gains; and the fallback date-notice runs *"no later than 15 days after it acts upon the request,"* so the time for giving it never starts if the Board never acts. **A guard cannot expire on a duty that has not arisen**, which is the reviewer's own §5 null result, and it is why only the 30-day reasons-notice needed excluding.

**Edit 2 is the remedy that replaces the one taken away**, because the member who genuinely needs an answer must not be left with nothing. Pass 16's fix direction was to leave her to subdivision D 1, the definition and subsection M — and I checked those, and **D 1's day-for-day extension is keyed to the Board *giving* the statement or notice late, so it does not fire where the Board never gives it at all**, and the definition's own tolling-rescue sentence is keyed to the month *"in which the Board last acts."* Both require a Board act. So edit 2 gives her a floor keyed to the **expiry of a fixed period** instead, which is the lesson I have had to learn twice: a limb that depends on a Board act with no cap is the defect, not the cure. It is confined to a request *"the filing of which tolled"* a period under subsection M, and M 2 tolls only the first such request, so it cannot be repeated.

### R-1 (serious, E6 with E7) — drafted out

E6 widened the involuntary-separation extension trigger from *"facts from which it is required by this subdivision to determine that an involuntary separation occurred"* to *"otherwise learned of the involuntary separation,"* while the extension **date** remained a pure function of the separation date and the Board's knowledge remained only a condition in the proviso. So the later the Board learns, the further in the past the date it must hand her: separation 1 March, ninetieth day 30 May, first day of the next month 1 June; the agency never files the notice the bill requires of it; the Board learns 1 December; **her final qualifying retirement date "is that first day" — six months gone.**

I traced every candidate rescue and none reaches her. The definition's second-month floor is keyed to *"the statement required by this definition"* — the initial statement, long since given. The rescission limb's formula applies only where a subdivision 2 determination is being rescinded, and none was made. And **the clause-(iii) deeming limbs do not reach her either**, even as widened by E12, because the G 4 extension date is not a date the definition requires to be stated. So she fell to subdivision 2: her purchased credit reduced to what her payments bought at standard cost, her money refunded, and the Board's own 60-day clock expired before it learned.

**Edit 3 gives the extension limb the floor the rescission limb already has, and does one thing more.** The 90-day vesting condition in the same subdivision had equally expired — pass 14's corrected *"61 usable days and not 90"* can be **zero** or negative here — so the edit provides expressly that her retirement on or before the floor date satisfies it. Without that second limb she would have a usable date and still lose the vesting branch.

**The occupancy consequence, disclosed.** The floor depends on when the Board learns, which can be long after the separation, so a reservation can stay charged against the $3,000,000 for that period. **I enacted it anyway**, for three reasons: the member can compel the date herself, because the same subdivision lets her *"file with the Board written evidence of an involuntary separation"* and obliges the Board to determine within 30 days; without the floor **even the diligent member who files that evidence late gets a past date**, since her own filing is a date on which the Board "otherwise learns"; and the alternative is that she loses purchased credit through her employer's default and the Board's lateness, which is the one outcome every directive on this issue forbids. It adds no new **category** of unbounded occupancy — the rescission limb already has one, and that is §7 item 85.

### R-2 (serious, E9) — drafted out on the reviewer's second option, not its first

E9 cured pass 15's M-5 by re-pointing the clause-(iii) redetermination clock to *"the date on which the Board determines that clause (iii) of this subdivision applies."* Pass 16 counted that phrase — one occurrence, E9's own — and then searched for any provision obliging the Board to make that determination or fixing a time for it. **There is none.** So the amount settled was never fixed, subsection N's duty to pay *"the amount settled"* had no amount, and subdivision D 2's second sentence kept the reservation charged against the $3,000,000 while the figure that would release the excess was never determined.

**Pass 16 offered two fixes and I took the second.** Its first was to key the period to the settlement event. **That re-creates M-5 exactly.** M-5's complaint was that the clock could begin before the Board could know the duty existed; the settlement date in this limb is the date her final qualifying retirement date passed, which is precisely the date the Board may not yet know about. The reviewer's reason for preferring the first option — *"E9's problem was that the clock preceded the Board's knowledge, not that it ran from a date"* — is, read against M-5 itself, the reason not to take it.

**Edit 4 supplies the duty**: a 60-day deadline measured from a date that always exists, a reasons-notice in 15 days, a subsection J report line, express subsection M review, **and a fallback clock that runs from the expiry of the 60 days if the Board never acts** — so the new duty cannot itself become a limb that depends on a Board act with no cap.

### R-3 (serious, E3) — the first half drafted out; the second half is §7 item 93

In subsection M 2 the capped thing is the **member's** tolling and the excluded thing is the **Board's** overrun, so the exclusion clause means *the Board's lateness shall not eat her allowance.* It works because the capped party and the delaying party are different people. E3 lifted it verbatim into subdivision G 4, where the capped thing is the Board's **own** periods — and the two parties became the same, so the clause split:

- **Reading A** — the overrun is not counted toward the 120 days but the Board's clocks stay stopped throughout it, so **the Board buys itself unlimited time on its own clocks by being late on her request.** The cap caps nothing.
- **Reading B** — the overrun is excluded from the non-running, so the Board's clocks run during its own overrun, and **a subdivision 2 determination may cut her credit while her reconsideration is unanswered.**

**Edit 5 states directly what the cap is for**, so neither reading survives, and the same words remove R-8's stranded referent. **The second half — the member whose reconsideration succeeds after the determination has taken effect, for whom subdivision G 4 has no rescission limb — is §7 item 93**, raised independently by MOO-120's pass 12 as its S-4 with candidate text drafted and a recommendation to enact. Two reviewers reaching the same gap from different directions is the strongest argument for enacting it; two divergent repairs in front of the Director would be worse than one, so I drafted none.

### R-4 (serious, E5) — the impossible command removed; the bound is §7 item 100

E5's exception was conditioned on the Board **giving** the notice late. Where the Board **never gives** it, the condition failed, the unqualified 120-day outer limit stood, and subdivision G 2's third sentence forbade the determination from taking effect before notice: **two mandatory commands in direct conflict, with no way to obey both.** Edit 6 makes the limit yield in both the late-notice and the absent-notice case, and carries the §3 referent tightening in the same words.

**What edit 6 does not do, and I am not claiming otherwise.** It does not give the absent-notice determination an effective date, so it does not bound the withholding of her allowance — which subsection F expressly blesses as not a collection, offset or withholding. In the late-notice case the position is coherent and still unbounded, where before E5 the 120-day limit was a bound even though it was unsatisfiable. **Bounding it is a money provision and it is §7 item 100**, with three options drafted at §7 below. **Edit 16 is the half I could take now**: a failure to give that notice within the period allowed is a line in the subsection J report, so it is visible rather than silent, on the model the Director's own store revision 44 put into subsection C.

### R-6 (moderate, E1) — drafted out, and it is the evidence for §7 item 84

Two provisions take their date from the settlement **event**, which store revision 47's bar can negate: the death-and-disability rescission limb's reinstatement duty, whose **only** deadline was *"no later than the date on which the certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision"*; and the recertification-before-redetermination sequencing duty. **Edits 14 and 15 give both of them data that do not depend on a settlement occurring**, so option (a) at §7 item 84 no longer carries the defect and the Director's choice there is now purely structural. Pass 16 grades R-6 moderate on severity and calls it *"the most decision-relevant finding in this pass"*, and says expressly that the bar does **not** strand the death benefit: the rescission, the restoration of credit, the crediting of service and the death benefit are independent duties and all survive.

## 5. Cross-reference sweep — performed, in both directions, on all sixteen edits

**Result: no conforming amendment is required outside the sixteen edits and none is made.** No section joins or leaves the act, no designator is renumbered, and the title line is unchanged. Nine checks, with the three that could have failed in the file at §5.30.

1. **One insertion would have stranded four live references and was re-cast because of it.** The R-13 rule was first drafted as a **new sentence** immediately after the definition's 12-month bound. That would have displaced the **three** *"the preceding sentence"* references in the tolling-rescue sentence and the *"the two preceding sentences"* reference in the floor sentence, all of which point at the bound. **It is enacted as a proviso inside the bound sentence instead, so no sentence count in the definition changes.** Verified after the edit: *"Notwithstanding the two preceding sentences"* occurs once in the bill text, and the tolling-rescue sentence is byte-identical to its pre-edit form.
2. **Every other insertion was checked for the same failure.** The edit 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 insertions each sit immediately after the sentence they refer to, and the sentence following each contains no ordinal reference. Edit 3's effect on *"If the member does not **so** retire"* was checked specifically: the new sentence provides expressly that retirement on or before the floor date satisfies the 90-day condition, so *"so retire"* reads consistently.
3. **The referent edit 6 names is unique on the face.** *"no less than 30 days"* occurs twice in the bill text — subdivision G 2's notice sentence, which is the referent, and the referent phrase itself. The rival candidate pass 16 identified, store revision 47's own E5 sentence, **does not require** notice no less than 30 days before effect, so it cannot be read as the referent and the circularity pass 16 warned of cannot arise.
4. **Nothing is stranded.** *"90 days allowed by subsection M"* — 0 occurrences. *"the following sentence"* — 0. *"identity of that agency"* — 0. *"settlement the Board so makes"* — 0. *"in no event later than 12 months after the date of the involuntary separation"* — 0.
5. **Subsection M 2's own words are untouched.** *"the 90 days allowed by this subsection"* occurs once, in M 2, and was not re-opened; pass 16 notes the same latent mismatch exists there and routes it as an addendum to §7 item 72 rather than re-opening it, and so do I.
6. **The agency-default information is not lost by edit 9.** Subdivision G 4's duty to *"state every failure of a state agency to give that notice of which the Board becomes aware in the report required by subsection J"* is present and untouched.
7. **Enactment 3 clause (i) is self-consistent after edits 12 and 13**, and the subsection N accounting limb that clause (iii)'s subsection J duties consume is now preserved with them.
8. **The deleted cap leaves nothing pointing at it.** The sentence that follows the rescission limb runs from *"the date on which the member is so approved or dies"* and is unaffected.
9. **No figure moved.** In §1: `$3,000,000` once, `$170,000` twice, `[20]` once, *"July 1, 2029"* three times, *"July 1, 2033"* once — all identical to store revision 49. *"12 months"* falls from nine to eight, which is the expected arithmetic of edit 11 deleting two occurrences and edit 10 adding one.

## 7. §7 item 100 — the three drafted options

**None is enacted.** Each is one insertion into subdivision G 2.

**(a) A backstop effective date.**

> Notwithstanding any other provision of this subdivision, a determination under this subdivision takes effect no later than 180 days after the determination date whether or not the Board has given the notice required by this subdivision, and the Board shall give that notice no later than the date on which the determination takes effect.

*Cures the withholding completely. Takes away the notice-before-effect protection pass 4 required, in the one case where the Board is already in default.*

**(b) Pay the allowance, subject to later adjustment — pass 16's own suggestion, and my recommendation.**

> Where a determination under this subdivision has not taken effect within 180 days after the determination date, the Board shall pay the member's retirement allowance, computed on the service credit credited to the member under the election, notwithstanding that the determination has not taken effect; and where the determination thereafter takes effect the Board shall adjust the allowance prospectively to the amount payable on the service credit retained under clause (i) of this subdivision, shall give the member written notice of the adjustment and of the reasons for it, and shall not collect, offset, or withhold any amount paid to the member before the adjustment.

*Keeps her protection and ends the withholding. Its cost is that the trust pays an allowance that may later be reduced; the no-collection words are what keep it inside subsection F and the no-clawback directive.*

**(c) Statutory interest on the arrears.**

> Where the first payment of a retirement allowance includes an amount under this subdivision that would have been payable from the effective date of retirement, the Board shall pay interest on that amount at the rate stated in subdivision B 4 a of § 51.1-142.2 from the date on which it would have been payable.

*Answers the funding point and not the withholding. It charges the trust for the Board's lateness, which is a money provision no cited document directs.*

## 8. What this revision does not fix, and who owns it

- **§7 item 89 is still a FATAL finding, carded to the Director and enacted nowhere**, as are items 90 to 99 from store revision 49. Nothing in pass 16 or in store revision 50 touches them.
- **The sixteen changed places have had no adversarial pass of their own.** [MOO-140](/MOO/issues/MOO-140) is the bounded pass 17.
- **The Director's list runs to item 100** and I resolved nothing on it by drafting. Items 84, 85, 93 and 73 are annotated with pass 16's evidence; item 100 is new.
- **No figure is derived or moved anywhere in this revision**, and pass 16 examined none. Two occupancy mechanisms are recorded for [MOO-134](/MOO/issues/MOO-134) if useful — R-11's clause-(ii) extension chain and R-12's E5/E13 compounding — with **direction indeterminate on the text; the reviewer asserts none and neither do I.** Two further occupancy effects are this revision's own and are disclosed: edit 3's floor and edit 10's exclusion both lengthen the period a reservation may stay charged, each reversible in one sentence.
- **Pass 16 concedes no Va. Const. art. X, § 7 defect** — subsection N's duty is expressly *"from an appropriation made for that purpose"* and so is self-limiting, and subsection K preserves accepted elections without creating a payment duty. **No document of ours may concede one.**
- **Two parties bearing a real cost who are not on the stakeholder map**, on pass 16's routing to the Stakeholder Analyst: the involuntarily separated member whose agency never filed, and the small agency identified by name in a transmittal to the money committees. Edit 3 answers the first in the text and edit 9 answers the second; both remain unmapped.
