# Revision 22 — the full record

**Internal working draft material. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel. Pre-decisional.**

This document carries the complete record for store revision 22 of [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8). It is split out because `bill-text-s8` reached the platform's 524,288-character document ceiling. **The bill text itself is in `bill-text-s8` and nowhere else. Nothing in this document is operative text.** `bill-text-s8` carries a short pointer to each part below, at §0.0000000000000000, §5.11, §6.0-21, §7 items 27 to 30, and §8.

**Document key note:** this document's key is `rev21-record`, which is a misnomer — it was created before the canonical write landed and the store assigned revision **22**. The key is left as it is because `bill-text-s8` links to it; the content throughout refers to **revision 22**.

---

## Revision 22 — the four MOO-65 answers completed, and the MOO-82 review dispositioned

**Internal working draft. Not a Division of Legislative Services bill. Not reviewed by counsel.
Pre-decisional.**

The Director answered the four [MOO-65](/MOO/issues/MOO-65) repairs on 12 October 2026: **F-1
Candidate B**, **F-2 both repairs**, **F-4 the long form**, **F-8 enact**. The four answers are now
fully enacted, across two revisions by two runs:

- **Store revision 21, written by a concurrent run of this agent, enacted F-2** — both the earlier
  determination trigger and the make-whole first payment — in subdivision G 2, in its own wording.
- **Store revision 22, this one, enacts the other three**: **F-1** in both definitions in subsection
  A, **F-8** in subdivision D 1, and **F-4** in subdivision G 4's death-deeming. It also **repairs
  three defects [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) found in the enacted text**, one of which (m-1) is a
  repair to revision 21's F-2(b) sentence rather than to anything I wrote.

**Five edits in four provisions. No other section moves and the bill title does not grow.**

### a. Two corrections to my own record, before anything else

**1. This is revision 22.** My comment on [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) at 00:50 called this work
"revision 18" and reported that the canonical write had failed with a 409. Both halves need
correcting. Under the rule this document's parent adopted at §0.00000000000b — *the revision number is
the document-store revision number, and nothing else* — the number is assigned by the write, not by
the drafter. While [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) sat on the Director's card, a concurrent run of this
same agent wrote store revisions 18 through 21 (pass 5 and the S6 review, then
[MOO-79](/MOO/issues/MOO-79)'s four residuals, then F-2). **Store revisions 18 to 21 are therefore
theirs, and mine is 22.** The body parked on [MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) as `bill-text-s8-rev18` is
superseded by this record and **must not be pasted over `bill-text-s8`** — it was built on store
revision 17 and would silently revert four revisions of other work.

**2. The six edits I planned became five, because a concurrent revision had enacted two of them.**
Revisions 18 to 21 changed §1 in twenty or so places, four of them inside provisions this revision
also touches. Re-reading §1 before writing, rather than trusting the patch I had parked, is what
caught this:

- **G 2 — F-2(a) and F-2(b) were already enacted** by store revision 21, in wording equivalent to the
  text I had drafted (*"the earlier of the member's final qualifying retirement date **and** the date
  on which the member retires in a retirement that is not a qualifying retirement"*, against my *"the
  earlier of (a) … or (b) …"*). **I left their wording and did not re-enact mine.** Two drafters
  enacting the same approved repair in different words is how a section acquires an inconsistency for
  nothing. **What I did add to G 2 is m-1 only** — their F-2(b) sentence carries the *"before that
  date"* ambiguity verbatim, and §c explains the repair.
- **D 1 — a different, narrower interim repair to the F-8 defect was already in**, reading *"stating
  an effective date of retirement that is **the effective date of** a qualifying retirement."* That
  cures the category error — a date is not a retirement — by a different route than the text the
  Director approved. **The approved text is enacted and the interim wording is superseded**, because
  the approved text does a second job as well: it states the member's duty as a prediction about her
  own future retirement, which is what subsection F actually requires of her, and
  [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) §6 tested and cleared that predictive duty expressly. Either wording
  would have been defensible; nothing else turns on the difference.
- **G 4 — a sentence had been inserted immediately after the death-deeming sentence**
  (*"Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, where the member dies before completing payment …"*), so
  the F-4 anchor no longer matched. Re-anchored on the following sentence; **the F-4 clause still
  attaches to the death-deeming sentence and to nothing else**, which is what the long form was for.

Every one of the five edits was applied by single-occurrence assertion rather than by hand, and §1 was
diffed afterwards: the only paragraphs that differ from store revision 21 are the two definitions,
D 1, G 2 and G 4.

### b. The redline, all five edits

**1. § 51.1-142.4 A, "qualifying retirement" — F-1 Candidate B, plus the S-1 scope repeat and the M-2
reorder.** Reproduced in full because three edits land in one sentence:

> *"Qualifying retirement" means a service retirement under § 51.1-153* ~~the allowance for which is
> calculated in accordance with subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155 and is not reduced under subdivision A 2
> or A 3 of that section,~~ *with an effective date of retirement that is the first day of a month, is
> no earlier than the member's earliest qualifying retirement date, and is no later than the member's
> final qualifying retirement date,* <u>the allowance for which retirement is calculated in accordance
> with subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155 and is not reduced under subdivision A 2 or A 3 of that section,
> in each case determined as though no option had been elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 and
> no lump-sum distribution had been paid under § 51.1-165.01</u>*.*

**2. § 51.1-142.4 A, "unreduced retirement eligibility date" — F-1 Candidate B, plus the S-1 scope
repeat.** The operative limbs are word-identical to the limbs in edit 1, from *"is calculated"* to the
end, which is what [MOO-62](/MOO/issues/MOO-62) required:

> *… and receive a service retirement allowance that is calculated in accordance with subdivision A 1
> of § 51.1-155 and is not reduced under subdivision A 2 or A 3 of that section*<u>, in each case
> determined as though no option had been elected under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01 and no lump-sum
> distribution had been paid under § 51.1-165.01</u>*.*

**3. Subdivision D 1, last sentence — F-8 as approved, superseding the interim wording.**

> *The member shall file the notice of retirement required by § 51.1-153,* ~~stating an effective date
> of retirement that is the effective date of a qualifying retirement~~ <u>stating as the effective
> date of retirement a date on which the member will retire in a qualifying retirement</u>*, no later
> than the later of …*

**4. Subdivision G 2, fourth sentence — m-1 only.** The sentence itself is revision 21's F-2(b):

> *… the first payment of the retirement allowance shall include every amount that would have been
> payable to the member from the effective date of retirement had the determination been made before*
> ~~that date~~ <u>the effective date of retirement</u>*.*

**5. Subdivision G 4, second sentence — F-4 long form.**

> *… as though the member had retired in a qualifying retirement on the date of death*<u>, and for that
> purpose the requirements of the definition of "qualifying retirement" in subsection A that the
> effective date of retirement be the first day of a month and fall no earlier than the member's
> earliest qualifying retirement date and no later than the member's final qualifying retirement date
> shall not apply</u>*.*

**S-1 and M-2 have no separate location** — S-1 is inside edits 1 and 2 and M-2 is inside edit 1. They
are counted as repairs rather than as edits because each is a change the Director did not pre-approve,
and §c states the ground for each.

### c. Three repairs I enacted that the Director did not pre-approve, and why each is drafting and not policy

The commission said *"no other section moves."* None of these moves another section; all three are
repairs to words this revision was enacting anyway, and none changes which member passes either test.
I am naming them rather than letting them ride inside an approved edit.

**S-1 — the trailing section list attached to only one of the two counterfactuals. Serious. Enacted.**
Candidate B, as the Director approved it and as I drafted it at 00:50, read *"as though no option had
been elected and no lump-sum distribution had been paid under § 51.1-165 or § 51.1-165.01."* On the
doctrine of the last antecedent (*Alger v. Commonwealth*, 267 Va. 255, 259 (2004)) the two sections
qualify only the nearer limb, leaving *"no option had been elected"* **unbounded as to section** — a
disregard of unknown width inside the provision that decides whether a member keeps credit she bought
with her own money. Worse, the reviewer found that a careful reader is *pushed* to that reading:
§ 51.1-165 contains **no lump-sum distribution at all** — its only payment forms are the A 1 straight
life, A 2 joint and last-survivor and A 3 level income options and the B 50/10 option — so my intended
distributive reading made *"lump-sum distribution … under § 51.1-165"* a null reference, and the
presumption against meaningless words (*Jones v. Conwell*, 227 Va. 176, 181 (1984)) favours the reading
that avoids it. Enacted as the reviewer drafted it: the sections are repeated on each limb, bounded to
what each section actually contains. **The null reference is retired.** This expresses the policy the
Director chose — a disregard of payment-form choices under those two sections — rather than changing
it, which is why I treated it as drafting.

**M-2 — the insert interposed a modifier between the allowance limbs and the date requirements.
Moderate. Enacted.** Candidate B's words sat between *"not reduced under subdivision A 2 or A 3"* and
*"with an effective date of retirement that is the first day of a month …"*, so the nearest antecedent
of that *"with"* phrase became the **hypothetical** no-option retirement rather than the actual one —
on which reading the three date requirements are trivially satisfied and the final-qualifying-
retirement-date cap drops off the actual retirement. That cap is load-bearing for pricing. Repaired by
**reordering the definition rather than by adding a word**: the date requirements now sit immediately
after *"a service retirement under § 51.1-153"*, where they belong, and the allowance limbs and their
counterfactual sit last, with nothing after them for *"in each case"* to reach. The relative pronoun is
given an express antecedent — *"the allowance for which **retirement** is calculated"* — so the
reorder does not create the mirror defect. **No requirement is added, removed or altered; the sentence
says what it said in a different order.**

**m-1 — "that date" had two candidate antecedents. Minor. Enacted, on another run's sentence.**
F-2(b), as enacted by store revision 21, reads *"… had the determination been made before that date,"* where *"that date"* could be the effective date
of retirement (intended) or the date the determination takes effect (on which reading the sentence is
circular and pays the member nothing). Replaced with *"the effective date of retirement"* in terms. It
is repetitive and it is unambiguous; in a make-whole payment provision I will take the repetition.

### d. Two things I found in the surrounding text that the review did not have, and they cut in opposite directions

I scoped [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) to the six provisions reproduced in the issue description, and the
reviewer said in terms that they had not seen the rest of G 3 and G 4 or the definitions of *"earliest
qualifying retirement date"* and *"final qualifying retirement date."* That scoping was my choice and it
cost accuracy in both directions.

**S-2 is substantially cured by a sentence already in D 1, and the reviewer did not have it.** The
finding is that clause (ii) of D 1 lets the member file up to 30 days after a late Board statement with
no outer bound, while the same sentence preserves *"the limitation in subsection E of § 51.1-153"* — a
hard bar on an effective date more than 90 days before filing — so a five-month Board delay could push
her effective date past her final qualifying retirement date and fail the definition. **The citation is
right and the mechanism is real.** But D 1's **last** sentence already provides that where the Board
gives the statement late, *"the member's final qualifying retirement date is extended by the number of
days by which the statement is late, [and] the member may state an effective date of retirement that is
no earlier than the first day of the month following the month in which the Board gives the
statement."* Run the reviewer's own facts through it: a statement 533 days late extends the outer date
by 533 days and lets her name a **prospective** effective date in the month after the statement, on
which § 51.1-153 E is never engaged, and the extended window still contains it. **The extension is
automatic on lateness, so I could not construct a case where a late statement alone defeats the
definition.** What survives is narrower: the member who *chooses* to backdate under clause (ii) instead
of taking the extension can still meet the 90-day bar, and nothing in D 1 tells her that the extension
is the safer route. That is a notice point and it is cheap to fix. **Item 27** carries it with the three
candidate texts; I have not enacted any of them, because each either disapplies a Chapter 1 limitation
or adds a deeming provision to G 4.

**S-3 is worse than the review states, and the aggravating sentence is also in text the reviewer did
not have.** The finding is that F-2(a)'s clause (b) starts the G 2 clock at the member's actual
retirement, so the Board can be commanded to cut back and refund before a pending disability
retirement is approved, and G 4 contains no unwind. Confirmed, and there is a second sentence in G 4
that makes it bite harder: ***"No certified subsidy is settled under this subdivision after the
reservation for the election has been released or after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has
taken effect."*** So once the G 2 determination takes effect, G 4 settlement is **affirmatively
barred**. On approval of the disability retirement, G 4's opening words say subdivisions 2 and 3
*"shall not apply"* — which argues her service credit revives — while that later sentence says the
subsidy can no longer settle. **The member's credit and the money that pays for it come apart.** This
needs two clauses and they are new provisions, so it is **item 28** and not enacted.

### e. Disposition of all twelve revision-18 findings and the two new ones

| Finding | Severity | Disposition in revision 22 |
|---|---|---|
| **S-1** scope of the trailing section list | serious | **ENACTED** — edits 1 and 2. §c. |
| **S-2** § 51.1-153 E's 90-day cap vs clause (ii) | serious | **NOT ENACTED — item 27.** Substantially cured by D 1's existing extension sentence; residual is a notice point. §d. |
| **S-3** disability race, G 4 has no unwind | serious | **NOT ENACTED — item 28.** Confirmed and aggravated. Two new clauses. §d. |
| **M-1** G 2(b) vs G 4's involuntary-separation deadline | moderate | **NOT ENACTED — item 29.** Reviewer says enact; I agree; it adds a trigger to a deadline the Director set on [MOO-44](/MOO/issues/MOO-44). |
| **M-2** insert interposed between limbs and date requirements | moderate | **ENACTED** — edit 1, by reorder. §c. |
| **M-3** insert is surplusage, and § 51.1-165.01 B keys to the same concept | moderate | **NO TEXT NEEDED — answered on the record.** Subsection A opens *"**As used in this section**:"*, so the definition cannot govern § 51.1-165.01 B's PLOP tiers and the circularity the reviewer describes cannot arise. The reviewer's fix direction — *"for purposes of this section"* — is already in the section's own preamble. Recorded in §5.11. |
| **m-1** *"that date"* ambiguous | minor | **ENACTED** — edit 4, on revision 21's F-2(b) sentence. §c. |
| **m-2** catch-up carries no interest; ~90-day zero-allowance window | minor | **RECORD AND MEMO.** Not a defect in the repair; a residual of G 2's structure. Routed to Editor for the memo's risk section. |
| **m-3** § 51.1-168 B / I.R.C. § 415(b) escapes the disregard | minor | **CONSIDERED, NO TEXT.** A § 415(b) cap is neither an option elected nor a distribution paid, so the insert does not reach it. Population is negligible at VRS multipliers; adding a third counterfactual would cost more clarity than it buys. Recorded in §5.11. |
| **m-4** `vrs_erf.py` rule-of-90 and 60/5 eligibility cites | minor | **NOT MINE.** Model code. Routed to Fiscal & Impact Modeler and Statutory Researcher. No bill text implicated. |
| **N-1** § 51.1-155.1 retirements may not be *"under § 51.1-153"* | moderate, new | **NOT ENACTED — item 30.** One cross-reference settles it, in whichever direction the Director chooses. Same question as F-7, already with Statutory Researcher. |
| **N-2** § 51.1-155.1 B is computed under A 2 with the reduction waived, not under A 1 | minor, new | **NOT ENACTED — item 30**, with N-1. The B member is economically identical to the A and C members and fails the positive limb; if the gateway opens it should open for her or the record should say why not. |

**Three of the reviewer's six answers confirmed my reasoning with authority** — the § 51.1-165 D and E
revocation case, the 50/10 test case (§ 51.1-155 A 5 read with § 51.1-165 B), and the F-2(b)
retroactivity question, which they could not break. **Two of my answers were wrong in a way that needs
text**: Q4 should be enacted, and Q5 is not harmless. On Q2 I was right about the risk I named and
wrong about the one I did not.

**And the review confirmed one thing worth keeping in view:** my decision to drop the noun *"election"*
from Candidate B — because subsection A defines *"Election"* as the qualifying military service
election — turns out to be load-bearing rather than merely tidy. § 51.1-165.01 calls the partial
lump sum an *"option"* throughout (B 1, C, F), so *"no option had been elected … under § 51.1-165.01"*
reaches the PLOP **election**, which is the event that reduces the allowance under § 51.1-165.01 C. The
distribution itself is not paid until the first monthly annuity payment under § 51.1-165.01 D — that
is, typically **after** the settlement test runs. Had the option limb not reached § 51.1-165.01, the
payment limb would have been trivially satisfied at the test date and F-1 would have failed for every
PLOP member. It is the limb I was least relying on that does the work.

### f. What revision 22 does not do

- **It does not enact S-2, S-3, M-1, N-1 or N-2.** All five are drafted in §7 items 27 to 30 and none
  is in the bill. Four of the five would add a provision or move a section outside the commission; the
  fifth (S-2) turns on a choice among three fixes that is the Director's.
- **It does not revisit anything [MOO-62](/MOO/issues/MOO-62) closed.** Both limbs stay, there is no
  *"solely"*, there is no tier test, the zero-reduction member still passes, and Option 2 stays
  declined. [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) attacked all of these and could re-open none of them.
- **It does not change the word-identity of the two tests' operative limbs.** Edits 1 and 2 keep them
  identical from *"is calculated"* to the end, which is the instruction. What the review correctly
  killed is my *argument* that word-identity is what prevents the two tests selecting different
  cohorts — it is not, because one test is modal and the other actual. §5.11 states the narrower claim
  that survives.
- **It does not touch the record of revisions 18 to 21.** Those are a concurrent run's work on
  [MOO-79](/MOO/issues/MOO-79) and pass 5, and nothing in this revision reverts any part of them except
  the single interim D 1 wording that the Director's answer supersedes (§a).

### g. No priced quantity moves

Every figure in the package prices the admitted cohort — the unreduced subdivision A 1 cohort reached
through § 51.1-153 A, B 2 or B 3 — **as settling**. The F-1 defect, left standing, would have made
actual experience *cheaper* than priced, by refusing settlement to admitted members who elected a
survivor option or a partial lump sum and releasing their reservations. The S-1 and M-2 repairs move
the text further toward the basis already modelled; they do not move the basis. Edits 3 and 5, and m-1,
touch the timing and form of determinations that the trust and the appropriation already carry.
**Nothing in §3, `model-s8-s9` or the [MOO-53](/MOO/issues/MOO-53) reprice needs re-running on account
of revision 22.**

The one thing the review found that **the file cannot answer** is not a defect in revision 22 and is
not mine to close: **no published artifact reports the share of the S8 population that retires at an
A 1-unreduced door**, which is the quantity that decides whether subsection G 2 is an exception path or
the main one. Four of the six changes the two revisions made are in G. Routed to Fiscal & Impact Modeler with the
reviewer's two asks. Until it is reported, the claim that G 2 is an exception path is an assumption in
this document rather than a finding.

---

## 5.11 Cross-reference check — revision 22

### 5.11 Revision 22 — the five edits, the two new citations, and the claim that survives

**Performed on the text as written, after the re-anchoring described in §0.0000000000000000a.**

**Two citations are new to this document, and both were retrieved verbatim from
`law.lis.virginia.gov` and read in full (11 and 12 October 2026), then independently re-verified by
[MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82).**

| Citation | What it provides | Why the insert names it |
|---|---|---|
| **§ 51.1-165** | Optional benefits. A 1 straight life; A 2 joint and last-survivor; A 3 level income; B the 50/10 joint and last-survivor option. A and B pay *"the actuarial equivalent of the retirement allowance otherwise payable to him."* D permits revocation; E fixes what is payable on the contingent annuitant's death. | The **option** limb. **§ 51.1-165 contains no lump-sum distribution** — confirmed against the full section — which is why the counterfactual does not pair it with the distribution limb. |
| **§ 51.1-165.01** | Partial lump-sum distribution. B 1–3 set the 12/24/36-month tiers; C sets the options and provides that *"the monthly amount of the service retirement allowance otherwise payable … shall be **reduced on an actuarially equivalent basis** to reflect the payment of such lump-sum distribution"*; D fixes payment at the first monthly annuity payment; F addresses the election. | **Both** limbs. The section calls the PLOP an *"option"* (B 1, C, F) and also pays a distribution, so both counterfactuals have work to do under it. |

**Correction to §5.9's account of these two sections, carried here so the error does not survive in the
record.** §5.9 and my revision 8 comment both said that §§ 51.1-165 **and** 51.1-165.01 pay *"the
actuarial equivalent of the retirement allowance otherwise payable."* That is verbatim correct for
§ 51.1-165 A and B and **wrong for § 51.1-165.01**, which instead reduces the allowance on an
actuarially equivalent basis under subsection C. The finding is unaffected — if anything the lump-sum
case is the stronger of the two, because that allowance is literally reduced — and it is the second
reason the counterfactual had to be governed by *"in each case"* rather than attached to the
calculation limb alone.

**A third section was considered and is deliberately not cited: § 51.1-168.** § 51.1-165.01 C requires
the computation to *"also reflect the provisions of subsection B of § 51.1-168,"* which is the
I.R.C. § 415(b) benefit cap. A § 415(b) reduction is neither an option elected nor a distribution paid,
so the counterfactual does not disregard it, and a capped allowance is arguably not
*"calculated in accordance with subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155."* The affected population is negligible
at VRS multipliers, and a third counterfactual would cost more clarity than the case is worth.
Recorded as considered rather than fixed ([MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) m-3).

**The five edits chased through every provision that consumes them.** Edits 4 and 5 in the table below are the G 2 trigger and fourth sentence, enacted by store revision 21 and chased here because revision 22's m-1 repair and F-4 clause interact with them.

| Edit | Provision | Consumers chased | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 | the two definitions in subsection A | all five uses of *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* (the definition of *"eligible member"* clauses (v), (vi) and (vii); subsection C clause (ii); subdivision G 3's last sentence; subsection E's last clause) and all sixteen occurrences of *"qualifying retirement"* (1 definitional + 15 uses: D 1, F ×3, G 1, G 2, G 4 ×2, I ×2, J ×3, K ×2) | **No conforming amendment required and none is made.** Every consumer takes the defined term whole; none restates either test, and none depends on the internal word order the M-2 reorder changed. |
| 1 | the M-2 reorder | the three date requirements, which subdivision G 4's new F-4 clause now disapplies **by description** | **Checked and consistent.** G 4's clause names the three requirements by their content (*"the first day of a month"*, *"no earlier than … earliest"*, *"no later than … final"*), not by position in the sentence, so the reorder does not strand it. |
| 3 | D 1's last sentence | § 51.1-153 (the notice duty), § 51.1-153 E (the retroactivity limitation), subsection F (which cures notice-invalidity), the *"final qualifying retirement date"* definition (which supplies the written statement and the lateness extension) | **No amendment made.** One interaction found and it is adverse — **item 27**, and §0.0000000000000000d explains why the lateness extension substantially answers it. |
| 4 | G 2's opening words | G 4's involuntary-separation sentence, which states its **own** 60-day deadline for the same determination | **One interaction found: two deadlines for one duty. Not cured here — item 29.** |
| 4 | G 2's opening words | G 4 clauses (i) and (ii), and G 4's bar on settlement *"after a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect"* | **One interaction found and it is serious — item 28.** The earlier trigger can fire the determination before a disability approval or a death that would have switched G 2 off, and the bar then prevents the subsidy settling. |
| 5 | G 2's fourth sentence | the retroactivity sentence in the *"qualifying retirement"* definition; subsection F's *"no other consequence shall attach"*; subsection M's review right | **Disjoint and consistent.** The definitional sentence reaches only a member whose retirement **is** a qualifying retirement; G 2 opens on the member who does not so retire. No member is inside both. Independently tested by [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) Q6, including the near-miss of the qualifying retiree whose subdivision 1 settlement is slow, and it holds: G 2's payment bar is keyed to *"the determination required by **this subdivision**,"* which exists only for the non-qualifying member. |
| 6 | G 4's death-deeming | the *"qualifying retirement"* definition's three date requirements, and the remaining G 4 sentences on partial payment and recertification | **No conforming amendment required.** The clause switches off the three date requirements and nothing else; the allowance limbs still apply, so the deemed retirement is still an A 1-unreduced one. |
| — | S-1, M-2, m-1 | — | Inside edits 1, 2 and the G 2 fourth sentence; chased with them. |

**M-3 disposed of by the section's own preamble, with no text.** The reviewer's concern is that
§ 51.1-165.01 B 1–3 set the PLOP tiers by reference to creditable service performed *"after the date he
was first eligible for an unreduced service retirement allowance"* — the same concept this bill
defines, now with a counterfactual attached — so a member could argue the bill's definition governs her
PLOP tier, which would be circular. **It cannot arise.** Subsection A opens ***"As used in this
section:"***, which confines every definition in it to § 51.1-142.4. § 51.1-165.01 B takes its date
from its own words and from Chapter 1, not from this section. **The scope limiter the reviewer asks for
is already there**, and adding *"for purposes of this section"* to one definition inside a subsection
already so limited would imply that the other fourteen definitions are not. No change made.

**The claim I withdraw, and the narrower one that survives.** §5.5 said the word-identity of the two
tests is what prevents the admission test and the settlement test selecting different cohorts.
**[MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) was right to break that and it is withdrawn.** The two tests are not the
same kind of test: *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* is **modal** (the earliest date the member
*may* retire and receive an A 1 allowance) and *"qualifying retirement"* is **actual** (the retirement
*"the allowance for which **is** calculated"* that way). Identical words can therefore select different
members, and word-identity hid that rather than preventing it — which is how the payment-form sections
went uncited through 263,000 characters of this document. **What survives is narrower and is a claim
about revision 22's text, not about its symmetry:** both tests now disregard the same two payment-form
choices in the same words, so a member who elects a § 51.1-165 option or a § 51.1-165.01 partial lump
sum is neither admitted by one test and refused by the other, nor the reverse. That is a result of the
counterfactual being in **both** definitions, not of the definitions resembling each other. In the
modal definition the counterfactual is declaratory — the earliest date on which a member *may* retire
was never movable by a payment-form election — and it is carried for the symmetry
[MOO-62](/MOO/issues/MOO-62) required. The reviewer tested the enacted insert for whether it **admits**
anybody the limbs exclude and, subject to S-1 which is now repaired, could construct no such route.

**Result: no conforming amendment is required outside the four provisions revision 22 touches, and none is made.** Three
interactions were found, all of them inside subsections D and G, and all three are open items (27, 28,
29) rather than silent repairs.


## 6.0-21 Drafter's note — revision 22

### 6.0-21 Ambiguities resolved in revision 22

**Four resolved by drafting choice, and five deliberately not resolved.**

1. **Whether to bound the option limb by section, or leave it unbounded.** Bounded. The Director chose
   a counterfactual naming two sections; a last-antecedent reading of the approved words would have
   bounded only the distribution limb and left the option limb unlimited. I read the choice of those
   two sections as the policy and the unbounded reading as a drafting accident, and repaired it by
   repeating the sections on each limb. **Had I read it the other way the fix would have been to delete
   the sections from both limbs, which would have been a policy change — so the direction of the repair
   was not free, and this is the ambiguity I resolved.** §0.0000000000000000c.

2. **Where to put the counterfactual, and what to do about the pronoun it stranded.** The insert sat
   between the allowance limbs and the date requirements, which gave the *"with an effective date"*
   phrase a hypothetical retirement as its nearest antecedent. I repaired it by **reordering** rather
   than by adding words, because every additive fix I drafted (parentheses, a second sentence, a
   *"in the case of the retirement actually taken"* tag) either put punctuation into a definition that
   has none or repeated the three date requirements. The reorder creates one new problem and I fixed it
   in the same edit: *"the allowance for which"* would otherwise reach across the date requirements for
   its antecedent, so it reads *"the allowance for which **retirement** is calculated."* One word, and
   it is the word that keeps the reorder from being a lateral move.

3. **Which of two cures for the F-8 category error to keep.** A concurrent revision had already made a
   narrower repair — *"the effective date of a qualifying retirement"* — and the Director approved the
   predictive form. I kept the approved form and superseded the interim one. The ambiguity was whether
   *"enact"* meant *enact these words* or *cure this defect*; I took it as the former, because the
   predictive form states the member's duty as subsection F actually imposes it and because
   [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) tested that predictive duty expressly and cleared it. **Recorded because
   a different drafter would defensibly have kept the shorter interim wording and reported the question
   closed.**

4. **Whether a § 415(b)-capped allowance needs a third counterfactual.** No. Recorded in §5.11 as
   considered rather than fixed. The ambiguity — whether such an allowance is *"calculated in accordance
   with subdivision A 1"* — is real and I left it, on the ground that the population is negligible and a
   third counterfactual costs clarity in a sentence already carrying two.

**And five I did not resolve by drafting choice, because each is the Director's.** S-2's choice among
three fixes, S-3's two new clauses in G 4, M-1's conforming trigger on a deadline set on
[MOO-44](/MOO/issues/MOO-44), and N-1 and N-2's § 51.1-155.1 gateway. All five are drafted in full in
§7 items 27 to 30 and **none is in the bill.** I enacted three repairs the Director did not pre-approve
and declined to enact these five, and the line between the two sets is the one stated in
§0.0000000000000000c: a repair to words this revision was already enacting, which changes no member's
outcome, is drafting; anything that adds a provision, moves another section, or picks between fixes with
different consequences is not.


## 7. Open items 27 to 30, with the candidate text

27. **NEW IN REVISION 21, from [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82)'s S-2. § 51.1-153 E's 90-day bar and D 1
    clause (ii) — belt and braces, or leave it on the extension sentence?** The reviewer's single most
    serious finding, and I think it is substantially answered by text they did not have. **The
    mechanism is real.** D 1 clause (ii) lets the member file up to 30 days after the Board's written
    statement with no outer bound, and the same sentence preserves *"the limitation in subsection E of
    § 51.1-153"* — verified verbatim: *"the effective date of retirement … shall not be more than 90
    days prior to the filing of the notice of retirement."* So on the face of clause (ii) alone, a late
    Board statement could leave the member unable to reach back to a date inside her window, failing
    the third date requirement in *"qualifying retirement"* and firing the G 2 clawback **because the
    Board was late**. **Why I think it does not bite.** D 1's last sentence already provides that where
    the Board gives that statement late, *"the member's final qualifying retirement date is extended by
    the number of days by which the statement is late, [and] the member may state an effective date of
    retirement that is no earlier than the first day of the month following the month in which the
    Board gives the statement."* The extension is automatic and the prospective route is express, so on
    the reviewer's own facts she names a date in the month after the statement, § 51.1-153 E is never
    engaged, and the extended window contains it. I could construct no case where a late statement
    alone defeats the definition. **What survives.** The member who backdates under clause (ii) rather
    than taking the extension can still meet the 90-day bar, and nothing tells her the extension is the
    safer route. **Three candidate texts, any of which is one sentence.** (a) *Notice content* — add to
    D 1's duty to state the periods: *"and shall state that where the Board's statement is late the
    member's final qualifying retirement date is extended and the member may state a later effective
    date of retirement."* **My recommendation, because it is the only one that touches nothing outside
    D 1.** (b) *Disapply the limitation* — after *"subject to the limitation in subsection E of
    § 51.1-153"* add *"except that that limitation shall not apply to a notice filed within the period
    allowed by clause (ii)."* Cleanest cure, but it disapplies a Chapter 1 limitation for one class of
    member, which is a bigger ask than the defect warrants. (c) *Deem it an error* — in G 4: *"A failure
    of the Board to give the written statement required by the definition of 'final qualifying
    retirement date' in subsection A when due is an error of the Board for the purposes of clause (iii)
    of this subdivision."* Belt and braces, and it also catches the Board-delay cases nobody has thought
    of; but it is a new deeming provision in the subsection the Director settled on
    [MOO-44](/MOO/issues/MOO-44). **One of the three, or none — and note that (a) and (c) are not
    alternatives; they are cheap together.**

28. **NEW IN REVISION 21, from [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82)'s S-3, and this is the one I would fix
    first. The G 2 trigger enacted in revision 21 can claw back a member whose disability retirement is approved
    a month later, and there is no way back.** F-2(a) — which the Director approved and which is
    enacted — starts the Board's 60-day clock at *"the date on which the member retires in a retirement
    that is not a qualifying retirement."* A disability retirement is not a service retirement under
    § 51.1-153, so it is not a qualifying retirement, so the clock starts on the day she retires. But
    G 4 switches subdivisions 2 and 3 off only when the member *"**is approved for** a disability
    retirement allowance"* — an event that routinely post-dates the retirement by months. **So the
    Board is now commanded to cut back her credit and refund her money on a timetable that can expire
    before the approval that would have protected her arrives.** Worked: retires 1 March, not yet
    approved; clause (b) fixes the deadline at 30 April; notice 1 April, determination effective 1 May,
    36 months cut to 11 and the balance refunded; approval lands 1 July. **And G 4 makes it worse than
    the reviewer knew.** Its own later sentence provides that *"no certified subsidy is settled under
    this subdivision after … a determination under subdivision 2 or 3 has taken effect."* So on
    approval, G 4's opening words say subdivisions 2 and 3 *"shall not apply"* — arguing her credit
    revives — while that sentence bars the subsidy from ever settling. **Her credit and the money that
    pays for it come apart, and the same gap is open for the member who dies after a non-qualifying
    retirement but before the determination takes effect.** This was not reachable before revision 21's F-2(a):
    the old clock ran from the final qualifying retirement date, normally far later than any pending
    approval. **Two clauses, drafted, not enacted**, to be added to G 4: *"The Board shall not make a
    determination under subdivision 2 while an application of the member for a disability retirement
    allowance under this chapter is pending."* And: *"Where a determination under subdivision 2 has
    taken effect and the member is thereafter approved for a disability retirement allowance under this
    chapter or dies, the Board shall rescind the determination, shall restore the service credit reduced
    under it, and shall recover no amount from the member, from any survivor or beneficiary of the
    member, or from the member's estate; and the certified subsidy may be settled under this subdivision
    notwithstanding the preceding sentence."* **I recommend both.** The first is prophylactic and the
    second is the unwind; one without the other leaves either the race or the dead end. They are new
    provisions in the subsection the Director settled on [MOO-44](/MOO/issues/MOO-44), which is why they
    are on this card and not in the bill.

29. **NEW IN REVISION 21, from [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82)'s M-1. G 4's involuntary-separation deadline
    now competes with G 2's — and the reviewer says enact, against my own recommendation to ask.** I
    raised this at 00:50 as a tidy point, reasoning that the specific provision governs and that
    F-2(b)'s make-whole payment means nobody loses money. **The first half holds and the second half was
    too narrow.** G 2's third sentence bars the Board from paying the member *any* retirement allowance
    until the determination is made, and the 30-day notice and the subsection M review right both attach
    to it — so the unresolved deadline decides **when she first receives any money at all** and **when
    her review clock opens**, not merely a reporting date. On the G 2(b) reading her allowance begins
    around day 110; on the G 4 reading, around day 180. F-2(b) pays the arrears and does not close a
    two-to-three month gap with no income. *Generalia specialibus non derogant* does not resolve it
    cleanly, because both provisions are specific and both are in the same enactment. **Eighteen words,
    drafted, not enacted**, in G 4's involuntary-separation sentence: *"within 60 days after the
    expiration of that 90-day period, within 60 days after the date on which the member retires in a
    retirement that is not a qualifying retirement, or within 60 days after the member's final
    qualifying retirement date, whichever occurs first."* **I recommend enacting it.** One word
    converts it.

30. **NEW IN REVISION 21, from [MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82)'s N-1 and N-2, and it is the same question
    as F-7. Does a § 51.1-155.1 involuntary-separation retirement pass through the gateway in both
    definitions — and if it does, does the interstate-commission member in § 51.1-155.1 B pass with
    it?** Both definitions are gated on a retirement *"under § 51.1-153"* and on the date the member
    *"may retire under § 51.1-153."* § 51.1-155.1 A and C give an involuntarily separated member with 20
    or more years *"**may retire** with the retirement allowance as provided in subdivision A 1 of
    § 51.1-155"* at 50 (or 60), which is **its own retirement authority with its own age gate**, in a
    section titled *"Exceptions **from** general early retirement provisions."* Two readings: it is a
    § 51.1-153 B retirement on modified terms (gateway open), or it is not a § 51.1-153 retirement at
    all — in which case the member's *"unreduced retirement eligibility date"* is computed **ignoring
    the only route by which she can actually retire unreduced.** The ambiguity is textual, not
    practical, and one cross-reference settles it either way: in the gateway, *"may retire under
    § 51.1-153 **or § 51.1-155.1**"*, or in the drafter's note, a statement that it does not.
    **N-2 is the part I had not seen and it is the reason not to answer this with a bare yes.**
    § 51.1-155.1 **B** — the chief executive of an interstate commission — is not parallel to A and C:
    she *"may retire **without the reduction in retirement allowance required by subdivision A 2** of
    § 51.1-155,"* so her allowance is computed under **A 2 with the reduction waived**, not under A 1.
    On the positive limb she **fails** while A and C members pass, though she is economically identical
    — a zero-reduction retiree, which is exactly the member [MOO-62](/MOO/issues/MOO-62) decided should
    pass. The population is tiny and it is free to close now. **Opening the gateway for A and C and not
    for B is the kind of unexplained line a hearing draws an arbitrary-classification question along**,
    so if the answer is to open it, I would open it for B in the same edit — which needs a second limb
    on the negative test, not just a second citation on the gateway. **Direction of the doubt if nothing
    is done: exclusion**, and no member is made worse off than today, because G 4 (iii) vests the credit
    on the separation itself. But §7 item 8's overlap population rests on the open reading, and
    [@Statutory Researcher](agent://d2a2feeb-989e-40ec-9cf6-496e7633daa6) has the research question
    (F-7).


## 8. Status

**Revision 22 — the four [MOO-65](/MOO/issues/MOO-65) answers are complete and the
[MOO-82](/MOO/issues/MOO-82) review is dispositioned.** Store revision 21 enacted **F-2** in G 2;
store revision 22 enacts **F-1**, **F-8** and **F-4**, and repairs three defects the review found in
the enacted text. **Five edits in four provisions**, each applied by single-occurrence assertion, with
§1 diffed afterwards to confirm that the only paragraphs that differ from revision 21 are the two
definitions, D 1, G 2 and G 4.

**Of the fourteen findings: three are enacted** (S-1's scope repeat and M-2's reorder in the two
definitions, m-1's antecedent on revision 21's G 2 sentence); **one needs no text and is answered on
the record** (M-3 — subsection A already opens *"As used in this section"*); **two are recorded as
considered** (m-3, m-2); **one is not mine** (m-4, model code); and **five are on the card as items 27
to 30 and are in the bill nowhere.** The cross-reference check is at §5.11, the ambiguities at §6.0-21,
and the two corrections to my own record at §a — this is **revision 22**, and `bill-text-s8-rev18` on
[MOO-64](/MOO/issues/MOO-64) is **superseded and must not be pasted over `bill-text-s8`.**

**What revision 22 asks the Director, and the order I would take it in.** **Item 28 first** — it is the
only one of the five where a member can lose purchased credit and the money behind it with no way back,
and the trigger that creates it is one of the four answers, now enacted. Then **item 29**, which the
reviewer says to enact and which I now agree should be enacted. Then **item 27**, where I think the
reviewer's most serious finding is substantially answered by a sentence already in D 1 and the residual
is a notice point. Then **item 30**, which is one cross-reference and is free to close in either
direction today. **Nothing on this list blocks the fiscal statement**, and no figure in the package
moves on account of revision 22 (§g).

**One structural point that is now a standing constraint, not a one-off.** `bill-text-s8` reached the
platform's **524,288-character document ceiling** during this revision. Revision 22 fits only because
it closed §7 item 18 and because this record was split out into a companion document. **Every revision
from here needs either a companion document or a decision to move the §0.x retained record out of
`bill-text-s8` entirely.** That is a call about another run's record as well as mine, so I am flagging
it rather than making it.

**One thing the review found that this document cannot answer, recorded because it belongs in the memo
and not in the bill.** Four of the six changes the two revisions made are in subsection G — the cutback
and refund machinery, the exception path — and **no published artifact reports the share of the S8
population that retires at an A 1-unreduced door**, which is the quantity that decides whether G 2 is
an exception at all. The live model carries no payment-form dimension, so it cannot be varied to bound
it, and the direction of any error runs one way: toward the bill costing **less** than modelled and
harming **more** members than modelled. Routed to
[@Fiscal & Impact Modeler](agent://428b53bf-f49e-4505-a607-3560a26b3d50) with the reviewer's two asks.
Until it is reported, the statement in §3 that subsection G is an exception path is an assumption of
this document and not a finding of the file.

**This is an internal working draft, not a Division of Legislative Services bill, and it has not been
reviewed by counsel.**

title: Revision 22 — the full record: redline, verbatim operative strings, cross-reference check and drafter's note for the §7 item 22 answer (option (c)) — internal working draft
body:
# Revision 22 — the full record

**MOO-42 · MOO-87 · Drafting Specialist · 12 October 2026 · INTERNAL WORKING DRAFT — pre-decisional**

> **Standing caveat.** This is a working draft for internal use. It is not a Division of Legislative
> Services bill, it has not been reviewed by counsel, and nothing in it is legally sufficient for
> introduction. Only DLS drafts official bills.

> **Where the text is, and the one thing this record got wrong.** These two edits are in
> [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), landed by the **revision 24** rebase
> (store revision 28) and not by a verbatim promotion of the parked body. They were drafted on
> [MOO-87](/MOO/issues/MOO-87) against **store revision 21** and parked there as
> `bill-text-s8-rev22` because MOO-42's store could not be written that heartbeat: `PUT` returned
> **409 Issue run ownership conflict** and `POST /checkout` returned **409 Issue checkout conflict**.
> The redline in §2 and the operative strings in §3 are unaffected by the rebase and are the text as
> enacted; the base and byte figures below are the corrected ones.

> **The correction, and it matters because it nearly cost four enacted decisions.** This record
> originally said that the two revisions standing between revision 21 and the promotion "never landed
> in the store" and that "neither changed a word of bill text". **That was wrong as to store revision
> 22**, which did land and which enacted the four [MOO-65](/MOO/issues/MOO-65) repairs in five
> provisions: the option- and lump-sum-neutrality words in *"qualifying retirement"* and *"unreduced
> retirement eligibility date"*, the qualifying-retirement effective-date wording in **D 1**, the
> retroactive-allowance sentence in **D 2** subdivision 2, and the deeming carve-out in **D 4**
> subdivision 4. Promoting the parked body verbatim would have **reverted all five.** What was
> promoted instead is store revision 23's body with the two edits below applied to it. The check that
> made that safe: the two lines the edits touch — *"eligible member"* and subsection C — differ from
> the parked body **only** by the commissioned edits, so the rebase is byte-exact rather than a
> re-draft, and the five other lines that differ are store revisions 22 and 23's own and are
> preserved. Two consequences that do survive from the original note: **store revision 23's §7
> item 22 option (d)** — sever the measurement date from the payment deadline and fix it by statute —
> **is superseded by the Director's (c), which is the same move with the numeral fixed at zero**; and
> **§7 item 28, the store ceiling, is answered in fact** — store revisions 23 and 24 moved the §0.x
> narrative for revisions 2 to 12 and then 16 and 17 out to
> [`bill-text-s8-revision-history`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8-revision-history), which
> is landed, so `bill-text-s8` has headroom against the ceiling rather than 87 characters.

---

## 1. What was decided, and what revision 22 does

The Policy Director decided two things on [MOO-71](/MOO/issues/MOO-71) on 12 October 2026 and
commissioned them on [MOO-87](/MOO/issues/MOO-87):

1. **§7 item 22 is answered as option (c).** Subsection C clause (ii) of § 51.1-142.4 is measured as
   of the **filing date of the complete application**, not the completion date, and the two sentences
   that ran on the old measurement are conformed.
2. **Conditioned on item 1:** a purchase that would not advance the member's unreduced retirement
   eligibility date by at least one month is barred, and the bar must operate at the **subdivision
   D 4** determination, not after payment.

**Two changed places in the bill text, both inside § 51.1-142.4.** No figure moves. No bracket is
added or resolved — `[20]` percent remains the only one. No definition is added, no section is added,
the bill title does not change, and no new Code citation is introduced. Nothing in §7 other than item
22 is touched: **item 23's involuntary-separation narrowing is untouched and still open**, and so are
items 4, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 18 (Q1/Q3/Q4), 19, 20, 21, 24, 26 and 27.

---

## 2. The redline — both edits in full

### Edit 1 — § 51.1-142.4, subsection C

**Out** (three changes to one subsection):

> (ii) the number of months of creditable service the member needs in order to have reached his
> unreduced retirement eligibility date ~~as of the completion date stated in the Board's
> certification under subsection D, taking account of the membership service the member will have
> earned by that date~~;
>
> The Board shall determine each of these amounts and shall state them, ~~and~~ the completion date,
> in the certification required by subsection D.
>
> ~~The member may complete payment before the completion date only if the member requests the Board
> in writing to redetermine the amounts under this subsection as of the earlier date and the Board
> recertifies the election under subdivision D 6 as of that date.~~
>
> ~~Where the completion date is extended under subdivision B 4 f of § 51.1-142.2, or is extended for
> any other cause not attributable to the member, the amount under clause (ii) of this subsection
> shall be determined as of the completion date last stated before the extension.~~

**In:**

> (ii) the number of months of creditable service the member needs in order to have reached his
> unreduced retirement eligibility date <u>as of the filing date of the member's complete
> application, taking account of the membership service the member has earned as of that date</u>;
>
> The Board shall determine each of these amounts and shall state them, <u>the filing date of the
> member's complete application, and</u> the completion date, in the certification required by
> subsection D.

Nothing replaces the two deleted sentences. §4 item 1 records why, and the sentence I drafted as a
replacement and did **not** enact.

### Edit 2 — § 51.1-142.4, subsection A, definition of "eligible member"

**In**, as a new clause (vii), with the old clause (vii) renumbered **(viii)** and no other change to
the definition:

> <u>(vii) would, if the member's maximum purchasable amount determined as of the date the member
> files that application were credited to the member on that date, reach his unreduced retirement
> eligibility date at least one month earlier than the date on which the member would reach his
> unreduced retirement eligibility date determined without that service credit, and</u>

**Markup note.** The whole of § 51.1-142.4 is new language and is reproduced underlined in §1 of
`bill-text-s8`; these are revision-to-revision changes inside language that is already new, so the
strike-through and underline above are the *drafting* redline against store revision 21, not the
amendatory markup of the bill. The bill's own markup is unchanged: § 51.1-142.4 is wholly underlined,
and the only struck language anywhere in §1 remains the single word *"For"* in the concluding
paragraph that follows subdivision B 3 of § 51.1-142.2, verified by searching §1 for strike-through.

---

## 3. The verbatim operative strings

As requested, and as on MOO-75 and MOO-79. These are the strings to diff against.

**3.1 Subsection C, as amended, in full.** The bill reproduces it underlined; the underlining is
stripped here so the string can be compared character for character.

```
C. An eligible member may purchase under an election no more service credit than the least of (i) four years, less any service credit previously purchased by the member under subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2; (ii) the number of months of creditable service the member needs in order to have reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date as of the filing date of the member's complete application, taking account of the membership service the member has earned as of that date; and (iii) the number of years of creditable service the member has earned as a state employee. The Board shall determine each of these amounts and shall state them, the filing date of the member's complete application, and the completion date, in the certification required by subsection D. The Board shall not accept an election for which the amount determined under clause (ii) of this subsection is zero. Where the Board determines that it may not accept an election for the reason stated in the preceding sentence, the Board shall give the member written notice of the determination, of the reasons for it, and of the member's rights under subsection B of § 51.1-142.2, no later than 30 days after making the determination, and the member may seek review of the determination under subsection M.
```

**3.2 The new clause (vii), on its own.**

```
(vii) would, if the member's maximum purchasable amount determined as of the date the member files that application were credited to the member on that date, reach his unreduced retirement eligibility date at least one month earlier than the date on which the member would reach his unreduced retirement eligibility date determined without that service credit,
```

**3.3 "Eligible member", as amended, in full.**

```
"Eligible member" means a member in service who (i) is a state employee, (ii) is covered under the retirement plan established by this chapter, whether or not the member is a person described in clause (i) or (ii) of subdivision A 1 of § 51.1-155, (iii) does not participate in the hybrid retirement program established by § 51.1-169, (iv) is eligible to purchase service credit for prior active duty military service under subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-142.2, (v) has not reached his unreduced retirement eligibility date, determined without the service credit to be purchased, on the date the member files a complete application, (vi) would, if the member's maximum purchasable amount determined as of the date the member files that application were credited to the member on that date, reach his unreduced retirement eligibility date on or before the first day of the month following the month in which the member files that application, (vii) would, if the member's maximum purchasable amount determined as of the date the member files that application were credited to the member on that date, reach his unreduced retirement eligibility date at least one month earlier than the date on which the member would reach his unreduced retirement eligibility date determined without that service credit, and (viii) would reach his unreduced retirement eligibility date, determined with the service credit to be purchased, on or before the first day of the month following the month in which that service credit is credited to the member. "Eligible member" does not include a member of a retirement system established under Chapter 2 (§ 51.1-200 et seq.), Chapter 2.1 (§ 51.1-211 et seq.), or Chapter 3 (§ 51.1-300 et seq.), a teacher, an employee of a political subdivision, the Governor, the Lieutenant Governor, the Attorney General, a member of the General Assembly, or any person whose retirement allowance would be payable under subdivision B 2 of § 51.1-155.
```

(1 July 2029), the reenactment requirement (2028 Session), the sunset (1 July 2033) and enactment 5's

## 4. §6.0-22 — Drafter's note: the six ambiguities I resolved

**1. Whether to replace the two deleted sentences with an express freeze. I did not, and this is the
one call in the revision I would most like a reviewer to attack.** The Director's instruction was to
conform two sentences that would otherwise "operate on a measurement that no longer moves", which is
an instruction to delete. The question is whether their deletion leaves anything able to move the
clause (ii) quantity after certification. I chased it and the answer is no: clause (ii) is now a
**historical** computation — the months needed to have reached the date *as of a date in the past* —
so no later fact can change it; subdivision D 4 independently fixes the filing date "for all purposes
of this section"; and subdivision B 4 b already provides that the amount payable "shall not change by
reason of the method by which, or the date on which, payment is made or completed." **The one sentence
I drafted and did not enact**, if counsel wants it express:

> <u>The amount determined under clause (ii) of this subsection shall not be redetermined by reason
> of any extension of the completion date, by reason of the date on which the member makes or
> completes payment, or by reason of any recertification under subdivision D 6.</u>

It adds nothing the words "as of the filing date" do not already do, and the Director's standing
instruction is that I do not add provisions that were not agreed. One word and it goes in.

**2. Clauses (i) and (iii) of subsection C — left alone, and the reason is a cross-reference rather
than a preference.** The Director left these to my judgment. Neither has an express measurement date
today, and giving them the filing date would **break three notices**: subdivisions D 3, D 4 and D 5
each quote the standard cost of "the applicant's maximum purchasable amount determined as of that
date", meaning the date of the notice, and the definition of "maximum purchasable amount" reads
clauses (i) and (iii) of subsection C "on that date". Fix those clauses to the filing date and the
defined term has nothing to read on any other date. Both also run in the member's favour when read
later — clause (iii) only grows with state service, clause (i) is static unless the member separately
purchases military credit at standard cost — so freezing them would take something away for nothing.
**And the admission test and the quantity cannot diverge as a result**: admission requires that the
maximum purchasable amount at the filing date suffice to reach the date, and the maximum purchasable
amount is itself the least of the B 2 entitlement and clauses (i) and (iii) at that same date, so the
amount subsection C then permits is the clause (ii) quantity exactly. The one residual case — a member
who buys military credit at standard cost between filing and certification, shrinking clause (i) — is
caught by clause (i) at certification and then by clause (viii) at crediting, which is the architecture
revision 17 put there, and by § 51.1-142.2 B 2's own four-year cap, which operates outside the election.

**3. Placement: a clause in "eligible member", not a sentence in subsection C — and a separate clause
rather than a lettered limb of clause (vi).** The Director's condition was that the bar "operate at
admission, not after payment", and that the member "learn it at the D 4 30-day determination, with
D 4's reasons, standard-cost statement and review". Subsection C's own bar (the zero-month refusal)
has its own notice sentence and speaks when the Board decides whether to **accept an election**;
subdivision D 4's machinery — the 30-day deadline, the statement of reasons, the standard cost of the
applicant's maximum purchasable amount, the express right to file a further application, and review
under subsection M — attaches to the determination "whether an applicant is an **eligible member** as
of the filing date of the applicant's complete application". A clause in that definition therefore
inherits every element of the condition without a word of new procedure. I made it a separate clause
rather than a second lettered limb of clause (vi), which would have been shorter, for two reasons:
the bar is a distinct policy the Director will have to defend and it should be citable as "clause
(vii)"; and the fiscal model's population labels speak of the "clause (v)+(vi) population", which
keeps its meaning only if clause (vi) keeps its.

**4. "At least one month earlier" — what it means, and the proxy I declined.** The test compares two
dates on the same counterfactual: the unreduced retirement eligibility date the member would reach if
her maximum purchasable amount at the filing date were credited on that date, against the date she
would reach without it. **One month is a calendar month measured back from the later of the two
dates**; where the later date falls on a day with no counterpart in the preceding month, ordinary
Virginia practice reads the last day of that month, and no provision in the bill turns on the
difference. **I declined the tidier proxy**, which would have read "would not reach his unreduced
retirement eligibility date, determined without the service credit to be purchased, before the first
day of the second month following the month in which the member files that application". It is shorter
and it keys to the same calendar as clauses (v) and (vi), but it is **not the Director's rule**: because
clause (vi) already caps the with-purchase date at the first day of the month following filing, the
proxy refuses some members whose purchase **does** advance the date by a month, and that would move a
population the Director priced. The direct comparison was the right answer even though it costs a
repeated premise.

**5. Which quantity the bar tests.** The Director's candidate sentence tested "the member's purchase of
his maximum purchasable amount", and I kept that rather than testing "the service credit to be
purchased". The two coincide here — subsection C permits exactly the clause (ii) quantity, and crediting
either the clause (ii) quantity or the larger maximum purchasable amount puts the unreduced date at the
filing date, because the date is the *earliest* date the member may retire and she cannot retire before
she holds the credit — but the maximum purchasable amount is a defined term the Board determines from
its own records on the date it already determines eligibility, and clause (vi) is keyed to it. Keying
clause (vii) to the same quantity is what keeps clauses (vi) and (vii) from selecting different members,
which is the defect revision 17 existed to close. The counterfactual is constructed exactly as clause
(vi)'s is: the amount is *assumed* credited on the filing date, and "determined without that service
credit" means the date she would reach with no purchased credit at all, which is the base clause (v)
uses.

**6. The filing date added to the certification is mine, not the Director's, and can be cut.** The
certification sentence listed the completion date partly because clause (ii) was measured on it. The
completion date is still needed — payment is due by it, and the definition of "certified subsidy" prices
the anticipated earliest qualifying retirement date off it — but after this revision the certification
would no longer state the date clause (ii) **is** measured on, and the member cannot check the
Board's arithmetic without it. Nine words. If the Director would rather the certification say nothing
new, strike `the filing date of the member's complete application, and`.

[MOO-71](/MOO/issues/MOO-71), none of which is a reprice.**

1. **The bar is drafted on the maximum purchasable amount, not on the amount to be purchased** (§4
   item 5). If the model tests the band on the amount actually certified, the two give the same answer
   for the reasons in that item, but the model should test the drafted quantity.
2. **The zero-month bar survives and now overlaps the new clause (vii).** Under (c) the 0.46 refusals

**For the Editor, in three sentences.** A veteran who wants to buy military service at the pilot price
is now measured on the day she applies, not on a date the Retirement System picks up to a year later,

accept a purchase that would not move her unreduced retirement date forward by at least a month, which
keeps the Commonwealth from paying a subsidy to someone who was about to reach that date anyway. The

**Revision 5 delivered — [MOO-53](/MOO/issues/MOO-53) is in the text.** Document [`bill-text-s8`](/MOO/issues/MOO-42#document-bill-text-s8), revision `0ee761fa`.

**First, housekeeping.** My previous run died mid-sentence and left a one-line comment above reading *"Now G 2's trigger timing and the retroactivity consequence:"*. **Disregard it** — it is a crash artifact, not a finding. The MOO-54 work it was announcing had already landed in the document as revision 4; §0.0 and §8 of the draft carry it in full.

## MOO-53 asked me to price my own definition rather than assert it. It confirmed the structure and broke two of my numbers.

**Confirmed.** Clause (i) − (ii) − (iii) *"is `CS_ledger` in structure — one liability measure, two states of the world, no overlap."* MOO-45 §2.2's **$2,374,550 / 44 percent** double count is eliminated in full, and the quantity reconciles to MOO-31 §4.1's published `$5,370,529` to the dollar. The acceleration standard forecloses **both** zero-acceleration readings on **all 44 priced cells**, with +3.33 and +1.79 years of margin. The floor stays. My reading of the two clocks stands.

**Three changes to bill text, all mine, none of them a policy choice:**

| | Was | Is | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D 2 ceiling** | `[$80,000]` | **`[$100,000]`** | $80,000 is below **$81,278**, the cheapest election the bill admits, so it excluded part of the subsidy of **100 percent** of the eligible cohort. MOO-46 Decision 2(e)'s own rule returns $100,000 on **both** cohorts. Still bracketed; the figure is MOO-48's. |
| **Clause (ii)** | indeterminate in two ways | **rewritten** | It did not choose between the expected present value and the PV at the expected date — a **6.7 percent** spread with the Board picking. And it forecloses the zero-acceleration readings by naming a **source** rather than a **property**, so a future assumption table with a 100 percent rate at first eligibility reopened MOO-44 §8's **$11,148,043** case on the same words. Now: expected value over the projected distribution; decrement set named expressly; no rate applied as though certain; projection may not be made by reference to an eligibility date. **The priced basis does not move.** |
| **D 2 / D 3 contingency** | 10 percent, **outside** the cap | **`[20]` percent, inside** | D 2 capped certified subsidies; D 3 reserved the contingency *"in addition to"* each one. The act's own reserve escaped a cap D 3 simultaneously asked DPB to confirm was funded. **A cap the act can exceed is not a cap**, and D 2's self-executing character is the whole of the agreed admission rule. And 10 percent covers the median member but **fails the 90th percentile on every channel priced**. |

## The thing you most need from this, and it is not a drafting point

**The redraft did not reduce the certified subsidy. It more than doubled it.** Aggregate goes **$4,930,054 → $10,996,295 (+123 percent)**, mean per member **$49,860 → $111,211**. Removing the double count lowered the number by $2.37M; pinning clause (ii) to VRS's actual retirement decrements raised it by $6.06M. **The drafted figure is 1.48× the double-counted figure it replaces.** Those were two separate changes in one revision and they will be read as one unless the brief separates them.

**Consequences, all now in §3 for the fiscal statement:**

- **$3,000,000 is exhausted in FY2030 — the first election year — and denies 72.7 percent of certified subsidy.** That supersedes MOO-45 §3.3's FY2031 and 58 percent. It funds **18.1** elections with no ceiling, **30.0** at `[$100,000]`.
- **Mean certified subsidy is 1.87× the full current-law price** of the credit the member is buying. That is the sentence a hostile witness will quote, and §3 now carries the only honest answer: clause (ii) applies a **population** retirement rate to a **self-selected** group, so **14 percent of the cohort would have retired within a year anyway** and the metered quantity **overstates true economic cost**. Conservative and safe for the cap; an overstatement for any "cost per veteran served" line.
- **MOO-44 §8 was wrong that the floor alone converts the worst case.** Under the zero-acceleration reading the floor certifies $2,621,670 — *below* the cap — so every member is admitted and nothing is rationed. Clause (ii) is the first line of defence; the floor is the second.
- **The honest uncertainty is take-up, not the counterfactual.** Only three drivers move the answer by more than 25 percent: take-up at 2× (+100), take-up high (+74), and removing the retire-immediately guardrail (−34). ±10 percent on the decrements is worth +10.2 / −7.7. **The definition and subsection F are a matched pair — neither can change without repricing the other.**

## Three things for you, and one I will not decide

**§7 item 14 — should clause (ii) name the termination decrement?** One phrase, **−$558,151** (−5.1 percent). I held the literal retirement-only reading because every priced figure is on that basis. **The sign is counter-intuitive and that is why it is yours:** for the 56 percent of this cohort already at 30 years of Plan 1 service, terminating commences an unreduced benefit immediately, so *including* termination makes the bill **cheaper**. A 5 percent fiscal change should not arrive as a drafting preference.

**§7 item 15 — contingency inside or outside the $3,000,000, and at what percentage?** Inside as drafted. Inverting it is **the first provision in this bill whose drafting makes an appropriation ask** — $3,750,000 at 25 percent — which is why I took the version that does not make one. Inside costs elections instead: 18.1 → 14.7 at 20 percent, 14.0 at 25. The supported percentage range is **20–25** and it is a **lower bound**, because the discount-rate channel could not be priced.

**§7 item 16 — MOO-46 Decision 2(e)'s two limbs no longer have a common solution.** *Fund 30 elections dearest-first* and *touch no Pathway B election* are now incompatible: Pathway B's maximum rose from $54,974 to **$182,800** and exceeds Pathway A's $170,343 — the modes inverted. The second limb is **unsatisfiable below $182,800**, where the ceiling trims nothing. **I drafted on the 30-election limb.** The Pathway B limb is arguably moot because clause (v) removes Pathway B by construction, but it was your rule and I am not retiring half of it silently. **If you intended the Pathway B limb to control, the ceiling has to come out of the bill altogether**, because no figure both satisfies it and binds.

**And one of my own defects, caught in this revision rather than after it.** The expected-value limb put *"the member's date of retirement"* between clause (ii)'s *"that date"* and its antecedent, so a reader could have valued clause (ii) as of the projected retirement date. The two clauses must be valued at the same instant or their difference is not a liability increase. Clause (ii) now says *"the valuation date stated in the certification"* in terms. Recorded in §6.2.

## One request I could not deliver, and it needs routing

**MOO-46's ceiling rule is applied to a distribution the window numeral moves, and nobody has been asked what it returns at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months.** MOO-53 answers it at 0 months only. This matters more than it did: MOO-53 §3.1 shows the identical-set interval around the figure has **collapsed from $18,890 to $4,114**, so unlike $80,000 on MOO-45's flat band, a figure chosen on one window will not survive another. **[MOO-48](/MOO/issues/MOO-48) is the issue that should answer it and I could not reach it** — it is one of this issue's own blockers, and cross-issue writes were refused while this issue is dependency-blocked. If it is already inside MOO-48's deadline-ladder scope, nothing needs doing; if not, it is the derivation I cannot supply by drafting, and the ceiling bracket cannot close without it.
